title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7208: Support jobs on non-x86 architectures
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7208: Support jobs on non-x86 architectures

State: closed
Opened: 2022-04-08T15:03:22Z
Closed: 2023-09-12T16:10:13Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High, Area: JobWrapper
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7208

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2022-04-08T15:03:22Z)

We want CRAB to support jobs running on non-x86 architecture, i.e. PPC or ARM.

At the moment there is not any non-x86 machine in the global pool [1], but they may be added in the future and we want to be prepared, with a solid understanding on how the arch is selected.

#### step 1: run jobs on arm64 when the user request it

If I understood correctly, the desired process needs to be

1. the user sets `$SCRAM_ARCH` in his env. crab client passes it to the crabserver when the user run `crab submit`.
2. TW uses the value of `$SCRAM_ARCH` to set "+DESIRED_Archs" in the JDL.
3. during the matchmaking, condor uses "+DESIRED_Archs" to match the "arch" classad advertised by the pilot.

Maybe we also need to set `+TARGET_Arch` in the JDL, but we do not think it will be necessary.

We should already have 1. and 3. in place. From a quick look at the code, it seems that we can achieve 2. simply improving [2], maybe with a mapping in common with WMCore, with an approach similar to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7191, but I may be wrong.

#### step 2: allow to run a job on multiple architecture

We are still not sure if this will ever be required.

This would be similar in spirit to https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11228.

However, CRAB does things a bit differently that WMCore and we still have some open questions.

For example, we currently take the scram_arch from the environment that the user submitted the task from. Under what circumstances we can widen it? For example, a user submits a simple task from x86 lxplus. When is the code that the user need to run allowed to run on arm as well?
Should we detect it somehow (hard) or should the user explicitly allow his code to run on arm as well with a new crab  client option?

Any comment, improvement, further explanation is very welcomed! :)

#### further references:

- https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/issues/11401

---

[1]. The pilots publish the architecture of the site in which they landed with the "arch" classad. at the moment only `X86_64` is present

```plaintext
# 2022-04-08, ~16.00 cern time
> condor_status -pool vocms0814.cern.ch -af arch | sort | uniq -c
 154675 X86_64
```

[2]

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/01c1bdd55853164a55a669cfa581212d17cf5682/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L364-L372

will be a byproduct of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7084

## Comment (mapellidario, 2022-12-13T11:03:16Z)

From a [discussion](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/gqrckwuo53y7dfk8jpk4x64jza) on cern mattermost

> REQUIRED_ARCH is something CRAB should set. Can be a comma separated list of architectures (including "any" if the job can run on any architecture)

I must admit that I am a bit confused. We have `REQUIRED_ARCH`, `TARGET.ARCH`, [desired_arch](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/452dc411e5c279a72d8129ca5692d00d331b0a7e/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L369) and [DESIRED_Archs](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/452dc411e5c279a72d8129ca5692d00d331b0a7e/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L116) and it is not clear to me which variable is used for what and if we can deprecate some of them. For example, I only find "old" references to `DESIRED_Archs` in WMCore, maybe we can stop using it in CRAB as well.

@mmascher Would you have any suggestion and up-to-date reference?

## Comment (mapellidario, 2022-12-13T11:09:20Z)

- He used `CMSSW_12_5_2` for `el8_aarch64_gcc10`. ("I picked a recent CMSSW version and one of the aarch64 scram arch")

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-06-02T16:34:35Z)

There is an alternative, which is using the `qemu` emulator, it looks promising, but I have not managed to solve all the quirks yet.

Open a shell on lxplus, make sure you use bash. Clone this repo https://github.com/cms-sw/cms-bot and cd into it.

```plaintext
[dmapelli@lxplus901 cms-bot]$ export SCRAM_ARCH=el9_aarch64_gcc11
[dmapelli@lxplus901 cms-bot]$ source ./dockerrun.sh
[dmapelli@lxplus901 cms-bot]$ dockerrun bash
[..., ignoring some errors...]
[I have no name!@lxplus901 cms-bot]$
```

then make sure that you can read from cvmfs with `ls /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch`, then you can

```
scram list CMSSW
cmsrel CMSSW_13_1_0
cd CMSSW_13_1_0
cmsenv
crab submit --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY -c ppc-crab.py
```

```plaintext
ERROR: Exception: The X509_CERT_DIR variable is not set and the /etc/grid-security/certificates/ directory cannot be found.
```

```
qemu: Unsupported syscall: 293

gsi.conf  vomsdir
```

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7502: Collect statistics on datasets usage in CRAB

State: open
Opened: 2023-01-20T11:59:16Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7502

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-01-20T11:59:16Z)

This issue tracks progress of work initiated by @dynamic-entropy also building up on https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/projects/14

We have 2 ambitious goals:

 1.  understand dataset fragmentation (when a small datasets is made of several blocks places "one here, one there" well enough to give us if we should embark in "coalescing datasets before submitting tasks" or not and what we may gain (may include understanding of error reasons as well)

 2.  understand dataset use and reuse and tape recall performance and well enough to tell us if we could extend the use of T2 space as a dynamic cache rather than a place of static datasets pre-location waiting for users to access them

## Comment (belforte, 2023-01-20T12:10:01Z)

as agreed in CRAB meeting, I kick this off by pasting here the summary of the presentation made by @dynamic-entropy which had been sitting in meeting minutes for months by now.

FYI @dynamic-entropy @dciangot @KatyEllis  @mapellidario @novicecpp . Feel free to add and better clarify current situation (e.g. I had a chat with Rahul on zoom before Xmas, but did not take notes) and what other or different goals we should have. I only wanted to have a place where we write things, not to impose my view.

```
Rahul showed some slides on his latest work with the dataset usage by CRAB.
There are some slightly confusing results, for example why there is a peak of usage ~40 days
after the first usage. Is this one user?
This repo can be cloned and run on SWAN: https://github.com/dynamic-entropy/CRABAnalysis.
The “crab_historical.ipynb” is the desired notebook.

Update from Rahul:
Rahul showed his Jupyter notebooks showing e.g. a histogram of dataset popularity
for CRAB jobs in the last 2 years.
He described wanting to run a ‘simulation’ to find ways to improve placement of data for CRAB jobs.
Rahul working on command to insert “user data” from  local disk to Rucio managed storage.
See https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/issues/275  . See above on new reporting guideline.

Reposting lines for Rahul still unclear, there’s a codi document to keep track
of questions which we are editing, but not clear that changes to it are noticed.
We agree with Diego that we will ask him to report in this meeting weekly
on work on “the CRAB active dataset” and “what data is on disk, why”,
and encourage him to use group channels in MatterMost
so we can all help and at least make sure that he gets coherent messages.
```

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-01-27T13:36:29Z)

### description

When a job finishes, we use condor_chirp to retrieve its exit code:

The log should look like

```plaintext
======== Figuring out long exit code of the job for condor_chirp ========
==== Long exit code of the job is 0 ====
======== Finished condor_chirp -ing the exit code of the job. Exit code of condor_chirp: 0 ========
```

but I noticed that with the new jobwrapper I was getting (for example, at https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/dmapelli/230127_122119:dmapelli_crab_20230127_132116/job_out.1.0.txt ):

```plaintext
======== Figuring out long exit code of the job for condor_chirp ========
/srv/condor_exec.exe: line 63: python: command not found
==== Failed to load the long exit code from jobReport.json.1. Falling back to short exit code ====
==== Short exit code of the job is 0 ====
======== Finished condor_chirp -ing the exit code of the job. Exit code of condor_chirp: 0 ========
```

### solution

force python3 at this line:

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f01f865625031b93709f311425b44b49923adae3/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L56

a PR is on its way

Labels: Priority: Medium, Status: In Progress, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7513

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-01-27T16:02:58Z)

RFC for [CRAB Disaster Recovery and Backup](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-disaster-recovery-and-backup.html) documentation.

Feel free to put your comment here or edit [crab-disaster-recovery-and-backup.md](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/cms-crab-docs/-/blob/d7a04c56cb0bb92391449d360e3629455abd4164/docs/technical/crab-disaster-recovery-and-backup.md) directly.

@belforte @mapellidario @KatyEllis please review.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-01-28T18:17:22Z)

comments:

1. I think that this should be removed, it may be intersesting to have in the general CRAB REST setup documentatio, but it does not help disaster recover
```
It is possible to ask DBA to roll back our schemas to any point in time within the last six months. But it will spawn a new schema instead of reverting to the current one.
```
2. files in S3 are removed automatically, I will change this line.
```
We never clean up, but it is bound to the lifetime of the task.
```
3. I checked our S3 documentation and found that the current automatic expiration policy is not documented, nor it is documented how to check it. We need to fix this and document how to (re)created the S3 containers.
4. Losing one Schedd should be better described. If we loose VM but CEPH volumes are saved, we can recreate VM and connect same volumes, tasks will be automatically restarted. If we loose one or both volumes, we loose everything

Do you need help with the Runbook for recovery ? I think we should write separate recovery procedure "from scratch" for each component. Also make sure we include things like openstack keys for crab-secretes. More than a disaster here, if Dario leaves CMS we need new S3 tokens.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-01-28T21:14:32Z)

answering my concern in 3. above, for lack of a better place I dump here this:
```bash
belforte@lxplus8s15/~> s3cmd getlifecycle s3://crabcache_prod
<?xml version="1.0" ?>
<LifecycleConfiguration xmlns="http://s3.amazonaws.com/doc/2006-03-01/">
	<Rule>
		<ID>p845g9ez7o36wijg25vg5div2pfj8eshm6srktlfa0qy6b4u</ID>
		<Prefix/>
		<Status>Enabled</Status>
		<Expiration>
			<Days>33</Days>
		</Expiration>
	</Rule>
</LifecycleConfiguration>
```
I made `s3md` work by following blindly instructions in https://clouddocs.web.cern.ch/object_store/s3cmd.html

**N.B.** the Openstack project name is `"CMS CRAB"`

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-01-30T13:12:02Z)

The only suggestion I have is that we can actually backup the github issues and pull requests to gitlab [1].

I have never done anything similar so I can not estimate how long it takes (~1h? ~1d?), but it does not seem too complicated. The only thing we need to be aware is that if we want the authors of the issues/pullrequests to be consistent, we need to add to our profile in gitlab.cern.ch the email that we use in github, as the gitlab docs mentions it:

> Before you begin, ensure that any GitHub user you want to map to a GitLab user has a GitLab email address that matches their [publicly visible email address](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/users#get-a-user) on GitHub.

This webpage explains it a bit better [2], it should be enough to browse to [3] and add there our github email address. We may also want to contact Diego before starting the import.

[1] https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/import/github.html#import-your-github-repository-into-gitlab
[2] https://jsramblings.com/keep-authors-when-importing-from-github-to-gitlab/
[3] https://gitlab.cern.ch/-/profile/emails

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-01-30T13:15:12Z)

>  I think we should write separate recovery procedure "from scratch" for each component

I agree. I suggest that we write a specific page "Install from scratch" for each component inside its directory. For example, I would place the REST "install from scratch" here [1].

Then either at the end of the Disaster recovery page that Wa created or in another new page, we link all the "install from scratch" pages. This is to avoid some repetitions among the "disaster recovery" pages and the "usual documentation about each component" ones.

[1]: https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/cms-crab-docs/-/tree/master/docs/technical/crab-rest

## Comment (belforte, 2023-01-30T14:09:27Z)

> The only suggestion I have is that we can actually backup the github issues and pull requests to gitlab [1].

CMSSW is using this already. So in case we can get instructions from e.g. Shahzad. Yet I am not sure that it is needed. In any case it would be better to have a CMS-wide (or at least O&Cwide solution), there are many GH backup tools around

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-01-30T14:17:16Z)

CMSSW is backing up code, not issues or PRs [1]. Or are they using a different repo for the issues?

[1] https://gitlab.cern.ch/cms-sw/cmssw/-/issues

## Comment (belforte, 2023-01-30T14:23:38Z)

I see. thanks Dario. But let's move to a different place the discussion on GH backup. Does not belong to this document. At this moment we have no backup and can only recover code from local clones.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-02-01T13:55:14Z)

Thanks for comment! I fixed the docs as Stefano suggested.
I agree to change runbook to "install from scratch" and put it on the component docs.

Lets me list things I need to do:
- [x] Sync issue from GH (open new issue)
- [ ] "Install from scratch" section for each crab component (open new issue)
- [ ] Add more info each component to answer these questions:
  - What is it?
  - How code/data are managed?
  - What happen if we lose all data?
  - Backup procedure?
  - Support contact?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-10-31T16:12:33Z)

Here is the [disaster recovery docs](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-disaster-recovery-and-backup.html) but we still lack the "Install from scratch".

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-02-02T10:42:17Z)

Quickly copy from minutes: Need to check if Rahul had done anything. Stefano has some useful code from Nick.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-02T15:56:05Z)

Here's the pointer to Nick's code which indicates how to plot the amount of storage space used by taperecall
https://github.com/belforte/utils/blob/master/notebooks/RucioTapeRecallUsage.ipynb
missing part is to extend this to all RSE's
and of course this should be somehow turned into somthing that we can see in Grafana

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-03-21T16:14:59Z)

Tomorrow at 11.00, I will have brainstorming session with Rahul (@dynamic-entropy) to setup monitoring to `crab_tape_recall` account.

These are questions from myself:
1. How to check if user abuse inputblocks to recall dataset for all block with seperate crab task? (i.e. submit 100 tasks to get 1 PB of RAW dataset)
1. (from O&C week's live note) Can we monitor the volume of tape recall over time?
1. How many duplicate rule (same dataset but recall from different crab tasks)?
1. Time series for tape recall per users, group by (and/or) number_of_rule/number_of_dataset/total_size(/?).
1. Time series for percentage recall successed vs failed (failed: STUCK and REPLICATION that longer than 14 days).
1. How long does it take for rule to change state from REPLICATION to OK?
1. (How do we get info from expired rules?)

@belforte @mapellidario @KatyEllis  Feel free to add more.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-23T14:31:16Z)

List of questions that monitoring should answer:
1. is it used/useful ? (how often is used, by how manym etc,)
2. does it work ? (success vs. fail)
3. how long does it take ?
4. how much data does it move ?
5. how much disk does it keep occupied ?

Then there are annoying details ... does some user abuse, can we use it to spot bugs/inefficiencies in data placement, which sites does it use .. which one can spend a lot of time on but really depend on the big picture first. And things we are curious about like what happens if rules expire before it is satisfied and in case how many rules hit that limit ... and should update rule expiration daily so that it is 14 days after last file on tape ? (now it is 14 days after request, since initial experience was that it takes a few hours and only exceptionally a couple days).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-03-23T20:08:48Z)

Thanks Stefano.

From meeting with Rahul today I cannot build any panel yet. Most of data we want are not ready to query in opensearch.
- Simple question like "usage over time" need to query database snapshot.
- If we want to group by crab user for usage, we need to do extra work to get this info (extract from did).
  - Usage per user need a lot of work (list rule > list content of each rule to get size > sum size group by user) .
- `How long does it take?` No data besides state from database snapshot.

Well, it is more complicated than I thought.

## Comment (dciangot, 2023-03-24T07:32:12Z)

@novicecpp  I agree, I think there is no way around using db snapshot via spark analitix for this kind of information. I have a baseline from which you can start play with. I did some basic analysis on tape recall some time ago.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-24T09:47:29Z)

I am not sure that tracking by user is important. By datatier and primaryDataSet would be enough (to be clear those are the T and P in : datasetname = /P/S/T ), We need to make it easy to find which dataset a taperecall rule refers to. We are free to change how containers we use are named if that helps.

There is also a clear "architectural" question: much of the info can be gathered from CRAB's TW logs as well. Do we go that way ? Or stick with what's available in Rucio ?

Is used quota per account available in OpenSeach ? Could it be added ? If not, could we start with some "automation" around [Nick's two lines](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7517#issuecomment-1413968908)

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7518: take care of secondary dataset location
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7518: take care of secondary dataset location

State: open
Opened: 2023-02-02T15:18:46Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Medium, Status: Available
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7518

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-02-02T15:18:46Z)

CRAB should be aware of secondary input data location, make sure it is accessible and run jobs where either primary or secondary data are as appropriate (using remote reading for the lighter data)
A possible action list is
- [ ] find out how to identify the secondary data set (config. may only indicate "userParent")
- [ ] add code in DBSDataDiscovery (the place where we talk to DBS) to find the needed parents and check location with Rucio
- [ ] if data are not on disk, decide if to ask a recall or give up and bump recall work to user
- [ ] if all data is on disk, decide if to use as DesiredSites the location(s) of primary or secondary. If Tier is different (RAW/SIM/RECO/AOD..) decide based on that. If same tier (sim + pileup e.g.) check for "pileup" string in db name. Or simply check dataset size and run where the dataset with most bytes is located

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7538: add support for indicating a Rucio container as input
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7538: add support for indicating a Rucio container as input

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-16T17:33:17Z
Closed: 2023-03-10T14:08:20Z
Labels: Status: Done, RUCIO, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7538

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-02-16T17:33:17Z)

* allow processing of a set of files described only by a Rucio container, no DBS.
 * only allow `splittingByFile` in this case.
 * do not allow a secondary dataset

User will specify something like:
```
config.Data.InputDataset = 'scope:container'
or
config.Data.RucioContainer = 'scope:container'
```
(which needs a corresponding CRABClient issue). But from CRABServer side we should assume
that somehow the `scope:container` did makes it to TW/DBSDataDiscovery , possibly reusing existing
`tm_dbs_url` and `tm_input_dataset`

FYI @dciangot

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-17T09:24:21Z)

I am currently leaning toward:
* keep `tm_input_dataset` as is with the dataset(container) name
* use the new functionality to store a `key:value` in `tm_user_config` to store a possible Rucio scope, and check for it very early in DBSDataDiscovery . Then the DID to be used for data discovery will be:
```python
    did =  kwargs['task','tm_user_config','rucioScope'] + ':' +  kwargs['task','tm_input_dataset']
```
- [x] check how this will interact with new blocklist feature ? Is this useful ? Can surely leave for later.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-22T17:05:45Z)

I have tried to modify [DBSDataDiscovery](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py) adding `if` statements here and there.
But that makes it hard to read and to get right w/o breaking things. I gave up after a few days trying.

I am leaning toward adding a new `RucioDataDiscovery` instead to be instantiated in the [Handler](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/518c4760055b4ee232129209ccfaf428a69c28dd/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py#L157-L161) like
```python
    if task['tm_job_type'] == 'Analysis':
        if task.get('tm_user_files'):
            handler.addWork(UserDataDiscovery(config=config, crabserver=crabserver, procnum=procnum))
        elif task.get('tm_user_config') and task['tm_user_config'].get('rucio_scope'):
            handler.addWork(RucioDataDiscovery(config=config, crabserver=crabserver, procnum=procnum, rucioClient=rucioClient))
        else:
            handler.addWork(DBSDataDiscovery(config=config, crabserver=crabserver, procnum=procnum, rucioClient=rucioCl
```
Advantages:
 *  I can't break current functionality

Disadvantages:
 * have to maintain same code in two places

So I may do a first implementation with a lot of replicated code (in progress), but the way to go is to refactor  [DBSDataDiscovery](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py) to be simple skeleton which may change for `DBSDataDiscovery` vs `RucioDataDiscovery` and a set of common functions to do "all work".

That step  may indeed be disruptive. I will need @novicecpp help to minimize chances of regression.

I gladly accept input on how to proceed otherwise, of course @mapellidario @dciangot @novicecpp
we can talk about it tomorrow e.g.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-27T22:56:56Z)

this will be done with the above CRABServer PR and with [this](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/pull/5189) PR in CRABClient where the new configuration parameter is introduced:
```python
config.Data.rucioScope = 'scope'
# examples
config.Data.rucioScope = 'cms'
config.Data.rucioScope = 'user.belforte'
```
I am nor sure if there's any value in supporting alternative syntax as well:
```python
config.Data.InputDataset = 'scope:container'
```
it is just more work[1] for ... which gain ?

[1] e.g. one of these:
* change client to parse and send rucioScope anyhow, but so fare client does never do this kind of manipulations
* change inputDataset validation in REST and possibly split it there and fill different DB fields
* change inputDataset validation in REST, pass it along with possibly `scope:` in front and parse it early in the task handling when deciding which DataDiscovery action to instantiate for this task. Makes it more complex what is now very straighforward code.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-01T10:54:41Z)

an initial implementation of this is in #7556
But that is not a good solution yet. Will keep this open even if we merge that.

Things to decide/do:

- [x] Fully implement support for Rucio DIDs in crabConfig even if name does not fit DBS lexicon for inputDataset
- [x] Do we do that via a new DB column, or adding to `tm_user_config` ?
- [x] Do we report bad configuration in TW or directly in REST ? (e.g. attemption split by lumi  with Rucio)
- [ ] more ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-01T17:16:25Z)

Curent plan, @dciangot please review (expecially last part about what we do not support
- no changes to CRABClient
- user specifies a Rucio did in place of data.inputDataset
- REST is modified (slightly) to allow storing it in `tm_input_dataset` ( a new `RX_RUCIODID` regexp is introduced to validate a Rucio DID)
- Handler.py decides if to put DBSDataDiscover or RucioDataDiscovery in the action list for this task
- RucioDataDiscovery assumes a proper DID in  `tm_input_dataset` : `scope:container` and does the needed
- in RucioDataDiscovery we
   * fail if splitting is not `FileBased`
   * fail is `secondary dataset` or `use_parents` in user config (no parentage, no lumi info in Rucio)
   * ignore inputblocks (if user wants a smaller container, they create it in Rucio).
   * ignore tape locations
   * do not support tape recall (do not want people to use cms:/a/b/RAW to go around limits iin DBSDataDiscovery)
   * automatically support partialDataset, since there is no tape recall it is straightforward to only use the blocks with a valid replica

That should do at least for the use case of "user creates some data locally ON DISK" and wants to register them in Rucio.

Those "not support" also minimize code overlap with DBSDataDiscovery !

Should those data ever go on tape I think we should assume the policy that "it is up to user to do this, if and when and where user will have access to a tape storage". So it will be user problem to retrieve from tape to disk before using in CRAB input.

Should we ever come to "some official production CMS data are only described as a Rucio container, not in DBS"... well... we will review and recode.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-06T16:59:34Z)

Implementation of plan as in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7538#issuecomment-1450525216 is now complete in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7556

Some final cleanup and this can be closed.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7542: condor_chirp - summary of current problems
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7542: condor_chirp - summary of current problems

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-17T17:37:49Z
Closed: 2024-08-23T10:57:05Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: Medium, Area: JobWrapper
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7542

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-02-17T17:37:49Z)

### What happens, brief

We have problems with condor_chirp both in production and with the new jobwrapper. I am still not sure if the two are not correlated and I think that my investigation for the new jobwrapper can help with current production problems.

fyi: @belforte @mmascher @novicecpp

##### production

Stefano noticed two similar errors with condor_chirp in production jobs running in slc6 that failed [1].
condor_chirp does not seem to have problems with jobs that finish successfully in production [2]

The current code that we run in production is [3].

##### new jobwrapper

While debugging https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7510 I came across a similar error and made some investigations.

With el8 and cc7 everything works. With scl6 I'm having some troubles.

### Cause of the problem (as far as i understand it)

I think all boils down to which python version is selected by `gwms-python`. When it selects py2.6, condor_chirp fails. This happens also in production when a job fails. When it selects python >= 2.7 everything is ok.

### what can we do in CRAB?

I think we have a couple of options:

a. Merge the PR https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7510 as is now (we use `gwms-python` for parsing the json with the exit code)
  - this will make all the jobs running in slc6 to have a wrong `Chirp_CRAB3_Job_ExitCode` until we manage to make gwms-python can select python >=2.7 (maybe from comp?). This can be done in crab or in gwms.
  - the regression with current production will not be great. the exit code from condor_chirp is already broken in production with jobs that fail, we will temporarily break it also for successful jobs
  - This would be the only problem that I know of with the new jobwrapper, it does not seem to affect many users and will be like this only until we find a fix

b. Change crab code in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7510 so that we force gwms-python to select a comp python >=2.7.
  - ~~I am still not sure how to do it, it will postpone the release of jobwrapper yet again~~
  - This seems reasonably simple, see comment below

~~I think that the pressure to push the jobwrapper onwards is greater than having condor_chirp exit code correct for only a small fraction of jobs.~~

~~Stefano, would you be ok to introduce temporarily a small regression to relieve us from the stress of not having the new jobwrapper in production?~~

Stefano, I would ask you still one more day to improve #7510 to fix this, then I will be ok deploying the new  jobwrapper to production.

Marco, do you think that you can do anything with gwms-python on gwms side? Or do you think that it would be easier to force it to select python 2.7 in CRAB land? I mean, if we are the only ones encountering this problem it may be easier to deal with it ourselves.

Please, notice that even if we change in #7510 the code that parses the json with the exit code from using python to something in bash/grep [4], condor_chirp will still use gwms-python and have problems with all slc6 jobs.

### what happens, long

I run many tests:

- multiple cmssw version
- multiple OS
- letting jobs finish correctly and killing them by setting a very short max runtime
- changing the env where condor_chirp is called
   1. leaving the env as is at the end of the job (current code in #7510), or
   2. sourcing the startup environment just before running condor_chirp. (which would be the same as using `cleanEnv=True`). You can appreciate the difference between these cases in the logs by looking at the pythonpath just before condor_chirp runs. This is achieved by running `.  $JOBSTARTDIR/startup_environment.sh` just before running condor_chirp. This file should already be present in current production [4], but with the new jobwrapper it is more complete and trustworthy [5].

If the information that follows is not enough, I can quickly run some more tests. I am used to it at this point and can quickly test anything you want

##### production

I managed to replicate on test11 what we see in production, running a task [230217_155816:dmapelli_crab_20230217_165813](https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230217_155816:dmapelli_crab_20230217_165813) where i forced the job failure. In this case, test11 code is the same as production with some debugging added just before running condor_chirp [6] .

- [job_out.1.0.txt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/dmapelli/230217_155816:dmapelli_crab_20230217_165813/job_out.1.0.txt) (job retried because "removed due to wall clock time limit"). slc6, cmssw 7, job ok, gwms-python 2.7.13, condor_chirp ok ✅
- [job_out.1.1.txt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/dmapelli/230217_155816:dmapelli_crab_20230217_165813/job_out.1.1.txt). slc6, cmssw 7, job failed, gwms-python 2.6.6, condor_chirp failed 🚫

So: gwms-python tends to select py2.7 from COMP, unless something goes wrong (for example on job failures) and it selects py2.6

##### new jobwrapper

the most results notable are

- task [230217_141417...](https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230217_141417:dmapelli_crab_20230217_151412). slc6, cmssw7 , job ok, leave env as is, `gwsm-python` points to 2.6.6: condor_chirp failed 🚫

- task [230217_143047...](https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230217_143047:dmapelli_crab_20230217_153045). slc6, cmssw 7, job ok, sourced container startup environment, `gwsm-python` points to 2.6.6: condor_chirp failed 🚫

The new jobwrapper always use a COMP environment with py3, also on slc6. gwms-python seem to prefer py2, there is no py2.7 from comp, it only finds the system python, which is py2.6 and is too old for condor_chirp.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-02-17T17:54:01Z)

i can confirm that by sourcing a py2.7 COMP environment just before running condor_chirp in `gWMS-.. .sh`  [1], then condor_chirp works as expected even with a successful slc6 job using the new jobwrapper [2].

I do not have more time today, I can come back to this issue on monday, but I think I can update #7510 with a switch. If I detect an slc6 OS, I source py2.7 from COMP before running condor chirp.

Sorry for the noise, I am still open to better suggestions.

And sorry if it took almost a whole week to debug the problem :sob:


## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-19T11:57:22Z)

thanks Dario for thorough investigation,
but I beg to disagree with your approach here, possibly because I am simply lost in this long list of tests.
I would rather approach this as:
1. you can't solve all world's problems
2. what exactly is failing at this point  ? If is only chirping of the job exit code when running on SL6 ... well, so be it and move on with life. Did you look at the fraction of jobs which use SL6 ? [1]
3. anyhow first thing is to test `condor_chirp` in the startup environment: does it work there ?
  * YES: ok, go to 2.
  * NO: hand it to SI (it is not our task to decide where they find python in the containers that they start and by attempting to do it we risk overlooking something, as Marco indicated pilots are common to CMS and other VO's).

I fear that you have spent more time already in this then it makes sense.

Rather, as discussed already, we should really avoid calling python inside "chirp the exit code" and do the FJR parsing before we leave the python env. or "prase in bash". Best thing IMHO is that when that FJR is created, the exit code is saved in a file.

And in the spirit of "JobWrapper restructuring using COMP env from /cvmfs" (a real nice thing which we did not have when the current wrapper was written), move execution of cmscp.py inside its own wrapper  so that gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh has no "python discovery" in it .

I believe in "simplify our wrapper and unify differenr implementation of same functionalities" more than in "solving all those odd problems which occupy 1/10^6 of the phase space while still taking a large fraction of our time".

job wrapper use condor_chirp when wrapper terminates to communicate exit code as a classAd. This proved to be a fragile operation. We should:

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7546: make sure old tasks are removed from condor queue
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7546: make sure old tasks are removed from condor queue

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-21T14:35:08Z
Closed: 2023-02-23T08:10:28Z
Labels: Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7546

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-02-21T14:35:08Z)

we have thousands of old task bootstrap jobs stuck in HOLD status in condor queues of all schedulers.
Dating back to 2020.
This should be harmless for condor.
But surely it is annoying and makes us so used to seeing so many held jobs that we may overlook problems.
See also this thread in MM : https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/7otyhpkhh3ni8gk3xpweuqh74e

Removing those held jobs is a bit tricky since they have these classAds
```
LeaveJobInQueue = true
PeriodicHold = time() > CRAB_TaskEndTime
```
Meaning that after a `condor_rm` jobs stick in the queue and are kicked back from status X (flagged for deletion) to H (Hold).

I managed to get rid of those jobs with:
```
sudo condor_qedit -con  qdate\<1671000000 PeriodicHold=Null
sudo condor_qedit -con  qdate\<1671000000 LeaveJobInQueue=False
sudo condor_rm -con qdate\<1671000000
```
where 1671000000 means `Wed Dec 14 07:40:00 CET 2022`,  I just picked some round number.

The question is why we leack jobs in hold status that way. Our cleanup procedure was supposed to take care.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T14:37:56Z)

I have cleaned all production schedulers except `vocms0106/107` so they can be used to investigate and fix the current cleanup procedure

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T17:48:19Z)

The problem is not urgent, but it is more efficient to look now that I have things in mind.
IIUC (IIRC etc.) cleanup happens via [JobCleanup.py](https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/blob/master/JobCleanup.py) which by the way has a very nice documentation piece at the beginning, which is [run as a crontab](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/crabschedd.pp#L228-233)

/data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts come from [vocmshtcondor module](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-module-vocmshtcondor/-/blob/a6bc3819803eb1d6ecbf0dba73da8a62087786b0/code/manifests/structure.pp#L142-156) (thanks to @novicecpp for this hard-to-find tip)

And of course we should move that `JobCleanup.py` to our repository, it is  completely CRAB specific !

I guess the problem is then in [clearDagFromQueue](https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/blob/master/JobCleanup.py#L91-99) function
```python
def clearDagFromQueue(dagList, scheddObject):
    logging.info("List of ClusterIds to be cleared from the queue: %s" % dagList)
    #pprint.pprint(dagList)
    if DRYRUN:
	pass
	# scheddObject.edit(dagList, "LeaveJobInQueue_dryrun", 'False')
    else:
	scheddObject.edit(dagList, "LeaveJobInQueue", 'False')
        scheddObject.act(htcondor.JobAction.Remove, dagList)

```

comparing with my by-hand procedure above it misses the part about removing the periodicHold which may cause the job to go into Hold before it is removed from the queue.

Maybe in earlier versions of condor removal from queue was faster, maybe it all depends on the mood of the day of the schedd (the schedd daemong give priorities to things which have to do with running jobs and does thing like Periodic* when load is low without any particular period). Maybe we added the periodicHold after we wrote JobCleanup. Maybe we simply made a mistake and did not test well enough.

I will look into changing the code in vocms0106 and see what happens after crontab has run again.

And ..yeah.. another thing to move to python3 before the `#!/usr/bin/python` at the top gives us problems

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T18:04:32Z)

I was wrong :smile:
the [clearDagFromQueue](https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/blob/master/JobCleanup.py#L91-99) may actually be working. The problem [this line](https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/blob/master/JobCleanup.py#L106)
```python
        constraint = '( (JobUniverse =?= 7) && (TaskType=="ROOT") )'
```
which selects (w/o good reason) "primary dagmans" . While since automatic splitting came in we also have PROCESSING and TAIL dagmans.
Indeed, looking at old held jobs
```
belforte@vocms0106/crab> condor_q -con 'jobstatus==5&&qdate<1671000000' -af tasktype |sort|uniq -c
   3365 PROCESSING
   3582 TAIL
belforte@vocms0106/crab>
```
held dagmans of type `ROOT` are from last month
```
belforte@vocms0106/crab> condor_q -con 'jobstatus==5&&tasktype=="ROOT"' -af qdate|head -4
1673716498
1673716535
1673716809
1673717108
belforte@vocms0106/crab> date -d @1673716498
Sat Jan 14 18:14:58 CET 2023
belforte@vocms0106/crab>
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T18:11:37Z)

indeed we are leaking a fraction of dagmans we run, not all of them . Given that each scheduler has only O(8k) held jobs.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T20:51:46Z)

all of this was known as of 5 years ago https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5691 sigh
:sob:

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-21T21:13:06Z)

fix tested on vocms0106, all good. Making a PR on SI gitlab:
https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/merge_requests/61 for master branch
https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/-/merge_requests/62 for qa branch

will close once those are merged

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7548: Parse cmsRun stdout/err to detect corrupted root files
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7548: Parse cmsRun stdout/err to detect corrupted root files

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-22T13:19:34Z
Closed: 2023-09-18T13:34:23Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7548

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-02-22T13:19:34Z)

There are cases where cmsRun fails w/o creating a FJR with details, e.g. segmentation faults or corrupted input files. In the latter case the details are in the xroot exception which is printed to stdout/err but CMSSW framework only sees a generic failure.
It is also possible for CMSSW to exit with an alas generic 8021 whiel stderr has things like
```
Fatal Exception (Exit code: 8021)
An exception of category 'FileReadError' occurred while
[0] Rethrowing an exception that happened on a different thread.
[1] Reading branch patJets_slimmedJetsPuppi__RECO.
Additional Info:
[a] Fatal Root Error: @SUB=TBasket::ReadBasketBuffers
fNbytes = 2154, fKeylen = 121, fObjlen = 20636, noutot = 0, nout=0, nin=2033, nbuf=20636
```
or
```
Fatal Exception (Exit code: 8021)
An exception of category 'FileReadError' occurred while
[0] Calling InputSource::readFile_
[1] Reading branch EventAuxiliary
Additional Info:
[a] Fatal Root Error: @SUB=TStorageFactoryFile::ReadBuffersSync
Storage::readv returned different size result=263352 expected=323232
```
The telling string is `Fatal Root Error` which makes this different from "object such and such is not present in this data file".

We should add a step in the wrapper where cmsRun stdout/err is parsed whenever the application fails w/o a FJR and set a proper exit code ourselves. This part could be common with WMA (e.g. part of existing FJR parsing).

May need to define a new exit code for corrupted files.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-17T10:41:28Z)

another example (this job exited with 8021 btw) Not clear to me if msg is from xroot or cmssw and if we manage `no such device` as a possible file corruption. Given also that this error appears  transient https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/corrupted-files-mit-please-help/2690

```

== CMSSW: ----- Begin Fatal Exception 17-Jul-2023 06:15:16 EDT-----------------------
== CMSSW: An exception of category 'FileReadError' occurred while
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7552: Question: how should we handle missing keys in tm_user_config?
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7552: Question: how should we handle missing keys in tm_user_config?

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-24T17:02:45Z
Closed: 2024-08-23T15:28:07Z
Labels: Type: Question, Priority: Medium
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7552

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-02-24T17:02:45Z)

Moved from discussion in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7547.

The current code (which I wrote myself) handles the keys as we do to column from db, meaning keys are always available for the client (TW/PUB) to use.
We define all possible keys in [RESTUserWorkflow](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/27fe22629968c70171c1a44976a6538cf702f823/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py#L564) when we receive user input.
The problem appears when we deploy both REST and TW. While we stop the old TW before deploying the new REST, some tasks are not processed. When we start a new TW, those tasks will get the error because the new key does not exist.
To prevent this, we patch the unavailable keys in [RESTWorkerWorkflow](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/27fe22629968c70171c1a44976a6538cf702f823/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTWorkerWorkflow.py#L157).

The pain point is that I need to add new keys in 2 files. I add it into `RESTUserWorkflow` but usually forget to add it in `RESTWorkerWorkflow`.
From the latest production deployment, we failed 9 tasks because of this.

Main question here is: how can we improve this?

Is it possible to define new keys only in `RESTUserWorkflow` and let `RESTWorkerWorkflow` reuse it?
Should we treat the keys as optional and handle the key missing in TW, as Stefano commented in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7547#issuecomment-1441398505 ?
Or adjust how we deploy? let the old TW run and wait until all old tasks get processed, then deploy the new one.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-24T17:34:08Z)

I suspect that there are 2 different issues here.

1) there are two places: where we write (RESTUserWorkflow) and where we read (RESTWorkerWorkflow) [1]. So it make sense that if we ensure that we set a default for all things when we write, it is enough. And indeed your original code works well !
2) whenever we change REST or TW or both we have to worry about backward compatibility with the services data stored by previous versions in the DB and with clients of old service which may need updating. I am not sure that we can find a general solution here. Of course we always struggle to make backward-compatible development, but at times that's not enough. I am open to ideas of course. "Be careful" is easy to say, but it is not a guarantee.

[1] let's not go into naming nor why both do some read and write, but the flow for config. params is that one.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-24T23:03:34Z)

put a comment in RESTUserWorkfow to remind us to change RESTWorkerWorkflow as well ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-23T15:28:07Z)

something one can discuss for years. Better address case by case

config

```
| =inputBlocks= | list of string | (Analysis) Specify blocks to process in the form of DBS block name or block UUID string. CRAB will only discover (do tape recall if necessary) and process these blocks. See [[this FAQ,https://linktofaq]] about tape recall. Require =Data.inputDataset= to be set.|
```

faq
```
---+++ How can I request tape recall for RAW data tier in CRAB?

%TWISTY{mode="div" showlink="Show" hidelink="Hide"}%
Now you can request tape recall for *any data tier*, but CRAB only allows recall on blocks via =Data.inputBlocks= configuration parameter with the sum of block size must not exceed 5 TB.

In example, we want to recall =/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153= and =/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5= from [[https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?instance=prod/global&input=block+dataset%3D%2FZeroBias%2FCommissioning2021-v1%2FRAW,/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW]] dataset.

CRAB config will be:

<verbatim class='config'>
config.JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'
config.Data.inputDataset = '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW'
config.Data.inputBlocks = [
    '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153',
    '/ZeroBias/Commissioning2021-v1/RAW#8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5',
]
# or provide only block UUID
#config.Data.inputBlocks = [
#    '214fbb11-2d5c-4b8c-8ee5-b68de1d89153',
#    '8760f6e6-6c5e-4c65-854d-02d4bc3312c5',
#]
</verbatim>

Note that you still can request tape recall for whole dataset from =*AOD*= tier.

%ENDTWISTY%
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7558: Error when running GPU custom plugin with crab (libcrypt.so.2: cannot open shared object file)
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7558: Error when running GPU custom plugin with crab (libcrypt.so.2: cannot open shared object file)

State: closed
Opened: 2023-03-02T16:23:17Z
Closed: 2023-03-08T16:31:29Z
Labels: Type: Question
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7558

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-03-02T16:23:17Z)

I got this error when I tried to run custom gpu plugin task from @AdrianoDee
https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230302_132243:tseethon_crab_adriano_gpu_customplugin_prod_20230302_142207/job_out.4.0.txt
```
== CMSSW: unable to load /srv/CMSSW_13_1_0_pre1/lib/el8_amd64_gcc11/pluginMyGPUAnalyzerPluginsPortableCudaAsync.so because libcrypt.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
It also happen when run in `crab preparelocal` in lxplus8-gpu. But, run directly via `cmsRun runAnalyzer.py` is works fine.

**Step to reproduce**

Custom plugin code: https://github.com/AdrianoDee/DiMuonSoAAnalyzer
cmsenv: `CMSSW_13_1_0_pre1`
SCRAM\_ARCH: `el8_amd64_gcc11`
Client: crab-dev `v3.230227`
OS: `lxplus8-gpu`

- Run this command to prepare environment
    ```
    cmsrel CMSSW_13_1_0_pre1
    cd CMSSW_13_1_0_pre1/src/
    cmsenv
    git clone https://github.com/AdrianoDee/DiMuonSoAAnalyzer
    scram b -j 8
    ```
- To submit to crab, use crabConfig and customized pset from https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230302_132243:tseethon_crab_adriano_gpu_customplugin_prod_20230302_142207/debug/
- To run directly with original pset
    ```
    cd DiMuonSoAAnalyzer/DiMuonSoAAnalyzer/python/
    cmsRun runAnalyzer.py
    ```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-02T17:03:36Z)

Is this "as simple as" crab job wrapper does not set el8 arch? sent from Stefano's mobile

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-03-02T17:26:23Z)

I am not familiar with jobwrapper but CMSSW logs said that it ran with `Architecture: el8_amd64_gcc11`.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-03T09:18:58Z)

OK, I tried. Nothing trivial then. I will have to reproduce this myself then may be able to dig for clues.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-03-06T15:54:10Z)

After private chat with Stefano, we discovered that `scram b` was run in my local machine without setup properly build environment. Thus, `scram b` link the custom plugins to latest libcrypt `libcrypt.so.2` which only have in my local machine.

To solve this, setup build environment by execute `cmssw-el8`. It will start el8 singularity container and attach shell to it. Then, run usual `scram b`.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-03-08T16:31:29Z)

After `scram b` error is solved, [my job](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230306_151832:tseethon_crab_adriano_gpu_customplugin_prod_20230306_161801/job_out.2.2.txt) got FileReadError but I do not know why. I specify runRange from Adriano config as workaround and finally jobs are finished without error.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7560: Migrate CRAB to PYPI ecosystem
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7560: Migrate CRAB to PYPI ecosystem

State: closed
Opened: 2023-03-02T17:17:55Z
Closed: 2024-10-31T16:17:46Z
Labels: Priority: High, PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7560

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-03-02T17:17:55Z)

In short, WMCore already moved to PYPI on production, and we are happy to move too.
But we need to discuss with WMCore developer on how much effort is needed and whether they can give documentation and some support.

-------------

Below are info moved from meeting minutes:
- Wa: Quick update about migrate to PYPI in WMCore (source: Aroosha) It's a good idea to move but we need to figure out how much effort is needed. We need to do it at some point when wmcore does not support building with rpm anymore.
- They already deployed on production.
- https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/pypi
- It is so simple that I can reuse the base image from [docker/pypi/dmwm-base](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/pypi/dmwm-base) to run [notebooks/DatasetsOnDisk.ipynb](https://github.com/belforte/utils/blob/master/notebooks/DatasetsOnDisk.ipynb).
  - Notebook requires dbs and rucio python client which I never manage to install in my own machine.
  - Install jupyterlab in single command! See example [Dockerfile](https://gitlab.cern.ch/tseethon/crab_docker/-/blob/master/crabutils/Dockerfile)
  - I did not try WMCore though
- How do I search for other dependencies we need besides WMCore?
  - CRAB rpm’s spec files
  - Do we need myproxy/gfal2/voms-proxy-* inside the container?
- Well, there is still a lot of work to convert the CRABServer package from RPM to PYPI.
- How to steal from WMCore:
  - look at this github project https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/projects/8
  - and this label: https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/labels/containerization
- We are happy to move from rpm to PYPI. We must ask WMCore developers whether they can give documentation and some support. For sure we do not want to be the only CMSWEB app. which needs rpm’s . None of us has time to dig into details now, we open a GH issue and come back to this in one month or more. Need to appoint one of the group

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-12-04T23:41:22Z)

I am ready to open POC PR.

Design choice of the POC in summary:
- Directory
    - crabrest: cicd/crabserver_pypi/
    - taskworker: cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/
- Each image has it own `requierments.txt`,
    - wmcore deps [requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/1459b0fa6d78aec48693cff736c746a658321e7d/requirements.txt#L23C1-L23C58)
    - For crabrest, it is slim down version of WMCore
- Install WMCore with `pip install --no-deps WMCore` and install dependencies manually.
    - Official is including `gfal2-python` but they actually install it separately when [build docker image](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/bff12695b0eadf10177a917af1ed1b46172131cb/docker/pypi/reqmgr2ms-unmerged/Dockerfile#L14-L16).
    - Also, to slim down crab rest image.
- User inside container is crab3 (id 1000)
    - I do not like the way WMCore get services name from user name in the wrapper script [(manage)](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/bff12695b0eadf10177a917af1ed1b46172131cb/docker/pypi/dmwm-base/manage#L19C23-L19C23).
- WMCore version's source of truth is in [cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ed0faed5534536c68430a16d1db8a73ec88255b8/cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt) where I use the same format as pip.
    - `requirementsParse.py` helper script to print git repo and version separate by space for load as array in bash
- Start the container (make it run forever) with `/data/run.sh`.
    - Start services with `/data/manage` for crabrest and `/data/start.sh` for taskworker.
    - In crabrest, move all cert/secret/config setup to [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e1694450edb901b18e97259aa7f4087233bcfca4/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh) and set CMD (args of ENTRYPOINT)  to `/data/run.sh`.
- Need custom script for deploy services
    - crabrest: [custom helm chart](https://github.com/novicecpp/CMSKubernetes/commit/4c21b69287456d0be29e61b8d5bf6a644fe6bcd0)
    - taskworker: [runContainer.py](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/4004c186a2f9561e8403b36126715507b76a43df/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/runContainer.sh.patch)
- `python-ldap` is broken with new wmagent pypi image. See comment in [CMSGroupMapper.py](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/4004c186a2f9561e8403b36126715507b76a43df/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py#L27-L29).
- Use [tini](https://github.com/krallin/tini) wrapper as PID 1 mainly to make container stop faster.
    -  https://github.com/krallin/tini/blob/master/README.md#why-tini
- Rebuild should idempotent, you can build as much as you want, but still
    - OS package will update to latest version of packages maintained by OS distribution.
    - Pip dependencies only pin to minor version of requirements.txt, not pin to the hash like Pipfile.lock/Poetry.lock (yet).
- Still lack ability to run from GH.
- Never test Publisher.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-12-18T04:27:09Z)

Lets me explain the poc of PyPI https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8088 here.
First of all, forget the design choice https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7560#issue-1607196899 for now. I will come back to it later.

The goal is **"Remove RPM build"**.

Because we remove the RPM "building system", we need to come up with our own replacement. What I actually do is convert [crabtaskworker.spec](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/blob/comp_gcc630/crabtaskworker.spec) to our own building system, which is based on [the PyPI containers from WMCore](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/pypi).
Note that I did not touch the Python packaging, which is worth tracking in a separate issue, but the image building will involve the CI to some extent.

Things I keep in mind while developing this:

1. The less code change in `src/python`, the better.
1. No clone CRABServer, use local file.
    This will simplify how we run on local machine and also in CI.
     If there is a change, the builder will always pick from local files. No need to commit and push.
And for the CI, in the gitlab-ci model, CI jobs always run on the commit. No need to pass repo/branch/commit to the CI. Just push, and then CI will run.
1. If we want some files on the internet, commit the endpoint in this repo.
     For example, the WMCore version I want to install is in [cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8088/files#diff-5f6c3363105e2c25d0bf95fa7becf90b238f1197ce5e5e823d56e8c5c617a893). Any format is fine as long as you commit it and CI can pick it up.
1. It should be able to run in your local machine.

So here is what I came up with:

1. **Building**
    Simply run single `docker build` command from repo's root directory:
    ```bash
    # go to git root directory
    cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
    # build crabserver
    docker build -t registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabserver:manual . -f cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile
    # build taskworker
    docker build -t registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:manual . -f cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile
    ```

2. **Running**
    Because of Dockerfile in both image are a bit long, I will show how I run the container first, hope it will help you understand Dockerfile better.

    - **TaskWorker:** `ENTRYPOINT` is `tini` wrapper (please see explanation in the design choice), and `CMD` is executing [crabtaskworker_pypi/run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f66997e6f40cc702b4c1bf05980a9ae62249ea17/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/run.sh). `run.sh` call [crabtaskworker_pypi/start.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f66997e6f40cc702b4c1bf05980a9ae62249ea17/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/start.sh) which spawn TaskWorker process in background, then run sleep forever.
    - **CRABServer:** CRABServer is a bit complicated because it needs to be integrated with the K8S manifest. There is a setup step created by CMSWEB operators. I adapt it and put it together in [crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f66997e6f40cc702b4c1bf05980a9ae62249ea17/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh) and make this script as `ENTRYPOINT`. Basically, container start to run `entrypoint.sh` script until [line 53,](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f66997e6f40cc702b4c1bf05980a9ae62249ea17/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh#L53) then exec the [crabserver_pypi/run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f66997e6f40cc702b4c1bf05980a9ae62249ea17/cicd/crabserver_pypi/run.sh) which will spawn the crabserver process and run cat on the fifo log forever.

3. **Dockerfile**
    Dockerfile should be a self-explanatory step, a.k.a., how do I build the container. Please see ["Design Choice"](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7560#issuecomment-1839733761) for the sort of question "Why is it doing this and that?". And please let me know if I did not make it clear enough for you to understand.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-01-30T13:43:27Z)

Here is the guide on how do I build and run CRAB REST image.
(Bear with me, it is a bit long. CRAB TaskWorker images will be in another reply).

To build it, simply run:

```
docker build -t registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabserver:manual . -f cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile
```

Where working directory is `path/to/crabserver/repository`.

The [Dockerfile](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile) is straightforward:
- [Line 16](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L16): Install `tini` from `apt`. `tini` will send SIGTERM to all children processes and make container stop faster.
- [Line 19](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L19): Copy `tnsnames.ora` from CMSWEB image.
- [Line 28-30](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L28): install service dependencies and wmcore via pip.
- [Line 32-35](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L32-L35): install CRAB code by copy file from local to `/data/srv/current/lib/python3.8/site-packages` and install html/css/js to `/data/srv/current/data`.
- [Line 42-46](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L42-L46): install mandatory directory that need.
- [Line 49](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L49) copy service starting scripts to `/data/`

Then we execute `wmc-httpd` to start REST service.
Note that I simply copy code from source to `/data/srv/current/lib/python3.8/site-packages` and export `PYTHONPATH` to this directory in [manage](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/5dd0a31c9545e5e16a395aba0b1b955f1bf37b23/cicd/crabserver_pypi/manage#L41). This will change to PyPI packaging and install via `pip` in the future.

-----------

There is a "deployment convention" for WMCore/REST services that specifies how services read/write files (logs/credential/state/config/etc.).
This will explains why we need this [Dockerfile lines 42-46](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L43-47) and also has an effect on how we deploy in the Kubernetes environment, which I will explain in a later section.

There are 4 directories where the service read or write files.

1. `LOGDIR=/data/srv/logs/crabserver`
This is where services write log to. In version 2022 and earlier, this directory is [mount to CephFS](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/5446006c73d5dfb7123fbee318264134cb611b1c/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml#L195-L196).
But after we switch to writing log to stdout we did not use it anymore.

2. `AUTHDIR=/data/srv/current/auth/crabserver`
This is where we store `CRABServerAuth.py`, robotcert/hmac/proxy(?) that setup by CMSWEB.
Services read this file via [exporting PYTHONPATH](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/blob/94cdfb184264bf11139f417f30565a1881a8e209/crabserver/manage#L37) and [run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/crabserver/run.sh#L60) script preventing copy `config.py` to this directory.

3. `STATEDIR=/data/srv/state/crabserver`
This is where services write temporary file into (`-d` arg of `wmc-httpd` in [manage#L51](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/blob/94cdfb184264bf11139f417f30565a1881a8e209/crabserver/manage#L54))
We also store fifo file `crabserver-fifo` to let service write logs to.

4. `CFGDIR=/data/srv/current/config/crabserver`
This is where `config.py` is stored. Service only `config.py` via positional argument of `wmc-httpd`.

**In the new PyPI image, the convention and path are still the same.**
But, replace the old [manage](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/blob/94cdfb184264bf11139f417f30565a1881a8e209/crabserver/manage) script to new [manage](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/manage) where the new one is based on the new [manage in dmwm-base image](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/pypi/dmwm-base/manage).

------------

The next part is how we deploy this CRAB REST on CMSWEB Kuberenetes cluster.

Currently:
- We store all config/creds/secrets as Kubernetes Secrets and mount it as volumes, see [crabserver.yaml#L262-L283](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/5446006c73d5dfb7123fbee318264134cb611b1c/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml#L262-L283).
- We [inject](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/3019f11449c31d7092a4b1351db23bbc3d808a6b/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml#L99-L101) the [setup-certs-and-run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/3019f11449c31d7092a4b1351db23bbc3d808a6b/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml#L23C3-L30) then execute [run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/crabserver/run.sh).
- The upper part of [run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/crabserver/run.sh#L1-L65) copy files from secrets's mounting path to the "WMCore/REST deployment convention" I explained above.
- Then execute [manage](https://github.com/dmwm/deployment/blob/94cdfb184264bf11139f417f30565a1881a8e209/crabserver/manage#L37) to start service.
- Finally, loop over `cat crabserver-fifo` to read log to container stdout.

**The new PyPI still use same way but replace upper part of old [run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/crabserver/run.sh#L1-L65) with new [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh)**.
Then setup Kubernetes manifest file in container specs section will look like this:
```yaml
containers:
  - image: registry.cern.ch/crab/crabserver:pypi-2ea9d1429ebe56c527b53f17b4adb4503a4f095f
    name: crabserver
    command:
      - /data/entrypoint.sh
    args:
      - /data/run.sh
    ...
```

New process execution flow will be:
- Execute [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh) to copy the files from secret mounts.
- Then run the new [run.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/run.sh) (with `tini` wrapper)
    - [run.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/run.sh) start service process by execute new [manage](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/manage).
        - [manage](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/manage) setup necessary environment variables for service process and then execute `wmc-httpd` and exit.
    - Then, run infinit loop `cat crabserver-fifo`, as main process to make container run forever.

--------------

Finally, the dependencies.

I use [wmagent-base](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/pypi/wmagent-base/Dockerfile), which based on [dmwm-base](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2b0454f9205cb8f97fecb91bf6661b59e4b31424/docker/pypi/dmwm-base/Dockerfile), as baseimage of CRAB REST. This image provides:
- Oracle library.
- libcurl
- cmsweb binary (cmsweb-ping/cpy_exporter)

For python dependencies install via pip in [requirements.txt](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/requirements.txt), I strip it from [WMCore requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/requirements.txt), by do trial-and-error adding package to our `requirements.txt` until no more dependency error.

WMCore version is specified in [wmcore_requirements.txt](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt). It will read by [requirementsParse.py](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/requirementsParse.py) which print space-separate repository and version (tag). The current POC only [get version number and pass it to pip](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L28-L29), cannot replace with src in custom repository yet.

--------------

I explicitly not pass any argument to `docker build` but commit it as files (e.g. [wmcore\_requiements.txt](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/79a8ab854b221926b3f32bf2e8058fd5f0d1efd7/cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt)). This way CI can notify changes and build the new image automatically.
And `./start.sh -g` or equivalent feature is not available at the moment.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-13T14:56:39Z)

One things I forgot to mention in CRAB REST image is, where WMCore/REST get those data files of CRAB UI?

The answer is this file, [FrontPage.py](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/46ff962b1d6de17db7cca8cc08425ad602e26cf5/src/python/CRABInterface/Pages/FrontPage.py), the **absolute path of `./data/{html,script,css}`** is defined in this file.
The magic is come from [line 13](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/46ff962b1d6de17db7cca8cc08425ad602e26cf5/src/python/CRABInterface/Pages/FrontPage.py#L13). For example,
- The path of this file: `/data/srv/HG2401b-5ac8fb32fb299de758852f123c281791/sw.crab_master/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabserver/v3.240201-7d39eda58270523b4acf410cd7bca48b/lib/python3.8/site-packages/CRABInterface/Pages/FrontPage.py`
- Output of `rsplit('/',6)[0]` is `/data/srv/HG2401b-5ac8fb32fb299de758852f123c281791/sw.crab_master/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabserver/v3.240201-7d39eda58270523b4acf410cd7bca48b`
- Then use result above as prefix path of `./data/{html,script,css}` and then feed to `WMCore.REST.Server.RESTFrontPage ` class.

So, as long as you deploy `data` directory 2 level upper of PYTHONPATH (in this case same level as `lib` directory of `lib/python3.8/site-packages`), no matter the path of PYTHONPATH it is, it always works.

That is why Stefano added [this hack](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/a6612ad45ea6ca79915e71e343cc29a97418973a/docker/crabserver/addGH.sh#L43-L47) to addGH.sh to make web UI works in GH mode. I think new PYPI image will also use this hack and fix it later when we support install CRAB with `pip`.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-13T17:59:51Z)

abut the previous comment https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7560#issuecomment-1941698865 it goes w/o saying that any idea about how to simplify is welcome. I can sort of understand the original implementor line of thought that there is a generic application in /data/srv/.../myApp and below that there's lib with the code and data with files including html, but we would surely prefer that location in the server and location in the GH tree are more closely related.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-14T08:19:25Z)

I want to move it into [data files](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/datafiles.html#accessing-data-files-at-runtime) and refer the path from PYTHONPATH. Also, pip will handle update for us when we install updated version.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-30T00:30:39Z)

For the last part, the Publisher.

It is simpler than I thought. No extra environment variables is needed. Startup scripts can copy-paste from TaskWorker (`start.sh/stop.sh/manage.sh` in [crabtaskworker_pypi](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi)) then tailored to suit the Publisher's needs.

However, there are 2 major changes and 1 discovered bug I want to introduce (compare to the code in the [current master](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/)).

1. Share `run.sh` like RPM image.

I am reinvent the wheel here :sadge:
New `run.sh` is placed in `/data/run.sh` and the decision to execute which `start.sh` is depended on `$SERVICE` (e.g., `/data/srv/${SERVICE}/start.sh`, just like [RPM run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/Docker/run.sh)).
I tried to separate it once, but the similarity of the code is 80%.

2. Symlink is done in the `run.sh` step. Not building a container step.

In current master, I have done this in the build step ([Dockerfile#L104-107](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L104-L107)), but then realized that there is an extra directory that needs to be symlinked for Publisher ([PublisherFiles](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/Docker/run.sh#L49)).

3. Bug(?) in the original `Publisher/stop.sh`: cannot start service if the time of the next cycle has passed.

This is what I discovered when I tried to run Publisher PyPI for the first time. The problem is the result of 2 combinations:

- For REST and TW services, the `./manage.sh start` is actually a restart action, for convenience, and it works very well.
- The [Publisher/stop.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/src/script/Deployment/Publisher/stop.sh) does not support stop if the next cycle run is less than now. The result of [line 22](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c09182159e0397155da20c56e07d7859ce6d7029/src/script/Deployment/Publisher/stop.sh#L22) will be minus and will fail condition `[ $delta -gt 60 ]` next line.

We can fix the condition, and everything will be fine. But I think the function is a bit fragile, and there should be a better way to do this. So, I am not fixing it. I separate `start` and `restart` command so `start` action only runs `start_srv` function instead.

-------------

PR is coming soon.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-30T07:22:56Z)

I guess we never tried until now to stop a Publisher which had never ran !
Fine with the change, but you need to put some protection in the new `start` so that it fails if Publisher is already running or falls back to `restart`

With a bit a of day-after-wisdom, I wander if we have too many symlinks and should rather re-arrange the directory tree. All those directory names are configuration variables, should be easy to rename them.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-30T20:29:52Z)

> With a bit a of day-after-wisdom, I wander if we have too many symlinks and should rather re-arrange the directory tree. All those directory names are configuration variables, should be easy to rename them.

IMO, the symlink that we still need is the config file, where we can switch to other files on-the-fly without stopping puppet.
Other than that, it can be replaced by configuration+`docker run -v /host:/container` (need to modify `runContainer.sh`).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-30T22:08:47Z)

With https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8368/commits/c547da07104247eda74761db8e1261f285ed7da5, first line of `DOCKER_VOL` will expand to something like this:
```
+ DOCKER_VOL='-v /data/container/:/data/hostdisk/ -v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/cfg:/data/srv/Publisher/cfg -v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/logs:/data/srv/Publisher/logs -v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/PublisherFiles:/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles -v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/'
```

Then, switch the `config.General.taskFilesDir` to `/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles` on [Publisher_scheddConfig.py#L35](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/c7d4596afd3cb9a8c03c2659b47224a3b800e081/code/templates/crabtaskworker/publisher/Publisher_scheddConfig.py.erb#L35).

thanks @novicecpp , given what you wrote in previous comment, which I fully agree with, I think that we do not need all of those mount either.
Shall we open an ad-hoc thread and review this ?

With a bit a of day-after-wisdom, I wander if we have too many symlinks and should rather re-arrange the directory tree. All those directory names are configuration variables, should be easy to rename them.

I encountered this problem today after stop Publisher for too long to make sure TW is up and running.
Let's create the new issue to tackle this.

I think the last part here is documentation.

I remembered it is hard for Vijay to figure it out even we already have a new, simpler Dockerfile.
It is not like we `pip install crabtaskworker` and done. There are specific paths in container that we use and specific way to run containers.

At least give a new guy a map where to look at.

Sorry. I do not have time to do this.

But at least everything is written down in the Dockerfile, [crabserver](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/19b1bf76091ffe6a275683be5adf716310714ff6/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile), [crabtaskworker](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/19b1bf76091ffe6a275683be5adf716310714ff6/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile).

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7569: Take aways from spring O&C week
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7569: Take aways from spring O&C week

State: closed
Opened: 2023-03-17T13:22:52Z
Closed: 2024-08-23T10:34:37Z
Labels: Status: On Hold, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7569

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-03-17T13:22:52Z)

takeaways from  [talk by Dima](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1256427/contributions/5302294/attachments/2613543/4516299/2023-03-17%20Disk%20Space%20Management%20Options.pdf)  (see also [live notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qeo2YZ9zgQFDBpF0cRT8yDXTYURznRdqx5Foq68bBzA/edit#heading=h.nj0gfrlutmaw) page 34) were discussed by us in [googleDoc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Du9VNTlbYZ15WQ2MflY9_l2F4RR3cXiZyi0vyXS4H0w/edit) and distilled into following action items for us
 - [x] crab tape recall should not recall across atlantic #7589
 - [x] help users deal with tails #7595
 - [x] allow processing of blocks which miss some files #7573
 - [x] Lock data on disk when submitting a task #7592
 - [x] report progress of tape recall (and expiration) in crab status #7593
 - [x] setup monitoring of tape recalls #7517
 - [x] implement `crab recall --dataset=.... --sites=... --days=...` #7594
 - [x] help users find whether a dataset is fully on disk
   - [x] improve reporting from TW #7596
   - [x] implement  `crab checkdataset ....` https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5191

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-13T22:28:32Z)

I set as TOP priority because we need to make plans for this. As soon as every thing has an ad hoc issue assigned, set on HOLD. Then close when all actions are done

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-04-14T12:14:13Z)

From live note:
> Consider efficiency of recalling from tape, easier to recall large blocks of files than lots of little groups. There need to be operational procedures in place to minimize the pain

Do we need to take any action about this?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-14T12:23:43Z)

No, this is for Rucio to worry about. And IMHO not even Rucio should care. There are other SW layers between Rucio and the tape drives : FTS and the local site storage managers, usually sites run tape management software which builds a queue of requests and reorders them to minimize tape mount/dismount/seek (i.e. tape wear).

We could worry about "if user asked for one block today, maybe they will ask for next block next week, so it would be better to recall two or more blocks now" or "if this is a small dataset, even if they asked for a block, recall it all".
But it is difficult to say how much it would help.

There is one action that we should do anyhow, to make our side cleaner, and that will also help here:
* if user asks for a non-AOD (i.e. no autorecall) tier, but overall size is <10TB, recall it anyhow w/o bothering to ask for a list of blocks.
I was about to open an issue for this !
