That is clear. Thanks Stefano.

> if user asked for one block today, maybe they will ask for next block next week, so it would be better to recall two or more blocks now

Hmm, interesting. I will try to look at monitoring later if it can detect this behavior.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-14T16:14:36Z)

I doubt you will find anything in monitoring. It just sending thoughts to explore small corners of phase-space.
The more "realistic" scenario I can imagine is:
I somehow decided a need to process dataset  /A/B/RERECO which is 1 PB.
I find that CRAB only let me get 10TB at a time.
So I submit 10 tasks to get 100TB.
As soon as they complete, I submit more.

This did not happen yet, and it may never, but once we tall people "only 10TB at a time" sooner or later someone will do.

From site POV, better recall 1 PB "now" and get done with it. From our POV, maybe this will only happen  rarely, maybe user will get tired after 200TB, maybe we will be able to detetc and stop, maybe we will discover that we can safely allow 100TB instead of 10TB so that "a piece a day for 100 days" will not happen.

Maybe time to worry about what information to send to ES in order to monitor things. Parsing a free format comment field in the rule (the only way we have now) is not good.

State: closed

Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7573

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-03-27T15:28:08Z)

when user specifies `partialDataset=True` in task submission configuration:

 * current behavior is to process whatever blocks are on disk w/o triggering a tape recalls
 * we should extend to process whatever files are on disk, including inomplete block replicas.

See some discussion e.g. in [CMS-talk](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/cannot-find-any-valid-file-inside-the-dataset/20761/27)

Note that [our documentation](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile) already says:
```
Allow to process input dataset that is only partially on disk.
Normally, when CRAB finds out that some files of the input dataset are not fully replicated on disk,
CRAB will issue tape recall to Rucio and wait for all files to be on disk before running the task.
If partialdataset is True, CRAB will submit task to condor immediately without request tape recall
and process the files currently on disk
```

 - [x] change code
 - [x] update documentation

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-28T14:49:17Z)

An initial quick implementation would be to change this
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e2e09dde7ebedf1450df67450e3c77bda03c113f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L356
to be
```python
    if item['state'].upper() == 'AVAILABLE' or usePartialDataset:
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-28T14:51:44Z)

the only shortcoming that we see is in the case that the parially available blocks are at multiple sites, that will cause jobs to run at ANY of those sites, regardless if they host full replica or only one file. Those use cases are hopefully rare and we rely on:
* if users said: `usePartialDataset` . They must be happy with whatever they get and ignore file read errors (8028)

## Comment (belforte, 2023-03-29T23:18:29Z)

I have coded so that:
- if a block has full replicas, use those RSE's
- otherwise use all RSE's which have (part of) the block
and of course keep skipping blocks which are only on tape

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7594: implement `crab recall`
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7594: implement `crab recall`

State: open
Opened: 2023-04-14T07:48:12Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Question, Priority: Medium, Status: On Hold
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7594

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-04-14T07:48:12Z)

develop a way for users to request recalls w/o submitting a task, also includes the possibility to simply request a replica (maybe not `crab recall`, but `crab getdata` ?
```
crab recall --dataset=.... --sites=... --days=...
```
Requires change also in CRABClient

Should use different Rucio account than for automatic tape recalls (`crab_tape_recall`) so that we can set different global/local quotas.
Will also need a different set of policies.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-14T15:54:35Z)

we have been discussing this for months now. It is technically straightforward especially after last refactoring of tape recall code in TaskWorker/RucioActions .
But  still not clear what exactly the need is.
 * We can surely provide a “crab recall” by which does the same as automatic recall but w/o submitting a task.
 * Is it worth ? useful ?
 * Doing more is easy technically, problem is which policies to enforce.
 * We nee DM Ops buying in and setting of proper policies.
 * Once we give such a tool to every user, the problem is when to say no.

There's also an evolution of DM policies about what to keep on disk anyhow, geared for Run3 in https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSTRANSF-687
Maybe we can simply wait for that to be finalized and listen to users.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-14T15:57:02Z)

technical detail: my current idea is to create an entry in CRAB's TaskDB like submit does, but with a different command (RECALL), when TW Handler finds, it will call a new "recall" action. I think about a solid week of work.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7598: Refactoring RUCIO_Transfers.py

State: closed
Opened: 2023-04-14T17:53:41Z
Closed: 2023-07-19T08:56:39Z
Labels: Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7598

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-04-14T17:53:41Z)

Open this issue for discuss design and ask some questions.
The current goal is https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7524 .

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-04-14T17:55:53Z)

**This proposal is now obsolete.**

--------------------

I am propose change on [monitor\_locks\_status()](https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/blob/0f37bb5ef61acb2127fdb97b97e77cbd33d96b85/scripts/task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py#L591-L688).

This function get replicas info by drill down from container name to get replicas info (list dataset -> list rules -> list replicas).

I propose change it to:
- Add first bookkeeping of rule ID when the rule is created (For a new code, it is at [BuildTaskDataset.createDataset()](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/0082a15ef8e8fedfe844ac8344697506350daf85/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/BuildTaskDataset.py#L108))
  - In the map of `{ruleID: datasetName}`
  - If duplicaterule is raised, better to get ruleid and ensure it already in bookkeeping
- Then in new `monitor_locks_status`, loop over above list, and do usual stuff.
  - I want to ensure that replicas we track is only from the rules we created.
- Also, remove [id2lfn\_map](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1f17608a8baa29ad042e229035794def865c23b3/scripts/task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py#L634-L640) checking from this function because we agree to seperate container for track status and publish container.
- Second bookkeeping for "OK" replicas is done per dataset.
  - In format of `datasetName` per line.
  - skip the rule where dataset name match with this bookkeeping.
  - I don't want to write full replicas name to the file because we use too much IO in schedd machine.

@belforte what do you think?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-19T08:56:39Z)

Refactoring is done via  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7587 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7675 and https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7649.  The design has quite changes compare to original RUCIO_Transfers.py scripts.

Closing this issue and move to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7632.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7603: improve TapeRecall Rucio rule handling
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7603: improve TapeRecall Rucio rule handling

State: closed
Opened: 2023-04-17T20:27:05Z
Closed: 2023-05-25T08:38:24Z
Labels: Type: Question, Status: On Hold, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7603

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-04-17T20:27:05Z)

as noted in #7530 , must improve the handling of Rucio rule for tape recall

- [x] whenever possible use the DBS dataset name and scope for the container #7641
- [x] try to avoid rule duplication (requires the above) #7641
- [x] make rule expire 30 days after data is recalled #7590 and  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/bbd2caba3073c50f7acdb6f6fa0536be547a01bd
- [x] allow 30 days for tape recall (this can be questioned) part of #7590
   * eventually we decided to make it 15 days before task expires and leave rule there 7 more days in case we want to debug somehting

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-20T11:01:49Z)

we reviewed this in todays CRAB meeting. All in all could not find a strong motivation for doing this and changing from current setup has drawbacks too.
 * dataset name is now in the rule comments field
 * since we allow to recall list of blocks, at times we need am ad-hoc container name anyhow
 * it is good to be able to connect rule to task
 * not clear that having multiple rules on same set of files (with different container name) is a problem in/for Rucio, all in all it is working now.
    * But let's make sure that there will not be multiple request to FTS to copy same file to same destination

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-25T09:03:07Z)

thinking more about duplicate rules, even if they do not harm, they annoy at least, by resulting in duplicated lines in the HTML table which lists pending rules from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1837785/234227119-d38be857-d8c9-4b71-8296-92e21e0a0042.png)

finding tasks which waits on a given rule can be done via Task table, since we store rule id in one column. So we only need a new API and then can easily add a column in the HTML table with pointers to task(s)

There is also a clear benefit aside avoiding duplicates :
 * using `cms:/...` container name whenever possible, will make it easy to connect with rules from DM ops

So I am inclided again about doing this change, even if we make the extra effort of adding one new API. @mapellidario @novicecpp I welcome your advice

## Comment (belforte, 2023-05-08T09:58:18Z)

plan (discussed in chat Stefano, Dario, Wa on May 8)
 - [ ] change the tape request to use as container name in the rule `cms:DBSdatasetNameHere'
    - [ ] use `name =DBSDatasetName_partial` and if we detect that this container already exist, simply add the new blocks to it
     - [ ] Extend the rule LIFETIME
     - [ ] Update size info in the comment
 - [ ] Add a new REST API (or a new subresource to Task API) to list all tasks which have a given value of `tm_ddm_reqid`
 - [ ] more ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-05-17T16:46:29Z)

Above plan can not work
1. container name has to end with `/TIER` and `TIER` has to be one of the predefined ones. Can not have `/blah/blahblah/AOD_partial`
2. can't reuse containers which ask for single block recalls, would recall also all blocks asked for years ago... need a unique name every time

## Comment (belforte, 2023-05-18T09:35:35Z)

New plan:
 - [x] modify `requestTapeRecall` to accept either a dataset name or a list of blocks #7641
    * when full dataset recall is sent, use `cms:datasetname` ad DID and if rule already exist, extend lifetime
    * when a list of block is sent do like now and create a DID in our scope using taskname
 - [x] modify `DBSDataDiscovery` to send dataset name when appropriate #7641
 - [x]     Update size info in the comment

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7609: schedd - use a smaller openstack flavor
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7609: schedd - use a smaller openstack flavor

State: closed
Opened: 2023-04-20T11:53:16Z
Closed: 2024-02-07T11:00:59Z
Labels: Priority: High, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7609

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-04-20T11:53:16Z)

#### introduction

CMS O&C have been asked to assess whether the CPU usage in CERN Openstack is reasonable.

Usage in this context means "number of CPUs that are allocated to instantiated physical or virtual machines", there is no distinction between idle or busy CPUs, nor between "normal" and overcommitted VM flavors.

#### details

In CRAB, we use CPUs mainly for our schedd VMs. If we want to reduce the number of CPUs that we allocate, this is where to start having a look at.

We had many ideas on how to achieve this, but the easiest and more promising is to simply switch to a smaller openstack flavor, from `r2.2xlarge ` (16cpu, 60GB) to `r2.xlarge ` (8cpu, 30GB).

According to our grafana dashboard [1], this flavor should suit our needs

#### plan

agreed

- [ ] create a couple of `r2.xlarge` schedd VM
- [ ] add it to the global pool
- [ ] let them run for some months
- [ ] assess theit cpu and memory usage over time

Still open question

- [ ] do we need/want to remove a running schedd? i would say we do not really need to...
- [ ] should we also reduce the size of the itb schedd? or do CMS SI need them to be as big as current production schedds for their scale tests? I will ask Nikos.

---

[1] https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/4kCVgxE4z?orgId=11

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-04-20T15:52:23Z)

> do we need/want to remove a running schedd? i would say we do not really need to...

Point is to make sure new smaller machine have same load as old one. You may drain the old one or adjust weight in https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-shedds-config.json

we are happy as we are

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7610: tune RSE list for large dataset recalls
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7610: tune RSE list for large dataset recalls

State: closed

Labels: Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7610

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-04-20T14:26:23Z)

this is to keep track of discussion which we started today in CRAB Meeting.
current policy:
*  if dataset < 50TB --> use `grouping=ALL` : Rucio places data in a single site
 * otherwise, pick (size/50TB+1) RSE's from the list and hand those to Rucio using `grouping=DATASET`

Questions:
1. keep 50TB as threshold ? move to 100 TB ?
2. there are recall requests for 450TB samples, does it make sense to scatter in 10 sites ? Should we put a cap on the number of sites ?
3. how does `grouping=DATASET` work ? Will Rucio try to spread evenly, or try to put all at a single site if that site has enough quota ? Rucio [documentation](https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/client_api/ruleclient#add_replication_rule) says:
   * ALL -  All files will be replicated to the same RSE.
    * DATASET - All files in the same dataset will be replicated to the same RSE.
    * NONE - Files will be completely spread over all allowed RSEs without any grouping considerations at all.

@KatyEllis volunteered to follow up on 3. with Rucio developers

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-25T21:14:15Z)

thanks to @mrceyhun  I have looked at size distribution for (MINI)AOD(SIM) datasets.
https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/iYTDX6P4z?orgId=11
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1837785/234411663-ed818ffa-24f9-412f-aa00-7e0074626493.png)
(in the plot above I selected >5TB in top menu and added legenda for visibility)

Clearly the recalled datasets at O(450)TB are odd outliers (B-Parking) and moataset we may want to recall are below 100TB and if we wanted to split, I would split sort of 100 TB per site `nsites = int(size/100) + 1`

@KatyEllis do you agree ?
I'd like to push this change in coming release

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-27T13:29:58Z)

in todays CRAB meeting we agreed to simply use `grouping=alll` for all datasets. And monitor how it goes.

As a matter of caution, I will keep current code in place, simply raise the current limit for dataset splitting from 50 to 1000 TB.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f785d252ec2153bd207127b765f8f756ffeea1cc/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L175
We reject anyhow requests above 1PB.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7614: TW containers must take pki bundle from host
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7614: TW containers must take pki bundle from host

State: closed
Opened: 2023-04-24T14:40:10Z
Closed: 2023-04-24T14:46:28Z
Labels: Priority: Critical
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7614

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-04-24T14:40:10Z)

CERN updated their root CA and all things stopped to work.
It came out that we take `/etc/grid-security/certificates` from the host, but that is not relevant, since SSL stuff picks first the content from `/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem`

We managed to updated that bundle on the VM hosts via
```
yum install -y CERN-CA-certs
update-ca-trust
```
(note that in this case `yum update` was not working ! )

But in order to make the containers use the new bundle in place of the one which was current when the base image (`cmsweb`) was created, we need to munt the bundle from the host.

More info in:
https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/gzsneygpu3b4jki1umk9x5aweh

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7632: RUCIO_Transfer.py: Things need to be done before run test in larger scale.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7632: RUCIO_Transfer.py: Things need to be done before run test in larger scale.

State: closed
Opened: 2023-05-12T10:31:22Z
Closed: 2023-11-17T15:28:07Z
Labels: Priority: High, RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7632

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-05-12T10:31:22Z)

The goal of this issue is to track todo lists that need to be done before we can run automated tests at large scale.

Things need to be done are (mostly copy from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7524#issuecomment-1543590542):

- [x] Fix `add_replicas` to try again instead of fail them (It should not failed on this step).
- [x] Update correct status to database when files transfer is completed.
- [x] bookkeeping locks monitoring.
  - Need to review it again because it is affected by separating publish and transfer container.
- [x] 1 container for multiple tasks (separate publish and transfer container)
  - However, there is no guarantee it will survive race condition, especially when close the dataset and open new one.
- [x] Fix rucio config broken on `T2_DE_DESY`, and more. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7740
- [x] Make it run on dev environment.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-05-12T10:56:07Z)

I have not tried to really understand the problem with DESY, but I find it hard to image that a well run site like T2_DE_DESY has a bad configuration, maybe this is us who did not understand how to use the information (so we can fix silently) or, worse, some insufficient specification on how sites should be configured. If the latter it can happen on more sites and we need to get Rucio and SiteFacilities involved.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-05-12T10:59:56Z)

About that the site config is not actual problem but it is CMSRucio itself that have weird configuration with temp area.
I have consulted with Rahul and he suggested to open issue in CMSRucio repo and discuss there.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-05-12T11:04:40Z)

yeah, it is a thin and blurred line how much temp_RSE config is a site responsibility vs. a CMS-Rucio vs. a CMS_SiteFacilities responsibility. DIfferent people likely have different ideas where that line lies and all those things change with time, of course

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-06-21T10:24:12Z)

All list above is now solved (note for broken sites on `T2_DE_DESY` and `T2_UK_SGrid_Bristol` is fixed by hardcode in the scripts.)

3 things that still needs to figure it out before closing this issues.

- [x] Close the dataset when (in OR)
  - It has 100 files
  - 6 hours have passed since last time a block was added to DBS for this task
  - The task has terminated (this was done as a courtesy to user, in case you have a task with 10 jobs, which completed in 1h and do not want to wait 6h to have crab status to say “publication completed”)

If we close it when the above conditions meet, the next iteration will create a new dataset immediately, and it will close in the next 6 hours. So we have many closed datasets without any replicas inside a container. In theory, it may be alright because we use block names in db to publish to DBS, which always has one or more files in it.

- [x] When `crabConfig.Data.publication=False`, `publishname` is always same (`FakeDataset/fakefile-FakePublish-5b6a581e4ddd41b130711a045d5fecb9/USER`).

It need to be unique value for each task. Workaround for this is to disable register replica in publish container, but it will defeat the reason of have files manage in Rucio.

- ~~What should we do if replicas stuck form n hours?~~ no need to do anything. Postjob will mark it as failed when time has passed, and we ignore the transfer container after the tasks is end of life.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-21T10:32:44Z)

>   If we close it when the above conditions meet, the next iteration will create a new dataset immediately, and it will close in the next 6 hours.

why do we create a new dataset if we have no files to put in it ? Seems something easy to avoid.

I am not sure I fully understand 2nd point. Let's talk about it. In case it should not be too difficult to create a FakeDataset which is unique for each task

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-06-21T11:08:09Z)

> why do we create a new dataset if we have no files to put in it ? Seems something easy to avoid.

I agree. It should easy to fix but maybe require a lot of code change, same as fake publication.
I will have a look.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-21T11:16:29Z)

1. look at transfers.txt
2. no new file ? exit (even as simple as count lines and compare with stored last-line value)
3. use current code

fake publication, I do not know off-hand.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-06-29T07:48:58Z)

Closing dataset when time has passed is easier to fix than I though. Now it fixed in my private branch. Closing when the task is completed is another story. There is no easy way to do at the moment.

For FakeDataset I added fix in [PostJob.py#L1627-L1630](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/47e8804964bc23b760cae497e4e33d3cd24a0942/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L1627-L1630) file. I am not sure if this is proper solution or just workaround. Also, I wonder why we update `tasks.tm_output_dataset` in postjob instead of in REST/TW.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-29T12:31:14Z)

> why we update tasks.tm_output_dataset in postjob instead of in REST/TW.

because the PSET hash to put in there needs to be computed by CMSSW using CMSRun output file, which is best (only) done on the WN, and at this point TW is out of the loop and the guy who processes the job output is the PostJob.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-29T12:40:30Z)

> I am not sure if this is proper solution or just workaround.

IIUC we still have a FakeDataset here, simply a different one for each task. Which is what we require in order to have a different container for each task. So I'd call it a fix .

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-20T08:26:26Z)

- [x] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7741

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-11-17T15:28:07Z)

All done.

State: closed

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-05-30T12:19:01Z)

As reported by a user [1], the pset tweaking sometimes breaks [2].

It seems that there is a mismatch between the variable type that we set (int) and the one that david scripts use (uint) [3].

It is not clear to me why this has not been noticed before, unfortunately i do not have time to look at it today, so i will not self-assign this issue to me. I can have a look tomorrow.

I am quite puzzled

I am running the job locally with preparelocal.

Using uint32 and maxEvents=0 at [1] and similar lines makes the PSet tweak be ok, but then the cmsRun execution fails [2].

Since I submitted a very similar task (filebased splitting, same cmssw version, same scram arch) [3] and evth seems ok, I start suspecting that something is wrong or unexpected with the user pset.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7650: PSet tweaking on WN breaks if a MC PSet is used in Analysis task

State: closed
Opened: 2023-06-01T10:04:59Z
Closed: 2023-06-02T14:13:52Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7650

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-06-01T10:04:59Z)

as found after user problem report in #7648

I believe that the problem orginates in running an Analysis task with a PSet which contains modules meant for MC production (GEN step). For analysis we need maxEvents=-1 to "dummyfy" it so to use runs/lumis instead to decide what to process. But for MC we set it to a positive integer to really mean maxEvents so there is no:
```
ValueError: -1 is not a valid <class 'FWCore.ParameterSet.Types.uint32'>
```

I am not sure how best to prevent this. Maybe CRABClient could refuse to submit if `config.JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'` but ther PSet contains `process.source = cms.Source("EmptySource")`.
We could avoid calling `cmssw_handle_nEvents.py` for CRAB tasks which use `Analysis` "plugin" , it looks like it could do [1]
I guess that I am confused because I do not know what a `producer` exactly is in the CMSSW process .

Maybe a quick chat with David Lange will solve all doubs i.e. confirm that we can safely restrict use of  `cmssw_handle_nEvents.py` to MC tasks. @mapellidario you can ask in person which may work better, but if you prefer that I do on MM, let me know

[1]
the PSet after CRAB's tweaking (i.e. before `cmssw_handle_nEvents.py` ) has this interesting piece
```
process.source = cms.Source("EmptySource",
    fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring('/store/group/lpcdisptau/Staus_M_100_100mm_13p6TeV_Run3Winter23/GENSIM/230526_095807/0000/TSG-Run3Winter23GS-LLStau_M100_ctau100mm_1.root'),
    numberEventsInLuminosityBlock = cms.untracked.uint32(100),
    skipEvents = cms.untracked.uint32(0)
)
```
and executing it leads to a reasonably clear error:
```
belforte@lxplus772/Ste> cmsRun tPS.py
----- Begin Fatal Exception 01-Jun-2023 11:55:58 CEST-----------------------
An exception of category 'Configuration' occurred while
   [0] Constructing the EventProcessor
   [1] Validating configuration of input source of type EmptySource
Exception Message:
Illegal parameters found in configuration.  The parameters are named:
 'fileNames'
 'skipEvents'
You could be trying to use parameter names that are not
allowed for this plugin or they could be misspelled.
----- End Fatal Exception -------------------------------------------------
```

## Comment (davidlange6, 2023-06-01T10:33:12Z)

should not maxEvents be int32? does the traceback say more about which module? The "fun" of that specific  tweak is that to support generators forked by cmsrun - the tweak looks for any producer module with parameter maxEvents and changes its value. (but this is there since many years, its not new in the python2-3 changeover) I can see why that might be hard to support in an arbitrary user PSet. I'm also unsure of a robust fix.

As for input sources.. The tweaking could be changed to check that the input source is not emptySource  before adding parameters (again, this is not new code..) - however, what does "analysis" and "emptysource" together mean as a use case? Maybe that is worth understanding first.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-01T10:42:36Z)

@davidlange6 hey ! I did not tag you !! Some AI think notifies you of CRAB issues where your name appears ? I better be careful what I write !

The use case here is "mistake". A bad PSet was fed to a crab task and we got a cryptic (for us) error. The point is how to make it easier for us if it happens again in 1y when we have forgotten everything .

In the end, the problem is that the produces has an `uint32` for `nEvents` while your script tries to insert it a "-1" value from `maxEvents` which is `int32`.

Somehow, both here and in WMAgent, safest thing may be to remove `producer.nEvents`, rather than try to change it, and leave it to CRAB/WMA to set `maxEvents` for the full thing.
(sorry for not using proper terms)

## Comment (davidlange6, 2023-06-01T10:50:28Z)

I got pinged separately:)

definitely defining analysis as having something other than emptySource would make sense to me (how else are mc and analysis differentiated in their set?)

I'm not sure I follow about nEvents? afaik, this tweak was in wma since a long time. The tweak could be adjusted to do the tweak only if the variable type is int32. That would make it more robust for example.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-01T10:50:58Z)

hmm.. I suspect I did not fully appreciate `forked by cmsRun`.
Better solution:
only use  `cmssw_handle_nEvents.py` if `process.maxEvents` is > 0

and leave it to user/developers to deal with improper use of `nEvents` in their producers

## Comment (davidlange6, 2023-06-01T10:52:19Z)

by forked I mean things like to generate events from a grid pack..

## Comment (davidlange6, 2023-06-01T10:52:52Z)

how does one get this pset with nEvents error?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-01T11:07:17Z)

> I'm not sure I follow about nEvents? afaik, this tweak was in wma since a long time. The tweak could be adjusted to do the tweak only if the variable type is int32. That would make it more robust for example.

We can't change the `process.maxEvents` to be `int32`, it needs to support `-1` value.
From CRAB side `process.maxEvents` is set to -1 when user declares to CRAB an "analysis" task which will use split by file/run/lumi vs. a "MC" task (i.e. no input) where split is done by events.

I guess that in the end we do NOT have a way to tell if a given producer is correct or not for this configuration. But EDM config. validation is a better place than CRAB job wrapper to figure out that !

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-01T12:19:16Z)

if one submits an analysis CRAB task using a Pythia PSet, eventually gets the same configuration error as at the bottom of initial comment, so if we go for the simple fix[*], we simply restore that same behavior also in case the PSet contains a forked producer.

[*]
```
only use cmssw_handle_nEvents.py in CRAB MC task.
```

Note that it is for user to specify if a task is MC or Analysis. Let's stick to that and not go into trying to decide in the code if the input PSet is one kind or another. A warning in CRABClient could make sense, but on such topic I'd rather let the user shoot himself in the foot and leave people freedom (e.g. if using a script around/instead of cmsRun)

## Comment (davidlange6, 2023-06-01T13:05:50Z)

```
this is the part which "can't be tweaked"

process.externalLHEProducer = cms.EDProducer("ExternalLHEProducer",
    args = cms.vstring('SMS-TStauStau-MM_mStau-100_slc7_amd64_gcc10_CMSSW_12_4_8_tarball.tar.xz'),
    nEvents = cms.untracked.uint32(100),
    numberOfParameters = cms.uint32(1),
    outputFile = cms.string('cmsgrid_final.lhe'),
    scriptName = cms.FileInPath('GeneratorInterface/LHEInterface/data/run_generic_tarball_cvmfs.sh')

```
Ok, so this is forking some generator process, and is one of the expected use cases of this tweak (as I understand it)

If you set nEvent =-1 here then the module will try to run ~forever. It doesn't make sense for this to be -1. I think the conclusion of set properly analysis vs mc is still valid.

State: closed

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-06-15T19:35:05Z)

the new code which recycle Rucio tape recall rules across multiple tasks
failed to deal with the following scenario:
* task A creates rule R
* later task B comes for same dataset and rule R is reused
* user kills task A - task is put in KILLRECALL
* TapeRecallManager deletes rule R and put task A in killed
* at this point task B points to a rule which does not exist in Rucio and will of course never succeed

<details><summary>Details from today's example</summary>
this resulted in messages like this in TaskRecallManager.log

```
2023-06-15 18:41:48,778:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Working on task 230615_062905:santocch_crab_singlemu-2016b
2023-06-15 18:41:48,778:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Task points to Rucio RuleId:  60350d44cf2a49d29de6e9688993903a
2023-06-15 18:41:48,832:ERROR:TapeRecallManager:Rucio rule id 60350d44cf2a49d29de6e9688993903a not found. Please report to experts
```

one can tell what's happened by listing rule history for the input dataset of that task:

```
belforte@lxplus814/cmsweb> rucio list-rules-history cms:/SingleMuon/Run2016B-21Feb2020_ver2_UL2016_HIPM-v1/MINIAOD
----------------------------------------

----------------------------------------

----------------------------------------

Time : 2023-06-15 03:29:14
----------------------------------------

RSE expression : T1_US_FNAL_Disk|T2_BR_SPRACE|T2_US_Caltech|T2_US_Florida|T2_US_MIT|T2_US_Nebraska|T2_US_Purdue|T2_US_UCSD|T2_US_Vanderbilt|T2_US_Wisconsin
Time : 2023-06-15 09:11:53
belforte@lxplus814/cmsweb>
```

and indeed

```
 belforte@lxplus814/cmsweb> rucio rule-info 60350d44cf2a49d29de6e9688993903a
2023-06-15 20:50:53,794	ERROR	No replication rule found.
Details: No rule with the id 60350d44cf2a49d29de6e9688993903a found
belforte@lxplus814/cmsweb>
```

and rule deletion was duly logged

```
2023-06-15 10:30:27,417:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Retrieving KILLRECALL tasks
2023-06-15 10:30:34,550:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Retrieved a total of 6 KILLRECALL tasks

2023-06-15 10:30:34,551:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Will delete rule 60350d44cf2a49d29de6e9688993903a
2023-06-15 10:30:34,576:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Will set to KILLED task 230615_032814:santocch_crab_singlemu-2016b
2023-06-15 10:30:34,658:INFO:TapeRecallManager:Done on this task
```

</detail>

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-15T19:37:39Z)

this problem is what made TapeRecallManager go for the first time through
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/b0e87839e79743850e292d35f012efc42344cb01/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/TapeRecallManager.py#L93-L97
which triggered the bugs in #7667 and #7669

## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-15T19:44:35Z)

the solution will be to use new `taskbyddmreqid` API
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/b0e87839e79743850e292d35f012efc42344cb01/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTTask.py#L108-L112
to list all tasks which refer to same rule as the task in KILLRECALL and only delete the rule if that task is the only one.

This is not 100% foolproof, there can be race conditions as TW thread does a DBSDataDiscovery and reuses a rule while another thread processes KILLRECALL and remove the rule. But changes of this are very small, and in the end, the result will be one task stuck in TAPERECALL which user will likely kill and submit again.
We can live with that, and avoid making code more complex.
- [ ] put comments in the (new) code explaining this

...     days = (today-created).days

...         oldRules.append(rule['id'])
...

0 are older than 60 dasy

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7705: fix sandbox use in job wrapper
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7705: fix sandbox use in job wrapper State: closed Opened: 2023-06-30T10:18:35Z Closed: 2024-09-30T11:55:10Z Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7705 ## Opening post (belforte, 2023-06-30T10:18:35Z) currently `sandbox.tar.gz` is expanded in two places (see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7681#issuecomment-1613144037 and comment below that) 1. `/srv` : so that e.g. `scriptExe` and additional `userFiles` are found where needed and as documented in [FAQ](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#How_are_the_inputFiles_handled_i) 2. `/srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z` so that "scram subdirectories" picked frome `$CMSSW_BASE` on submission host are placed in corresponding directories Furthermore, `PSet.py` and `PSet.pkl` are moved up from `/srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z` to `/srv` because that's the current directory where `cmsRun` command is executed. This overrides the ones places in `/srv` in step 1. We also have a real problem (**bug**) : new code to expand user tar files https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7661 only does that in `/srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z`, while user may expect this to be happen in `/srv` **NO**: reviewing the above one year later, user tar files are expanded in /srv, not /srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z. So I am not sure if anything is needed, aside good documentation so that we avoid going through things again.

We should expand the sandbox only once and place each file in the right place ! ## Comment (belforte, 2023-06-30T16:38:50Z) This is not particularly urgent at this point. But I'd rather do the cleanup sooner than later, to do it when we have things clear in memory and so that we also fix documentation and will never be confused again ## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-07-03T12:01:02Z) Instead of using multiple tar archives, which would require some changes, we can use a single archive, but change the directory where files are put inside of it. This would still require changes in both the client and the jobwr, but hopefully they will be a bit less invasive. For example, we could use `tarfile.add(..., arcname="srv/" + filename )` for the files that should go in `/srv` and `tarfile.add(..., arcname="cmssbase/" + filename )` for the files that need to go to `srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z`. in `CMSRunAnalysis.py:prepSandbox` we can extract the archive and then move all the directories from the archive to the desired final path. ## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-07-03T12:02:18Z) > We also have a real problem (bug) : new code to expand user tar files https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7661 only does that in /srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z, while user may expect this to be happen in /srv Maybe I am missing something, but why dont you execute the same extract command twice, both in `prepSandbox` and `extractUserSandbox`? are you waiting to for the cleanup and do not want to add any "dirty" fixes? ## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-03T12:50:02Z) neat idea, thanks. Indeed that way we can also easily make a backward compatible TW and avoid disruption. As to the second comment, indeed now I expand tar files only in `/srv` . But we need to change things a bit and only expand user sandbox after CMSSW_X_Y_Z directory has been created so we do all things in one place. ## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-03T13:18:19Z) let's map into things to do: - [x] modify TW to do sandbox expansion in only one place in the code after CMSSW_X_Y_Z exists and remove prepSandbox - [ ] expand in a temporary directory - [ ] if files appear with a flat structure, put them all both in `/srv` and `/srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z` (do not use explitic `/srv` string, of course, define a name for `job's starting directory` like e.g. `topdir` and use it consistently) - [ ] if files from sandbox are organized as `cmssw_base/..`. + `topdir/....` put each set in the proper place - [ ] expand tar files placed in `topdir` - [ ] modify CRAB client to archive files in the two `cmssw_base`and `topdir` directories - [ ] once old client is gone (also from PRE), cleanup wrapper to remove backward compatibility Note added on Sept 20: all actions listed above are not needed. Once we "`tarfile.add(..., arcname="cmssbase/" + filename )` for the files that need to go to `srv/CMSSW_X_Y_Z`." as @mapellidario cleverly pointed out in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7705#issuecomment-1618096011 , expansion inside `CMSSW_X_Y_Z` will be taken care of by the current iterative expansion of `sandbox.tar.gz` ## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-12T16:50:10Z) of course I have now forgotten everything... and will need to re-learn :-) ## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-16T16:37:16Z) after re-reading the issue and the code and a first attempt a documentation in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7754#issuecomment-2353270108 I am leaning toward * fix the documentation and leave code as is ## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-18T15:54:04Z) Well `CRAB3.zip` is not sent to the WN. No reason to reference it in the JobWrapper ! https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/b3b26dbd3c8aa617e6a0e03b6cfe8f23a5fc3c97/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L57 ## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-19T16:51:52Z) About the "sandbox expanded in two places". I will start by removing https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c8607f723248dff957d6146a25162d8f8128fbb/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L375 and incorporating the functionality in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c8607f723248dff957d6146a25162d8f8128fbb/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L392 so that at least things will be clear. Also it means that expansion is done after CMSSW_X_Y_Z has been created, opening the way for a "do it once". BEst option looks to me at some point to modify sandboxing in client so that $CMSSW_BASE is tarred into a CMSSW_X_Y_Z directory and then all files will automatically go in the proper place when the sandbox is iteratively expanded https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c8607f723248dff957d6146a25162d8f8128fbb/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L381-L387

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7713: Run CheckTapeRecall.py on a TW machine
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7713: Run CheckTapeRecall.py on a TW machine

State: closed
Opened: 2023-07-03T14:08:37Z
Closed: 2024-02-07T10:48:22Z
Labels: Priority: High, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7713

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-07-03T14:08:37Z)

Currently, we run the script CheckTapeRecall.py from a acron job owned by Stefano. We would like to run it in a centralized place instead, for example in a `crab-prod-tw*` machine.

In order to achieve this, we would need:

- [ ] write to eos with the `crab3` unix user of one of our VMs
    - This is worked a couple of weeks ago, but it is currently [broken](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=ticket&table=incident&n=INC3516468)
- [ ] an environment where to run the script from
    - one option is to convert the script to a recurring action
    - [ ] otherwise, we can execute it in a crabtaskworker docker container. I would rather go this way.
        - one option would be to create a new "runContainer.sh" script.
        - [ ] install pandas inside crabtaskworker environment. This will likely require to create a new `py3-pandas.spec` in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/tree/comp_gcc630
        - [ ] rucio requires X509_USER_KEY, X509_USER_CERT, RUCIO_ACCOUNT env variables . We will need to make sure that we properly set these.

I managed to run the script on crab-dev-tw02 [1], with some small modifications to what we currently have at the moment.

---

[1]

change the script not to use the proxy, but to use the service(cert|key).pem, as in [2], then

```bash
# open a TW container
source  /data/srv/TaskManager/env.sh

# install pandas, this will be done properly next time
# from here: https://www.redhat.com/sysadmin/install-python-pip-linux
wget https://bootstrap.pypa.io/get-pip.py
python3 get-pip.py
python3 -m pip install pandas

# these env vars will be included in the bash script that start CheckTapeRecall.py
cd /data/repos/CRABServer/script/Utils
export X509_USER_KEY=/data/certs/servicekey.pem
export X509_USER_CERT=/data/certs/servicecert.pem
export RUCIO_ACCOUNT=crab_server
python3 CheckTapeRecall.py

```

The result that I obtained is here: https://dmapelli.web.cern.ch/crab/20230703-checktaperecall/RecallRules.html

[2]

```diff
[crab3@crab-dev-tw02 Utils]$ git diff
diff --git a/scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py b/scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py
index 6276384..2738433 100644
--- a/scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py
+++ b/scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py
@@ -252,9 +252,9 @@ def ensureEnvironment():
     # make sure Rucio client is initialized, this also ensures X509 proxy
     rucio = Client()

-    proxy = os.environ['X509_USER_PROXY']
-    crab = CRABRest(hostname='cmsweb.cern.ch', localcert=proxy,
-                    localkey=proxy, userAgent='CheckTapeRecall')
+    # proxy = os.environ['X509_USER_PROXY']
+    crab = CRABRest(hostname='cmsweb.cern.ch', localcert="/data/certs/servicecert.pem",
+                    localkey="/data/certs/servicekey.pem", userAgent='CheckTapeRecall')
     crab.setDbInstance('prod')
```

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-07-05T06:54:27Z)

Error I accidentially found in TW:
```
2023-07-05 07:49:18,260:DEBUG:Worker,120:Process-5: SUBMIT work on 230705_054818:alebihan_crab_WJetsToLNu_HT-400To600_recovery_2 completed in 15 seconds: Status: ERROR
Error = Problem handling 230705_054818:alebihan_crab_WJetsToLNu_HT-400To600_recovery_2 because of invalid literal for int() with base 10: '0.1394' failure, traceback follows
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py", line 85, in executeAction
    output = work.execute(nextinput, task=self._task, tempDir=self.tempDir)
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py", line 103, in execute
    result = self.executeInternal(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py", line 332, in executeInternal
    self.requestTapeRecall(dataToRecall=dataToRecall, sizeToRecall=totalSizeBytes,
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py", line 434, in requestTapeRecall
    self.requestRucioTapeRecall(dataToRecall, sizeToRecall, tapeLocations, msgHead=msg)
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py", line 490, in requestRucioTapeRecall
    (RSE_EXPRESSION, grouping) = self.whereToRecall(
  File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230616-6cb8f108e2d006dcaad44b2b98777a25/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py", line 560, in whereToRecall
    availableSpace = int(rucio.list_rse_attributes(rse)['ddm_quota'])  # bytes
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '0.1394'
```
It cause by `rucio.list_rse_attributes(rse)['ddm_quota']` is a string and it can return floating point value which break `int()` function.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1223cef3f046f392c9bb7001c422f354024ae99d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L560

This is easy to fix by replace with `int(float(rucio.list_rse_attributes(rse)['ddm_quota']))`.

But, I did not see where `freeRSEs` is used in `WhereToRecall` method. Maybe should replace `largeRSEs` at [line 576](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1223cef3f046f392c9bb7001c422f354024ae99d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L560)?
And `freeRSEs` can be empty because all T1/T2 sites (except T2_GR_Ioannina is on the blacklist) reported ddm_quota less than 1,see below.

![Screenshot from 2023-07-05 08-41-03](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/8ecb9125-3a50-4180-a9d5-e46c382af9f6)

I leave this to @belforte hand to decide how to fix it.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-05T08:22:54Z)

Thanks Wa..
It looks like they changed ddm_quota in Rucio from number of bytes to a fracion (of total ?). Surely for good reasons. And as usual w/o asking if someone else was using this by any chance, @dciangot @dynamic-entropy @ericvaandering please remember us next time :-)
Sorry Eric, I know that from Rucio developers POV ddm_quota is a custom attribute configured by CMS and Rucio does not care and it is for CMS Rucio Ops to rule.. .but I do not know who exactly "Rucio Ops" is, i.e. who takes decisions on this, so am hoping that in such cases they consult with CMS Rucio Developers.

Useless complains aside, it is likely that `freeRSEs` is simply a leftover of some initial  implementation, in the end.. why not let Rucio decide where there is space and where not ? `largeRSE` is there as just another example of blacklisting unreliable sites w/o naming them explicitly. But `freeRSEs` ?

I will check history to be sure before I remove this freeRSEs.

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2023-07-05T08:31:27Z)

Hello @belforte
Yes, I changed these numbers to percentages. If it is quicker for you to fix, I will let you go ahead or I can convert them back to integers.

I am not sure, why you are using this as a number at all. All you should be doing is specifying it as weight in a rule.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-05T08:31:58Z)

once upon a time I was telling Rucio to scatter largish datasets (>50 TB) in multiple sites and to avoid multiple to be many, I was sending a short list of RSE's (handful usually) so had to make sure that those had quota available.
Then two things happened:
1) old useless rules were removed and we stopped having sites with >90% locked space
2) we decided to use grouping=ALL for all datasets, and leave it to Rucio to pick the one RSE

Everything clear.

thanks @dynamic-entropy , I hope my last comment explains why we were using this explicly, in addition to using it as a weight. In current implementation we do not need it. And will remove this part.

@novicecpp I would expect that this fully breaks tapeRecall and we need to fix immediately. No ?

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7718: Non-EDM outputs do not have checksums in transfers.txt which required by Rucio.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7718: Non-EDM outputs do not have checksums in transfers.txt which required by Rucio.

State: closed
Opened: 2023-07-06T08:28:10Z
Closed: 2023-07-19T08:38:58Z
Labels: RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7718

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-07-06T08:28:10Z)

File-to-transfer items in `transfers.txt` are updated by `PostJob.py`, which contains checksums `PostJob.py` read from json FJR.
But for the non-EDM files (including logs when `logsTransfer=True`), JobWrapper does not calculate checksums and puts them in FJR. So `PostJob.py` use [placeholder checksums](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/14116832382f142e3629352d5e0b6cf7a3b3a3d9/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2697) instead and passes to `transfers.txt`.

This break Rucio ASO because adler32 checksums is required for [add_replica](https://github.com/rucio/rucio/blob/85bb8a9e93f9515b5868e96349a59984eb63a110/lib/rucio/client/replicaclient.py#L238) API.

It does not break FTS ASO because we never pass any checksums to FTS jobs ([FTS_Transfers.py#L247-L342](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2c31e26c5903fbce0bcbe68f1217ed150ea043bf/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L247-L342)).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-06T08:31:07Z)

Original discussion on MatterMost (Thanks Stefano for great explanation).

**Q:**

I tried to copy task [230613_131234:christok_crab_ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M_700_MH2_M_200_1L](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230613_131234:christok_crab_ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M_700_MH2_M_200_1L) to run in test12 with my custom crabclient.
I found that copied tasks run in test12, especially tasks that have non-edm files, always had adler32 hash to 0 even though fjr json report correct hash (example [postjob](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230628_071411:tseethon_crab_copyoftask_notedmfile_test12_20230628_091312/postjob.3.0.txt) logs).

**A:**

[Job](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230628_071411:tseethon_crab_copyoftask_notedmfile_test12_20230628_091312/job_out.3.0.txt) has two output files `jettoolbox.root` and `miniaod2tree.root`.
In the [fjr](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230628_071411:tseethon_crab_copyoftask_notedmfile_test12_20230628_091312/job_fjr.3.0.json) both are listed but only the former has values for the checksums (adler32 and cksum). The [PostJob](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230628_071411:tseethon_crab_copyoftask_notedmfile_test12_20230628_091312/postjob.3.0.txt) only refers to `miniaod2tree.root`. At this point it makes sense that adler32 and cksum are 0 in PostJob, but I still can not say why:
1) second file does not have cksum values in FJR
2) PostJob only works on second file

I think the solution to mistery in the what happened on the grid node (note [1])
It looks that this task had an inusual [configuration](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0122/christok/230613_131234:christok_crab_ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M_700_MH2_M_200_1L/debug/crabConfig.py) [2] (skip EDM output from cmsRUn and only take a non-EDM file) and it is possible that simply in this case we do not have adler32/cksum from cmsRun (we do not compute those with "CRAB" code).

We need to keep in mind that non-EDM files are special, e.g. we do not publish them in DBS. And I believe that we
only use checksum to store them in DBS. Differently from file size, the checksums do not go in FILETRANSFERSDB. I am not sure that we send them to FTS in current ASO. It is also possible that if we do, and send 0, nobody on our side ever notices and FTS ignores it. All things to check.

Indeed already the original [PostJob](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0122/christok/230613_131234:christok_crab_ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M_700_MH2_M_200_1L/postjob.3.0.txt) has these lines

```
Tue, 13 Jun 2023 17:02:48 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob ASO job description: {'_id': '49bb163ba3505509828c029b790fcad9fe9da538072e7d2d7edffb78',
 'checksums': {'adler32': '0', 'cksum': '0'},
 'dbs_url': 'https://cmsweb.cern.ch/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader',
 'destination': 'T3_US_FNALLPC',
 'destination_lfn': '/store/user/christok/CRAB3_TransferData/multicrab-SingleLepton-CMSSW10_6_29-Run2018ABCD-dataVersion2018_106XUL-20Jun2022/ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M-700_MH2_M-200_1L_TuneCP5_13TeV-amcatnlo_pythia8/crab_ChargedHiggsToHW_HToTauTau_M_700_MH2_M_200_1L/230613_131234/0000/miniaod2tree_3.root',
And e.g. for log files, which we move via FTS, we have fake hardcode values https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2c31e26c5903fbce0bcbe68f1217ed150ea043bf/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2316
```

Sorry for long, multiply edited, message. We should probably follow up in some better way.

[1] this lines are "curious"
```
== JOB AD: CRAB_EDMOutputFiles = {  }
== JOB AD: CRAB_AdditionalOutputFiles = { "miniaod2tree.root" }
```
[2]
```
config.JobType.outputFiles = ['miniaod2tree.root']
config.JobType.disableAutomaticOutputCollection = True

I agree, I do not see why we should import htcondor in crabserver, I checked and it seems to be used only in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/CRABInterface/HTCondorDataWorkflow.py . It is not easy to tell what in CRABInterace is used and what it is not. Marco M. and predecessors have been too smart here. It depends on CRABServer configuration which kind of workflows is called.
This is why I have never dared to remove files in there.
OTOH e.g. crab status was redesigned long time ago to use the cached file prepared by task wrapper on the scheduler, we do no try to ask condor.

Of course first thing is to check that we can still build and run. Code cleanup will come later.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-17T20:19:02Z)

yeah.. that's how [/HTCondorDataWorkflow.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/CRABInterface/HTCondorDataWorkflow.py) sneaked in from a call to `DataUserWorkflow.py`
that\s the only file in CRABServer where `import classa` appears.
The trick is this line in `/srv/current/config/crabserver/config.py`
```
data.workflowManager = 'HTCondorDataWorkflow'
```
which directs the server to use `HTCondorDataWorkflow`  as per
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2365939e2777e4afa2077f2c6b485b899c1facde/src/python/CRABInterface/DataUserWorkflow.py#L13-L16

See also this [old note](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5690#issuecomment-395351592) from Marco

It is well past the time where it would make sense to have a workflow other than HTCondor, so
we may look into getting rid of those lines which Stefano can not possibly understand and simplify here as well.

If we want to hack our way into cleaning up, I suspect best way is to take one  crab-dev* machine and do brute force iterations of edit/start -d . Starting point IMHO is to remove https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2365939e2777e4afa2077f2c6b485b899c1facde/src/python/CRABInterface/HTCondorDataWorkflow.py#L42

you can also test "removing dependencies" as simply as "delete files in `/data/srv/current/sw.crab_master/slc7_amd64_gcc630/external/` (even simply rename in order to quickly revert). And if you end up in a mess, just restart the pod and the container will be refreshed.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7741: RUCIO_Transfers.py: RUCIO ASO does not have publish infomation to proper create publish container

State: closed

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7741

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-07-11T10:26:12Z)

In case the task has both edm and non-edm files, non-edm files always have `/FakeDataset` from PostJob.py.
RUCIO_Transfers.py grab the first item of `transfers.txt` and uses it as the container name.

For transfers container, any name should be fine as long as Rucio accepts and can link back to the task that was created.

But for publish container, this will be a problem if the first item is non-edm:

- It uses `/FakeDataset` as an incorrect container name. It should use the same name we put in db (`tasks.tm_output_dataset`).
- We publish non-edm files along edm files to DBS, which will raise the exception in publisher later.

To fix this, I will pass `delayed_publicationflag_update` flag to `transfers.txt` to let RUCIO_Transfers.py pick only files with `delayed_publicationflag_update=True` and add them to publish container.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-21T16:33:56Z)

I was expecting to find `dbs_blockname` filled in `transfersdb` only for files which need to be published in DBS.

Let me know. I am not attempting to publish yet, still working on the part which collects info from transfersdb and filemetadata and prepares json files to feed to Publisher/TaskPublish.py, so there is no special hurry.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-16T15:39:54Z)

current situation:
1. name of "sandbox" is passes a argument to the HTC jobs as "-a sandbox.tar.gz"
2. both "sanbox.tar.gz" and "CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz" are placed on job wrappers cwd (/srv) by HTCondor using "transfer_input_files"
1. [gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh](]https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh) it is a very thin wrapper which dumps ads, chirps exit codes and calls CMSRunAnalysis.sh and cmscp.py. The latter copied output to local /store/user/temp  and it is not relevant here
3. [CMSRunAnalysis.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.sh) sets up environment (including python) then
   1. untar   CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz
   2. adds CRAB3.zip and WMCore.zip to PYTHONPATH
   4. runs  CMSRunAnalysis.py
4. [CMSRunAnalysis.py]() , then
   1. parses -a argument into local variable archiveJob (which evaluates to "sandbox.tar.gz")
   1. calls [prepSandbox()](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ce559a11ef02c447f909ee166b7d48f218eb021d/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L375)
      * untars the "archiveJob" file in current "cwd" (/srv) and also expand any tar file found in there
   3. initializes WMCore and SCRAM
   5. calls [extractUserSandbox()](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ce559a11ef02c447f909ee166b7d48f218eb021d/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L392)
      * cd CMSSW_....
      * expand here ../archiveJob , but not tarfiles which may be in there
      * move up PSet* to /srv and set /srv again as cwd
   6. performs PSet tweaking
   7. runs cmsRun or script_exe

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7755: Adopting cmsrucio_import to CRABClient

State: open

Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-07-13T11:38:21Z)

Rahul wrote [cmsrucio_import](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/tree/master/UserDMTools/cmsrucio_import) to import user's files to Rucio. We need to decide if it worth to integrate to CRABClient.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-13T11:39:20Z)

My comments (move from meeting minutes):
- The script is pretty straightforward and requires only a rucio python client. It can easily integrate to CRABClient if we can import Rucio client in CMSSW env, or treat it as a standalone script like `crab checkdataset`.
- Concerns:
  - What does [rucio.client.uploadclient.UploadClient](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/blob/83a1cbbf48f30ce9bb85e1dcc408fd1e9c4e98d1/UserDMTools/cmsrucio_import/cmsrucio_import/main.py#L292C5-L292C55) use behind the scene for uploading files to temp_RSE?
  - How to estimate maintenance cost, especially edge cases from users.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-13T12:42:39Z)

> What does [rucio.client.uploadclient.UploadClient](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/blob/83a1cbbf48f30ce9bb85e1dcc408fd1e9c4e98d1/UserDMTools/cmsrucio_import/cmsrucio_import/main.py#L292C5-L292C55) use behind the scene for uploading files to temp_RSE?

I was so sure that the answer was `gfal-copy` that I was surprised you asked and had a look. It looks quite complex, what is used depends on the protocol which depends on the RSE configuration. But e.g. for `webDavb` it seems to using "plain" HTTP calls via the (external) [requests](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) package. That may ultimately need `libcurl.so` but there\s a chance that it works inside `cmsenv`. To be tested. NOPE ! `requests` needs `urllib3`

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-13T15:08:28Z)

shall we move this to CRABClient repo ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-13T15:28:59Z)

My comments:
 * I found the python difficult to understand, but I agree that this is my shortcoming. This mostly suffers from lack of 100f-view documentation: use example, a sketch of a user manual, some explanation of those YAML files
 * Since it is a new tool, I would not mind to wrap tings with "if python3" and only use when CRBAClient runs with py3, which should fix all code compatibility issues
 * I worry about `poetry` and `wheel` stuff. README is not clear in this regard, also there's a `pip3 install -r requirements.txt` but no `requirements.txt` file in the repo. Is that part about how to build a package for pip ? Why, since you can simply do `pip`install rucio` ? What does this need to depend on besides Rucio ?
 * we have to see about binary dependencies though, and worry that even python compatibility may be transient since moving to next version will be done independently in Rucio and CMSSW.
 * anyhow a lot is about did/rse manipulations which should be pretty safe to import in our code
 * The fear is that if we do nothing but simply tell users to fetch it  and use it, answering questions and providing good examples will be more work than bit the bullet , strip off al lthat we do no undestand, and just adopt `upload_..._and_create_rule()`
 * We should look into unifty code for dealing with RSE_Temp in here and RUCIO_Transfers

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-13T17:01:11Z)

We can safely ignore poetry (and also wheel). It is just python package manager to locks dependency to specific version and hash, prevent tamper (supply chain attack). We do not need that if we integrate into crab. Well, he forgot to put `requirements.txt` or proper `pyproject.toml` @dynamic-entropy

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2023-07-14T07:24:57Z)

Hello Stefano, Wa, Dario
I never received feedback (for no one was using it other than myself), so I never bothered to make changes and corrections.
My choice of poetry wasn't a wise one, from one recommendation to another, starting from typer.
( We can change all that, we had a chat with Dario, but alas! he stopped reminding me anymore :eyes: )

What is the intended timeline for this? I am happy to help in whatever direction you wish/decide to go.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-14T12:44:49Z)

thanks @dynamic-entropy , and do no take it bad that we started to talk about this w/o you.
The aim is to make sure that we have a tool which users can use and we can support.
Turning it into a 'crab importotorucio' has some obvious appealing but before we do we need to understand the dependencies, current and possibly future one.
We have suffered enough in the past when grid tools and CMSSW migrated from on SL version to another and from one python version to another on different timelines.
So we do not have a defined timeline for this, but I think that if we do not do it before end of the year, it is possible that we never do.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-18T10:30:43Z)

@dynamic-entropy Could you please update `requirements.txt`?

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2023-07-18T10:49:49Z)

Hello
( I did not take it badly, it was a joke about Dario stopping reminding me :sweat_smile: - i should have noted that others do not have context ).
I think I need to remove typer and poetry for this, but you can use this requirement file if you want to go ahead as is, https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/blob/af21943c6a53bf387155e4067fe6568938864a67/UserDMTools/requirements.txt

Cheers

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-18T13:05:46Z)

Thanks Rahul.
We are in the evaluation step and are figuring out how to migrate to CRABClient. Some information from you is indeed needed.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-07-20T10:37:31Z)

we have a chat in CRAB Meeting.
Some live notes:

* all in all it looks "little and easy" code, esp. after Rahul's clarifications
* so we decided to go for it and it has top be a "crab command". This is the only way to make users use it.
* how do we go ?
  * option 1)
     * have a standalone script inside crabClient and executed in a forked subprocess after `scram unstenv` like for `crab checkdataset`
   * option 2)
     * integrate rucio client calls in the code but inside an `if this CMSSW version is good for Rucio` (this may help in other cases as well, e.g. checkwrite)
   * option 3)
      * add our own commands in `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/current/bin` ? is it possible ? does it make sense ? Need to talk to Shahzad.
   * option 4)
      * long shot (pipe dream?): revert how CRABClient works, instead of running in CMSSW env,, run in a "pip" env and fork a subprocess with scram commands for the little code which needs to parse PSet.py and communicate with rest of code via JSON files

* who will do this ?
    * Nobody has time until September at least. Not even to plan details and figure out how long it will take
   * **Let's revisit around September 15 ?**

**NOTE** especially if we go for 1), work on CRABClient side is minimal. Issue is all about understanding exactly what needs to be passed to the rucio_import script, document, validate args etc. etc. Also a whole new set of arguments different from what we already defined makes it horrible the already uglysh code in e.g. ClientMapping. Some decisions to take etc. But it looks like most work will go in understanding how exactly the import script works, which we need to do anyhow.

and this must be move to CRABClient repo !

we have so many warnings and errors that risk to overlook real problems (it happened already with undefined variables).

4. things we can live with

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7765: refactor ServerUtilities.py
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7765: refactor ServerUtilities.py

State: open
Opened: 2023-07-17T08:09:08Z
Labels: Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7765

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-07-17T08:09:08Z)

Should have three files
* what is used also in CRABClient, hopefully very little, which needs to stay py2/3 compat
  * create new file name here (e.g. constants !)
* what is used only in server, so can move to py3 only and rely on pylint when changing
* accept also that some code like encodeRequest can be duplicated  or adapted to simpler use case and moved to ClientUtilities

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-08-07T14:58:12Z)

Just random though from reviewing https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7800
- Keep `ServerUtilities.py` for sharing code for both client and server.
- Move all utils.py files into single directory `src/python/utils` like [wmcore](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/tree/master/src/python/Utils) does.
  - This way, we can move `RucioUtils.py` into `utils/rucio/functions.py` and move `RucioActions.py` to `utils/rucio/actions.py`.
  - Also, mark `src/python/utils` directory exclusive for servers (REST/TW/PUB).

## Comment (belforte, 2023-08-07T15:28:02Z)

I like this idea, thanks @novicecpp
@mapellidario please add your thoughts. I defer further cleanup to after we have finalized this. No hurry.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-08-08T13:36:25Z)

Increased priority since it is good to have a plan. Which we will implement slowly

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-23T10:52:19Z)

hand to Vijay ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-24T09:05:56Z)

I will introduce `src/python/Utils` now. But I prefer to have few/no subdirectories there at this time, since I expect a limited number of files and there will be several utilities in common between TW and Publisher.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7766: add Njob in task to Task Table

State: closed
Opened: 2023-07-17T10:19:25Z
Closed: 2025-04-11T13:50:20Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support, Status: Done, Status: Available
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7766

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-07-17T10:19:25Z)

It helps when looking at user jobs e.g. in the [UI](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/u) to know how big was the task w/o going through remake+status or opening the (possibly large and slow) grafana page or the (possibly large and very slow) webdir
TW has the info after the splitting process, so can surely add easily

We do not have it for automatic splitting, can start by setting it to e.g. -1
if we want an integer there  (leave 0 for cases like splitter did not create any job).

For automatic splitting we'd need to add and edit it from preDag's as they run,
but maybe too much trouble

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-07-18T10:20:51Z)

This is what I also want but I do not like the idea to store this data in oracle just for monitoring.
Can we do it the same way  we do with `cache_status()` in [task_proc_wrapper.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2365939e2777e4afa2077f2c6b485b899c1facde/scripts/task_process/task_proc_wrapper.sh#L7-L10), dump the simple json and let web UI to fetch this file and display?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-12T08:45:46Z)

doing now, since it may also be useful for task scheduling: knowing how big are current tasks for a given user

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7767: add time range to CrabServer UI MONIT pointer
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7767: add time range to CrabServer UI MONIT pointer

State: closed
Opened: 2023-07-17T10:28:04Z
Closed: 2023-09-18T09:47:50Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support, Priority: High, Status: Available
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7767

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-07-17T10:28:04Z)

since the default is 30min, now it almost always fails to find the task as it builts URL like

https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=santocch&var-task=230714_100021:santocch_crab_singlemu-2017f

Need the same as in `crab status`

https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=santocch&var-task=230714_100021%3Asantocch_crab_singlemu-2017f&from=1689325221000&to=now

where from is in `msec` fom epoch, see
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/00d5e3ced6389fe328fe429eb41941a2a6a7f1d6/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/status.py#L460-L470

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-14T08:32:05Z)

@mapellidario @novicecpp this requires changes to
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/a344356b0708b0a6b9f181eb34715252afa63a04/src/script/task_info.js#L583-L584

AFAIU: extract task submission time from part of taskname before `:`, convert in msec from epoch and add it to the URL.
But I do not know `js` (JavaScript ?) and would take me a while to learn how to manipulate strings and arithmetic here. Does  maybe one of you know this stuff already and could assign to himself and do ?
It always annoys me when I need to look at someones taks and hit this thing that I click on the button and the task info is partilally available at best. If then I change the data in grafana, it shows me all tasks submitted since then by that user and I need to find the right one :-(

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-14T08:35:04Z)

The trick is move time range to 30 days. Always work for me.

I will do.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-14T08:40:54Z)

not all of the times for me. It may depend on whether the task has jobs submitted in last 30min so that it appears in the initial dashboard and can stick in the selection menu.

thanks !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7769: Publication is broken when using Rucio container as  input dataset
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7769: Publication is broken when using Rucio container as  input dataset

State: closed
Opened: 2023-07-17T21:05:59Z
Closed: 2024-01-25T12:28:55Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7769

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-07-17T21:05:59Z)

with e.g.
```
config.Data.inputDataset = cms:/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/AODSIM
```
TaskWorker part works and jobs run but `taskPublish.py` fails because it tries to insert that in DBS as input dataset
```
2023-07-17 22:50:29,099:INFO:PublisherMaster,696:TaskPublishScript done : b'DBS Server error: [{\'error\': {\'reason\': "DBSError Code:114 Description:DBS validation error when wrong pattern is provided Function:dbs.validator.Check Message:unable to match \'dataset\' value \'cms:/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/AODSIM\' Error: invalid parameter(s)"
```

I guess we can start by disabling publication in this case. Because in general we have no way to ensure that this rucio container maps to a dataset properly described in DBS `prod/global`.

Stick to
 * Publication in DBS requires input data in DBS.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-19T20:35:51Z)

.hmm... all in all.. if data processing produces valid FJRs and we have metadata for DBS.. why not simply stripping the initial scope in this case ?
@dciangot what do you think ?

## Comment (dciangot, 2024-01-19T20:40:19Z)

I think it will not hurt to disable it. If your input is from Rucio and not from DBS, It might be reasonable to say "I'm sorry, I can't do it".

Either way is fine, stripping out scope can be a solution, but it really depends on having strong use cases for that I think.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-19T20:43:01Z)

supporting is at least clear. DIsabling I am not sure if to do in client or in server, where exactly, how to communicate... too many decisions !
Let me try the easy way (stripping) and see if it works

fix tested OK on publisher_schedd.  Need to verity on Publisher_rucio

```python

            # TODO this shoudl be a function

State: closed

Closed: 2024-04-17T13:14:27Z
Labels: Priority: Medium, Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7782

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-07-20T16:50:52Z)

We are not using anymore the functions in HTCondorDataWorkflow.py that require talking directly to the schedulers.

However, maybe in the future we will find a good reason for talking to the schedds from crabserver, so we do not want to remove the rpm from py3-htcondor specfile from the crabserver image and we want to keep HTCondorDataWorkflow.py around in the current state (maybe freeze the file in its current forms in a copy with "old" appended at the end).

A good starting point would be https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/compare/master...mapellidario:20230717_py3htc10

we can remove htcondor from spec file unti needed, FWIW. I only worry about loosing code which we may not easily re-invent

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7788: make TapeRecallManager work for any TW name
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7788: make TapeRecallManager work for any TW name

State: closed
Opened: 2023-08-01T13:59:50Z
Closed: 2023-08-01T16:54:36Z
Labels: Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7788

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-08-01T13:59:50Z)

Current TapeRecallManager only acts on tasks submitted by same TW as it runs on.
This may marginally help when running multiple TW in parallel, so we can use same exact configuration for recurring actions.
But when we simply switch TasskWorker, like we did recently, tasks put in recall by previous TW were left un-managed.

Since we usually only run one TW, it is better to make TapeRecallManager independent of the TW name.
Even if we end up running two instances at same time, there should be no problem, at worst, in case of race, a task status is set to same `NEW` or `KILLED` value twice in a row.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7797: RUCIO_Transfers.py: Things need to be done before deploy on production
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7797: RUCIO_Transfers.py: Things need to be done before deploy on production

State: closed
Opened: 2023-08-04T12:34:36Z
Closed: 2024-02-14T10:32:00Z
Labels: RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7797

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-08-04T12:34:36Z)

While we are waiting for subtasks in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7632 to close, and waiting for [more test](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/ByvZ-kX4k/user-tseethon-cms-tasks-monitoring-globalview?orgId=11&var-user=tseethon&var-site=All&var-current_url=%2Fd%2FIF-s18qVk%2Fuser-tseethon-cms-task-monitoring-task-view&var-task=All&var-match_env=usertask_test12), here is a list of things that we need to do before we deploy Rucio ASO to production and starting ask user to use, that can be done in parallel:

- Changes in client
  - [x] ~~New crab args, storagArea = sitelocal/rucio~~ ([see  comment](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7797#issuecomment-1669685313))
  - [x] Enrich crab status (rucio rule id)
  - [x] Fix web ui
- User docs
  - [x] How does it work (transfer/publish container)
  - [x] How to request quota
  - [x] Example task submit with rucio aso
  - [x] Limitation
  - [x] Common FAQ and Troubleshooting
- Server
  - [x] Merge `rucio_transfers` to master
- Monitoring
  - [ ] Script crash (gathering "exception" logs using filebeat)

Note that these tasks are not include in this round:
  - Publisher
  - crab checkwrite
  - TW check Rucio quota before submit to schedd
  - Validation publish container
  - Rucio ASO scripts performance

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-08-08T14:03:59Z)

I decided not to add new client args (storagArea = sitelocal/rucio) because it will make it more confusing, especially when we need to debug later.
In example:
```python
config.Data.outLFNDirBase = '/store/user/tseethon/mytestoutput-1532'
config.Data.storageArea = 'rucio' # new args
```

When we submitting task to server we put `/store/user/rucio/tseethon/mytestoutput-1532` in `tm_output_lfn`, but when we trace it back what this value come from, it will not match what we see expect to see in client config until we notice `storageArea` option later.
