## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-08-07T14:48:24Z)

I am a bit surprise that `NameError` exception is not catch by `pylint`. For `uploadWarning`, it is understandable because it hidden in `self` which `pylint` does not design to detect that.

I think static type checker tools like `mypy/pyright/pyre` can detect this kind of bug but it is yet-another-3rdparty-software we need to maintain. (I use [pyright](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright) in my editor and it work quite well when I develop Rucio ASO, especially methods and variables hidden in `self` in [ASO/Rucio/Transfer.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8ff0d6f15fb1f15a6996149c6b181d379ce2c191/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Transfer.py)).

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-08-07T15:17:27Z)

I use vscode with pylance (which includes the functionality from pyright). It does not detect the NameError because it thinks that `config` is defined when running DBSDataDiscovery.py as main at https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/272175fa1c946e96a0428fa3e1893ea1f6b0f57a/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L494 .

So yeah, a tale of how static code analysis can only go so far

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7843: crabserver rest - use helm charts to deploy it
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7843: crabserver rest - use helm charts to deploy it

State: closed
Opened: 2023-08-19T13:23:39Z
Closed: 2024-08-23T09:57:04Z
Labels: Priority: Medium, Status: In Progress, Area: CI/CD, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7843

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-08-19T13:23:39Z)

At the moment, we use kubernetes manifest files to deploy crabserver rest [1].

However, the CMSWEB team wants to migrate the deployment of the services to use helm charts [2].

Which actions are required from us?

- [x] test helm charts on a cmsweb-testN cluster. Dario did on cmsweb-test11 and everything seems ok so far.
- [x] write brief documentation on how to deploy and operate the crabserver via the `helm` cli, instead of plain `kubectl`. Dario can do this anytime.
- [x] test helm charts on preprod. Dario prefers to do this under Aroosha's supervision
- [x] can we avoid using `helm` cli? shall we look for an alternative of `imagebot`, so that we can deploy crabserver from a jenkins job? Shall we look into github actions? This is not compulsory, it would just be a "nice to have"
- [x] use helm charts on prod. We do not have a timescale so far.

---

[1] https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml
[2] https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/helm/crabserver

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-28T11:17:06Z)

question now is:
 * how to deploy and track different versions in different clusters so that e.g. `helm list` or `helm history` are useful

We have:
 - chart version (used by GH atuomatic build tool to decide that a char has changed and rebuild)
 - appVersion inside chart (just informative for us)
 - image tag in the `values` file (indicates the tag of the docker container)

only the first 2 are shown by `helm list` and `helm history` . To see the deployed tag we need `kubectl get deployment`

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-03-28T12:37:35Z)

Following the brief discussion before the end of the weekly meeting, here is my proposal for helm:

**Using helm as configuration template.**

That means, we use helm to generate manifests from templates only, similar to `helm template crabserver . -f values.yaml | kubectl apply -f -`.

We throw away the chart version and appVersion, but it can replace with,

- To track the version/history, do rollbacks, etc., we use git feature to revert changes and apply them again (`kubectl rollout` also should work).
- To see the live info using usual `kubectl`.

Why? Because for CD tools like ArgoCD never apply manifest as helm. It use helm to generate the manifests, apply them to k8s, and then track the objects directly.
For the user, when we move to ArgoCD, we will never use `helm install/upgrade` but learn how ArgoCD works instead.

Each environment has its own value file; the common values file is `values.yaml` and the values file for the environment is `values-<k8s-cluster-name>.yaml`.
Our crabserver in helm directory will look like this:

```
crabserver/
├── Chart.yaml
├── templates
│   ├── ...
│   ├── deployment-deamonset.yaml
│   ├── deployment.yaml
│   ├── _helpers.tpl
│   └── ...
├── values-test12.yaml
├── values-test2.yaml
├── values-testbed.yaml
└── values.yaml
```

We apply helm with `helm template crabserver . -f values.yaml -f values-test12.yaml | kubectl apply -f -` (example for `test12`, rightmost `-f` has the highest precedence.)

About imagebot, as we know it does not compatible with helm. I propose to drop the imagebot and use serviceaccount credential to run kubectl/helm directly from CI jobs.

-------------------

So first step should be: make it work with manually apply for all environment. Then, we will make it work on Jenkins.

Here are the action items:
- [x] Ensure helm template crabserver . -f values.yaml | kubectl apply -f - is working in all environments.
- [x] Separate multiple environments into individual values files.
- [x] Set up crab's serviceaccount with a minimum rbac to access non-prod cluster.
- ~~[ ] Clone Deploy_TW and modify it to deploy the helm chart.~~

Note that my knowledge about helm is very limited. I never use it except to generate manifests from upstream charts.
If you have better practice or if there is a new helm feature that can benefit us, feel free to leave a comment.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7844: user sandbox - improvements needed for crab recover
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7844: user sandbox - improvements needed for crab recover

State: closed
Opened: 2023-08-19T13:39:05Z
Closed: 2024-05-24T15:42:57Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7844

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-08-19T13:39:05Z)

While investigating how we can submit a recovery task, we encountered some limitations in how we manage user sandboxes.

Their management has been designed to be allow the TW to submit a task properly, not to be reused after the task has already been submitted.

#### problem

When submitting a task, if the user sandbox is already present in the object storage, we simply re-use it. In particular, we do not check when it expires. This means that it is possible that when a task is submitted, the user sandbox that it is linked to expires in less than 30d. If we want to recover such a task, it is possible that its user sandbox is no longer in s3 when we execute `crab recover`.

#### solutions

Can we improve the sandbox management so that it is compatible with our current design of `crab recover`, which require the user sandbox to be present in s3?

I think we have a couple of options:

- [x] if we limit ourselves at recovering a task before 30d from its initial submission, then we can simply take the sandbox from the schedd webdir. I have already implemented this fallback and it works fine.
- [ ] otherwise, before we upload the user sandbox, we check if it already exists explicitly. if it is bound to expire soon, than we remove it and upload it again.

Keep in mind the following s3 features (this are design choices, not limitations):

- you can not change an object metadata after it has been uploaded. this helps guarantee consistency.
- if you set an expiry date on a bucket, it uses the upload time to decide when an object is bound to be deleted
- upload time is part of object metadata and it can not be changed!
- Dario does not want to change the bucket lifetime rules just to keep a couple of sandboxes around for a little longer

## Comment (belforte, 2023-08-19T19:15:32Z)

I like
```
 before we upload the user sandbox, we check if it already exists explicitly. if it is bound to expire soon, than we remove it and upload it again.
```
Since it would make things work "as originally intendend". Also could be implemented in the server fully transparenlty to client.
But have no idea how much work it is. Let's keep for "when we have free time" :-)

## Comment (belforte, 2023-08-19T19:30:15Z)

anyhow if it is only a matter of adding a call to `S3.Client.get_object_retention` it may be very easy

## Comment (belforte, 2023-08-21T14:51:12Z)

it is actually a different API
```python
bucket='crabcache_dev'
key='belforte/230804_162428:belforte_crab_20230804_182420/twlog'
rr=s3_client.get_object(Key=key, Bucket=bucket)
expiration=rr['Expiration']
expireDay=exp.split("\"")[1]
print(expireDay)
```
output
```
Tue, 15 Aug 2023 00:00:00 GMT
```
which somehow makes no sense since Aug 15 is passed.
Anyhow file was  created on Aug 4 (like the task) and retention day for that bucket is 10days so ExpirationDay is OK. Maybe S3 is like Rucio and expired objects are not purged immediately.
We can also hardcode that we keep things for 90 days and simply check object creation date

```
bucket='crabcache_dev'
key='belforte/230804_162428:belforte_crab_20230804_182420/twlog'
rr=s3_client.get_object(Key=key, Bucket=bucket)
expiration=rr['Expiration']
expireDay=exp.split("\"")[1]
print(f"expires      : {expireDay}")
print(f"last Modified: {rr['LastModified']}")

expires      : Tue, 15 Aug 2023 00:00:00 GMT
last Modified: 2023-08-04 16:24:55+00:00

```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-23T10:58:53Z)

Let's simply change retention time to 3 months !

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-05-24T15:42:57Z)

I migrated the document by Prajesh to our mkdocs [1], added a short section on how to use the `aws` cli that feels more immediate to use than the boto3 python api, then extended the lifecycle to 3 months on `crabcache_prod` bucket [2].

I will close this issue, in the future we can come back to this with better ideas if it is not enough.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7845: Use tokens for crab for backend service-to-service communication

State: open
Opened: 2023-08-19T14:25:18Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High, Status: On Hold, Area: Needed Feature
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7845

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-08-19T14:25:18Z)

Currently, we use x509 certificates for communication between our services. We need to move to tokens.

An incomplete list of the requests that **should** be authenticated with a token instead of with a certificate is

- [ ] TW, Publisher to cmsweb (crabserver, dbs, ...)
- [ ] TW to schedd (job submission)
- [ ] TW to rucio (data discovery)
- [ ] schedd to rest (postjob, ...)
- [ ] schedd to fts
- [ ] schedd to rucio

An incomplete list of the requests that **may** be authenticated with a token instead of with a certificate is

- [ ] TW to myproxy

See the CRAB Overview [1] for ideas on what i may have missed in these lists :)

---

[1] https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CrabOverview

Likely for 2025, we'll define better when new DevOp is here

Here is [the commit](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/commit/9bbb6ab019a6891967933d97ffe48937fb2ce5e9) left by Dario about the token, also available on branch [crabdev_taskworker_token](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/commits/crabdev_schedd_tokens?ref_type=heads).
The [puppet env](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-environments/-/commit/2ecdb96c2430135e2c97f5b5a9ac9486b84eaad6) will be deleted soon because it no longer has the machine in that env, which is fine.

And for the record, here the explanation from Dario:
```
hello, yeah, my fault. that machine is running condor_schedd from cern repositories and condor_credmon_vault from the osg ones (this package is only distributed by osg repos), and there was a mismatch between the two that broke yum update/upgrade.
- either you as florian to help you find in the cern repositories a condor version that matches the one from osg
- or you install condor itself from osg in that machine
you can replicate the error running yum upgrade as root user in that schedd
```

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-09-24T13:26:06Z)

and do not forget that in order to use tokens on the schedd you also need to change the JDL for the jobs, as described [here](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-components/crab-schedd/schedd-tokens.html) :)

## Opening post (lenzip, 2023-09-01T07:38:58Z)

Its is my understanding from [this discussion](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/possible-duplication-when-using-automatic-splitting-for-crab/21384/25) and [this comment](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42323#issuecomment-1701200063) that crab already produces a json file with the lumis to process in each job (in addition to the CMSSW PSet), as part of the job preparation. I'd like to request that this is documented, so that tools running on nanoAOD via script, instead of CMSSW, can parse it.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-01T10:37:11Z)

@mapellidario can you take care as the current "job wrapper man in charge" ?

Ideally we could do a bit of preparatory work in PreDag and only ship to each job the info it needs, instead of the full list, getting rid of the concern which I debated with David Lange in that cms-talk discussion about size of the run_and_lumis.tar.gz.
Maybe at that point we can even decompress the json files in the grid working dir.

Anyhow a  first simple step could likely be to tweak https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/TweakPSet.py to produce a run/lumi json file in the standard "lumimask" format as per https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/WMCore/DataStructs/LumiList.py. You can surely find the best way ahead.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7863: improve reporting of WebDav failures
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7863: improve reporting of WebDav failures

State: closed
Opened: 2023-09-05T15:03:11Z
Closed: 2023-11-07T19:53:30Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7863

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-09-05T15:03:11Z)

when destination storage disk quota is full, we now get the very cryptic
```

       1 jobs failed with following error message: (for example, job 33)

            Got recoverable stageout exception:
            Stageout failed with code 1.
            There were 2 failed/killed stageout jobs.
            Failure reasons (per document) follow:
            - ff11f76e2e9c4e4995650140cd007241a928dfaacd12aa723d95b723:
              -----> ASO log start -----
              ['TRANSFER [5] TRANSFER ERROR: Copy failed (3rd pull [...CUT...] Full log at https://fts3-cms.cern.ch:8449/fts3/ftsmon/#/job/07771d46-4bd8-11ee-b329-fa163e1db714']
              <----- ASO log finish ----
              The last failure reason is recoverable.
            - c103599795542cbc94307f30d2782506873a71fbdeaa0a5323c5e96f:
              -----> ASO log start -----
              ['3rd push). Last attempt: Transfer failure: Remote side failed with status code 507 [...CUT...] Full log at https://fts3-cms.cern.ch:8449/fts3/ftsmon/#/job/07771d46-4bd8-11ee-b329-fa163e1db714']
              <----- ASO log finish ----
              The last failure reason is recoverable.
```

Note that now FTS query reports both the 3rd pull and 3rp push messages. As Mihai (FTS developer) already pointed out, it would be better if 3rd pull already reported 507 instead of `Copy failed with mode 3rd pull: copy HTTP 400 : Server Error ` (which is in FTSMON log but for some reason not in ASO report).

Now that we use WebDav,  status codes are HTTP ones and [HTTP 507](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/507) is "Insufficient Storage" and so this indicate full disk at destination. We should clearly report this to user with exit code `60323 - User quota exceeded. ` and add a line telling user to check their quota. Such errors are automatically retried, if users act quickly they can make next job submission successful.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-05T17:11:50Z)

I was trying to have a first look at where to change and found a bad bug.
All failed transfers in the task https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230905_015748%3Aciperez_crab_GluGluSpin0ToGammaGamma_W_5p6_M_750_TuneCP2 from where the above example was taken, ended from FTS site with the same reason, correctly fetched by FTS_Transfer.py as clear also in the script log
```
belforte@vocms0144/transfers> grep Failure transfer_inject.log |head -1
2023-09-05 07:29:45,648: Failure reason: TRANSFER [5] TRANSFER ERROR: Copy failed (3rd pull, 3rd push). Last attempt: Transfer failure: Remote side failed with status code 507
belforte@vocms0144/transfers>
```

But looking in transfersdb I see e.g this for the `root` file in one CRAB job
```
tm_transfer_failure_reason | 3rd push). Last attempt: Transfer failure: Remote side failed with status code 507
```
and this for the corresponding `log` file:
```
tm_transfer_failure_reason | TRANSFER [5] TRANSFER ERROR: Copy failed (3rd pull
```

I think that the problem is that the failure reasons for all files in the same FTS jobid are uploaded to REST in a single call with `subresource='updateTransfers'` as a list. This list is somehow transformed from `['r1','r2',...'rn']` to `r1,r2,...,rn` and then in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py#L170
it is fed to  WMCore's `makeList` which " Make a python list out of a comma separated list of strings" so  each failure reason ` Failure reason: TRANSFER [5] TRANSFER ERROR: Copy failed (3rd pull, 3rd push). Last attempt: Transfer failure: Remote side failed with status code 507` is broken into two parts at the middle `,`

A quick hack could be to remove any `,` from FTS messages.
Better yet to properly manipulate a list of strings all the way from client to Oracle.
Code involved from our side should be
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/ServerUtilities.py#L452
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py#L26
and of course the call to `makeList`

Maybe the error cure is simply to use `validate_strlist` in stead of `validate_string` in e.g.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py#L46
and do the same in the other cases where this has not hit us yet.. but better be prepared.
Hopefully `validate_strlist` will deal also with a single string.

This deserves an ad hoc issue. But fixing this will surely help to get correct failure reasons to parse in PostJob. WebDav errors are bad enough w/o this extra complexity !

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-05T17:31:31Z)

:-(
I had added `HTTP 507` already to the list of string-to-look-for-to-assing-stageout-error in
https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blame/de110ccf6fc63ef5589b4e871ef4d51d5bce7a25/src/python/WMCore/WMExceptions.py#L325-L327
in https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11328

But that does not capture `failed with status code 507` ...  I guess at that time I was looking at output of straight `gfal_copy` from local file to a WebDav server, in `crab checkwrite` context. 3rd party copy messages are ... different.

I'd hate to wait for a new WMCore release for this !
Am considering a temporary hack also in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/ServerUtilities.py#L354-L369

(but the danger is that we never clean this up)

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-05T17:39:54Z)

given that `STAGEOUT_ERROR` is not used anywhere in WMCore, but only in CRAB, maybe we should simply move
https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/de110ccf6fc63ef5589b4e871ef4d51d5bce7a25/src/python/WMCore/WMExceptions.py#L272
and following

into https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/ServerUtilities.py which is the only place where it is used !!!

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-07T17:29:32Z)

I have moved `STAGEOUT_ERROR` to our repo https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7995 and removed it from WMCore https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11787

Next PR will add the missing `failed with status code 507`

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-07T10:56:13Z)

hmm... not reallty. I tested code with pdb and
`params.kwargs['list_of_failure_reason']="['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']"` is turned by `validate_str` to
```
(Pdb) mys.kwargs
{'subresource': 'updateTransfers', 'list_of_failure_reason': "['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']"}
```
while `validate_strlist` yields
```
(Pdb) mys2.kwargs
{'subresource': 'updateTransfers', 'list_of_failure_reason': ["['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']"]}
```
Which is even worse to hanlde !
Now the problem is to turn  the string
```
"['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']"
```
into the python list `['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']` while `makelist` output is

Could this be a bug in `makelist` ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-07T11:15:49Z)

The problem seems to be that when `makelist` splits its argument at each `,` it handles quotes as string characters, does not read `'r1,r2'` as a substring to be kept separated, indeed it strips away all `'` and `"` chars.

The fact is that due to the way our API's are constructed (?) we are simply dealing with the  "stream to string" representation of a python list and a crude `eval` would do !
```
# reasons w/o commas
(Pdb) safe.kwargs['list_of_failure_reason']
"['r1 R1', 'r2 R2', 'r3 R3']"
(Pdb) eval(safe.kwargs['list_of_failure_reason'])
['r1 R1', 'r2 R2', 'r3 R3']

# reasons with commas
(Pdb) mys.kwargs['list_of_failure_reason']
"['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']"
(Pdb) eval(mys.kwargs['list_of_failure_reason'])
['r1, R1', 'r2, R2', 'r3, R3']
(Pdb)
```

Maybe a side effect of not using a well defined format for passing args, like e.g. JSON. We handle everything as a single string and this has "limits".

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-07T11:34:30Z)

At this point I am reluctant to change https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py introducing calls to `eval`, in a way it should be done everywhere, not just for `list_of_failure_reason`.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-11-07T15:20:41Z)

Hi @belforte, sorry for joining late.

Are we supposed to use `encodeRequest(data, listParams=['list_of_ids', 'list_of_failure_reason', 'list_of_...'])` on client side and `validate_strlist()` on server side?
Is there any reason why we stick with the current code and do `makeList()` on server side later?

There's a lot of confusion and inconsistency in how thow calls have been coded and used around. In a way, if we go down the path which you indicate, we should get rid of that `makeList`  everywhere in RESTFileTrasnfers.py and use `encodeRequest(data, listParams=)` instead in  FTS_Transfers.py . In the end the answer to "Is there any reason why" is two-fold:
1. fear
2. lazyness

When an exception occurs at `add_replicas()`, the code always exits and cannot continue processing other files.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e7c14e3115c53c5542bb0884d618a45397f5886c/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py#L157-L168

This task has an error the first time it runs, making all other transfers stuck forever (and fail eventually).
https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/230906_020712:tseethon_crab_rucio_transfers_usertask_test12_20230906_040707/SPOOL_DIR/task_process/transfer_rucio.log

The code needs to handle this error, skip problematic files, and continue processing others.
Otherwise, it wastes resources; recovery task need to compute every job again.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-06T11:25:19Z)

This is a site configuration problem.
We may also terminate the task here and bump the problem to CMS-Rucio/Site admins to fix.
The important thing is to have a very visible alarm.
I presume that by the time this goes into production all temp T'2s, including `rse=T2_UK_London_Brunel` (if I parsed correctly the log) will be in good shape. But we can expect some site to change things and break later on.
Best would be to have a continuous test of Temp RSE's.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-06T13:10:55Z)

Yes, this is configuration problem.
But the part that our service cannot continue to work still bother me, and this issue happen more often than I thought.
I will keep looking for solutions and keep changes to a minimum.

>  Best would be to have a continuous test of Temp RSE's.

I agree. I would kindly ask DM team to do that.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-06T13:15:49Z)

I fear that we will have to use our jobs as testing. DM team people have their hands very full.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7874: puppet - logrotate config should be 0644
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7874: puppet - logrotate config should be 0644

State: closed
Opened: 2023-09-14T08:48:07Z
Closed: 2024-09-18T14:42:12Z
Labels: OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7874

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-09-14T08:48:07Z)

#### problem

While managing the cronjob for spark, i noticed that `logrotate` ignores some of the config that we setup in puppet because we set the config files to have `mode = 0755`, while lograte requires it to be `mode = 0644` [1]. This affects both taskworker and schedd machines.

This is inconvenient, but can also be a problem. For example, on vocms059 the file `/var/log/crab/JobAutoTuner.log` is 130MB, starting from 202-07-26.

<details>

```plaintext
[root@vocms059 dmapelli]# ls -lh /var/log/crab/
total 134M
-rw-r--r--. 1 root   root   257K Sep 10 00:00 cleanup_home_grid.log
-rw-r--r--. 1 condor condor 131M Sep 14 10:34 JobAutoTuner.log
-rw-r--r--. 1 root   root   2.4M Sep 14 06:10 JobCleanup.log
[root@vocms059 dmapelli]# head /var/log/crab/JobAutoTuner.log
2020-07-26 11:26:58,250:INFO:JobAutoTuner,44:=========================================================================
2020-07-26 11:26:58,251:INFO:JobAutoTuner,57:-------------------- JobTimeTuner.py was not enabled --------------------
2020-07-26 11:26:58,251:INFO:JobAutoTuner,71:-------------------- CMSLPCRoute.py was not enabled  --------------------
2020-07-26 11:26:58,251:INFO:JobAutoTuner,76:-------------------- Routes added by Overflow.py  --------------------
2020-07-26 11:26:58,251:INFO:Overflow,1003:=================== An Overflow object instance start! ===================
2020-07-26 11:26:58,252:WARNING:Overflow,937:Config key: JAT_OVERFLOW_serviceKey not set in condor using the default value.
2020-07-26 11:26:58,252:WARNING:Overflow,937:Config key: JAT_OVERFLOW_serviceCert not set in condor using the default value.
2020-07-26 11:26:58,252:WARNING:Overflow,937:Config key: JAT_OVERFLOW_level not set in condor using the default value.
2020-07-26 11:26:58,266:WARNING:Overflow,937:Config key: JAT_OVERFLOW_collector not set in condor using the default value.
2020-07-26 11:27:00,305:INFO:JobAutoTuner,88:=========================================================================
[root@vocms059 dmapelli]# tail /var/log/crab/JobAutoTuner.log
  File "/data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/JobAutoTuner.py", line 79, in main
    overflow.run()
  File "/data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/Overflow/Overflow.py", line 1190, in run
    self.overflow(jobsInThisSchedd, self.config.ovLevel, self.config.ovType)
  File "/data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/Overflow/Overflow.py", line 1122, in overflow
    if self.estimator.needOverflow(jobObj):
  File "/data/srv/SubmissionInfrastructureScripts/Overflow/Overflow.py", line 508, in needOverflow
    currIdleTime = jobObject["ServerTime"] - jobObject["QDate"]
KeyError: 'ServerTime'
2023-09-14 10:34:04,385:INFO:JobAutoTuner,88:=========================================================================
```

</details>

#### solution

We need to change the mode for logrotate config file from 0755 to 0644, for example here:

https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/fa42ad9d8145566ca8330f7b19e7ea4d6352fa6f/code/manifests/crabschedd.pp#L195

---

[1]

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7881: CVMFS failed to mount in TW machine
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7881: CVMFS failed to mount in TW machine

State: closed
Opened: 2023-09-15T11:35:06Z
Closed: 2024-02-07T10:39:02Z
Labels: OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7881

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-09-15T11:35:06Z)

Sometimes, when we deploy TaskWorker we get this error:
```
docker: Error response from daemon: error while creating mount source path '/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF': mkdir /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch: permission denied.
```
This error is due to `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch` disappearing, and it does not automatically remount when needed.
Manually triggering remount (via `cvmfs_config probe`) does not work either.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-15T11:38:39Z)

Workaround is to force restart manually by:

```
# run as root
cvmfs_config killall
sleep 60 # or wait a bit
cvmfs_config reload
cvmfs_config probe
```

Dario and I "heard" that autofs is the root cause.

Andrea's suggestion is to just get rid of autofs and manually manage umounts and mounts by

```
# Umount with

cvmfs_config umount

# then mount with

mount -t cvmfs cms.cern.ch /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch
mount -t cvmfs unpacked.cern.ch /cvmfs/unpacked.cern.ch
```

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-18T11:35:15Z)

Fortunately, there is `mount_option => 'mount'`  in [CERN IT cvmfs's puppet module](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-module-cvmfs/-/blob/ba8b79ae36d49d197557d2591e9b406985d577eb/code/manifests/init.pp#L30), which puts mount entries to `/etc/fstab` and it will mount automatically after reboot.

I have applied changes to `crab-dev-tw03` and it works perfectly. See diff: https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/compare/a425fd4461e7aeb556ec502fff80736db3541afb...crabdev_taskworker?from_project_id=4758&straight=false
The changes in bump latest cvmfs to 2.11 (from 2.5) and install fuse3 built.

Note that converting from autofs to mount with fstab needs some manual intervention steps:
- Unlink `/etc/auto.cvmfs`
- Remove `/cvmfs program:/etc/auto.cvmfs` line from /etc/auto.master
- Reboot, make sure there is no autofs entries in  /proc/mounts (`grep autofs /proc/mounts | grep cvmfs` should not return anything).

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-07T10:39:02Z)

@novicecpp tried but experience is that forcing mount at VM start time leads to more error than current setup.
So we keep it as it and have a recipe for recovering https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7881#issuecomment-1721132428

```
== CMSSW: File: ///mnt/hadoop/cms/store/mc/HC/GenericTTbar/AODSIM/CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/00000/0A11E55B-0876-E711-9647-FA163EB8F562.root at byte:153972288, branch:HcalNoiseSummary_hcalnoise__RECO.present, entry:1485, badread=1, nerrors=1, basketnumber=9
== CMSSW:
== CMSSW: ----- End Fatal Exception -------------------------------------------------
```

All of them went away in following, automatic, job resubmissions.
Only [one job](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0155/sciaba/231018_120358:sciaba_crab_HC-205-T2_US_MIT-105024-20231018140301/job_out.56.2.txt)  kept failing 3 times, but direct inspection (rucio get plus gfal-sum) adler32 checksum is fine.

We already knew that MIT is not top-of-the-class as robustness, but other than that... have not learn anything yet.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-31T14:22:39Z)

Still the only corruption reports are the read errors at MIT `badread=1, nerrors=1, basketnumber=...` also one case with `badread=0, nerrors=1..`
and the only suspicion are again at MIT with the very cryptic
```
    "== CMSSW:       [a] Fatal Root Error: @SUB=TBasket::ReadBasketBuffers",
    "== CMSSW: fNbytes = 581760, fKeylen = 119, fObjlen = 600644, noutot = 0, nout=0, nin=581641, nbuf=600644",
```

I will
- [ ] change the "detection" code to move the former from `corrupted` to `suspicious`.
- [ ] review the conditions under which I now set exit code to 8022

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-07T21:11:15Z)

More than a month into this. Only recorded problems are form HammerCloud transient read errors (usually fixed in next automatic retry). All such errors have exit code 8021 (means file open is OK and there was a read error).
Plain corruption like truncated file onlly happened in my test and has exit code 8020 (error in open).

I think I have spent too much time on this already.
Will try to keep checking summaries once a month, but that's all.
I have added this to my acrontab
```
`# every week make a summary of CRAB corrupted file reports
30 05 */7 * * lxplus8.cern.ch /afs/cern.ch/user/b/belforte/utils/MakeCorruptedFileReportsSummary.sh
```
that script `MakeCorruptedFileReportsSummary.sh` is:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
mkdir -p /tmp/belforte
cd /tmp/belforte
rm -rf ProcessBadFilesList.py
wget -q https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/raw/master/scripts/Utils/ProcessBadFilesList.py
python3 ProcessBadFilesList.py > /dev/null
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-13T09:46:09Z)

**DAMN** I was fooled by the fact that HC jobs could write reports, but directory tree `/eos/cms/temp/user/BadInputFiles` lacked the needed permission for users to write. I guess Sciaba identity has special privileges on EOS.
I had tested that user jobs could write initially, but forgot about the needed config. when moving to a better-named directory.

I have now done `chmod g+w -R` and `chmod o+w -R` and tested again with a user job.
Need to reset the "wait and see".

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-13T11:14:40Z)

corrupted file reports are now coming in like rain... oh well.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-17T16:06:07Z)

I have now setup automatic daily reporting of bad input files, check of disk replicas size and Adler, and suggestion of which replica can be marked as BAD after making sure that there is a tape replica and handed this over to CMSRucio and CMS DM folks.
References:
https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSTRANSF-766
https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/issues/403

Daily reports are available at links in https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/CsnjLe6Mk/crab-overview?orgId=11&refresh=1h&from=1700063958182&to=1700236758182&viewPanel=116

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7894: Service certificate needed to authenticate against Rucio
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7894: Service certificate needed to authenticate against Rucio

State: closed
Opened: 2023-09-28T19:45:40Z
Closed: 2023-10-19T15:09:41Z
Labels: Priority: Critical
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7894

## Opening post (ericvaandering, 2023-09-28T19:45:40Z)

I now believe that the issue we experienced with Rucio on Sep 27/28 is that Apache on Alma9 (and/or its version of OpenSSL) is unwilling to accept host certificate as a client certificate. As far as I can tell, the two certs which have problems are host certs and all the certs which don't have problems are user or service account user certificates.

Alan is going to verify this with a new robot certificate he's obtained. If true, CRAB will need to do the same so that we are not held back from upgrading Rucio.

I have looked if there is a way to change this behavior on the Rucio side and have found nothing.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-28T20:28:50Z)

Dario, Wa, can you kindly follow up ? Thanks

Eric, our DN is
/DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=computers/CN=tw/crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch
note `CN=tw` which makes it a service certificate, not a host one.  Isn't that enough ?
Does Rucio/Alma want the "Robot" string in the DN ?

## Comment (ericvaandering, 2023-09-28T20:36:04Z)

Every one that fails has OU=computers. Every one that succeeds has OU=Users.

I tried explicitly today with your certificate and the Rucio robot certificate and removing all rucio tokens between attempts.

Both are fine with Rucio 1.31 (Centos 7). Rucio works OK on Rucio 32 (Alma 9), CRAB does not.

One of the Rucio guys told me to check to make sure your certificate was not 1024 bits. It's not, it's 4096 while mine is only 2048.

So I posit that there is *something* that the Apache/OpenSSL server does not like about OU=computers certificates and how they are generated or signed.

I have added a crab_input user to Rucio integration and we can test there before going back to the latest production.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-28T20:44:02Z)

Got it/ I see that Alan got
```
subject= /DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=Organic Units/OU=Users/CN=cmst1/CN=718748/CN=Robot: cms t1
```
so we need the same. @mapellidario @novicecpp you can check with him or Panos on how to get one for CRAB.
We also need to figure out if we want to use the same on all machines or have a few prod/preprod/test ones.

## Comment (ericvaandering, 2023-09-28T20:58:18Z)

Once you have them, please let me know the DNs and which accounts they belong to. We'll start with integration, as I said.

Thanks for your cooperation!

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-28T21:23:05Z)

Dario and I will take care tomorrow.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-09-29T14:27:07Z)

We have a robot certificate for our crab's service account `cmscrab`. I added the `.p12` file in the crab secrets repository together with the pwd to open it, then extracted it to cert+key in `crab-preprod-tw01`.

```plaintext
[crab3@crab-preprod-tw01 ~]$ export X509_USER_CERT=~/.globus/robocert.pem
[crab3@crab-preprod-tw01 ~]$ export X509_USER_KEY=~/.globus/robokey.pem
[crab3@crab-preprod-tw01 ~]$ openssl x509  -subject -dates -noout  -in $X509_USER_CERT
subject= /DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=Organic Units/OU=Users/CN=cmscrab/CN=817881/CN=Robot: cms crab
notBefore=Sep 29 13:49:29 2023 GMT
notAfter=Nov  2 13:49:29 2024 GMT
```

However I am not sure what needs to be done now. How shall we properly map it to the service account in voms, cric and then rucio?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-30T11:09:27Z)

Mapping in RUcio rests with Rahul and/or Eric
I have now added it to VOMS to facilitate import in CRIC if/as needed. But am not sure whether Rucio requires that.
As long as we only plan to use this for Rucio, I guess we wait for more instructions from Eric

## Comment (ericvaandering, 2023-10-02T08:02:00Z)

Since it's been tested, I guess the next step is I add the DN to the production and you can switch at your leisure. Then, at some later point I can restore the auth server to the latest version and you will not notice. I've added the DN to all 4 CRAB accounts in production Rucio.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-02T09:46:31Z)

I am not sure that CRAB Robot cert. was tested with latest Rucio version on ITB.
Is e.g.  preprod running that way ? @mapellidario @novicecpp even if you wrote things in MatterMost, can you add a couple lines here ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-02T09:50:24Z)

>  4 CRAB accounts in production Rucio.

Interesting ! I am aware of `crab_server`, `crab_tape_recall` and `crab_input`,what's the 4th one ? @ericvaandering

## Comment (ericvaandering, 2023-10-02T10:01:54Z)

`crab_test_group`

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-10-02T10:33:24Z)

Thanks Eric.
If we are not in hurry, I will switch CRAB Taskworker to use Robot cert next week.

## Comment (ericvaandering, 2023-10-02T11:13:44Z)

I'd really prefer to resolve this during this week if we can. What's the reason for picking next week?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-10-02T18:24:41Z)

Because we have O&C week, I usually avoid touching production when I do not have full time focus on it.
But sure, we can do it this week.

```
crab3       14  0.1  0.2 426712 36296 pts/0    Sl+  19:51   0:04 python3 /data/srv/TaskManager/v3.230921-839a45450c3aae116b7f80aa57567361/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.230921-839a45450c3aae116b7f80aa57567361/lib/python3.8/site-packages/TaskWorker//MasterWorker.py --config /data/srv/TaskManager/current/TaskWorkerConfig.py --logDebug
```

Maybe I am simply confused ?

thanks for reassuring me

I added the certificate to crab_test_group. I issued the command before, so I'm not sure why it wasn't there. Now I issued the command AND checked the results!

@ericvaandering CRAB TaskWorker is now running with the robot cert. and the fix for automatic splitting. We are ready for you to switch production Rucio server to new version at your convenience.

see e.g.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7895#issuecomment-1750322572

```
'231006_093458:cmsbot_crab_20231006_113457', 'combinedStatus': 'FAILED',
```
but the test is classifies as "TestPassed"
```
{'dbStatus': u'SUBMITTED', 'testResult': 'TestPassed', 'jobsPerStatus': {'finished': 5}, 'TN': '231006_093458:cmsbot_crab_20231006_113457', 'combinedStatus': 'FAILED', 'publication (fail/tdb/DBS)': '0/0/0'}
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-06T16:25:12Z)

that was an automatic splitting task. Ultimate cause is that things failed early in the PreDag phase so no job was submitted but the probe jobs. In this case the current https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py finds that all jobs succeeded and declares "test passed".
This makes impossible to detect failures in PreDag like we had today due to Rucio cert https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7897

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-06T16:42:35Z)

Current test will also show a fake "passed" if dagman is not started for whatever reason

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-06T19:28:50Z)

I have added the check on schedule status, but the question is what to do when task fails to submit any (non-probe) jobs.
For generality I am falling back to resubmission.
In case of persistent problem (but in new code e.g.), the test will stay in `'testResult': 'TestResubmitted',` until all retries are consumed.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7932: report to Monit list of root branches read by users
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7932: report to Monit list of root branches read by users

State: closed
Opened: 2023-10-11T16:05:59Z
Closed: 2024-02-03T18:21:39Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High, Area: MONIT
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7932

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-11T16:05:59Z)

@nsmith- expressed interest in looking at which AOD branches are read by users of AOD in CRAB.
Generally speaking adding this information to CRAB seems a good idea.
So @mapellidario and myself looked at how to implement.

**Current status**

Currently CRAB gets  back from the worker node a shortened version of `FrameworkJobReport.xml` in json format `fjr.json` which is produced by [WMCore's FwkJobReport/Report/parse](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/56143c9011322f65159c9d904256a30cdaeed68b/src/python/WMCore/FwkJobReport/Report.py#L136)

There is no branch information in that file.

The original  `FrameworkJobReport.xml` instead has lines like
```
<ReadBranches>
<Branch Name="recoTracks_globalMuons__RECO." ReadCount="600"/>
</ReadBranches>
```

**Proposal**
changing WMCore would take long time and we will be left anyhow with extracting info from `fjr.json` in the PostJob and sending it to Monit somehow.
We rather would like to
1. we modity CRAB JobWrapper so that it
 * parses `fjr.xml` e.g. via python3 built-in parser
 * extract a "string" with the list of branches as comma-separated (blank separated ?) words
 * chirps this to HTCondor as a classAd
   * `CRAB_ReadBranches="B1,B2,B3....,Bn"
2. @nikodemas should then modify https://github.com/dmwm/cms-htcondor-es/blob/master/src/htcondor_es/convert_to_json.py to catch this Ad for completed jobs and add it to what is sent to MONIT so that it is available in ES and HDFS.
   * IIUC info will stay in ES for 30days and HDFS for 1y. If  we need it for longer some kind of aggregation has to be devised.

@nsmith- Will this do ? Is it OK to ignore ReadCount ? Can you parse that multi-word string ?

## Comment (nikodemas, 2023-10-12T07:32:27Z)

Hi @belforte,

I think we save completed jobs only in OpenSearch (in [es-cms.cern.ch](https://es-cms.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover?security_tenant=global#/?_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-15m,to:now))&_a=(columns:!(_source),filters:!(),index:'0f3117a0-d2e6-11ed-bdae-e3cf8c07f2fc',interval:auto,query:(language:lucene,query:''),sort:!()))) and to include a new field in there no change of code is needed. We also save all jobs in [monit-opensearch.cern.ch](https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover?security_tenant=global#/?_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-15m,to:now))&_a=(columns:!(_source),filters:!(),index:dd1ba850-d169-11ea-966a-e1c0a7950cea,interval:auto,query:(language:lucene,query:''),sort:!())) for 40 days and HDFS for 3 years (might be reduced to 18 months in the near future) and for this we would need to modify the script you referenced (https://github.com/dmwm/cms-htcondor-es/blob/master/src/htcondor_es/convert_to_json.py#L441-L540).

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-12T07:41:51Z)

thanks @nikodemas . I find it a bit odd that we keep completed jobs info only for 30 days and running (not complete yet) info for 3 years. That means job info dump every 15min.. should not be  a big effort to keep one extra entry per job when job terminates ! Anyhow we need to hear from @nsmith- about the proposed format before we finalize implementation. I am not familiar with HDFS searches.

## Comment (nikodemas, 2023-10-12T07:51:54Z)

Oh I forgot to mention that completed jobs are kept for 18 months in [es-cms.cern.ch](https://es-cms.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover?security_tenant=global#/?_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:now-15m,to:now))&_a=(columns:!(_source),filters:!(),index:'0f3117a0-d2e6-11ed-bdae-e3cf8c07f2fc',interval:auto,query:(language:lucene,query:''),sort:!())).

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-12T08:05:06Z)

nice, thanks. I still fail to see the rational for an incomplete picture in HDFS, but hopefully it was a conscious decision with strong arguments behind. I am also curious if there's anything which looks at classAd history overy time for a a job which ran 1 year ago !

## Comment (nsmith-, 2023-10-12T22:13:56Z)

String parsing by splitting according to a special character in PySpark [is possible](https://spark.apache.org/docs/3.1.2/api/python/reference/api/pyspark.sql.functions.split.html). I would find a list of strings a bit easier to use, though I suppose that requires more work to implement. Comma should be a safe character, but ROOT does seem to allow branch names with a comma. I do not know if CMSSW does. I'm asking Matti now.

As for read count, in principle even if one entry is accessed we would expect to need the whole branch available, so I think it is safe to ignore ReadCount, other than whether or not it is greater than 0 of course.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T08:13:19Z)

List of strings should be fine.
Looking e.g. at https://es-cms.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover?security_tenant=global#/doc/0f3117a0-d2e6-11ed-bdae-e3cf8c07f2fc/cms-2023-10-13?id=<email>%2398651751.0%231697182894%231697183344
we have this field in the JSON. If this format is ok we can surely format the list of branches in the same way.

 "CRAB_SiteWhitelist": "['T2_CH_CERN_P5', 'T2_UK_London_Brunel', 'T2_US_Florida', 'T2_ES_IFCA', 'T2_US_Nebraska', 'T2_US_Vanderbilt', 'T2_US_Wisconsin', 'T2_US_Purdue', 'T2_CH_CSCS', 'T2_ES_CIEMAT', 'T2_IT_Pisa', 'T2_CH_CERN_HLT', 'T2_CH_CERN', 'T2_DE_DESY', 'T2_IT_Legnaro', 'T2_US_Caltech', 'T2_US_UCSD', 'T2_UK_London_IC', 'T2_UK_SGrid_RALPP', 'T2_IT_Bari', 'T2_IT_Rome', 'T2_UK_SGrid_Bristol', 'T2_DE_RWTH']"

I hope it is same format in pyspark (i.e. spark sees the full JSON doc).

So we skip branches with ReadCount=0, if any, correct ?
I guess we should run a test and if it all looks ok, push to production.
Nick, I think we can report for all tasks, you can always use CMSPrimaryDataTier to fillter AODs

## Comment (nsmith-, 2023-10-17T22:34:08Z)

Yes, I can easily read lists of strings in spark, just confirmed!

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-18T07:12:06Z)

thanks, onward we go.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-09T20:54:35Z)

time to takle this. @nsmith- do you have by any chance a PSet (and AOD dataset) at hand that I can use to produce a FJR.XML with the desired info and use it as test setup for dev and test ? The PSets which we use for CRAB validation all drop everything to be quick and simple.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-12T13:54:14Z)

@nikodemas @nsmith-
longish story short. I have tested the plan as in the top comment,
but it [turns out](https://lists.cs.wisc.edu/archive/htcondor-users/2023-November/msg00053.shtml) that `condor_chirp` only accepts 1024 chars attributes.

Pretty useless given the huge list of branches.
I can easily bring a file with the list back to the scheduler, or add to existing `fjr.json` which will eventually be sent to WMArchive. WMArchive info is eventually on HDFS, I think (@nikodemas )
1. I do not know if WMArchive needs a given format, ignores extra fields
2. Any other way be which I can make those `fjr.json` available ?
3. @nsmith- the list of branches in my simple test has 517 branches and is 30K long (!). Do you want that ? Or could it be somehow shorteneed e.g. listing only the first string before `_` in the list (135 elements, 3K) or the first 2 (to disambiguate things like `double` or `fload`) (359 entries, 18K)

Nick, how should we look at this ? It is just a "once" things to get a sense of things so we go for a quick hack ? Or should it become something which we do for good, so become part of the stable infrastructure and needs a "proejct" ? Maybe a small one, but still somehitng were multiple groups are involved, agreements has to be obtained, implemented with all proper documentation etc. Not a big deal.. but not a one afternoon thing either. Who will look at that information ? Do we need to worry avoid visualization as well ? WMArchive so far is mainly used by P&R to follow workflows progress, and I do not know how they access it.

## Comment (nsmith-, 2023-11-12T22:45:33Z)

Honestly, I think the extent to which it has long-term value depends on what we see the first time we look. If it turns out everyone reads every branch, then there is not much point. But if the hit rate (number of branches accessed vs. total number in file) is low universally, and different datasets have different hit rates, then we have something actionable and worth keeping long-term stats for.
In terms of splitting by `_`, generally all 4 fields are important, so I'm reluctant to try some data reduction scheme.
Perhaps it's worth a short meeting to discuss options?

## Comment (nikodemas, 2023-11-13T09:35:43Z)

> WMArchive info is eventually on HDFS, I think

Yes, it is under `/project/monitoring/archive/wmarchive/raw/metric/`

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-13T10:11:08Z)

Thanks @nikodemas .If I wanted to test, since I am not good with HDFS, is there an OpenSearch index which I can use ?
@nsmith- let's explore the WMArchive path then. I am not sure if a meeting would help, whom should be present  ? I suspect that the easiest is to try, and in case, ask Valentin, who will say that he's no allowed to work on it anymore, but may still answer.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-13T17:01:16Z)

nope.
the WMA document looks extremely "terse" when compard to FJR https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover#/doc/60770470-8326-11ea-88fc-cfaa9841e350/monit_prod_wmarchive_raw_metric-2023-11-13?id=1c80c2dc54e545d7bec3fbf649deaf7e

and when I select WMA from a CRAB task I do not even have ways to select on input data or username (which would be needed for testing) https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover#/doc/60770470-8326-11ea-88fc-cfaa9841e350/monit_prod_wmarchive_raw_metric-2023-11-13?id=19f12f4bfb794264a63ff05ac306aa5d

Looks like only a very small subset of the info is stored in WMArchive. I guess we should check with WMCore people,  I really do not know anything about this, and am a bit surprised that this info can be used for practical purposes.

I have added the ReadBranches list to the WMAFrameworkReport.json which is uploaded and got no error. But since I can't find my one entry in the ziliions of entries....But I very much doubt that the info was stored :-(

We could setup some independent CRAB-to-HDFS channel, but that's quite some work. Maybe piggy back on what was done last summer by Dario, Wa and Ek-ong ? I do not know details @nikodemas what do you think ?

Ideally this information should be available together with other job related info in `monit_condor_prod_raw_metric_*` index, where we tried to put it initially by disguising it an HTCondor classAd. So one can correlated with input data, used time, number of jobs etc.
But atm the only viable solution seems to me that we put it somewhere (EOS ?) where the spider can fetch it and push it to the MONIT pipeline, which looks very ugly to say the least.

I am our of ideas, maybe a use case to bump up to CERN MONIT team ? Can they aggregate data streams ?

During the summer's work CMS Monitoring only helped CRAB to get the full Oracle table dumps into the HDFS, so I am not sure if that helps here. The data injection to OpenSearch was done by your team.

I can discuss this with @leggerf and @brij01 (also adding them to the discussion in case they have some immediate suggestions) and maybe ask MONIT for their advice if that is needed.

thanks @nikodemas, yes the Summar work was about getting info from an Oracle table into MONIT, so I agree it does not apply. The problem here is that "a largish list from every job" is a lot of data in the end, and even to get a sense of things as @nsmith- indicated, we need something like a month of data to figure out patterns. This is a never-looked-at-before topic AFAIK so we have no previous wisdom to guide us.
How to get that non-trivial amount of data in HDFS is something I really do not know how to do, simple as that !

Thanks for followin up

## Comment (nsmith-, 2023-11-14T16:57:52Z)

One thing worth mentioning is that, although the list of branch names is long (up to 500 for AOD) and each name is long (ending up with 30kB figure as @belforte mentioned above), the number of unique branch names across all jobs is very small, not much more than the number per job. So it will compress extremely well, FWIW.
As a hacky solution to start understanding the problem, if we can find a way to send this list from the CRAB production server to a message queue, I can deal with reading messages and storing the results somewhere. Of course, if we can get it into HDFS without much pain, all the better.

## Comment (leggerf, 2023-11-14T17:26:50Z)

sorry this is a long thread so I might be missing details. A few comments:
- we can for sure setup another flow to write this data to HDFS which can be used later in spark jobs to aggregate with condor data, but why can't this info be condensed in a Condor ClassAd? There is no way to do it? This would be the best solution
- we cannot "enrich" the data in the spider, because the spider needs to run in 12 minutes and we cannot add the overhead of reading from EOS
- OTOH MONIT does run some "enrichment" jobs for other data flows, for example FTS data. We can ask what their requirements are for that

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-14T17:38:22Z)

Thanks @leggerf ,  I think you got it !
* the list of ReadBranches is too long to fit in a ClassAd
* I understand the difficulty of adding another data source to the spider !
* if we can aggregate on HDFS side, useful keys would be "taskName" and "jobId" (yeah I will look up exact name and format in `condor_raw_data` and replicate). I would limit this to successful jobs so we do not worry about retry count

maybe @Panos512 ,  who the other day setup a rucio-to-ES pipeline in a few minutes, can also help with ideas ?

Anyhow, @leggerf you are going to follow up with CERN MONIT, right ? If we can have a proper solution via HDFS and avoid the above, things will be much more clear.

## Comment (nikodemas, 2023-12-06T16:35:34Z)

Hi, just to have the progress documented - there is a SNOW ticket `RQF2479427` for CERN MONIT regarding this.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-06T16:48:47Z)

thanks @nikodemas , please note that the SNOW ticket is now in status "waiting for user", they asked you to fill-in some info. Since you were at the meeting (and we were not) I would not know how to jump in and do it for you.

@nsmith- what do you think about getting a list of branches so that  we can fill a bit-mask with Y/N ? Is that list "existing" ? Or do we have to read one file from every possible dataset to find out ? For a first test we do not need a complete list, but something like "in half of the jobs half of the read branches are in the list", then we report "number of read branches not in our list". ## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-22T14:02:26Z)

The new wrapper
* adds the list of read branches to `job_fjr.1.0.json` which is returned to the scheduler as `fjr['steps','cmsRun','ReadBranches']`
* reports the number of read branches as classAd `Chirp_CRAB3_BranchNumber`
* compares the list or read branches with a reference kept in https://belforte.web.cern.ch/belforte/Branches

```python
"""

run:

> export CRABTEST_OPENSEARCH_SECRET='XXXXX'
> python3 send-branches.py

result:

- single document: https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover#/doc/3829fac0-bc68-11ee-b776-cb346cc4cf26/monit_prod_crab-test_raw_branches-2024-01?id=db01c4ab-f1c3-79b6-74e4-b98232bf0aa1
- multiple documents: https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/goto/a8e5474ea4daa93df5908bb595316639
"""

import requests
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth
import os
import json

USER = "crab-test"
PWD = os.getenv("CRABTEST_OPENSEARCH_SECRET", "empty pwd")

def send_opensearch(document):
    r = requests.post(f'https://monit-metrics.cern.ch:10014/{USER}',
                        auth=HTTPBasicAuth(USER, PWD),
                         data=json.dumps(document),
                         headers={"Content-Type": "application/json; charset=UTF-8"},
                         verify=False
                         )
    print(r.status_code, r.text)

def create_document(branches):
    doc = { "producer": USER,
            "type": "branches",
            "branches": branches,  # a list of strings
            }
    return doc

def main():
    doc = create_document(read_branches())
    send_opensearch(doc)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-11T16:27:17Z)

see below for details. There are two things here
- [x] make `crab checkwrite` in Jenkins work (now fails on Jenkins side)
- [x] make the test report failure when it does not (in case problem is in CRABClient) - moved to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5223

@mapellidario and myself found that in Jenkins ClientValidation was only executing the minimal `submit` and `status` tests when running on CC8. That was meant to be only for SL6. So we modified [CRABServer_ClientValidation](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/view/CRAB/job/CRABServer_ClientValidation/) to execute full test suite on CC8 as well.

But when submitted I found that `chekwrite` test fails with a problem in contacting Rucio [1] and, worst, the test is still declared successful.
I need working client tests in order to validate changes that I am doing to CRABClient to import Rucio client API. So need to fix this a first priority.

Fixing the test to report error may be "as simple as modify CRABClient to exit with an exception in this case".
Fixing the problem looks hard because:
 - if I run this in `cmssw-cc8` singularity container myself, it works
 - the robot certificate is known to Rucio, since this test works for SL7
 - it is the same error which I got inside Jenkins with even simpler tests when trying to test new client which has `from rucio.Client import client; rucio=Client()`
 - in current (even dev) CRABClient the call to Rucio is executed in a subprocess after a `scram unsetenv`

I wrote a very simple Rucio testing script [1]  , and it runs happily on both cmssw-cc7 and cmssw-el8 singularity containers. But I had to make sure `RUCIO_ACCOUNT=cmsbot` while the test runs as user `cmsbld`. echo ""

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7944: Publisher monitoring - acquired files by task panel is empty
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7944: Publisher monitoring - acquired files by task panel is empty

State: closed
Opened: 2023-10-13T09:26:10Z
Closed: 2023-10-13T20:57:09Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done, Area: MONIT, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7944

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-10-13T09:26:10Z)

### problem

While investigating the recent alerts from Publisher,
I noticed that something is wrong with publisher monitoring
in "Taskworker Internals" dashboard.
In particular, the panel "acquired files by task" is empty
since 2023-09-14 from about 10am, when Wa deployed v3.230913.

And it makes sense that it is empty, we populate that
panel parsing [3] this logger.debug [4], but the Publisher
loglevel is set to info [5].

Does anybody know how this could work before? Sorry if I have only questions so far :)

### solution

If we rely on a line on our logs for our monitoring, that line should at least be of loglevel `info`. I propose to change [4] to `.info()`

---

[1] https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/pGEgCEMSR?orgId=11

![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/16376695/04c4a129-d268-498c-835e-6f4032e3df7e)

[2] https://cms-logbook.cern.ch/elog/Analysis+Operations/3838
[3] [(grok)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/50a9f8aa9d8ae6f55034cc62e3b6a27870b2c522/src/script/Monitor/logstash/crabtaskworker.conf#L105)
[4] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blame/50a9f8aa9d8ae6f55034cc62e3b6a27870b2c522/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L448
[5] https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/5b5bc1eb01d01a7858c7980a32d982876505897e/code/templates/crabtaskworker/publisher/Publisher_scheddConfig.py.erb#L38

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T09:29:56Z)

was [5] changed ? Or was it a change in the Publisher code ? last one is surely possible, esp. if logs changes with a CRAB version change !

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T13:17:01Z)

AFAICT `config.General.logLevel ' (from [5]) is never used in the code. But we do set log level to INFO in the  intialization, since ever. I am looking, so far failing to see what made that printout disappear

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T13:19:14Z)

Let's compare v3.230913 with previous one

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T13:49:11Z)

I saved earliest Publisher master log files in `/data/srv/Publisher/logs/processes/SAVED`

```
...
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T14:02:49Z)

a possibility is that we had always been starting Publsher with -d flag. But the [/data/run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/Docker/run.sh) script only does `start.sh -c` and has not changed since 2 years ago. pff..

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:01:09Z)

I can't find any explanation for whey the log level was effectively set to DEBUG until September.
I can accept that when putting in Puclisher_Rucio I messed up something in the effort of consolidating, but nothig seems changed. Also looking at code from v3.230220 the log level is set to INFO.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:02:33Z)

Can we deploy the previous Publisher on a test VM and see what happens ?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:19:22Z)

I am running Publisher_schedd in crab-dev-tw01 and it seems it does print the logger.debug as well. Digging.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:35:48Z)

OK. Found.
As feared it is a bug introduced when I put in a common wrapper to start Publisher_schedd and Publisher_rucio
In this line I take `debug` flag from the option in `start.sh` command
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/50a9f8aa9d8ae6f55034cc62e3b6a27870b2c522/src/python/Publisher/RunPublisher.py#L49
while earlier the Master was instantiated via this line
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/50a9f8aa9d8ae6f55034cc62e3b6a27870b2c522/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L766
and so the `debug` flag has the default value
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/50a9f8aa9d8ae6f55034cc62e3b6a27870b2c522/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L81

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:42:30Z)

THis clearly suffers of "confused history" where the `debug` flag was used both to activate a `pdb` breakpoint and to set loglevel.
But I do not feel like refactoring all of that.

So we can restore previous behavior by forcing again `debug=True` or put all messages we care about at loglevel INFO.
All in all I prefer the latter. But the former is safer.

@mapellidario what do you suggest ? A view from the outside can surely help !

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T15:43:25Z)

If OK with you, I will cleanup this issue deleting all those comments which I added to help me tracking my investigation

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-10-13T16:25:31Z)

Instead of deleting them, you could hide them marking as "outdated". How you investigated this issue may be useful for future operators!

In any case, I agree that we should set to "info" all the logs we care about, considering as authoritative source of truth the file with list of grok expressions

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T17:16:27Z)

thanks for the advice Dario. It is too late to change tonight though.
Well.. as to "how to debug" I should have not trusted looking at one line of code and simply tested with pdb right away, would have found the flag `debug=True` and onward from there !

since now we encourage users to use dataset not fully recalled from tape
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/65bd86caae2b590c148284ea62c3b7b124584162/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/TapeRecallManager.py#L140-L143

let's start by locking by full blocks(Rucio datasets) even if it triggers some silent tape recall. We'll worry about going down to file level if really needed.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7958: Add new CI pipelines (wishlist)
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7958: Add new CI pipelines (wishlist)

State: open
Opened: 2023-10-18T10:42:23Z
Labels: Area: CI/CD, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-10-18T10:42:23Z)

(Thanks a lot @mapellidario and @guyzsarun for the ideas and advice!)

With 2 main goal in mind:

-   Reduce manual work that cost time to do.
-   Prevent human error that cost time to debug.

This will boost our productivity (sorry, I do not know how to measure it) and enable rapid deployment on production.

The new *N* pipelines:

- [x] Automatically deploy master branch on preprod.
      Why? Eliminating the time to deploy the new image and trigger testsuite.
- [ ] Manually trigger deployment of latest tag on production and ensure new tasks can run properly.
      Why? Improvement of current Deploy_TW/Server pipeline; tagging the new release as `-stable`, deploy it on prod, **AND** run testsuite to make sure everything is ok.
      Now in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8689
- [x] Automatically deploy specific none master branch to dev env and run testsuite.
      Why? This is what I want personally, I need to make sure my code is running perfectly fine before I can open PR to other team member to review.
- [ ] Automatically trigger testsuite when puppet qa/master has new changed
      Why? <https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/8764zq4n6i815brt787b5br4fh>
- [ ] Automatically put the new CRABClient\'s release to crab-dev and open PR to cms-sw/cmsdist
      Why? It take *A LOT OF CONCENTRATION* to create proper PR (to put correct version name in spec file open PR).
      Now in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8583
- [ ] Automatically apply new credentials on kube/vm from crab-secrets and update credentials for CMSWEB team can apply to new cluster.
      Why? Infra as a code: describe what we should do when we need to change credentials instead of writing some documentation.
      Now in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8017
- [ ] Automatically test CRABClient against all supported cmssw version.
      Why? Current Jenkins need manual trigger for each cmssw version.

I will write implementation details for each pipeline in separate issue, but I am open for discussion here about priority and worthiness.

My plan is to have the first 3 pipelines before end of the year.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7959: improve runtime check on CPU abuse
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7959: improve runtime check on CPU abuse

State: open
Opened: 2023-10-18T13:37:15Z
Labels: OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7959

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-18T13:37:15Z)

We currently have this in our scheduler config

SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE = .... || ((RemoteSysCpu + RemoteUserCpu) > (2 * RequestCpus * (Currenttime - JobCurrentStartExecutingDate))=?=True))

Which is meant to kill jobs which are using 2 time more CPU time than Clock time.
On some new machines somehow job initialization steps cause this to trigger in <20 seconds, before the user application starts.

We should change adding the requirement of a minimum running time, 5 minutes e.g.

So somehow add `&&(Currenttime - JobCurrentStartExecutingDate)>5*60` but I am not sure of how exactly to place this in the classAd, consultation with SI is needed, I think HTCondor has some way to test classAd expressions too.

The file to change on the machines is `/etc/condor/config.d/82_cms_schedd_crabschedd_generic.config` which comes via puppet from https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/cmsgwms-htcondor-configurations/-/blob/cern/configs/82_cms_schedd_crabschedd_generic.config?ref_type=heads#L213

See the discussion in https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/qw47wth4e7bzdncqnxw1py951e

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-18T13:42:45Z)

**NOTICE** I have temporarily changed `/etc/condor/config.d/82_cms_schedd_crabschedd_generic.config` on vocms098 and disabled puppet on it
```
[root@vocms068 ~]# cat $(puppet config print  agent_disabled_lockfile); echo ""
{"disabled_message":"Stefano says: keep stable"}
[root@vocms068 ~]#
```
we need to get enable again the agent in one or two weeks or the machine will be kicked out of the hostgroup

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-18T13:44:14Z)

**NOTICE2** It would be good to have a way to push a different condor env via puppet on test machines like `vocms068` before applying to production schedulers. Is that possible now ? We may want to add to our documentation

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-10-18T13:52:42Z)

Quick and dirty way to override config in puppet:
https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/compare/7aa922ddccf16ea70ca7ff79367e771938bb915b...62d9302b2872d366a61d19d6b32f7878547bab73?from_project_id=4758&straight=false

(The change already committed in `crabdev_schedd` env/branch).

One quick question, do you need to restart condor/services/jobs to make new periodic remove effective?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-18T14:46:07Z)

awsome !
quick answer to quick question:  `sudo condor_reconfig`

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-18T14:52:06Z)

It will only apply to new jobs. Jobs already submitted will not be changed not even if you restart everything, you would need to do a `condor_qedit`. But of course there's no such need here

## Comment (mmascher, 2023-10-18T15:08:36Z)

> Marco Mascheroni can you tell us the correct syntax to change RemoveHighCpu so that it waits until e.g. 5min from job start ? Please answer in [dmwm/CRABServer#7959](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7959)

This is what I would do (not tested):

```
RemoveThreshold = ((JobUniverse=!=7)&&(JobUniverse=!=12)&&(((NumJobStarts>9)=?=True)||((NumShadowStarts>19)=?=True)) || ((DiskUsage>27000000)=?=True))
RemoveHighCpu = ((RemoteSysCpu + RemoteUserCpu) > (200 * RequestCpus * (Currenttime - JobCurrentStartExecutingDate))=?=True)
TenMinutesRuntime = ((Currenttime - JobCurrentStartExecutingDate) > 600)

SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE = ($(RemoveThreshold) || $(RemoveHighCpu) && $(TenMinutesRuntime))
SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE_REASON = \
   strcat("Job removed by SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE due to ", \
        ifThenElse(($(RemoveThreshold)), "** NumJobStarts OR NumShadowStarts or DiskUsage over limit", \
               ifThenElse(($(RemoveHighCpu) && $(TenMinutesRuntime)), "** CPU usage over limit ", \
                        "undefined reason." \
                               ) \
                                    ) \
                                       )

```

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-18T15:37:45Z)

ASO entries in https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/mtQFDScGk/cms-fts-metrics do not have RSE info

Looking at FTS raw info in ES  it seems to me that Rucio transfers use FTS metadata to convey this information e.g. in
[this doc](https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover#/doc/80773820-d0bb-11ea-a34a-f59641c8979f/monit_prod_fts_raw_start-2023-10-18?id=ecc11622-40aa-9520-3172-4d05bd8189c9)
we find `data.file_metadata.src_rse` and `data.file_metadata.dst_rse T2_AT_Vienna`

while the `.file_metadata.*_rse` fields are not preset in [ASO case](https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/app/discover#/doc/80773820-d0bb-11ea-a34a-f59641c8979f/monit_prod_fts_raw_state-2023-10-18?id=e82867cc-208e-c331-3abb-a0213c966e9c)
where we have fields inserted by ASO as `job_metadata` e.g. ` data.job_metadata.userDN` and the only file metadata is `data.file_metadata.oracleId` which does not look like "CRAB"

I suspect we looked a this already and come to some conclusion that reporting file_meatdata was not possible, but it is worth revisit again and possibly talk again with FTS developers, maybe something has changed !

high prio, since either I do "this year" or I never do

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7976: Rucio ASO with multiple publish container
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7976: Rucio ASO with multiple publish container

State: closed
Opened: 2023-10-25T14:37:17Z
Closed: 2023-11-27T17:26:55Z
Labels: RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7976

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-10-25T14:37:17Z)

Continue from output files matrix in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7940#issuecomment-1761356342

It is hard to clear unwanted files from container, something like when users want to gather diagnostics file from worker node (logs/coredump/whatever) and save to destination site, but later want to clear his space and keep only EDM/T files.
Users needs to manually detach files from Rucio dataset using API/CLI, one by one, which is not trivial.

To make it more manageable, we will put files into different publish container separate by file type, `{EDM,TFile,Misc,Logs}`.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-11-14T17:02:49Z)

Let's start with the updated version of the output dataset table (see the original version [here](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7940#issuecomment-1761356342)) [1]:

| case | output edm | output tfile | output misc | publication | output dataset name | note                                                                             |
|------|------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1    | x          |              |             | T           | /GenericTTBar       |                                                                                  |
| 2    |            | x            | (x)         | T           |                     | fail in crab submit, `tm_publication` is `T` but no file to be publish           |
| 3    | x          |              | x           | T           | /GenericTTBar       | Success, but only publish edm                                                    |
| 4    | \>1        |              |             | T           |                     | fail in crab submit, not support multiple output dataset (deprecated feature)    |
| 5    | x          |              |             | F           | /GenericTTBar        |                                                                                  |
| 6    |            | x            | (x)         | F           | /FakeDataset        |                                                                                  |
| 7    | x          |              | x           | F           | /GenericTTBar       |                                                                                  |
| 8    | \>1        |              |             | F           | /GenericTTBar       | the output dataset will have `module_name` in it but only one output dataset [2] |

[1] This table only applies to `crabConfig` that has `outputDataset` tag.
[2] e.g., `/GenericTTbar/tseethon-ruciotransfer-1699972252-testout-94ba0e06145abd65ccb1d21786dc7e1d/USER`

-----------------------

This section of code determines what the `tm_ouput_dataset` should be:
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73db7465fddc22dfd8c05b4593ac6f690200a29d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2750-L2767

Basically, if your task has EDM file(s) in output, `tm_ouput_dataset` is always the real dataset name, not the `/FakeDataset`.

Complicated stuff is "case 8". When you have more than 1 EDM output, PostJob will append the `module_label` after OutputDatasetTag but before pset hash [2], in `compute_outputdataset_name()`:
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73db7465fddc22dfd8c05b4593ac6f690200a29d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L148-L177

Which still works the same way as written in https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling#Output_dataset_names_in_DBS

The trickiest part of "case 8" is how PostJob save the dataset name in `tm_output_dataset`.
Well, it is actually a single line of code, in [line 2767](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73db7465fddc22dfd8c05b4593ac6f690200a29d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2767).
This means that only **last** `outdataset` from the previous loop gets assigned to `self.output_dataset`, and updated to REST in [line 2037-2046](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73db7465fddc22dfd8c05b4593ac6f690200a29d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2037-L2046)
"**last** `outdataset`" here is the last key of `FJR['steps','cmsRun','output']` (Keys are the filename with striped extension) which gets sorted by `json.load()` in alphabetical order somehow (I counld not find any reference why it gets sorted like that but I have tested in cc7-python3.6 and it is always sorted).

----------------------

About how PostJob.py pass this information to ASO, I will not dive into PostJob.py code. But it can be summarized as follows:

- Each file gets its own `outdataset` as `outputdataset` in `transfers.txt`, where:
    - If the file is EDM, the real dataset name is used (computed by `compute_outputdataset_name()`.
    - Else, `/FakeDataset` is used.
- The order of transfer dict is as explain in *last outdataset* above.

See example of [transfers.txt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/231114_160228:tseethon_crab_rucio_transfers_manyedm_withnonedm_test12_20231114_170227/SPOOL_DIR/task_process/transfers.txt) where the task has 2 edm files and single misc file.
You can compare with [another transfers.txt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/231102_121313:tseethon_crab_rucio_transfers_hc1kj_withnonedm_test12_20231102_131304/SPOOL_DIR/task_process/transfers.txt) where the task has single edm files and single misc file.

those two files are uploaded here as well
[2-edm-transfers.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/files/13413324/2-edm-transfers.txt)
[1-edm-transfers.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/files/13413326/1-edm-transfers.txt)
