title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7986: rationalize use of HTTPRequests across Server and Client
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7986: rationalize use of HTTPRequests across Server and Client

State: open
Opened: 2023-10-27T09:20:11Z
Labels: Priority: Medium, Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7986

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-27T09:20:11Z)

There is too much duplication and name confusion now.
I propose the following structure:

* HTTPRequests is a file of its own with different implementation in Cient and Server
  * Server: HTTPRequestsPycurl.py
  * CLient: HTTPRequestsCurl.py
* usage: `from HTTPRequestsPycurl import HTTPRequests` etc.
* CRABRest becomes a common file/class (in ServerUtilities ? So it goes to Client as well w/o any other change)
* getDBSRest (only in Client atm) becames a new class DBSRest (how knows, may be useful in server too) (in ServerUtilities again?)

Problem/Question
  HTTPRequestsCurl  could be useful in Server as well as fallback ... who knows... so a single file/class with an extra argument ?
  beware that "import pycurl" breaks Client on some CMSSW versions and surely we do not want to import from WMCore.
 I.e. On server it may be good to have access to everyghing, buy on client we need "curl only", which is why back then we
 went for some code duplication and no file sharing.

@novicecpp @mapellidario opinions ? Is this worth pursuing ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-10-27T13:46:24Z)

This should do together with https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7765

I think it good to refactor but I cannot say it ok or agree with your proposal due to my limited knowledge (need to research and sleep on it for some time).

> HTTPRequestsCurl could be useful in Server.

IMO, no. Because of what you said `beware that "import pycurl" breaks Client`.
On servers, we have a single version that runs at a time, so we do not need to care much about backward compatibility. If it breaks, just hot-patch it and think about a long-term solution later.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-27T14:10:40Z)

thanks for pointing out to #7765 !

Indeed, let's sleep on it and take our time. It is little code and main thing is to avoid headaches

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7988: REST - new api that exposes the crab Oracle DB tables and indexes size
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7988: REST - new api that exposes the crab Oracle DB tables and indexes size

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-01T18:14:57Z
Closed: 2026-07-13T14:38:39Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Low, Status: Available, Area: MONIT
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7988

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-11-01T18:14:57Z)

It would be nice to have a panel in grafana where we can monitor the size of the oracle tables and indexes that we use for prod and preprod.

We could imitate what DBS is doing. Use this query [1] to get a result similar to [2], which is a json document.
DBS code is here [3]. However, we use partitioned tables, so we may need to use slightly different queries, as described in our db admin docs [4].

After a quick discussion in a crab dev weekly meeting, instead of a json, we may prefer to expose the stats in a flat format compatible with prometheus, so it can easily be scraped by existing CMS Monit infrastructure. In order to flatten DBS schema, we can use an approach similar to what wmcore is using to flatten cherrypy metrics [5].

---

[1] curl -L --key $X509_USER_PROXY --cert $X509_USER_PROXY "https://cmsweb-prod.cern.ch/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader/dbstats" | jq

[2] https://dmapelli.web.cern.ch/dmapelli/crab/20231101-dbs-dbstats/dbstats.json

[3]

function https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/28e02bde209af797af7d59d4f7e3baba25a98605/dbs/stats.go#L50 calling queries

- full table query: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_db_size.sql
- full index query: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_db_indexes.sql
- table size, by schema: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_schemas_size.sql
- index size, by schema: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_schemas_indexes.sql
- table size, by table: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_tables_size.sql
- index size, by table: https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/static/sql/stats_tables_indexes.sql

[4] https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-rest/database-admin.html#check-size-of-current-tables-and-indexes

[5]

- endpoint: https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/fbaabff7b705eafaf11c558bf1f04c95dece9f57/src/python/WMCore/REST/Server.py#L373
- using functions from https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/Utils/CPMetrics.py

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-13T14:38:39Z)

we will not do this

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #7989: TW monitoring - differentiate submitfailed caused by crab system from user errors
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #7989: TW monitoring - differentiate submitfailed caused by crab system from user errors

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-01T19:27:12Z
Closed: 2024-07-30T09:11:40Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support, Status: Done, Priority: High, Area: MONIT, Postmortem
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7989

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-11-01T19:27:12Z)

We receive an alert when the number of tasks that failed to be submitted in the last 2h is higher than a certain threshold.

However, tasks fail to be submitted both because of user errors (no quota at destination site, no dataset found in dbs, ...) and because of crab system (3000 running dagmans, crabserver rest could not contact oracle, ... ) or crab dependencies (rucio, ...) outages. This means that in order to monitor crab system availability, we receive false positives [1], which for example made us slow to respond to a recent rucio outage [1].

In order to improve our trust in our alerts, we would a new way of distinguishing tasks that are not submitted because of a system outage from the ones that are not submitted because of a problem with the user request.

Stefano proposed to introduce a new status `submitrefused`, which would have a different meaning from submitfailed :

- 1. `submitfailed` "crab system encountered a generic problem with task submission", which would indicate problems with crab itself or its dependencies
- 2. `submitrefused` "crab could not submit a task because of a problem in the user request"

I suggest that

- we create a new sql query + function that sets a task to `submitrefused`
- compile a list of task submission failures that would make sense to identify as user-related problems
- check in the code where those failures are triggered and switch to the new function.

---

[1] https://codimd.web.cern.ch/G8BrXmKZQPyfoizEUOCmVQ#

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-01T21:36:27Z)

No need for a new SQL/API. Code to set task status is already in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9cb5d51245477e0bfa68fd2fc14931a620f7df15/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/TapeRecallManager.py#L232-L246
As indicated in there, this is a good chance to move it to some common place, together with other methods which are now replicated here and there.

As to " code where those failures are triggered" we can surely do this a bit at a time starting from the most obnoxious things (stageoutcheck failure and inexisting dataset), the simplest way is probably to add a new Exception to be handled in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9cb5d51245477e0bfa68fd2fc14931a620f7df15/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L97-L116

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T14:33:58Z)

preliminary code in https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/add-submitrefused-7989 sets new SUBMITREFUSED status, but does not report reason in the Warnings.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T21:31:47Z)

<strike>* `uploadWarning()` must be called when the problem is detected before raising `SubmissionRefusedException`</strike>

I changed so that message is uploaded in Handlet.py. In the various places it will be enough to put
`raise SubmissionRefuseException(msg)`

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-24T19:16:47Z)

WHen StageoutCheck fails, things work now when running using sequential worker (`start.sh -g -d`) but using slaves pool, child processes etc. via `start.sh -g` the task is set to SUBMITFAILED instead of SUBMITREFUSED

I need to understand this before I raise SubmissionRefusedException in other places.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8012: TW load wrong Rucio client certificate
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8012: TW load wrong Rucio client certificate

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-17T14:13:20Z
Closed: 2023-11-18T15:08:37Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8012

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-11-17T14:13:20Z)

Yesterday, after Eric switched the Rucio auth server to a new version, we had an authentication problem report by users in [cms-talk](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/cannot-authenticate-to-account-crab-server-with-given-credentials/31744).

I found that changed from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7897 make TaskWorker always used cert from `config.TaskWorker.cmscert`, but not `config.TaskWorker.Rucio_cert`.
If we look at the logs, it clearly say it use `/data/certs/servicecerts.pem`:
```
2023-11-16 16:29:56,640:DEBUG:Worker:Process-3: Starting <function handleNewTask at 0x7f5daa938310> on 231116_152942:muahmad_crab_RunIISummer20UL18NanoAODv9-106X_upgrade2018_realistic_v16_L1v1-v1-UL-HLT-ZgammaJetsToBB
2023-11-16 16:29:56,641:INFO:RucioUtils:Initializing native Rucio client
2023-11-16 16:29:56,642:DEBUG:RucioUtils:Using cert [/data/certs/servicecert.pem]
 and key [/data/certs/servicekey.pem] for rucio client.
2023-11-16 16:29:56,657:INFO:RucioUtils:Rucio server v.32.3.1 contacted
2023-11-16 16:29:56,754:INFO:Worker:Uploading failure message to the REST:
Process-3: I just had a failure for Cannot authenticate.
Details: Cannot authenticate to account crab_server with given credentials

```
Because in the [TaskWorkerConfig.py](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/baf4cf6b8e28b685b866e3f21eff68f007054332/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb#L16), we set `Rucio_cert` to `Services` attribute of `ConfigurationEx`, not `TaskWorker`.
I was misunderstanding the `ConfigurationEx` scope that I thought somehow we have the same copy of `config.TaskWorker` and `config.Services` it can be used interchangeably.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8017: CI for update kube secrets from crab-secrets repo
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8017: CI for update kube secrets from crab-secrets repo

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-20T17:09:11Z
Closed: 2025-10-16T11:54:58Z
Labels: Area: CI/CD, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8017

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-11-20T17:09:11Z)

Today, I have updated the credentials of CRAB REST to the cmsweb secrets system, which needs to manually sync secrets from our source-of-truth (`crab-secrets`) to the cmsweb system.
This process is error-prone because I need to make sure I update the correct files, put the secrets in the correct place, and update the correct upstream systems.
Ultimately, it is time-consuming to both ensure it works properly and fix it if it does not.

The automatic CI step will help us relieve these kinds of issues.

The CI steps should be:
- Figure it out if the commit changing kube secrets files. Providing envs to next step.
- Apply secrets to all envs from output of previous step
  - Something like:
    - reading filename/env from previous step.
    - Apply to template files
    - execute `kubectl apply`
  - Make prod as manually trigger step.
- Testing if it work for all envs from first step
  - Either check 5xx from grafana or execute the testsuite.
- Apply change to cmsweb secrets system (omit detail of this part, will discuss privately).

One of CI "wishlist's" in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-12T10:12:19Z)

@belforte Ciao Stefano, this is not urgent na Stefano, please no worries, i wrote this just for record.

Here's detailed write-up of [MR4](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-secrets/-/merge_requests/4)

CI steps implemented:
1. **Validate Changes** - this acts as a safe-guard for pipeline triggering. Every times we create a merge request or push a commit directly, it will check and collect only the allowed changed secret files for further downstream CI Jobs otherwise it will early terminated the pipeline.
2. **Re-encrypt Secrets** - this step will decrypt the changed secrets from our CRAB SOPS + GPG  setup, then encrypts them into the CMSWEB SOPS+GPG protocol in as atomic operation as possible, Sensitive debugging output is suppressed here. it then returns a list of `reencrypted_secret_files` and their corresponding envs as Artifacts for the downstream jobs.
3. **Open merge request**: this step copies the re-encrypted secrets into central `services_config`, check out a new branch, commits, pushes the changes, and then opens a merge request via the API from the new `update-test14-testX...-secrets` (`source_branch`) to `test` branch to `services_config`.
4. **Check MR Status** - We poll the merge request every minute for up to 1 hr, checking for either the "merged" or "closed" status; otherwise, it's terminated. we are not polling for few days as originally planned, since that would waste the CI-runner resources for nothing, So 1hr is enough for a quick review and merge, otherwise we retry this job for another 1 hr checking.
5. **Deploy** - Since the affected environments already known from upstream jobs, here we check out latest `services_confg` on the `test` branch and deploy only to the affected environments.

This pipeline currently works only on the forked repos (`kphornsi/crab-secrets` -> `kphornsi/services_configs`). after i get the green lights from you guys, I will switch to the real repos/secrets/configs ones. Thanks!

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-12T10:26:02Z)

### Things left to do
- [ ] Activate in origin repos.
- [x] more Tests step? if things really works on all affected envs after deployed by either check 5xx from grafana.
- [x] [Optional] more refining around `scripts/deploy-secrets.sh crab crabserver`?.
- [x] [Optional] make prod as manually trigger step. (Right now we discard prod)

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-16T11:54:59Z)

Eventually, we didn't activated it in origin repos though.

I have done complete PoC around this imperative CI/CD styles and its works fine on my fork.

1. make a commit `kphornsi/crab-secrets`
2. kubectl apply secret directly to each cluster env
3. open MR to `kphornsi/services_config`
4. waiting for MR merged, otherwise failed.
5. done syncing live with origin.

But we preferred update k8s-secret manually though, because its worth waiting a bit converging to inuitive new ArgoCD style or any secret CI/CD pipeline on `origin/services_config` sometimes in next year.

this way we not confusing ourself twice, and eventually treat `services_config` as **Single source of Truth** for k8s-secrets.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8029: Understand Jenkins submission for SL6 releases (CMSSW_7)
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8029: Understand Jenkins submission for SL6 releases (CMSSW_7)

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-29T16:25:15Z
Closed: 2023-11-30T23:27:28Z
Labels: Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8029

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-11-29T16:25:15Z)

somehow there's evidence that in this case, even selecting "from GH, branch HEAD', task submission for ClientValidation (e.g.) used instead latest current deployed release in CVMFS. This does not make sense at first sight looking at code in https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/configure, https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/setupCRABClient.sh and https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/taskSubmission.sh

- [x] Is this real (reproducible) ?
- [x] Why ?
- [x] Should we change ?

reference: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8025#issuecomment-1830540956

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-30T11:07:20Z)

Looking "better" at Jenkins log
```
10:50:13 + /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/common/cmssw-cc6 -- ./taskSubmission.sh
[...]
10:50:43 gmake[1]: Entering directory `/build/cmsbld/jenkins/workspace/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/CRABServer/test/container/testingScripts/CMSSW_7_6_7'
[...]
10:50:48 gmake[1]: Leaving directory `/build/cmsbld/jenkins/workspace/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/CRABServer/test/container/testingScripts/CMSSW_7_6_7'
10:50:48 using CMSSW_7 on SL6. Setup/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc6_amd64_gcc900/external/curl/7.59.0
10:50:49 Cloning into 'CRABClient'...
10:50:54 cp: cannot create regular file `CRABClient/src/python/': No such file or directory
10:50:54 cp: cannot create regular file `CRABClient/src/python/': No such file or directory
10:50:54 cp: cannot stat `/build/cmsbld/jenkins/workspace/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/CRABClient/src/python/CRABClient/WMCoreConfiguration.py': No such file or directory
10:50:54 setupCRABClient.sh: line 67: /build/cmsbld/jenkins/workspace/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/CRABClient/etc/crab-bash-completion.sh: No such file or directory
10:51:02 CRAB client v3.231010
```

translation:
Jenkins script calls [TaskSubmission.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/taskSubmission.sh), first line there is https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/19adcac695227a6cc7918dfe3a25666831c226b5/test/container/testingScripts/taskSubmission.sh#L10

[setupCRABClient.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/container/testingScripts/setupCRABClient.sh) creates and builds the env. for CMSSW and then clones CRABClient in order to switch to "using client from GH HEAD". But something goes wrong and the clone does not create the directories hence
```
10:50:54 cp: cannot create regular file `CRABClient/src/python/': No such file or directory
```
more errors and the end of the story is that `taskSubmission.sh` uses the default CRABClient which came with cmsenv.

If is odd that `git clone` failed silently, but bottom line is that we need to catch errors and exit with failure, not go on.
I am bit surprised that bash does not do this by default. Anyhow

1. this was clearly a "strange outlier" (full disk ?)
2. I see no evidence that the error was specific of CMSSW_7 or the SL6 container

 FYI @novicecpp since you asked in the meeting "why the py2 lost compatibility error did not affect CMSSW_7"

## Comment (belforte, 2023-11-30T11:08:15Z)

We better fix this while understanding is fresh.
Increase priority.
@mapellidario can you take care ? Your bash skills surely exceeds mine !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8089: resubmission of successful jobs only works while Dagman is running
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8089: resubmission of successful jobs only works while Dagman is running

State: closed
Opened: 2023-12-06T17:58:27Z
Closed: 2024-01-11T17:21:32Z
Labels: Type: Documentation, Priority: Medium, Status: In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8089

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-12-06T17:58:27Z)

properly verify.
Why failed jobs can be resubmitted also later ?

If possible fix. Otherwise document.
Connects to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5273

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-08T19:12:43Z)

maybe "as simple" as: if some jobs fail there's a Rescue DAG which we can trigger into action. But if will only contain failed nodes. ANd possibly the DAG stays in HOLD.

Once the `dagman_bootstrap` job has exited the HTCondor queue, there is not way to restarting. A new `condor_submit` is needed.

It will be nice to complement this with pointers to the code.
But maybe for the time being is enough for closing on "document that successful jobs can only be resubmitted when task is running". After that... there is `crab recovery` and/or `crab clone`.

Anyhow I am not sure that there are really important use cases where successful jobs needs to be resubmitted !

User report in https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-resubmit-force-not-working/32482/6 was something like "I can't believe that those jobs were successful and I want to try again". Nope !

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-11T18:42:11Z)

in the meanwhile, here's a pointer to DAGMAN documentation
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-resubmit-failed.html
and to DagmanResubmitter code
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/39aef1a1eccf893b1a2d9aea9e85956565c1f81c/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py#L97-L113
and to AdjustSites.py which edits dagman logs
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/39aef1a1eccf893b1a2d9aea9e85956565c1f81c/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L458-L486

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-11T17:21:32Z)

there's already a follow up in  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5273 where this was resolved by adding a warning.
As definitive solution, we will deprecate resubmission of successful jobs https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5285

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8096: restrict access to our vms - force 2FA for schedds and TW's

State: closed
Opened: 2023-12-12T17:12:04Z

Labels: OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8096

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-12-12T17:12:04Z)

We would like to restrict the access to TW VM's and schedd machines, forcing two factor authentication.

We have multiple options:

- 1) make VM's  available only via aiadm
- 2) enable 2fa on the hosts themselves [1]

---

[1] https://config.docs.cern.ch/access/multifactor.html
~~https://indico.cern.ch/event/1267808/contributions/5324574/attachments/2616286/4522008/From%20IT%20with%20Love.pdf slide 4, `include multifactor`. We may ask nikos, spyros or other friends from cern it how to do it :)~~

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-01-31T17:24:52Z)

@belforte and @novicecpp I am experimentig with two factor authentication on crab-dev-tw02, I followed instructions at [1].

Can you confirm that:

- from lxplus, you need to insert the second factor, and that you can login into crab-dev-tw02
- from aiadmin, you do not need to insert the second factor to login into crab-dev-tw02
- that this is the desired behaviour

?

thanks! :)

[1] https://config.docs.cern.ch/access/multifactor.html#trusting-aiadm

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-31T17:43:39Z)

Yes to all. Thanks a lot !

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-01T14:47:17Z)

Same to me. Very nice. Thanks.

Could you apply to tw03 too? I want test ansible with multiple node. Single node is working fine.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-02-01T16:37:42Z)

Good! thanks for confirming. I will apply to all dev and preprod machines (waiting for about 2h for puppet to run on all machines)

- [x] `crabdev_taskworker`: `crab-dev-tw*`
- [x] `crabdev_schedd`: vocms068 vocms069, crab-preprod-scd03
- [x] `qa` : `vocms059`, `crab-preprod-*`

If we like it, I will apply the changes also to prod machines on monday

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-02T06:40:28Z)

Running Ansible with multiple machines works. Thanks.
However, you need to establish a socket to aiadm (`ControlMaster=auto`) and provide 2nd factor before running it. Otherwise, Ansible will pass the 2nd factor to only one node, and the other node's connection will fail.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-02T10:08:40Z)

Please, update Ansible instructions in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/scripts/Utils/crab-shutdown
(the only place where we have them :-( )
Better yet, a page in https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-schedd/how-tos.html on "how to execute a command on all schedds"

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-02T11:11:15Z)

**OUCH**
Jenkins can not log on TW VM's anymore in order to deploy new images.

We can of course login ourselves and do it by hand. Yet it is not as convenient, also Jenkins has the nice feature of seding a msg and recording log.

Ideas ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-02T12:03:29Z)

Like `$_aiadm_ips` in https://config.docs.cern.ch/access/multifactor.html#trusting-aiadm but we need to ask Shahzad what IP (or hostgroup) of the Jenkins instance.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-02-07T14:39:23Z)

## Problem

If I adapt the suggestion at [1] and create a list of ips with values both from the `aiadm` and the `vocmssdt` hostgroup [2], then SSH fails [3] complaining that a line sshd_config is too long [4] (openssh version `7.4p1`).

## Possible solutions

1. Move our machines to alma9, maybe the more recent version of openssh (`8.7p1`) has a higher limit of characters per line in `sshd_config`
    1. I can not find a "line %d too long" in https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/readconf.c as in this commit https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/61b8ef6a66efaec07e023342cb94a10bdc2254dc , so maybe recent versions of openssh do not have any limit. I could not find a definitive answer though
2. `multifactor` puppet module writes multiple lines `Match User "root" Address "137.138.53.187,...` if the list of ips is too long.
    - we would need to open a GH here: https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-module-multifactor/-/issues/new
4. Only add a couple of machines from `vocmssdt` to the list of trusted IPS (hoping that the IPs do not change over time)
5. Stop using Jenkins to deploy our services until we migrate our machines to alma9

What do you suggest?

---

[1] https://config.docs.cern.ch/access/multifactor.html#trusting-aiadm

[2]

```ruby
  $_aiadm_ips_hash = cernlib::hostgroups2ips('aiadm', true, ['global'], false)
  $_aiadm_ips = $_aiadm_ips_hash['ipv4'] + $_aiadm_ips_hash['ipv6']
  # Test for sanity.
  unless $_aiadm_ips.length() >= 2 {
    fail('Something wrong querying aiadm nodes')
  }

  $_vocmssdt_ips_hash = cernlib::hostgroups2ips('vocmssdt', true, ['global'], false)
  $_vocmssdt_ips = $_vocmssdt_ips_hash['ipv4'] + $_vocmssdt_ips_hash['ipv6']
  # Test for sanity.
  unless $_vocmssdt_ips.length() >= 2 {
    fail('Something wrong querying vocmssdt nodes')
  }

  $_trusted_ips = $_vocmssdt_ips + $_aiadm_ips

  class{'multifactor::pam_2fa':
    trusted_ips => $_trusted_ips,
  }
```

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-18T18:05:08Z)

The problem seems the known one that in Jenkins scritp we have
```
export PYTHONPATH=/cvmfs/cms-ib.cern.ch/jenkins-env/python/shared
```
near the top and that messes up the python env.
Moving it to the bottom right before
```
$WORKSPACE/cms-bot/create-gh-issue.py -r $Repo_GH_Issue -t "$issueTitle" -R message_CCVResult
```
solved the problem.
I also took this chance to stop using the container for SL7 here as well. Always use singularity.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8110: Latest WMCore broke jobwrapper
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8110: Latest WMCore broke jobwrapper

State: closed
Opened: 2023-12-18T00:33:48Z
Closed: 2024-04-24T12:36:14Z
Labels: Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8110

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-12-18T00:33:48Z)

I tried to run latest WMCore's master with patch from https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11790 and found error in jobwrapper:

```
==== FAILURE WHEN LOADING WMCORE AT Sun Dec 17 23:24:40 2023 UTC ====
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 585, in <module>
    from WMCore.WMRuntime.Bootstrap import setupLogging
  File "<frozen zipimport>", line 259, in load_module
  File "/srv/WMCore.zip/WMCore/WMRuntime/Bootstrap.py", line 28, in <module>
    from WMCore.BossAir.Plugins.BasePlugin import BasePlugin
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'WMCore.BossAir'
```
From https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/231217_231359:tseethon_crab_20231218_001357/job_out.1.2.txt

Import `BossAir` in `WMRuntime/Bootstrap.py` was introduced in https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11812.
It maybe just simple as `crabtaskworker` [WMCore's build_system](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/87ea437f508308b5e1d544a234a80e2a9911d5c1/setup_dependencies.py#L222C1-L226) did not include `WMCore.BossAir` package.

I will open PR to WMCore later (after new year).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-12-18T01:59:15Z)

I have added `WMCore.BossAir` to `crabtaskworker` in https://github.com/novicecpp/WMCore/commit/98f570d7e8c34a84222bda99d4ecac76049b771d and now it is working fine.

https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/tseethon/231218_002532:tseethon_crab_20231218_012531/job_out.8.0.txt

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-19T15:44:03Z)

@novicecpp should we change the dependency in WMCore master then ? IIUC this means that we will need to wait for a new WMCore release with that in order to build again.
Picking up specific changes aside (like storage.json or support for rhel9) it is good to use current production WMCore release.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-19T15:44:55Z)

~~No, see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8110.~~

Sorry, I thought this is CRABClient issue.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-19T15:48:52Z)

OK. Let's keep it open then

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-19T15:56:43Z)

In summary, we cannot bump to latest version until this issue is resolved.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-19T18:25:48Z)

Let's open a PR for WMCore then

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T10:26:58Z)

@novicecpp can we close this ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-24T12:36:14Z)

Yes! Thanks.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8126: fix mail sending from our VM

State: closed
Opened: 2023-12-19T21:12:43Z
Closed: 2024-03-13T14:20:01Z
Labels: Status: On Hold, Priority: TOP, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8126

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-12-19T21:12:43Z)

@mapellidario @novicecpp can you kindly take care ? I never understood how those mails from "root user" of
our VM's are configured and where we should put our hands in puppet for this. AFAICT we
define the "To:" only as argument to `sendmail::root_email: ` puppet "thing". Maybe you can get some help

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8127: crab-dev client broken in IB
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8127: crab-dev client broken in IB

State: closed
Opened: 2023-12-19T22:18:14Z
Closed: 2023-12-20T09:22:17Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: In Progress, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8127

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-12-19T22:18:14Z)

while running Jenkins CCV on all releases, I found that submission does not work for crab dev (the default) when using python2 (CMSSW_10_1 or earlier).
``
21:36:47 Traceback (most recent call last):
21:36:47   File "/cvmfs/cms-ib.cern.ch/sw/x86_64/nweek-02816/share/cms/crab-dev/v3.231204.00/bin/crab.py", line 17, in <module>
21:36:47     from ServerUtilities import FEEDBACKMAIL
21:36:47   File "/cvmfs/cms-ib.cern.ch/sw/x86_64/nweek-02816/share/cms/crab-dev/v3.231204.00/lib/ServerUtilities.py", line 230
21:36:47     truncMsg += f"\n[... message truncated to the first {msgLimit - 100} chars ...]"
21:36:47                                                                                    ^
21:36:47 SyntaxError: invalid syntax`
``
this is the bug #8028 introduced in server v3.231171 and now fixed with #8030

So I have asked for a rebuild of crab-dev in IB with latest server version v3,231215 https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/pull/8899

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-20T09:22:17Z)

fixed in last night IB. Thanks to Shahzad

failure is

bug seems clear

this line
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5a8a2aab15b1fc5393f51640425958a8ccd00b63/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioActions.py#L202
should rather be like this one
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5a8a2aab15b1fc5393f51640425958a8ccd00b63/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioActions.py#L258-L260
so to be compatible with
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5a8a2aab15b1fc5393f51640425958a8ccd00b63/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioActions.py#L37

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-10T17:32:26Z)

A better solution is to remove `rucio=` from the arguments and instead use internally `self.rucioClient`

tested https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/commit/309df0c1bfd9785cf466dbf58916b9ec0ddacf98 on crab-preprod-tw01 via `run from GH` using https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/fix-tape-recall-with-inputblocks and tape recall request was properly submitted https://cms-rucio-webui.cern.ch/rule?rule_id=6a1fa13254644de694119887a841b0be

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-01-11T16:52:01Z)

sometimes image build after release fails spuriosly because of this check
![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/e142e634-a46a-4377-bc74-906f6370024e)

Sometimes one of those "failure" word simply appear in the log for good reasons, like being
part of a commit
```
+ echo '(DEBUG)   \- PAYLOAD: {"action": "created", "release": {"body": "Bug fix release to solve tape recall failures when using an input block list #8140 \r\n\r\nBrings in a
```
which gets printed to the console because that comment is part of the release notes for https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/releases/tag/v3.240111

We can try to remember not to use those "errore/failure" words in the release note, but maybe we should look for a better way to check if build was successful. Maybe we can simply try to trust the exit code of the build script ?

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8169: Jenkins StatusTracking test fails in getting task status

State: closed
Opened: 2024-01-12T09:47:30Z
Closed: 2024-01-12T09:57:45Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP, Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8169

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-01-12T09:47:30Z)

from Jenkins log
<details>
  <summary>Click me</summary>
 <verbatim>

23:25:58 ATTENTION return value for 'remake' has been changed to a dictionary
23:25:58  format is {'commandStatus': 'SUCCESS' or 'FAILED',
23:25:58             'workDir': name of the work directory created}
23:25:58 Remaking crab_20240111_230304 folder.
23:25:58 Remaking .requestcache file.
23:25:58 Success: Finished remaking project directory crab_20240111_230304
23:25:58 Traceback (most recent call last):
23:25:58   File "./testingScripts/statusTracking.py", line 138, in <module>
23:25:58     main()
23:25:58   File "./testingScripts/statusTracking.py", line 126, in main
23:25:58     status_command_output = crab_cmd({'cmd': 'status', 'args': status_dict})
23:25:58   File "./testingScripts/statusTracking.py", line 19, in crab_cmd
23:25:58     output = crabCommand(configuration['cmd'], **configuration['args'])
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/cms/crab-prod/v3.231101.00/lib/CRABAPI/RawCommand.py", line 28, in crabCommand
23:25:58     return execRaw(command, arguments)
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/cms/crab-prod/v3.231101.00/lib/CRABAPI/RawCommand.py", line 51, in execRaw
23:25:58     cmdobj = getattr(mod, command)(logger, args)
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/cms/crab-prod/v3.231101.00/lib/CRABClient/Commands/status.py", line 49, in __init__
23:25:58     SubCommand.__init__(self, logger, cmdargs)
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/cms/crab-prod/v3.231101.00/lib/CRABClient/Commands/SubCommand.py", line 278, in __init__
23:25:58     SubCommand.validateOptions(self)
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/cms/crab-prod/v3.231101.00/lib/CRABClient/Commands/SubCommand.py", line 660, in validateOptions
23:25:58     if not os.path.isdir(self.options.projdir):
23:25:58   File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc7_amd64_gcc700/cms/cmssw/CMSSW_10_6_26/external/slc7_amd64_gcc700/bin/../../../../../../../slc7_amd64_gcc700/external/python/2.7.14-pafccj/lib/python2.7/genericpath.py", line 49, in isdir
23:25:58     st = os.stat(s)
23:25:58 TypeError: coercing to Unicode: need string or buffer, dict found
 </verbatim>
</details>

there's a `TypeError: coercing to Unicode: need string or buffer, dict found` coming from `status_command_output = crab_cmd({'cmd': 'status', 'args': status_dict})`
this is due to
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7b0e1b5d54f8bb30b54cc2dd331504eff8e0d7c5/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py#L121-L126
where `remake_dir` is handled as a string, but is instead a  dictionary !
clearly the code was not properly adapted to the new "each command returns a dictionary" standard for CRABClient.

See also these lines earlier in the log
```
23:25:58 ATTENTION return value for 'remake' has been changed to a dictionary
23:25:58  format is {'commandStatus': 'SUCCESS' or 'FAILED',
23:25:58             'workDir': name of the work directory created}
```

This indicates that we did not use StatusTracking test with CRABClient version v3.231010 or later :disappointed:

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-12T10:27:35Z)

things are more complicated
1. the Jenkins Check_Result test still uses the container, so it is not enough to push a change to master
2. the code in there is not really "scram independent" as I wrote, since now statusTracking.py used python2
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7b0e1b5d54f8bb30b54cc2dd331504eff8e0d7c5/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py#L1 but we should use python3 from CMSSW like we do with CRABClient. For simplicity and since we do not use any Rucio-related code here, let's stick with
- use python3 for CMSSW_12 or later
- use python2 otherwise

So we need to change this
```bash
#1.2. Run tests
# dario, 2022-11: why dont we need the singluarity container here?
# stefano, 2023-12: we do not use crab submit here, so do not use
#                   any CMSSW code and are "scram independent"
export DOCKER_OPT="-u $(id -u):$(id -g) -v /home:/home -v /etc/passwd:/etc/passwd -v /etc/group:/etc/group"
export DOCKER_ENV="-e inputDataset -e ghprbPullId -e SCRAM_ARCH -e CRABServer_tag -e Client_Validation_Suite -e Task_Submission_Status_Tracking -e Client_Configuration_Validation -e X509_USER_CERT -e X509_USER_KEY -e CMSSW_release -e REST_Instance -e CRABClient_version -e Check_Publication_Status"
export DOCKER_VOL="-v $WORKSPACE/artifacts/:/data/CRABTesting/artifacts:Z -v /cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security:/etc/grid-security  -v /cvmfs/grid.cern.ch/etc/grid-security/vomses:/etc/vomses  -v /cvmfs:/cvmfs"
docker run --rm $DOCKER_OPT $DOCKER_VOL $DOCKER_ENV --net=host \
$Test_Docker_Image -c 	\
'source setupCRABClient.sh; ./testingScripts/statusTracking.py' || export ERR=true
```

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-01-12T15:04:21Z)

error is
```
Will use CRAB configuration file ./rucio_transfers.py Error while loading CRAB configuration: cannot import name 'getUsernameFromCRIC' from 'CRABClient.UserUtilities'
```

which is "natural" since that method was moved to ClientUtilities and users are supposed to use `getUsername` and be happily ignorant about whether we get that from CRIC , IAM, SSO, or wherever else in the future.

That decision to go make user only use `getUsername` is so old in my mind that I am suprised that it was only finalized in v3.231201
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/commit/317824c1730669e5ecccd38d57ee3e76211a6227#diff-d027900a9545b3917b2fff49bbe456f602712944d04744da4c02ccdb6fab863c

Anyhow, this is easy to fix.

State: closed

Labels: Priority: High, Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8185

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-01-17T15:12:12Z)

- [x]  authentication problem for `crab_test` Rucio group. [CMSTRANSF-802](https://its.cern.ch/jira/projects/CMSTRANSF/issues/CMSTRANSF-802)
   * this is working now, but we should use a different e-group to avoid spamming Shahzad
- [ ] given how ST works, it is bad to have some tests with and some w/o publications.
   - [ ] Those different configs should be used in CCV tests
   - [x] ST tests are meant for running tasks with several jobs and verify that all complete OK, ideally we should check publication on all of them. Mostly as a transient after introducing publication check there is now an overall switch to check/not-check publication.
   - [x] if a way is found to make the publication check behave correctly in the two cases, I have no objection to using it, as long as it is a simple thing.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-19T17:05:24Z)

one simple, if crude, way to deal with publication could be to disable publication check in

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/d22b6c243edfefa3856343d6bcf0e70a8e4cf90e/test/container/testingScripts/statusTracking.py#L66
when ` task['taskName']` contains the 'nopub' string

## Comment (belforte, 2024-01-22T14:45:07Z)

I have made StatusTracking test skips tasks with "nopublication" in the name. Keep this open for the other two action: change e-group for Rucio and add pub/nopub to CCV

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T10:33:21Z)

e-group was done. Changes to CCV are better tracked in ad hoc issue. But atm I have no appetite for moving publication tests from ST to CCV.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-29T19:34:23Z)

`chirp` is called in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1d41fa3554c92583a3ad2c03036e74f9d24f83eb/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L77
where the exit code is picked from `jobReport.exitCode.txt` which is written in [CMSRunAnalysis.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py)

Since stageout is only called when exit code is 0
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1d41fa3554c92583a3ad2c03036e74f9d24f83eb/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L243-L245

it should be safe to overwrite the content of  `jobReport.exitCode.txt` e.g. in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1d41fa3554c92583a3ad2c03036e74f9d24f83eb/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L272-L274
without touching the dreaded `cmscp.py`

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8224: Plan for PyPI

State: closed
Opened: 2024-02-02T14:46:22Z
Closed: 2024-09-04T19:19:53Z
Labels: PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8224

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-02-02T14:46:22Z)

**Plan for PyPI**

**Goal: move POC to Production**
- [x] POC approval from team
- [x] CI for *automatically* test new pypi image.
    - The goal is, *when new code tagged, ci build and run status tracking against it, and report when test is finish.*
- [x] bring back `./start.sh -g` https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8253
- [x] Build from WMCore private repository.
- [x] Mark deployment version for release that will be on prod.
- [x] Update deployment.
    - [x] Make helm compatible with new pypi image, also move [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/5dd0a31c9545e5e16a395aba0b1b955f1bf37b23/cicd/crabserver_pypi/entrypoint.sh) from crab rest image to CMSKubernetes
    - [x] Update runContainer.sh scripts to make it work with jenkins Deploy_TW.
~~- [ ] Replace python-ldap with CRIC~~ Move to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8439
- ~~[ ] Move gfal miniconda to our Dockerfile and install gfal2-util~~ No need to do it for now.
- [x] Run the Publisher!!
- ~~-Rework TaskWorker data files, move everything to `setup.py`.~~ Next improvement.
    - ~~[ ] This part will take a lot of time, at least 2 weeks. I still do not know how to do it.~~
    - ~~[ ] Also, deprecating `CRABTASKWORKER_ROOT` and put data files inside package.~~
- ~~[ ] (optional) packaging crab code ready to install via `pip`.~~ Too low priority.
- ~~[ ] (optional) build on alma9~~ Too low priority
----------------

**Plan for CI**

Move to [#8267](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8267).

~~Sorry, I still cannot provide a clear path for what I will do with CI.~~

~~The high-level goals are to eliminate manual intervention, shorten feedback time, and make it easy to maintain.~~

~~I plan to switch from Jenkins to gitlab-ci which provides a declarative pipeline and makes it easy to write configurations, in exchange for extra maintenance.~~
~~I believe gitlab-ci has better practice and can do fast POC (and I am more familiar with it) compared to Jenkins. Even if the new CI does not get approved, I can apply those practices that "work" back into Jenkins.~~

~~I will start with the new PyPI CI from the *"Plan for Pypi"* above as a prototype.~~

~~After getting more experience, there is a long list of "CI wishlist" in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958 that needs to be done.~~

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-05T07:41:10Z)

about TaskWorker data files, current situation is surely not satisfactory, there are duplications and possibly extra stuff which we should cleanup. I agree to take a bit of time to review and simplify. Maybe we can build the tarballs when the container start ? All in all he current `updateTMRuntime.sh` takes only a couple seconds to run. And surely `htcondor_make_runtime.sh` is heavily dependent on the specifics of the installation via rpm's and should be heavily simplified.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-03-15T13:40:16Z)

Today, Alan asked me about what we are relying on current DMWM Jenkins because they need to migrate OS that use by the tools in Jenkins away from CC7.

Main problem for us is RPM build, the [comp_gcc630](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/tree/comp_gcc630) will not work anymore because it is native to CC7 and need to be migrated.

This mean,
- The CI that build PyPI image
- The Publisher PyPI
- Production testing.

need to be ready before June this year.

Another service/job we rely on is pylint/pycodestyle, but this is just Python process and can be install easily via pip.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-15T13:46:02Z)

if disaster happens, we should be able to start a CC7 container in the new Jenkins node and run the build that. But hopefully migration to PyPI can be completed :-)

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-08-01T15:00:42Z)

New PyPI images are now in production thanks to @aspiringmind-code and @mapellidario.

Still need to do `Build from WMCore private repository.` before I can close this issue.
But put it on hold until https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8522 done (avoid conflicts in Dockerfile).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-04T19:19:11Z)

Now, all tasks are done. I can close this issue!!
Thank you very much @belforte @mapellidario

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-04T19:32:23Z)

thank you @novicecpp  !!!
surely it was more work than it seemed at the time. But you tamed the beast !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8231: new format/location for MONIT secret file on schedulers
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8231: new format/location for MONIT secret file on schedulers

State: closed
Opened: 2024-02-06T21:57:24Z
Closed: 2024-02-15T14:10:59Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8231

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-02-06T21:57:24Z)

with ref. to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8214#issue-2112910251
we (Stefano, Dario, Wa) discussed and agreed to change to

filename :  `/data/certs/monit.d/MONIT-CRAB.json`

content:
```python
{
 "url": "https://monit-metrics.cern.ch:10014/crab",
  "username": "crab",
  "password": "PutRealPasswordHere"
}
```

we will use puppet in case we want to push to user `crab-test` instead of `crab`

@mapellidario please correct me if my memory failed me !

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-12T21:14:30Z)

@mapellidario is it on you or on me to deploy the secret file ?

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-02-13T16:09:50Z)

I deployed the secrets to all machines. dev, qa and master puppet branches.

- filename:  `/data/certs/monit.d/MONIT-CRAB.json` (as asked in this private message https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/mtdnsqsmeibbpcg6p4en64dxee)
- content: schema described in puppet, for example here for [tw](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/57c90b999134d10a76a7481923ecb798a245467b/code/manifests/crabtaskworker/certificate.pp#L117)
- I created a new page on our docs with a mapping between producers, credential files in tbag, opensearch instance and index:  https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-monitoring/crab-opensearch.html

check to which machines the file has been deployed with

```bash
wassh -c vocmsglidein -l root "ls /data/certs/monit.d/"
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-13T17:39:52Z)

I am fine with changing the `url` format. Still find that `monit-metrics-secrets.json` is a better name than `MONIT-CRAB.json`... but I guess changing that is too much work for you.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-02-14T08:21:32Z)

Not a problem changing the file name, I will do it :)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-14T10:36:36Z)

Please no changes anymore. I do not want to edit the file again.

Labels: Area: CI/CD, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8238

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-02-14T18:14:30Z)

Would be good to be able to classify/mark Jenkins GH issues as suceed/fail, not open/close.
Currently all  we can do is to close both OK and Fail. So we have no simple way to indicate if they succeded when referencing from other issues, e.g.  making a list for validation.

Maybe this need will go away when all tests will be run as part of a top level action like a PR or a release build and will simply be a report inside there.

Current situation is also bad because it pollutes our repository with a plethora of issues.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8253: PyPI: Bring back ./start.sh -g -d
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8253: PyPI: Bring back ./start.sh -g -d

State: closed
Opened: 2024-02-19T16:48:08Z
Closed: 2024-03-11T12:47:52Z
Labels: Priority: High, PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8253

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-02-19T16:48:08Z)

I have dropped `./start.sh -g -d` feature to rewrote the startup scripts. Now, it is time to bring them back.

The goals are:
- `./start.sh -g` should run code from Github in `/data/repos/{WMCore,CRABServer}`.
- Plus, for Taskworker, run update runtime **everytime** when executing `./start.sh -g` to rebuild the data files (TaskManagerRun.tar.gz) from GH repos.
- `/start.sh -g -d` should work.

I will open the PR and explain the idea here.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-20T09:37:06Z)

In the [#8254](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8254), there are 2 things, "How we run the app?" and "How we build the image?"

Let talk about on "How we run the app?" first.

---------------------

**How we run the app?**

From the first bullet in the goals above, user (us) is already in docker at `WORKDIR` path (`/data` from crabrest image and `/data/srv/TaskManager` for crabtaskworker image). The user wants to run code from the feature branch in CRABServer's private repo. What he/she does is:
- Checkout feature branch in `/data/repos/CRABServer`
    - `pushd /data/repos/CRABServer`
    - `git fetch <remote name>`, hardcoded in [CMSKubernetes/addGH.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/a6612ad45ea6ca79915e71e343cc29a97418973a/docker/crabserver/addGH.sh).
    - `git checkout -t <remote name> feature_branch`
    - `popd`
- Run `./start.sh -g -d` (fromGH mode, interactive).

My proposal is, make startup scripts into 2 files, `./start.sh` and `./manage`.

`./start.sh` resposible for:
- Entrypoint for user to execute command.
- Dealing with args (`-g`,`-d`).
- Setting 2 variables, `$DEBUG` mode and `$APP_PATH` point to python code. Both will passing to `./manage` later.
- (TaskWorker image) trigger buiding and deploy the data files.

`./manage` resposible for:
- Setup debug environment if `$DEBUG` is `true`.
- Export `PYTHONPATH` from `${APP_PATH}`
- Start+Stop CRAB process.

Each docker images has it own script but follow similar convention described above.

-------------------------

**How we build the image?**

Everything is nearly the same, except build data files in TaskWorker. There are 3 files changes:

*1. [build\_data\_files.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/38bf04c1b709c5d9bd13b7f5a62e1e3e5f1273e2/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/build_data_files.sh)*

This is a new file where I encapsulate the bulding step from [crabtaskworker/Dockerfile#L23-L27](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3af9d658271a101db02194f48c5cecaf5fab7725/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L23-L27) and add extra instructions to make the script able to test locally.
- Script get the path of CRABServer and WMCore repos from `$CRABSERVERDIR` and `$WMCOREDIR`.
    - We develop code in our local machine, we already have code from both repos somewhere, just point to it. No need to push/pull/clone again.
    - In CI, CI need to prepare both repos before execute the script.
- Specify `$INSTALL_DIR` and `$RUNTIME_DIR` to put all generated files single place, prevent it mess with local repo and easy to clean it up later.
    - However, WMCore does not support `--prefix` option in `setup.py`, so the files generate from setup.py always go to `$GIT_ROOT_DIR/build` directory. Fortunately when we run setup.py again it will clean up for us.
    - `$INSTALL_DIR` is "working directory" for this script.
    - `$RUNTIME_DIR` is the same but for `new_htcondor_make_runtime.sh`.

Script will run [new\_ht\_condor\_make\_runtime.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/38bf04c1b709c5d9bd13b7f5a62e1e3e5f1273e2/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/new_htcondor_make_runtime.sh) to generate `TaskManagerRun.tar.gz` and `CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz` (will explain later), follow by `setup.py install_system`. All needed files will be in `${INSTALL_DIR}/data`, ready to deploy.

Note that, default value for `$CRABSERVERDIR`, `$WMCOREDIR`, `$INSTALL_DIR`, and `$RUNTIME_DIR` is opinionated:
- `$INSTALL_DIR` and `$RUNTIME_DIR` is subdirectory of current directory (=working directory, =$GIT\_ROOT\_DIR).
- `$CRABSERVERDIR` and `$WMCOREDIR` is in the same directory.
    -  Unlike in CI, `$CRABSERVERDIR` is current directory, and `$WMCOREDIR` is subdirectory `./WMCore`. This is why I need to explicitly pass environment variable as seen in [Dockerfile](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/38bf04c1b709c5d9bd13b7f5a62e1e3e5f1273e2/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L25)

*2. [new\_htcondor\_make\_runtime.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/38bf04c1b709c5d9bd13b7f5a62e1e3e5f1273e2/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/new_htcondor_make_runtime.sh)*

Mostly modify to support to build files in `$RUNTIME_DIR`. The logic still the same, replace some path with absolute path and `popd/pushd` to correct directory.
Please see the changes in PR.

*3. [new\_updateTMRuntime.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/38bf04c1b709c5d9bd13b7f5a62e1e3e5f1273e2/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/new_updateTMRuntime.sh)*

This script is rewrote entirely from scratch, but do the same thing as original [updateTMRuntime.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3af9d658271a101db02194f48c5cecaf5fab7725/src/script/Deployment/TaskWorker/updateTMRuntime.sh) do:
- Build data files `./data` directory from GH to build directory. By running `./build_data_files.sh` to generate new data files to `/data/build/install_dir/data`.
- Do the backup by `/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/data/` to `/data/srv/current/lib/Original_data_files.tar.gz`.
- Copy `/data/build/install_dir/data` to `/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/data/`, do clean up before delete.

All path is hardcoded in the script to follow the deployment convention of TW container.

One main idea I want to point out here is, to make the scripts able to run locally as much as possible. Even though the new scripts are simplified versions of the RPM image, they are still too complicate and time-consuming. Also, this will reduce feedback time from the build/copy-paste/deploy/test loop when running on a remote machine.

--------------------------

That is all. Let me know if you have any questions.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-02-23T10:04:31Z)

**Strategical points**
* Stefano and Marco discussed a possible plan, and Marco also talked with Jaime.
* HTCondor23 is very little changed from HTCondor10 (it is effectively an Htcondor11, they decide to change numeration of versions to use the year as major version number, htcondor24 is still not out !)
* We can expect full compatibility:
   1). a scheduler with HTCondor23 can run in a pool where CentralManagers are HTCondo10 and viceversa. We can independently update schedulers one at a time and SI can independently work on collector and negotiator as they like
   2).  current python bindings (HTCcondor10) work with schedulers at HTC23. We can update all schedulers and only later worry about having HTC23 bindings in TW
   3) there is no change in condor logs format, so we can upgrade to HTC23 a running scheduler and it will resume all jobs which were running when it was stopped.
   4) corrollary of 3) : since all condor information is on /data disk (a CEPH volume) we expect to be able to shutdown one scheduler, rebuild the same VM on alma9, reconnect same CEPH volumes, and restart having it pickup where it left.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8267: Pipeline for automatically test new pypi image
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8267: Pipeline for automatically test new pypi image

State: closed
Opened: 2024-02-29T15:27:53Z
Closed: 2024-06-24T11:17:27Z
Labels: Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8267

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-02-29T15:27:53Z)

Move from second part of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8224

Requirements:

1. Automated everything, from code commits to reporting the test.
2. However, do not trigger build every time when committed.
    - In example, in feature branch, we do not want to deploy every time we push code there. Sometimes just want to save after finishing work.
    - Another example, test code is broken, it is a waste of time (and resources) to build it again.
3. Pipeline should deploy to proper environment.
    - We have 3 (private) dev environments. If Stefano's wants to test, it should pick the source from stefano's changes and run on dev/test2.

The fourth requirement is **to move CI to Gitlab** because:
- *Gitlab-CI is the platform I am familiar with.*
- Officially supported by CERN IT.
- Better practice than Jenkins (at least for the declarative part; everything is defined in `.gitlab-ci.yml`).
- I like the "Pipeline" concept.
    - You can use `CI_PIPELINE_ID` from the previous pipeline as a reference to get some cache/data.
    - Retrying the failed jobs/pipeline is easy to do on the Web UI.
    - Caching files between pipelines is easy to do. See [example](https://about.gitlab.com/blog/2022/09/12/a-visual-guide-to-gitlab-ci-caching/).
    - Dynamic pipeline generation, [see official docs](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/pipelines/downstream_pipelines.html#dynamic-child-pipelines).
- Runner (equivalent to Agent in Jenkins) is easy to deploy and manage. Basic executor (shell/docker/etc.) is ready to use in CERN Gitlab.
- The practice in Gitlab is good enough to become an example to apply to another CI platform (not just Jenkins).

Of course, there are some limitations:
- Pipeline is bound to the repository. If we want multiple pipline, there are 2 workarounds:
    - Generate pipeline on the fly (Gitlab CI feature.)
    - Create a blank repo that contains only CI scripts.
- Job retry is limited to 3 times (enforced by CERN Gitlab admin), and we cannot do delay retry like we do in Jenkins (CheckTestResult job).
- You need to deploy Runner by yourself, at least to running Apptainer.
- Need some synchronization between Github and Gitlab.
- What about Github, like WMCore?
    - I personally never used it before, need to explore what is limitations and *cost*.

My grand plan is to use this CI as the pilot to build another CI on our wishlist in [#7958](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-02-29T15:28:42Z)

Here is a technical overview. I split it into six parts:

- Flow (trigger & branch management)
- Pipeline
- Scripts
- Credentials
- Runner
- Synchronization between Github and Gitlab

**Flow**

This is the flow of CI I come up with:

- Dev push tags directly to their own forked CRABServer repository with a special format: `<cernusername>_<anytagname>`.
- We use `<cernusername>` deploy in the proper environment (dev/devtwo/devthree).
- Setup Github webhook to trigger Jenkins jobs to push tags to the Gitlab repo.
    - Point here is that we need to sync update code to Gitlab and trigger the pipeline to run.
    - See technical details in Synchronization between GitHub and Gitlab below.
- Pipeline started; use `<cernusername>` in the tag to determine which cluster needs to be deployed.
- The last pipeline stage will notify users of the results of the test suite.

**Pipeline**

Pipeline will have 4 stage: build -> deploy -> runtest -> checktest
- Build: Build docker image (currently use kaniko to build)
- Deploy: Deploy to Kubernetes cluster and VM (See *Credentials* section below on how we can authenticate with server).
- Runtest: Clone of [ExecuteTests-StatusTracking's jenkins job](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/CRABServer_ExecuteTests/).
- CheckTest: Clone of [CheckTestResult's  jenkins job](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/CRABServer_CheckTestResults/).

The details I will explain later when I have `.gitlab-ci.yml` files.

**Scripts**

The scripts are mostly taken from [testingScripts](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/test/container/testingScripts), plus some shell scripts we put in the Jenkins jobs. Modify it a bit to make it more suitable for the new CI.

These are the rules I enforce (to myself) while editing the scripts:
- Clone the CRABServer repo is done by the pre-job step; taking care by CI.
- When cloning WMCore or other repos or fetching files on the internet, the endpoint and version/hash should commit to the file inside the repo. Then read it at the build time to fetch it. With this and the above bullet, we can get rid of the step where we need to pass the arguments of the tag/branch manually.
- Make scripts more modular; do one job at a time. Most shell scripts in Jenkins jobs need to be fixed regarding this.
- Most importantly, scripts should be part of the repo. In case CI scripts need to be changed, we can commit changes together with the new feature code. CI always runs depending on the tag/branch that has the latest change. So fixing your own branch will not affect other people's branches (you have to reconcile with the master branch later, though).

**Credentials**

There are 4 credentials we need:
- [Build] `registry.cern.ch`: We can generate on harbor UI.
- [Deploy] `ssh-key` to `crab-dev-tw` machine: One time generation, plus bypass 2fa in those machines.
- [Deploy] Kubernetes serviceaccount credential: to deploy CRAB REST. See ["Manually create an API token for a ServiceAccount"](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#manually-create-an-api-token-for-a-serviceaccount).
- [Runtest/Checktest] CERN grid cert (`usercert.pem/userkey.pem`): We need the main cert in order to recreate the proxy. We can use one of our service accounts for this.

All credentials have now become `Variables` of `CI/CD` of gitlab repo. This is safe because:
- We do not allow (by default) forked repos to run the same CI resources and read the same variables.
- At least, only people who have gitlab access to this project (crab-operator + voc roles) can view pipelines and variables.

However, I need to verify this if I understand correctly.

**Runner**

`Runner` is equivalent to a Jenkins Agent, where it can spawn processes inside the machine.
`Executor` is the mode in which the Runner runs CI jobs.

We need 2 runners for each executor type:

1. Docker executor
Run jobs in a Docker container. For example, if we want to run kubectl, instead of installing it on the Runner machine, you only provide a custom Docker image, and the scripts (kubectl command) will run inside that container automatically.
This allows dev to have full control over the software needed in order to run CI jobs.

This executor is the same as `Kubernetes+executor` CERN IT (`Kubernetes+executor`, it is the same except running in container spawn inside kubernetes cluster).

2. Shell executor
Shell Executor is like running a shell natively on a machine. We need it to run `cmssw-el8`'s Apptainer (e.g., running `crab` command).
We use "Shell Executor," plus an extra wrapper, to run jobs inside Apptainer.

I choose to maintain this runner myself in exchange for gaining control of node setup, but there is docker+machine executor provided by CERN that we can also use.

**Synchronization between Github and Gitlab**

Because our main repo is on Github. We push code to Github. But pushing the code on both platforms is a bit too much (or not?). It would be better if we push code to Github, then some automation synced the changes to Gitlab.

One limitation of Gitlab is that you cannot trigger pipelines from the autosync feature of Gitlab. We need to push to Gitlab manually in order to trigger the pipeline.

What I plan to do is:

- Setup Github webhook to trigger Jenkins jobs, like we have right now when we publish a new release in main repo.
    - Need to setup a webhook for each forked repo.
- In jenkins jobs, pull repo, fetch tag, push to Gitlab

An alternative way is to write a sync service that pulls Github every 30s and pushes to gitlab.

This is the guide for PR https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8328

The pipeline does the build-deploy-test loop, where the "build" is building the new PyPI image and the "test" is executing the "status tracking" testsuite.

The CI contains 5 stages:

![Screenshot from 2024-04-08 14-53-58](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/67321507-67ff-4d62-98a6-0ba484b21d3a)

1. `prepare_env`: Prepare `.env` file for use across job in pipeline.
    The [parseEnv.sh](cicd/gitlab/parseEnv.sh) script parse the tag format `pypi-<env>-<name>` to get environment (see "Trigger" section below about triggering CI and tag format). Then, write appropriate environment variables to `.env`.
    `.env` is available for all jobs in the pipeline as pipeline artifacts (see [.gitlab-ci.yml#L30-33](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/.gitlab-ci.yml#L30-L33))
2. `build_docker`: Build container
    Build the containers from [cicd/crabserver_pypi](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/cicd/crabserver_pypi) and [cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/cicd/crabserver_pypi) using kaniko. This kaniko is not different from [what CERN offer](https://gitlab.cern.ch/gitlabci-examples/build_docker_image/). It is just from the early days when I played with Gitlab-CI, it still works fine. We can migrate to CERN kaniko later.
3. `deploy`: Deploy REST and TaskWorker.
    - Deploy REST in K8s: Change the image to the image built by this pipeline, wait until the readiness test passes. This step does not apply the Helm template or any kube  manifests to reduce job complexity. Operators need to apply proper manifests before running the pipeline.
    - Deploy TW on the TW machine: use the script in Jenkins Job [CRABServer\_Deploy\_TW](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/CRABServer_Deploy_TW/configure) to deploy with `deployTW.sh` script.
4. `run_testsuite`: Submitting status tracking test suite.
    In general, `executeTests.sh` is the entrypoint of job to execute `taskSubmission.sh` inside appropriate cmssw container to run `crab` command. I have removed all Github bot code from scripts to simplify the code, plan to add back later. Please see `executeTests.sh` and  `taskSubmission.sh` source code in "Appendix 1" on how it works.
5. `check_test_result`: check the test result submit by previous step.
   Same as step 4 `run_testsuite`, `executeStatusTracking.sh` is the entrypoint and `taskSubmission.sh` is real execution  which call `taskSubmission.py` later. The `executeStatusTracking.sh` is wrapped inside [retry.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/retry.sh) helper to emulate the retry machanism in Gitlab-CI (CERN gitlab retry is limit only 3 time).

#### Triggering

The pipeline is trigger only when push tag and the tag name should match regex `pypi-.*`. But, the legit tag we use in this pipeline is `^pypi-(devthree|preprod).*`, as defined in `VALIDATE_TAG` in [parseEnv.sh#L6](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/parseEnv.sh#L6). I use this pattern to get environment name to create set of environment variables to use in deploy and test stages.

#### Helper scripts

1. [retry.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/retry.sh) is the retry wrapper which can replace by CI system when they have [deley retry](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/19231) feature like in the Jenkins. The script retry only callee script exit with code `4`, and controlled by `RETRY_MAX` (default: 10) and `RETRY_SLEEP_SECONDS` (default: 5mins).
2. [credFile.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/credFile.sh) is for copy creds file from gitlab variable to working directory and change owner to CI user and mode to 0600. The script accept first arg as file path and print new absolute file path to stdout.

#### Variable (Credential)

(Note: setup these variables are not included in this document.)

We use CI variables (From WebUI, Setting -> CI/CD -> Variables) to set all secrets that are used in the jobs.

There are 6 CI variables that available for all job:

- `CMSCRAB_REGISTRY_URL`: CERN docker registry (Harbor) URL.
- `CMSCRAB_REGISTRY_USER`: Registry username.
- `CMSCRAB_REGISTRY_PASSWORD`: Registry password.
- `CRAB_TW_SSH_KEY`: ssh key to deploy on TW machine.
- `KUBECONFIG_FILE`: k8s client config, include credential to access k8s cluster.
- `X509_USER_PROXY`: Grid proxy certificate to use with `crab` command.

(Security) Attack surface: Only people who has access to crab3 group (cms-service-crab-operators) can access. (Need confirm) forked project cannot access variables nor project runners.

#### Practices

To make CI easy to debug later, I have enforce these rules while writing scripts:

1. With appropriate setup of cvmfs/voms/myproxy/container, all scripts must be able to run locally.
2. Always run script inside `$WORK_DIR` (default: `./workdir`, with some exception). This makes running the script on a local machine easy to clean up.
3. Following point 2, `$ROOT_DIR` is ALWAYS available when `$WORK_DIR` is defined, and always point to git root directory. This make script easy to call other script inside repo.
4. `$SCRIPT_DIR`, [one-liner to get script's location](https://stackoverflow.com/a/246128), is use when script want to call another script where it is the same level or sub directory. Use `$ROOT_DIR` instead when calling outside script's directory (e.g, use `${ROOT_DIR}/test/path-to/script.sh` instead of `../../test/path-to/another-script.sh`).
5. `set -euo pipefail` is a must. However, when source scripts in cvmfs we need to disable it because some scripts does not wrote with unbound variable or failure of pipe command in mind.

#### Run locally

I has separate scripts ([test\_executeTestsStatusTracking.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/st/test_executeTestsStatusTracking.sh), [test\_executeStatusTracking.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/cicd/gitlab/st/test_executeStatusTracking.sh)) for test running CI job locally.

The content of script is clone from [.gitlab-ci.yml](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/.gitlab-ci.yml) file, simply to avoid call the scripts too many level.

#### Appendix 1: Table of cloned scripts and its original

|                                                                                                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [deployTW.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/ci_gitlab_pypi/cicd/gitlab/deployTW.sh)                           | Jenkins Job [CRABServer_Deploy_TW](https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/CRABServer_Deploy_TW/configure)                                                                                                      |

| [setupCRABClient.sh](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/ci_gitlab_pypi/cicd/gitlab/setupCRABClient.sh)             | [test/container/testingScripts/setupCRABClient.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5f3ab24a9f3544995d920610b84405d2d2b4dc3a/test/container/testingScripts/setupCRABClient.sh)                           |

#### Appendix 2: CI Features for debugging

These feature are for debug CI only. To reduce time when waiting for docker build or tasks finish running.

1. If `MANUAL_CI_PIPELINE_ID` is specify, only `check_test_result` job is run. Simply to debug `executeStatusTracking.sh` and `retry.sh` scripts without submitting task again.
    - This is possible by using [fallback cache key](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/caching/#use-a-fallback-cache-key). At [.gitlab-ci.yml#L159-L166](https://github.com/novicecpp/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/.gitlab-ci.yml#L159-L166), default is `$MANUAL_CI_PIPELINE_ID` then `$CI_PIPELINE_ID` then CI default to `submitted_tasks_TS_latest` where it same across all pipeline.
    - This is assume we run on specific branch/tag, not newly pushed tag.
    - Usage:
        - At WebUI menu -> Pipeline -> top right "Run pipeline" botton ([we can use API to trigger pipeline](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/triggers/), but later)

    - This is assume we run on specific branch/tag, not newly pushed tag. See usage in 1.

5. If `$SKIP_DEPLOY`is not null, skip `deploy` stage (it should skip `build_docker` too, but later).

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-03-06T14:31:00Z)

In the CI, I have this error message when CI submit jobs in parallel (runner concurrrent is set to 4):
```
gfal-copy error: 17 (File exists) - Destination davs://eoscms.cern.ch:443/eos/cms/store/user/tseethon/crab3checkwrite_20240305_132750/crab3checkwrite_20240305_132750.tmp exists and overwrite is not set
```

This happened because we rely on uniqueness of timestamp at the second level, which is not enough.
Here is how [crab checkwrite](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/f754471bc1511805bdad2ed3972fa15318c92c31/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/checkwrite.py#L89-L91) construct LFN:
```python
        timestamp = str(time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
        self.filename = 'crab3checkwrite_' + timestamp  + '.tmp'
        self.subdir = 'crab3checkwrite_' + timestamp
        lfn = self.lfnPrefix + '/' + self.subdir + '/' + self.filename
```

As per your suggestion in MM,  appending the  `uuid.uuid4()` to `self.filename`  should be enough.

I will open the PR later.

## Comment (Todd-L-Miller, 2024-06-12T16:15:45Z)

> How do I put an integer as value in the Submit object ?

 	The semantics of the Python interface have changed to reflect the
underlying reality: the HTCondor submit language only understands strings.
Those strings sometimes/frequently convert into ClassAd values, but

> of course something like `jdl['priority'] = "10"` is accepted. Will it work ?

 	Yes, in exactly the same way it work if you wrote

priority = 10

in the submit file.  That's kind of the point of this change, that the
previous interface let people believe they were passing through integers
-- or worse, more complicated data structures -- through, when in fact we
were mostly just str()ingify them and hoping.

 	I've made a note of this for the migration guide, and if enough
people complain strongly enough, we might back off some of the changes.
(For instance, the semantics and syntax of converting ints to string and
back are known to work exactly as you might expect, so handling them
explicitly is probably OK, if people decide a little bit of confusion is
worth the convenience.)

-- ToddM

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-07T09:44:19Z)

configuration files in gitlab are pulled in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/822a6b76113bca2b7ffbcaab6aa6c69d16420ef0/src/python/CRABInterface/Utilities.py#L97

but avoiding the DOS attack is not that easy, since the call fails, there's no cached value and a new call is made every time a client contacts the REST. We do not have retry loops in the REST code itself here.
It may also be that it is not as much retry in the client(s) as queries from multiple clients (all postjobs and transfer scripts e.g.).

So I am not sure if we can (easily) do something.

Ismale point to https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/administration/settings/user_and_ip_rate_limits.html#response-headers but it seems a tool for them, not us.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-16T18:22:36Z)

Maybe we could avoid the "pull every 30min from gitlab in case we changed it" and rather push a config. change via K8s when a change is committed ?
@novicecpp  @mapellidario since we are fresh of discussion on K8s deployment..
given also that changes to that configuration happens rarely (mostly to disable/enable schedd's)

If we look carefully at  https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config.json?ref_type=heads we may even conclude that it is very static and could be part of the K8s template. And the only dynamic thing is the list of schedulers.
Of course the problem of the day was a typo in the list of schedulers ! And we should ask ourselves... why is that managed via the REST rather than be a TW configuration handled via puppet ? Now we change in gitlab and REST picks it every 30 min. If we do it via puppet it takes 2h.. so what ?

Nor puppet nor K8s existed when the current mechanism was thought of, and pushing changed to the REST required a new CMSWEB deployment which they would only do once a month. Now things are much different.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8277: remove use of  HTCondorUtils.AuthenticatedSubproces

State: closed
Opened: 2024-03-12T22:22:48Z
Closed: 2024-04-12T11:00:43Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8277

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-03-12T22:22:48Z)

it was needed when TaskWorker was using multiple X509 proxies at same time and needed to submit to schedulers with the user's proxy.
