title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8285: replace usage of deprecated classad.parseOld
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8285: replace usage of deprecated classad.parseOld

State: closed
Opened: 2024-03-14T20:48:45Z
Closed: 2024-03-25T22:37:02Z
Labels: Type: Bug, alma9
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8285

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-03-14T20:48:45Z)

with reference to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8258#issuecomment-1997664317

In El9/Alma9 with HTCondor 10.2 , RetryJob badly crashes at line 108 here
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8ad7dca366b8a6e4143d67a2eae7d57b2585946c/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L103-L118
with a core dump.

This part of the code is only executed when resubmitting a job/

Trying to open and parse same file on vocms059, HTC 10.0.9 on CC7 I get instead
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
classad.ClassAdParseError: None
```

So the error sort of understood.
Things are broken inside classAd.pareseOld(), which is anyhow [deprecated](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/v10_0/apis/python-bindings/api/classad.html#classad.parseOld) in HTC 10.0  , so can't ask Madison to fix it !

What  I do not understand atm is how can work on CC7 since classad.parseOld() fails there too, even if not so  explosively and in EL9.

Anyhow I will switch to the replacement classAd.parseAds which reads the out classAd file w/o errors on both CC7 and Alma9.

Given the complexity and obscurity of PostJob and RetryJob a strong validation will be important :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-15T09:43:19Z)

Looking for a simple example to post here, I found that the problem seems to come from the empty line at the bottom of the `SPOOL_DIR/finished_jobs/job.N.r` files.

Here's the reproduces on A:
```
belforte@crab-sched-901/~> condor_version
$CondorVersion: 10.2.0 2023-01-05 BuildID: 621409 PackageID: 10.2.0-1 $
$CondorPlatform: x86_64_AlmaLinux9 $
belforte@crab-sched-901/~> cat ADS-no-emptyline
cat: ADS-no-emptyline: No such file or directory
belforte@crab-sched-901/~> cat > ADS-no-emptyline
ClusterId = 246
belforte@crab-sched-901/~>
belforte@crab-sched-901/~>
belforte@crab-sched-901/~> cat ADS-no-emptyline
ClusterId = 246
belforte@crab-sched-901/~> cat ADS
ClusterId = 246

belforte@crab-sched-901/~> python3
Python 3.9.18 (main, Jan  4 2024, 00:00:00)
[GCC 11.4.1 20230605 (Red Hat 11.4.1-2)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import classad
>>> with open('ADS-no-emptyline','r') as fh: classad.parseOld(fh)
...
<stdin>:1: DeprecationWarning: ClassAd Deprecation: parseOld is deprecated; use parseOne, parseNext, or parseAds instead.
[ ClusterId = 246 ]
>>> with open('ADS','r') as fh: classad.parseOld(fh)
...
/usr/include/c++/11/bits/basic_string.h:1059: std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::reference std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::operator[](std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::size_type) [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits<char>; _Alloc = std::allocator<char>; std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::reference = char&; std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::size_type = long unsigned int]: Assertion '__pos <= size()' failed.
Aborted (core dumped)
belforte@crab-sched-901/~>
```

While on CC7:
```
belforte@vocms0199/~> condor_version
$CondorVersion: 10.0.9 2023-09-28 BuildID: 678199 PackageID: 10.0.9-1 $
$CondorPlatform: x86_64_CentOS7 $
belforte@vocms0199/~> python3
Python 3.6.8 (default, Nov 14 2023, 16:29:52)
[GCC 4.8.5 20150623 (Red Hat 4.8.5-44)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import classad
>>> with open('ADS-no-emptyline','r') as fh: classad.parseOld(fh)
...
[ ClusterId = 246 ]
>>> with open('ADS','r') as fh: classad.parseOld(fh)
...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
classad.ClassAdParseError: None
>>>
```
our python code handes the 'None`, but not the assertion failure in C++

So we can start with removing the empty line at the bottom, and take a bit of time to fully validate replacing `classad.parseOld()` with `classad.parseAds()`, although in simple test this works perfectly fine.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-15T10:13:40Z)

the extra empty line is a "feature" of the stdout from `condor_q`. Adding `| grep =` in here should do
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8ad7dca366b8a6e4143d67a2eae7d57b2585946c/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L1943
At least as a quick patch to progress with testing on alma9

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-18T18:01:57Z)

there's actually a mix of all manners of using classad parsing in current code base.
All of these are used in various files
* the deprecated: `parse()`, `parseOld` - the former only support classAds in new formatn, the latter only in old format
* the valid : `parseOne()`, `parseAds()` - `parseAds` automatically adapts to new/old format

so there is no need to do extensive validation of the new `parseAds`, all in all i

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-19T20:20:37Z)

the new `classad.parseAds` is an **iterator** while `classad.parseOld` was returning a full classAd object :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2024-03-19T20:32:06Z)

looks like `classad.parseOne(filehandle)` is what we should use to replace `classad.parseOld`
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/api/classad.html

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8307: Too many false potisive alerts on mattermost from grafana
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8307: Too many false potisive alerts on mattermost from grafana

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-02T14:31:24Z
Closed: 2024-04-09T09:41:38Z
Labels: Area: MONIT, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8307

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-04-02T14:31:24Z)

We are receiving too many notifications on mattermost from grafana, for example [1].

From a quick googling session [2] it can be that we are making grafana query the data providers (prometheus, for example) too aggressively.

we have two options:

- [x] do not trigger an alert if a panel contains no data: should be simple to implement, will reduce false positives, but will likely miss some incidents.
- [x] reduce the frequency at which we check the value of a variable,
    - [x] for example, we do not really need to evaluate every minute if any of our k8s pod has more than 50 open fds.

[1]

```plaintext
Value: [no value]
Labels:

    alertname = DatasourceError
    grafana_folder = CRAB Alerts Alerts - MNg7eZF4z
    rule_uid = ee1322c8-065d-4b14-a182-745da00317a7
    rulename = NUMBER OF RUNNING DAGMANS PER SCHEDD alert
```

[2] https://community.grafana.com/t/intermitent-alertname-datasourceerror/103872/6

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-04-02T14:56:36Z)

So:

- [x] I reduced the evaluation time to 10min for every alert
- [x] I set "alert state if execution error or timeout" set "ok"  [1]

result
- [x] all alerts in "CRAB Alerts Alerts - MNg7eZF4z" in [grafana](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/alerting/list) are ok, not firing

let's see how the next week goes before marking this issue as solved.

---

[1]

![Screenshot_20240402_163907](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/16376695/c8a20955-34dd-410c-ba7e-3bc771b9c474)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-02T16:28:05Z)

why was this happening just now ?

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-04-09T09:41:39Z)

> why was this happening just now ?

This is a mystery, it can be any combination of grafana, prometheus and opensearch changes. I think the situation improved and will close this issue. If the problem appears again I will open a new one

Problem seem "just sine March" ! ![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/85a05b03-b683-4ec0-a70d-0e940aa85daf) I managed to look as users behind the failure (brute force hack with grep of those files to extract one lfn and get user name inside it) but there's no clear dominance. The user with today's problem (`tsheng`) only has two failed blocks and both refer to same task as discussed here ```text [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 tsheng]$ grep -m 1 tsheng /data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/*txt /data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/failed-block-at-1712021537.1638997.txt: 'lfn': '/store/group/phys_heavyions/tsheng/run23/Pythia8_DzeroToKPi_prompt_Pthat5_TuneCP5_5360GeV/MC_20240401_DIGI_v1/240402_010755/0000/signal_RAW_44.root', /data/srv/Publisher_files/FailedBlocks/failed-block-at-1712023306.5412498.txt: 'lfn': '/store/group/phys_heavyions/tsheng/run23/Pythia8_DzeroToKPi_prompt_Pthat5_TuneCP5_5360GeV/MC_20240401_DIGI_v1/240402_010755/0000/signal_RAW_76.root', [crab3@crab-prod-tw01 tsheng]$ ``` Maybe many failures were simply "DBS restart" during cmsweb migrations and succeeded after retry ? ## Comment (todor-ivanov, 2024-04-03T05:53:55Z) Hi @belforte from your messages above, I see the origins could be two here: * large blocks from CRAB side * DBS infrastructure issues during the last days on March. If the former, should we also start looking into ways to increase the limitations on the block size records from the DBS server side, or do you think it won't be needed? ## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-03T08:38:22Z) thanks for helping out @todor-ivanov . Let's do the simple thing and retry the publication in case it was the second. I will do and post result here. If it is the first indeed a starting point could be to compare with what WMA does, as it may suffer of same problem (classical pileup brings in many many files as parents in its effort to randomize events across a large minbias dataset). Or maybe it is a user misconfiguration that we better solve making it impossible to create such a mess :-) Forcing DBS to accept outlandish inputs should be last resort. Such things may create problems down the line as well. ## Comment (todor-ivanov, 2024-04-03T08:56:39Z) Thanks @belforte . I'll stay put, while watching the outcome from this particulate use case.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8316: use robot certificate to retrieve proxies from myproxy
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8316: use robot certificate to retrieve proxies from myproxy

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-03T21:09:08Z
Closed: 2024-06-24T10:44:20Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8316

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-03T21:09:08Z)

* Maarten [says](https://ggus.eu/index.php?mode=ticket_info&ticket_id=166121) that a robot cert is fine
* we can use the [current one](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/cmscrab-service-account.html#create-robot-certificate) which is already available in TW
   * of course need to have it added to authorized retrievers via e.g. GGUS
* need simply to change the [TW config](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb#L114-115) in puppet in order to use it
* then there will be no need to ask for adding host cert etc.  Everything taken care of by [puppet](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/manifests/crabtaskworker/certificate.pp#L97-113)
* we should update documentation of what the robot cert. is used for

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-03T21:11:21Z)

@novicecpp may I assign this to you ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-04T09:53:41Z)

I have added the request to enable the robot certificate to [GGUS](https://ggus.eu/index.php?mode=ticket_info&ticket_id=166121)

Once they say that they did it, please give it a try

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-17T10:57:20Z)

it was tested and added to delegation list.
What is needed is to update the TW configuration. These two lines
https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb?ref_type=heads#L117-118
should point to `/data/certs/robotcert.pem` and `/data/certs/robotkey.pem`

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-17T14:26:30Z)

reference: https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/208

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-24T10:41:58Z)

@mapellidario @novicecpp can we close this ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-06-24T10:44:20Z)

Yes. Thanks to Dario for taking care deployment.
https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/prod-tw-uses-new-robot-cert-for-myproxy/42569

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-24T10:45:29Z)

thanks !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8324: T2_DE_DESY_temp Rucio config changed, break Rucio ASO
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8324: T2_DE_DESY_temp Rucio config changed, break Rucio ASO

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-09T14:49:41Z
Closed: 2024-04-12T10:21:10Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8324

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-04-09T14:49:41Z)

There are 2 issues:
1. T2_DE_DESY_Temp's Ruico protocol has changed.

This break the hardcode I put in `RegisterReplicas.py`.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5f3ab24a9f3544995d920610b84405d2d2b4dc3a/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py#L303-L304

Good things is now DESY normal RSE and Temp RSE protocol consistent (FYI: We get `pfn` path from `rucio.lfns2pfns()` by passing normal RSE to function and assumed `Temp` area has same protocol).

**CURRENT** result from: `rucio.get_protocols('T2_DE_DESY_Temp')` (only davs):
```python
{'domains': {'lan': {'delete': 0, 'read': 0, 'write': 0},
   'wan': {'delete': 1,
    'read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_write': 1,
    'write': 1}},
  'extended_attributes': None,
  'hostname': 'dcache-cms-webdav-wan.desy.de',
  'impl': 'rucio.rse.protocols.gfal.Default',
  'port': 2880,
  'prefix': '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/temp/',
  'scheme': 'davs'}
```

**LAST YEAR** result from: `rucio.get_protocols('T2_DE_DESY_Temp')` (only davs):
```python
{'domains': {'lan': {'delete': 0, 'read': 0, 'write': 0},
   'wan': {'delete': 1,
    'read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_write': 1,
    'write': 1}},
  'extended_attributes': None,
  'hostname': 'dcache-cms-webdav-wan.desy.de',
  'impl': 'rucio.rse.protocols.gfal.Default',
  'port': 2880,
  'prefix': '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/store/temp',
  'scheme': 'davs'}
```

**T2_DE_DESY** does not change (paste it here for comparison)
```python
{'domains': {'lan': {'delete': 0, 'read': 0, 'write': 0},
   'wan': {'delete': 1,
    'read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_read': 1,
    'third_party_copy_write': 1,
    'write': 1}},
  'extended_attributes': {'tfc': [{'out': '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/unmerged/$1',
     'path': '/+store/unmerged/(.*)',
     'proto': 'pnfs'},
    {'out': '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/temp/$1',
     'path': '/+store/temp/(.*)',
     'proto': 'pnfs'},
    {'out': '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/$1', 'path': '/+(.*)', 'proto': 'pnfs'},
    {'chain': 'pnfs',
     'out': 'davs://dcache-cms-webdav-wan.desy.de:2880/$1',
     'path': '/+(.*)',
     'proto': 'webdav'}],
   'tfc_proto': 'webdav'},
  'hostname': 'dcache-cms-webdav-wan.desy.de',
  'impl': 'rucio.rse.protocols.gfal.Default',
  'port': 2880,
  'prefix': '/',
  'scheme': 'davs'}
  ```

Remove the hardcode should fix.

2. Rucio ASO break because issue above.

I expected Rucio ASO to survive exception cause by 1, mark job as fail, then let retry mechanism do the rest.
However, it not, and block indefinitely. This is due different exception is raised, `RSEFileNameNotSupported`, as shown in [rucio_transfer.log](http://vocms059.cern.ch/mon/tseethon/240408_114824:tseethon_crab_rucio_transfers_20240408_134822/SPOOL_DIR/task_process/transfer_rucio.log)

```
2024-04-08 19:47:17,240] [RucioTransfer.Actions.RegisterReplicas] [DEBUG] Registering replicas from T2_DE_DESY_Temp
[2024-04-08 19:47:17,240] [RucioTransfer.Actions.RegisterReplicas] [DEBUG] Replicas: {'e6410a90da68703fe3f2e70ba9c3eca00feaf74aa67b68d2299737f3': {'scope': 'user.tseethon', 'pfn': 'davs://dcache-cms-webdav-wan.desy.de:2880/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/store/temp/user/tseethon.d6830fc3715ee01030105e83b81ff3068df7c8e0/tseethon/ruciotransfers-1712576902/GenericTTbar/ruciotransfers-1712576902/240408_114824/0000/output_6.root', 'name': '/store/user/rucio/tseethon/ruciotransfers-1712576902/GenericTTbar/ruciotransfers-1712576902/240408_114824/0000/output_6.root', 'bytes': 633409, 'adler32': '5aa85c44'}}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/ASO/Rucio/Main.py", line 107, in main
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/ASO/Rucio/RunTransfer.py", line 54, in algorithm
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py", line 50, in execute
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py", line 170, in addFilesToRucio
  File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/x86_64/rhel9/py3/current/lib/python3.9/site-packages/rucio/client/replicaclient.py", line 279, in add_replicas
    raise exc_cls(exc_msg)
rucio.common.exception.RSEFileNameNotSupported: RSE does not support provided filename.
Details: Invalid prefix: provided '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/store', expected '/pnfs/desy.de/cms/tier2/temp/'

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py", line 10, in <module>
    main()
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6243/0/cluster9556243.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/ASO/Rucio/Main.py", line 111, in main
Exception: Unexpected error during main
Command exited with non-zero status 1
```

The line that catch exception:

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5f3ab24a9f3544995d920610b84405d2d2b4dc3a/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py#L180

It is safe to use just generic RucioException here, and improve the monitoring later to cache this type of error.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-09T15:16:14Z)

very good !! thanks.

Worth checking with Rahul that thing with Rucio@DESY are now stable

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-11T13:07:59Z)

Rahul told me it got fix from this change https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/pull/766/files
I still do not understand. Maybe @dynamic-entropy can elaborate more?

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2024-04-11T13:34:51Z)

The rucio script that parsed the tfc rules did not add a trailing slash in prefeix `/store/temp/rucio` and `store/test/rucio` for `_Temp` and `_Test` rses respectively.
This change ensures that.
This was an issue with configuring RSEs for tokens because of this, and Guy identified this issue.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8329: HTTP error 413 Request Entity Too Large when inserting blocks in DBS State: closed Opened: 2024-04-11T12:08:41Z Closed: 2024-04-15T07:57:57Z Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8329 ## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-11T12:08:41Z) we have again cases of blocks too big to be published, DBS server returns `HTTP error 413 Request Entity Too Large`
Detail: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.240325-e142b415228994babce71846cc653b98/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/crabtaskworker/v3.240325-e142b415228994babce71 846cc653b98/lib/python3.8/site-packages/Publisher/TaskPublish.py", line 935, in publishInDBS3 destApi.insertBulkBlock(blockDump) File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.240325-e142b415228994babce71846cc653b98/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/py3-dbs3-client/4.0.12/lib/python3.8/site-pack ages/dbs/apis/dbsClient.py", line 647, in insertBulkBlock result = self.__callServer("bulkblocks", data=blockDump, callmethod='POST' ) File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.240325-e142b415228994babce71846cc653b98/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/py3-dbs3-client/4.0.12/lib/python3.8/site-pack ages/dbs/apis/dbsClient.py", line 486, in __callServer self.__parseForException(data) File "/data/srv/TaskManager/v3.240325-e142b415228994babce71846cc653b98/slc7_amd64_gcc630/cms/py3-dbs3-client/4.0.12/lib/python3.8/site-pack ages/dbs/apis/dbsClient.py", line 512, in __parseForException raise http_error RestClient.ErrorHandling.RestClientExceptions.HTTPError: HTTP Error 413: URL=https://cmsweb-prod.cern.ch:8443/dbs/prod/phys03/DBSWriter/bulkblocks Code=413 Message=Request Entity Too Large Header=HTTP/1.1 100 Continue HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 04:51:02 GMT Server: Apache Content-Type: text/html Content-Length: 176 CMS-Server-Time: D=14222 t=1712724662049200 Connection: close ```text Body= 413 Request Entity Too Large

413 Request Entity Too Large

nginx
```
in a couple of seconds while earlier tests with old python-based server where timing out at 5minuts in CMSWEB FE. In the [most recent case](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/publication-failed/38246/7) DBS is failing that way on blocks with 31K lumis and 1MB size. Current publisher cuts blocks at 1M lumis !! and that was working https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/6670. Is the new DBS server setting this very strict limit now ? @todor-ivanov Or is this CMSWEB setting a 1MB limit on payloads ? @arooshap It seems same error as in https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/issues/11960 wich led to [this](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/8kbxjzzqf3gimbjh81fnsqrriy) short MatterMost thread. I am not sure the units in the `1m` and `3m` there, but the last error report is from Apr 10 (yesterday) I looked at recorded statistics from CRAB Publisher. Up to CRAB tasks submitted on March 26 blocks of up to 30MB were published successfully in DBS. But after that nothing 1MB or larger makes it through. Did something change with the beginning of April ? In DBS ? In CMSWEB ? I can look into making smaller blocks, but current issue is from a user who can't publish a block with 60 files. I'd rather not go to 10 files per block !! ## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-11T12:23:17Z) failed publications per hour in last 30 days clearly indicates how April is different from March. Of course user jobs are different, yet... ![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/1500f4d1-7db3-499e-bea5-60aa6a8701c1) from https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/M3Gzdv-SR?orgId=11 ## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-14T14:18:38Z) Problems persist, all blocks >1MB are failing ![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/27d11ed6-8b23-4f54-8ecd-01bce99e434d) This is not part of DBS/CMSWEB specification and I do not have a way to cut things in samller pieces. @arooshap @todor-ivanov ## Comment (arooshap, 2024-04-15T07:36:15Z) Hi @belforte, I just removed the limit contraints from the ingress in both production clusters. ## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-15T07:57:57Z) thanks a lot @arooshap ! ## Comment (todor-ivanov, 2024-04-15T09:43:40Z) hi @belforte, > Did something change with the beginning of April ? > In DBS ? In CMSWEB ? I can tell for sure, nothing has changed on April related to DBS. No extra limitations has been enforced. BTW, Did @arooshap's intervention fix the problem. I was advocating in the past (even for the WMCore issue) that the problem should be resolved by increasing the Frontend limits, but people are afraid of hitting further limitations down the chain (e.g DBS). ## Comment (arooshap, 2024-04-15T09:56:10Z) @todor-ivanov yes, it is related to the ingress limits. Just to correct something, we are not imposing any limits on our frontends. It was the nginx that we are using in the backend. The service is maintained by the CERN IT. So, by default, it was imposing the size constraints(which have now been removed). ## Comment (todor-ivanov, 2024-04-15T10:14:42Z) hi @arooshap > which have now been removed That's actually great Thanks!

this is now deprecated in HTCondor.
We should change to
```
 result = schedd.submit()
```
where `result` will be an ` htcondor.SubmitResult` object

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8336: use a Submit object, not a classAd (dagAd) as argument to schedd.submit

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-15T21:26:55Z
Closed: 2024-05-31T14:36:54Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High, Area: Code Cleanup, Area: HTCondor
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8336

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-15T21:26:55Z)

an [htcondor.Submit](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/api/htcondor.html#submitting-jobs) object should be used as first argument to `schedd.submit` in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6f65ad6a5dd413d6f4aa078aae86dd5ceb63edf5/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L543
as documented in the `submit` paragraph of [interacting with schedulers](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/api/htcondor.html#interacting-with-schedulers)
see also https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8333#issue-2239797786

Use the [syntax  of submission file](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html#submit-description-file-commands) so that description is simpler and more clear and conversion to classAd is [done](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/users-manual/submitting-a-job.html#submitting-a-job) by HTCondor

This is a bit non trivial since we need to make sure that all submission ads are properly handled, submitting a few test tasks is not enough to validate.

Hopefully DagmanSubmitter will be easier to read after this.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-29T17:11:45Z)

harder than I thought :-(

After some struggle I got to the point of submitting a dagman to the scheduler which as by design is in HOLD waiting for spool() command as in the current code
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f499fd55e4a762ada09ae07e53a78fba034cd804/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L548-L549

But I can't find a way to make `schedd.spool()` work. Documentation appears inconsistent with reality.
I have sent a mail to support
<details>
<summary>mail text</summary>

Hi. I am trying to move to new way of submitting in python bindings
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/api/htcondor.html#interacting-with-schedulers

But am facing an unexpected obstacle which I do not know how to solve.
Can you help ?

I am using bindings from HTCondor 23.7.2

Since in context of CMS CRAB we submit to remote schedulers,
I have to use

submitResult = schedd.submit(submit_object,...)
schedd.spool(the correct arg !)

So far we have been using the old format
clusterId = schedd.submit(classAd, returnAd)
schedd.spool(returnAd)

I have converted my code which used to pass a classAd object
to create a submit object and I think I getting there since
I get a SubmitResult object with the expected content
(Pdb) type(submitResult)
<class 'htcondor.htcondor.SubmitResult'>
(Pdb) submitResult.cluster()
104893441
(Pdb) submitResult.first_proc()
0
(Pdb) submitResult.num_procs()
1
Pdb) type(submitResult.clusterad())
<class 'classad.classad.ClassAd'>

But I can't find a proper argument for schedd.spool()
the documentation says:

spool(ad_list) → None :

    Spools the files specified in a list of job ClassAds to the condor_schedd.

    Parameters

        ad_list (list[ClassAds]) – A list of job descriptions; typically, this is the list returned by the jobs() method on the submit result object.
    Raises

        RuntimeError – if there are any errors.

Note the :
typically, this is the list returned by the jobs() method on the submit result object.

But the submit result object does not have a jobs() method !!

I tried
schedd.spool(submitResult.clusterad()) , but (abbreviated)
Boost error:  did not match C++ signature:

I tried with a list, but
(Pdb) schedd.spool([submitResult.clusterad()])
*** htcondor.HTCondorIOError: DCSchedd::spoolJobFiles:1:Job ad 0 did not have a proc id
(Pdb)

submitResult.clusterad() has a 'ClusterId' attribute but indeed not a ProcId nor Proc not "proc id"
(Pdb) submitResult.clusterad()['clusterid']
104893441
(Pdb) submitResult.clusterad()['procid']
*** KeyError: 'procid'
(Pdb) submitResult.clusterad()['proc']
*** KeyError: 'proc'
(Pdb) submitResult.clusterad()['proc id']
*** KeyError: 'proc id'
(Pdb)

I am out of ideas

Thanks
Stefano

</details>

Here's ToddM's answer
```
> But submitResult object does not have a jobs() method

    I'd always assumed that the documentation meant "the Submit object's jobs() method", but I'd never actually tested it; it turns out to be just a little more complicated than that.  Full example that seems to work for me follows.  (Job will go on hold because it doesn't produce the
specified output, but that makes it easier to check if everything got spooled correctly.)  Let me know if this works for you.

-- ToddM

#!/usr/env/env python3

import htcondor

collector = htcondor.Collector()
location = collector.locate(htcondor.DaemonTypes.Schedd, "azaphrael.org" )
schedd = htcondor.Schedd(location)

submit = htcondor.Submit("""
    universe = vanilla
    executable = /bin/sleep
    arguments = 1
    transfer_executable = false
    should_transfer_files = true

    transfer_input_files = /tmp/input.txt
    transfer_output_files = output.txt

    queue 1
""")

result = schedd.submit(
    submit,
    spool=True
)

wtaf = submit.jobs(
    count=result.num_procs(),
    clusterid=result.cluster(),
)
schedd.spool(list(wtaf))

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8342: use new format for periodic remove reason
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8342: use new format for periodic remove reason

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-16T14:06:01Z
Closed: 2024-09-16T08:43:20Z
Labels: Type: Question, Priority: High, Area: Code Cleanup, Area: HTCondor
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8342

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-16T14:06:01Z)

See https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSSI-113

 As of HTCondor > 9.5, the can be achieved using `SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE_NAMES` :  https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/configuration-macros.html#SYSTEM_PERIODIC_HOLD_NAMES

 Code to replace is in
 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6f65ad6a5dd413d6f4aa078aae86dd5ceb63edf5/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L161-L175

This will need changing too
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6f65ad6a5dd413d6f4aa078aae86dd5ceb63edf5/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L257-L278

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-14T08:28:33Z)

hmm... The current [documentation](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/search.html?q=periodic_remove_name&check_keywords=yes&area=default#) lists SYSTEM_PERIODIC_REMOVE_NAMES (part of schedd config) but not for the plain PERIODIC_REMOVE that we can [put in JDL](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html#submit-description-file-commands)

I can ask HTC support, but sounds like this can be closed
All in all current code is not that hard to read

Let's make a "can this be understood" test with @aspiringmind-code

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-16T08:43:20Z)

I showed the code to @aspiringmind-code and we agreed to leave it as is.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8350: add timeout for TW actions

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-24T09:40:28Z
Closed: 2024-09-19T10:08:38Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8350

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-24T09:40:28Z)

with reference to
https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-task-queued-on-command-submit-for-a-while/39714
we have no protection against the situation where TW slaves get stuck for many hours.

So far this has been rare, but we can't risk users to keep submitting stalled tasks and make system grind to halt.

Can start with e.g. 1hour timeout and monitor

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T09:54:25Z)

@novicecpp do you agree to take this once CI/CD is done ? Should not be too much work, but I do not have a specific implementation plan in mind.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T10:23:52Z)

related to #7720

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-24T12:37:24Z)

Yes. I can but not immediately after CI.
I need to go back to PyPI to make Publisher work with PyPI image.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T20:43:44Z)

PR https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8352 is related to this

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-16T08:27:20Z)

@belforte do you have any implementation idea in mind?

My idea is to kill worker process entirely if it reach timeout threshold.

There is 2 ways to achieve this:
- Use [concurrent.futures.Executor](https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html#concurrent.futures.Executor) to spawn child thread of worker process (with `max_workers=1`) and use result timeout (similar to `join()` in `multiprocessing`) as a signal to terminate the child. Simple enough, in exchange for the extra overhead of spawning threads (also, later we can refactor multiprocessing part by replacing it with concurrent.futures at MasterWorker)
- Save the timestamp of the start/end of each iteration of the worker process on MasterWorker, then calculate the timeout from the timestamp and [terminate](https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.Process.terminate) the worker process if it reaches the threshold. This requires a separate queue for each process to prevent [data corrupt from process terminated](https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#pipes-and-queues), which will add complexity on how we distributing the tasks to each process's queue. The advantage of this way is there is no extra overhead from thread spawning.

Acknowledge: Thanks Dario for the brainstorming!

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-16T08:46:22Z)

I had no ideas !
firsrt way seems better than the second. But I was hoping that we could act inside the Handler. And keep it simpler.

Something like this maybe https://python.pages.doc.ic.ac.uk/2021/lessons/decorator/03-application/02-timeout.html ?
The good thing is that relies on standard python [signal.alarm(time)](https://docs.python.org/3/library/signal.html#signal.alarm)
See also https://pypi.org/project/timeout-decorator/
(I just googled things up now).

Anyhow, both of you surely know more than me !

Unrelated, using `concurrent.futures` is appealing, but I a bit worried about the amount of work. Yet if it allows to fork a process for each new task instead of slaves which persists for days it may be worth.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-16T09:04:22Z)

I did not consider signal option because it is not work well with `multiprocessing`,  most of solution I found on the google required some hackish approach ([for example](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/40672264/python-dynamic-multiprocessing-and-signalling-issues)).

let's move enable and test to a different issue

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8351: investigate running more than 200 tasks on one scheduler

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-24T10:18:45Z
Closed: 2026-04-13T10:29:30Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Medium, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8351

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-24T10:18:45Z)

* it is an old limit, current hardware may support more
* as far as Stefano knows, it is controlled by this in `/etc/condor/config.d/82_cms_schedd_crabschedd_generic.config`
```
START_SCHEDULER_UNIVERSE = (TotalSchedulerJobsRunning < 200) && ((ShadowsRunning is undefined) || (ShadowsRunning < .95*$(MAX_JOBS_RUNNING)))
```
* Stefano tried, and failed, to increase by adding a modified `START_SCHEDULER_UNIVERSE` in `/etc/condor/config.d/99_local_tweaks.config` with
```
START_SCHEDULER_UNIVERSE = (TotalSchedulerJobsRunning < 250) && ((ShadowsRunning is undefined) || (ShadowsRunning < .95*$(MAX_JOBS_RUNNING)))
```

TO DO
- [x] find why adding to `99_local_tweaks` failed even after schedd stop/start given that
 ```
belforte@vocms0106/config.d> condor_config_val START_SCHEDULER_UNIVERSE
(TotalSchedulerJobsRunning < 250) && ((ShadowsRunning is undefined) || (ShadowsRunning < .95*15000))
```

- [x] missing that. Try by editing directly `82_cms_schedd_crabschedd_generic`
- [x] overload one production scheduler with real work and see if we can push further

- [x] decide on new policy if any, knowing that
   * a larger limit may give more flexibility to deal with short-lived crisis
   *having too many tasks active at same time will make them run slower as they compete for CPU

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2026-01-19T09:13:04Z)

The trick was to change MAX_RUNNING_SCHEDULER_JOBS_PER_OWNER as well, as suggested by Marco.
vocms0120 was overloaded and the limit set to 250 was hit on 19/11/2025.
Policy can be changed going forward if need arises. For now, 200 limit is ok.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-19T10:06:13Z)

Well... we know how to increase the limit now, but have no data to tell us if we can run with a higher limit or not. Still need to "overload one production scheduler with real work and see if we can push further", when we tried Nov/Dec 2025 we had to stop due to full spool disk, but do not know for certain if the disk overuse was due to too many tasks vs. too many tasks in a short time or whether we may have problems with memory or I/O. Which makes this more challenging than a simple policy change.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-13T10:46:25Z)

thanks for closing @aspiringmind-code , but wouldn't it be better to close with a summary of the investigation ? Can we run more than 200 tasks, or not ?

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2026-04-13T13:03:00Z)

@belforte Oops clicked close issue instead of close with comment.
We tried to increase max-running-dagmans to 250 and run the VM "continuously", but it looks like that we hit I/O limits on condor spool disk.  The sched vocms0197 was suffering from high load and condor daemon had been (automatically) restarting with frequent scheduler crashes and loss of corresponding monitoring.
Best to stick to 200 limit.

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-24T17:03:25Z)

#### WEB_DIR:
in https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/cleanup_home_grid.sh?ref_type=heads
we remove directories last changed  60 days ago or more
```
find /home/grid -maxdepth 2 -mindepth 2 -type d -ctime +60 > /tmp/oldtasks
```
#### SPOOL_DIR
in https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/clean_condor_spool_dir.sh?ref_type=heads
we remove 14 days after task is over
By the way, we do not cleanup HC after 7 days since now it runs with owner `crabtw` like everything else, need to filter on e.g. `crab_userhn` or (better) on `CRAB_UserRole = "production"`
```bash

echo --- SPOOL DIR clean up
echo ----- HC files clean up
condor_q -all -const 'TaskType=?="ROOT" && Owner=?="cmsprd" && (time() - EnteredCurrentStatus > 7 * 86400)' -af Iwd | xargs rm -rfv
echo ---
echo "--- Clean up finished tasks or hold tasks if their status did not changed last 14d."

condor_q -all -const 'TaskType=?="ROOT" && (JobStatus=?=4 || JobStatus=?=5) && (time() - EnteredCurrentStatus > 14 * 86400)' -af Iwd | xargs rm -rfv
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-26T15:41:56Z)

hmm... I got it all wrong !!!

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-26T15:58:02Z)

the way things work is:
1. JobCleanup.py takes care of task end-of-life removing them from the queue and deleting spool and web dirs
2. The purpose of `cleanup_home_grid.sh` is unclear, possibly was put there to catch anything that slipped through, that's why it uses a safe 60d threshold
3. The purpose of `clean_condor_spool_dir.sh` is similarly unclear. It removes SPOOL_DIR very soon (two weeks afer task completed) and maybe it was put/kept there to take care of early cleanup of HammerCloud, which is fine, but should not be mixed

So I'd rather say that:
* HammerCloud nees to removed earlier, best would be to set an earlier `CRAB_TaskEndTime` classAd when we submit them
 and make no changes to `JobCleanup.py`. We can do some emergency cleanup by hand in the meanwhile.
* The reason to keep SPOOL_DIR around is to allow resubmission of failed tasks which are in HOLD status. It would make sense to remove e.g. job and postjob logs, but files needed for resubmission must be kept.

OTOH I am puzzled that we do not see problems because of early disappearance of SPOOL_DIR. Something more to understand?

In a way I am remembering, re-discovering, re-proposing the "old" plan from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/4681#issuecomment-302336451
!!

OK, Finally I found it in https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/JobCleanup.py?ref_type=heads#L56
```python
    homeDir="/home/grid/%s/%s"%(crabDag.task["Owner"], crabDag.task["Crab_ReqName"])
```
Now all tasks run with `Owner = crabtw` !! So that variable always points to non-existing directory names and all WEB_DIRs are only catched by the fall-back `cleanup_home_dir.sh` after 60 days.

Need to change to

```python
    homeDir="/home/grid/%s/%s"%(crabDag.task["CRAB_UserHN"], crabDag.task["Crab_ReqName"])
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8354: add a per-user policy to tape recall
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8354: add a per-user policy to tape recall

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-24T17:13:20Z
Closed: 2024-07-16T16:25:48Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High, Status: In Progress, Status: On Hold
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8354

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-24T17:13:20Z)

last week two users managed to put tape recall requests for a total of about 7PB

We can't deliver that "timely" nor can they process all that data. Clearly they do not know what they are doing.

We want to put a limit  on how much each individual user can request at any given time, i.e. until all of her/his previous requests are satisfied.

We had an initial discussion in DM Ops MatterMost, moving here to converge on a concrete proposal and implement it.

@dynamic-entropy

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-24T20:28:29Z)

Rahul, currently each rule that we create has a comment like this
```
Comment:                    Recall 605 GBytes for user: sleontsi dataset: /Charmonium/Run2016E-21Feb2020_UL2016_HIPM-v1/MINIAOD
```
Format is fixed becasue we use it for our monitoring

I am open to change to (or add as) a rule metadata.

I think that what we need is a small database of how much a given user has already in recall in order to make a decision whether to accept a request or not.

Can you summarize how you do this for automatic recall ?

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2024-05-03T17:55:20Z)

Hello, Stefano
I saw your mail. Did they just repeat the jobs that triggered the recalls?
Does this need to be taken urgently? I wanted to do some tests on my own to pitch a concrete proposal before saying anything, hence the delay.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-03T18:36:58Z)

Simply I had not done anything until now. I think he will be careful. But we do not want to continuously watch things.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-10T14:36:48Z)

On Hold, waiting for a proposal from @dynamic-entropy on how to track usage by user.
As a reminder currently limits to each request are applied here
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5ca7cae6d4ebe374f945eb46a7768a64c2b24fa2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L474

And currently those are in English:
* tiers in `['AOD', 'AODSIM', 'MINIAOD', 'MINIAODSIM', 'NANOAOD', 'NANOAODSIM']` are recalled no matter how big
* other data tiers are recalled if recall request is <50TB
   * users can indicate a list of blocks which fits if dataset is too big

Beyond that the old plan was to have a global quota cap on `crab_tape_recall` account. Couple of years ago Nick told me that this cap was there but for technical reasons was not implemented in Rucio. I do not know any details on that.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-15T14:18:05Z)

Stefano and Rahul had a chat. Proposal:

* tape recall rules will be created with `account=username` and `activity="Analysis Tape Recall"`  and `askApproval=True`
* Rahul will make RUcio accept that activity.
* Rahul will make sure that only `crab_tape_recall` account  can create rules in this activity and they will be automatically approved. This will avoid that the rule is charged to the user  Rucio quota on the selected RSE
* CRAB will ask Rucio for all rule belonging to the user wich this activity and compute the overall size (Rahul has code example to do it https://github.com/dmwm/CMSRucio/blob/5469bb52226ce9cde59eb7b538fcb96cde386a1f/src/policy/CMSRucioPolicy/permission.py#L179-L186 )
* CRAB will then apply the limit and communicate to user accordingly
* per-user-limit will be set in coordination with Comp.Ops. We can start with 200TB total

we prefer to do the check in CRAB code because Rucio does not have a way (yet) to communicate to the user what the usage is etc. Only a yes/no.

If computing the total size for a user takes too long, we will reconsider

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-16T09:33:25Z)

implementation tasks in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioActions.py
- [x]  add the quota check in DBSDataDiscovery/executeTapeRecallPolicy ?
- [x] add user limit in ServerUtilities with all other constants ? Or in TW config like e.g. `maxTierToBlockRecallSize` ? i.e. in https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb#L107-108
- [x] pass `activity` as arguments to `createOrReuseRucioRule` . Account can be selected inside there since `self.username` is available
- [x] make sure that rule is removed once data is recalled so that user regains their quota. Modify TapeRecall recurring action. Now data will be locked as soon as task is submitted, letting rule to expire in 1h is fine.

Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8364

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-04-26T16:38:21Z)

in https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/JobCleanup.py?ref_type=heads#L56
```python
    homeDir="/home/grid/%s/%s"%(crabDag.task["Owner"], crabDag.task["Crab_ReqName"])
```

But now all tasks run with `Owner = crabtw` !! So that variable always points to non-existing directory names and all WEB_DIRs are only catched by the fall-back `cleanup_home_dir.sh` after 60 days.

Need to change to

```python
    homeDir="/home/grid/%s/%s"%(crabDag.task["CRAB_UserHN"], crabDag.task["Crab_ReqName"])
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-12T21:33:19Z)

The reasong is that `optional=True` does not work for `inputdata` in e.g.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/19b179e7708b84731c11df9948039211852de1a1/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py#L375
because the in cases like this (or fpr privateMC) the client puts in the URL "nothing" `&inputdata=&` but the REST codes sees a empty string `''` as value, not `None` or no keywork, so the `optional` in the validation does not do anything https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/e4628ce9ab25f5015b71197a42eb09d630286318/src/python/WMCore/REST/Validation.py#L79
```python
def _validate_one(argname, param, safe, checker, optional, *args):
    val = param.kwargs.get(argname, None)
    if optional and val == None:
        safe.kwargs[argname] = None
    else:
        safe.kwargs[argname] = checker(argname, val, *args)
        del param.kwargs[argname]
```

I am fixing the REST now. But I think the Client should simply omit the `inputdata` parame in the URL instead of specifyiin w/o a value. But I suspect that there are palces in the code where that `''` is used :-(  Maybe there was a conscious decision to have an empty string in Oracle instead of `NULL`

it will help me to recap how things work in more detail:
* PublisherRucio
   * uses one SQL query in filetransfersdb to find all files with `tm_publish=1` and `tm_publication_status=NEW` and set `tm_publication_status=ACQUIRED`. Then it select all the `ACQUIRED` and group by task.
   * forks one slave for each task
   * the slave goes through all files, looks for `tm_block_complete = OK` and creates a list of corresponding block names
   * then with same list of iles, fills a list of files for each completed block, retrieves FMD for each file and publishes the block

* PostJob
  * if jobs is successful[1],  hand it to ASO [2]. Then polls ASO status every 30min [3]
  * when transfer is completed [4]
  * upload input and output FileMetaData [5]
  * set in `transfersdb` : `publish=1` and `publication_status=NEW` [6]
  * exit and do not ask Dagman to rerun the PJ [7]

So **I was wrong** in  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8376#issuecomment-2124500392 . FMD are only uploaded when PJ detects "transfer complete", and files can't be published until FMD are available, so we can  not trigger Publisher before PostJob has completed.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8388: bug in FMD retrieve
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8388: bug in FMD retrieve

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-09T14:17:35Z
Closed: 2024-05-09T15:20:13Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done, Priority: Medium, Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8388

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-05-09T14:17:35Z)

this line
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/20aaf162e334451db4a74d88e790995892fe47be/src/python/CRABInterface/DataFileMetadata.py#L68
is likely broken since ever and surely makes no sense

It should be
```python
 'created': str(row.created),
```
where `row.created` is an object of type `datetime`

Now it returns instead a `CRABInterface.RESTBaseAPI._FakeLOB object` which makes it impossible to compare different ways of retrieving FMD since it is a pointer to a location in memory.

Clearly this value is never used in python code. It indicates the time the row was inserted in the DB and AFICT it is only used in these SQL queries
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/20aaf162e334451db4a74d88e790995892fe47be/src/python/Databases/FileMetaDataDB/Oracle/FileMetaData/FileMetaData.py#L112-L113
which are activated by an HTTP call with `delete` method
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/20aaf162e334451db4a74d88e790995892fe47be/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileMetadata.py#L110-L113

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/20aaf162e334451db4a74d88e790995892fe47be/src/python/CRABInterface/DataFileMetadata.py#L134-L144

used in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/FMDCleaner.py
which we do not run anymore.

All of this is  likely obsolete since we user partitions and partition dropping to cleanup the DB.

State: closed

Closed: 2025-04-11T13:50:20Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8394

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-05-10T14:42:38Z)

basically we want to be able to count running DAG's per user in order to do some task scheduling #7485

hmm.. maybe we can leave Task status alone and e.g. define later how and when exactly to call it FAILED but add a column with `Dagman Status` ?

In any case this should be one API call in cache_statup.py

Need to be able to also catch FAILED->SUBMITTED transition at crab resubmit time.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-10T14:44:33Z)

FYI @mapellidario , please comment as you see fit

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-06T17:44:50Z)

Best seems a new status column, imitating what `crab status` does atm
```
Status on the CRAB server:	SUBMITTED
Status on the scheduler:	SUBMITTED
```
leave it to `crab status` to combine, but mosty move to the AP all the dag status parsing which now happens in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/5079df8a21cd6acd9768d257fb390551cada6e1d/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/status.py#L350-L411

DAG Status will be `RUNNING|COMPLETED|FAILED`

This leave current task status untouched so there is no danger of messing with NEW/SUBMITTED/RESUBMITTING etc.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-06T17:46:03Z)

OTOH understanding what `crab status` does here is way from easy. First time that I try. And I have forgotten how exactly `cache_status.py` works inside the job_wrapper.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8401: PyPI release image/pipeline
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8401: PyPI release image/pipeline

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-14T08:10:24Z
Closed: 2024-06-24T10:50:56Z
Labels: Area: CI/CD, PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8401

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T08:10:24Z)

This is the part of [the new PyPI image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7560) and [the new automated pipeline](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8267).

The release image is the image that we use in prod. The only different between dev image and release image is the version string that service can use for report to monitoring system.

We are not commit the version string into source code but alter it in RPM build process instead:
- For REST, `version` variable is inside [src/python/CRABInterface/\_\_init\_\_.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c69980662cbd4fa76e3801b6f3085856032743d6/src/python/CRABInterface/__init__.py) ([crabserver.spec](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/blob/a5a0b8640d227a432388285b8c0a11dfd5c0706d/crabserver.spec#L35))
- For TW, `version` variable is inside [src/python/TaskWorker/\_\_init\_\_.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c69980662cbd4fa76e3801b6f3085856032743d6/src/python/TaskWorker/__init__.py) ([crabtaskworker.spec](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/blob/a5a0b8640d227a432388285b8c0a11dfd5c0706d/crabtaskworker.spec#L38))

If we build and deploy PyPI image from current master branch in production, we will get version report from our monitor as `development`, not proper version string like `v3.240305`.
So pre-release step is needed before building images.

One more thing is the image tag. It is better to differentiate between RPM and the new PyPI image. Also, CMSWEB requires the tag to have a `-stable` suffix to set the cleanup rules for non-stable tags and retain the latest stable tag forever.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T08:17:39Z)

@mapellidario @belforte, I would like to ask for consensus on the image tag.

I propose to suffix the image tag with `.pypi-stable`. For example, the image tag of [v3.240510](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/releases/tag/v3.240510) would be `v3.240510.pypi-stable`.

Do you guys agree?

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-05-14T08:21:15Z)

if we plan about dropping the "pypi" portion sooner or later, then yes I agree :)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T09:36:55Z)

why do we need `pypi` at all ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T09:41:17Z)

To prevent confusion during migration from RPM to PyPI in production.

I plan to still build RPM image until PyPI image is running in prod for at least 2 weeks.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T09:44:00Z)

but do we have `-stable` for RPM built images ? Maybe change tag name for those which will disappear ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T10:07:48Z)

> but do we have -stable for RPM built images ?

No. We never do it. It is not enforced by the system or anything. Now we have an automated pipeline, so we can do it automatically (to be fair, we can add more lines of code to Jenkins to automate this too).

> Maybe change tag name for those which will disappear ?

Sorry, no. This require more work to do so.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T11:19:13Z)

So no need to add pipy. -stable already tells that image comes from new pipeline

On May 14, 2024 12:08 PM, Thanayut Seethongchuen ***@***.***> wrote:

but do we have -stable for RPM built images ?

No. We never do it. It is not enforced by the system or anything. Now we have an automated pipeline, so we can do it automatically (to be fair, we can add more lines of code to Jenkins to automate this too).

Maybe change tag name for those which will disappear ?

Sorry, no. This require more work to do so.

—
Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub<https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8401#issuecomment-2109802868>, or unsubscribe<https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/AAOAVWOESE5LZAII6DPHJJTZCHPATAVCNFSM6AAAAABHVVAKWGVHI2DSMVQWIX3LMV43OSLTON2WKQ3PNVWWK3TUHMZDCMBZHAYDEOBWHA>.
You are receiving this because you were mentioned.Message ID: ***@***.***>

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T12:03:23Z)

Thanks for comments, Stefano, Dario.
From now on, the image tag of the new PyPI image will be `v3.YYMMDD-stable`.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T12:12:35Z)

For the pipeline part,

- 2 new stages
    - `pre_release`: Between `prepare_env` and `build_docker` to alter the `__init__.py` like we do with RPM build. Use CI cache to store change between stage.
    -  `release`: After the `check_testsuite` stage to retag the image.
- New tool call [crane](https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/README.md) are used for register the release tag to docker registry. It pull image from that built in previous stage, re-tag, and then push the new tag. Compare to Kaniko that need to rebuild the whole image everytime (see [GoogleContainerTools/kaniko#676](https://www.github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko/issues/676#issuecomment-597504724))
    - It is small binary file that can copy/paste to [buildtools](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/cicd/buildtools) and works out off the box.
- ~~`FORCE_RELEASE` variable will be used to skip  `deploy`, `run_testsuite` and `check_testsuite`.~~ Trigger CI with `SKIP_DEPLOY` and use release tag (this is simpler in CI config compare to add more variables).

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T14:14:06Z)

I am curious, how is `crane` here  different from a tiny script with three docker commands ? We should avoid binaries in GH as much as possible. Not all nice tools are still working 3 years in the future.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T15:05:19Z)

`crane` can run in userspace like kaniko, i.e., it can run inside any container.
I already thought about your concern and have the same solution as you said: simply switch back to the docker command.

But, it is OK to use docker command because we own the runner and have root access to use docker command. I switch to that.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T15:10:47Z)

> crane can run in userspace like kaniko, i.e., it can run inside any container.

:open_mouth:   I am talking about things which I do not understand, sorry. How does the runner get access to kaniko, I vaguely remember that you are not using the CERN-deployed one yet.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T15:35:44Z)

kaniko is a binary inside a container that can build images without calling the Docker daemon. Remember that calling the `docker` command means you ask the Docker daemon to do something; this requires privilege equivalent to root.

We run kaniko like we run CRAB REST in Kubernetes, no direct access to node resources, no root power.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T16:02:49Z)

yes, all stuff that I do not understand enough to have an educated opinion. Forget all I said on this topic. For running docker in the VM's we use unix group which does not give root-like privileges. We can still put binaries in a public container in S3, if crane can't be downloaded on the fly like in https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/blob/main/cmd/crane/README.md#using-with-gitlab (IIUC)

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-06-24T10:50:56Z)

Docs are done. Please take a look.

Explanation: https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-cicd/gitlab/pipelines/release.html
Tutorial: https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-cicd/gitlab/tutorial.html#running-the-release-pipeline

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8402: Reviewing how we bind mount the TW container
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8402: Reviewing how we bind mount the TW container

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-14T10:26:40Z
Closed: 2024-05-17T08:41:36Z
Labels: PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8402

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T10:26:40Z)

Before deploying the new [runContainer.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c69980662cbd4fa76e3801b6f3085856032743d6/src/script/Container/runContainer.sh) version, which requires a configuration change because of a path change inside the container, I would like to review all of the binding mounts we use for the TW container.

Stefano pointed out [in this PR comment](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8368#issuecomment-2098503494) that there are too many bind mounts appearing on runContainer.sh script. Here is the the list of bind mount when we deploy the Publisher_schedd:

The first half, the host's working directory:
- `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/cfg:/data/srv/Publisher/cfg`
- `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/logs:/data/srv/Publisher/logs`
- `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/PublisherFiles:/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles`
- `-v /data/srv/tmp/:/data/srv/tmp/`

As Stefano suggested, mounting the `/data/container/${SERVICE}` as a single path will be easier to manage, and the application already supports custom paths via service configuration files.

The second half, the host environments:
- `-v /data/certs/:/data/certs/`
- `-v /data/container/:/data/hostdisk/`
- `-v /cvmfs:/cvmfs:shared`
- `-v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/`
- `-v /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem:/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem`
- `-v /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem:/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt'`

This part is clear enough why we need it. However, the hostdisk (`-v /data/container/:/data/hostdisk/`) only for provide Filebeat configuration to Filebeat process inside container. Filebeat is not is not bundle in the new PyPI image and there is no plan to bundle it in the future.

EDITED: switch `-v /data/certs/:/data/certs/` to second half.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T10:39:16Z)

My proposal:

- Mount `/data/container/${SERVICE}` to `/data/container/${SERVICE}/hostdisk`
- Change configuration to `/data/container/${SERVICE}/hostdisk`, including cfg, logs, extra dir like `PublisherFiles`, tmp.
- Remove hostdisk, move Filebeat to Puppet.

The final bind mount should be:
- `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd:/data/srv/Publisher/hostdisk`
- `-v /data/certs/:/data/certs/`
- `-v /cvmfs:/cvmfs:shared`
- `-v /etc/grid-security/:/etc/grid-security/`
- `-v /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem:/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem`
- `-v /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem:/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt'`

@belforte What do you think?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-14T15:43:28Z)

I like it. Let's add a `/data/container/${SERVICE}/scratch` directory with write-all to facilitate file sharing to/from the container. I have been using hostidsk/tmp for that, creating it by hand.

What do you think about removing the last entry and replace it with a symlink in the container like it is in the host ? It is a bit wierd to mount twice the same file. I am not sure which way is "less obscure".  Maybe as simple as "Stefano does not understand PKI !!"

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-14T16:08:39Z)

> Stefano does not understand PKI !!

It is understandable. I do not know it myself. Different distribution/library/application use different path.
But keep both mount is better IMO. Mount same file for 2 different path cause no harm in future, and keep this responsible for "ops" unless we completely sure why we need both and tell "dev" to fix (do symlink in Dockerfile step).

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8411:  AdjustSites.py race condition
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8411:  AdjustSites.py race condition

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-16T06:13:02Z
Closed: 2024-05-16T16:32:02Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8411

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-05-16T06:13:02Z)

There is race condition where [AdjustSites.py#L393](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/d4b13331e9d5d5ab4656d0ff58beb67f787e64a7/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L393) is executed before TW could set task status to `SUBMITTED`

For example, with this task [240514_130645:crabint1_crab_rucio_transfers_20240514_150644](https://cmsweb-test12.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/240514_130645%3Acrabint1_crab_rucio_transfers_20240514_150644). The task status msg reported boostrap failure:

```
The task failed to bootstrap on the Grid scheduler. Crab resubmit will not work. Please send an e-mail to <email>.
Hold reason: 'This dagman does not match task information in TASKS DB'
```

When look at the `adjust_out.txt` at `vocms059:/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/4987/0/cluster9594987.proc0.subproc0/adjust_out.txt`, the logs reported:

```
2024-05-14 13:06:59.196789: Task status on DB: QUEUED, clusterID on DB: None, schedd name on DB: <email>;
clusterID on condor ads: 9594987, schedd name on condor ads: <email>
2024-05-14 13:06:59.196845: Exiting AdjustSites because this dagman does not match task information in TASKS DB
```

The task log from TW (`crab-dev-tw03:/data/container/TaskWorker/logs/tasks/crabint1/240514_130645:crabint1_crab_rucio_transfers_20240514_150644.log`):

```
2024-05-14 13:06:56,473:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Trying to submit task 240514_130645:crabint1_crab_rucio_transfers_20240514_150644 to schedd <email> for the 0 time.
2024-05-14 13:06:56,473:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Getting schedd object
2024-05-14 13:06:56,479:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Got schedd object
2024-05-14 13:06:56,511:INFO:DagmanSubmitter:User crabint1 mapped to local groups {'/cms', '/cms/production'}.
2024-05-14 13:06:56,511:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Finally submitting to the schedd
2024-05-14 13:06:57,266:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Condor cluster ID returned from submit is: 9594987
2024-05-14 13:06:57,267:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Submission finished
2024-05-14 13:06:57,267:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Pushing information centrally {'workflow': '240514_130645:crabint1_crab_rucio_transfers_20240514_150644', 'status': 'SUBMITTED', 'subresource': 'success', 'clusterid': 9594987}
2024-05-14 13:07:00,002:INFO:DagmanSubmitter:Summary of schedd failures/successes for slave process 1 (PID 22):
        crab3@vocms059.cern.ch:
                Number of successes: 1
                Number of failures:  0
Last successful submission: ClusterId 9594987 submitted to schedd <email>
```

Looking at timestamp, there are 3 seconds gap between dag submitted and update task status to rest, and AdjustSites.py error's timestamp is between this gap.

It never occurred to me when submitting with Jenkins or manual, but it happened occasionally when running the Gitlab-CI pipeline. It was very frustrating.

Should we add retry in AdjustSites or simply delay boostrap for 1 min?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-16T09:30:38Z)

Puzzling. It should be extremely rare that AdjustSites.py runs within a few seconds from submission. I have seen this in user reports rarely and usually in situation where uploading to REST fails and needs to be retried. A small delay like you suggest would not fix that.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-16T14:57:07Z)

Let me review the original motivation for this in #6151 and #6145

At first sight the only really safe way is (as usual) the one Brian suggested in #6151, but it complicates TW a lot.

OTOH, we have discussed to introduce new task statuses already: WAITING between NEW and HOLDING (which means "grabbed by TW") and COMPLETED/FAILED to signal that DAGMAN stopped #8394

So maybe adding ACTIVE (or call it RUNNING) is not too bad.

I propose to add a 30sec/1min sleep to avoid the "next condor schedd cycle happens instantly as soon as dag is submitted" and re-evaluate the above proposal as a better alternative to current check in AdjustSites

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-22T09:00:14Z)

As to catching the fact that slave aborts and task is left in QUEUED, the only info we have atm are these lines in `nohup.out` i.e. the `stdout/stderr` or the master worker:
```
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 TaskManager]$ cat nohup.out
[...usual messages about jwt and OpenSSL..]
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'boost::python::error_already_set'
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'boost::python::error_already_set'
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 TaskManager]$
```
We can possibly monitor-for or otherwise discover dead workers, but a restart will not fix (the QUEUED tasks will be processed again) and checking logs to find which task was being processed and what went wrong will take a lot of human time.

One way I can think f now it to change MasterWorker to fork a separate process for each task, up to a maximun number of concurrent ones. Like we do in PublisherMaster. Instead of the current fixed pool of slaves which get work from a shared queue.
That's quite a change, but may help in other ways too.

Another way is to check if slave is alive  inside the master loop and record somewhere the current task of a slave.
I do not know how to do it atm, but could be possible. TW slaves are instances of `multiprocessing.Process` like the MasterPublisher ones for which we already use the `is_alive`method

Checking on heatch of TW slave is something we "need to do" since ever, urgency comes and go as problems which make them die come and go.

@novicecpp I will welcome your suggestions
@mapellidario  I will welcome your suggestions

!!! Sorry Marco Mambelli if you were spammed.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-05-22T13:16:02Z)

I had experience with `subprocess.Popen`, I never really used multiproessing, so it took me a while to come up with a proper suggestion.

Long story short: I think that in `Worker.py` we need to regularly loop over every process in `self.pool` and:

- `p.join(0.1)`: join with a timeout, see [1]. if does not block forever, it blocks at maximum for `0.1` seconds, if the process is still running nothing will happen, if the process finished, then `p.is_alive()` and `p.exitcode` are updated
- `p.is_alive()`: this returns a consistent result only after a join!
- if it is not alive, check the exitcode. if it is not zero, remove this process from the pool and add a new one.

<details><summary> Example, that provides a longer explaination </summary>

```python
import multiprocessing
import time
import os
import signal

def worker(x, qout, pids):
    print(f"pid={os.getpid()}; input={x}")
    pids.put(os.getpid())
    time.sleep(10)
    qout.put(x*x)

def main():
    inputs = list(range(1,6))
    qin = multiprocessing.Queue()
    for i in inputs:
        qin.put(i)
    qout = multiprocessing.Queue()
    pids = multiprocessing.Queue()
    pool = []
    for _ in range(qin.qsize()):
        x = qin.get()
        p = multiprocessing.Process(target=worker, args = (x, qout, pids))
        p.start()
        pool.append(p)
    print("started the processes")
    pkill = pids.get()
    print("about to kill: ", pkill)
    os.kill(pkill, signal.SIGKILL)
    print("check if a process died")
    for p in pool:
        print(f" died(0)? pid={p.pid}; alive={p.is_alive()}; exitcode={p.exitcode}")
        p.join(timeout=0.1)
        print(f" died(1)? pid={p.pid}; alive={p.is_alive()}; exitcode={p.exitcode}")
    print("wait until all processes finish")
    for p in pool:
        p.join()
        print(f" finished? pid={p.pid}; alive={p.is_alive()}; exitcode={p.exitcode}")
    print("processes finished. results:")
    for _ in range(qout.qsize()):
        print(" ", qout.get())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

output

```plaintext
> python main.py
pid=564448; input=1
pid=564449; input=2
pid=564451; input=3
started the processes
pid=564453; input=4
about to kill:  564448
check if a process died
 died(0)? pid=564448; alive=True; exitcode=None
pid=564455; input=5
 died(1)? pid=564448; alive=False; exitcode=-9
 died(0)? pid=564449; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(1)? pid=564449; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(0)? pid=564451; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(1)? pid=564451; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(0)? pid=564453; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(1)? pid=564453; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(0)? pid=564455; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(1)? pid=564455; alive=True; exitcode=None
wait until all processes finish
 finished? pid=564448; alive=False; exitcode=-9
 finished? pid=564449; alive=False; exitcode=0
 finished? pid=564451; alive=False; exitcode=0
 finished? pid=564453; alive=False; exitcode=0
 finished? pid=564455; alive=False; exitcode=0
processes finished. results:
  4
  9
  16
  25
```

notice the lines:

```plaintext
 died(0)? pid=564448; alive=True; exitcode=None
 died(1)? pid=564448; alive=False; exitcode=-9
```

this means the before the join the value of `is_alive()` can not really be trusted, it can be outdated!

</details>

[1] https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.Process.join

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-22T13:47:44Z)

I think that `is_alive` can be trusted but you need to put some delay between these lines to give the process time to die
```
 os.kill(pkill, signal.SIGKILL)
    print("check if a process died")
    for p in pool:
        print(f" died(0)? pid={p.pid}; alive={p.is_alive()}; exitcode={p.exitcode}")
```
I added 1 sec sleep and it is OK, if I am not mistaken.

all in all, I use `is_alive` in Publisher and works even w/o `join`

Sorry if I was not clear, I want feedback on a plan. Not converge on all implementation details right away. I know how to start processes, I am not sure how exactly to change the Worker.py code which we did not touch "since ever" w/o too much risk. And I do not know a good way to tell which task was being worked on when process. crashed

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-05-22T14:00:11Z)

If the plan is "let's invest time to make sure that we detect dead workers", then I am all in.

if you need help with a plan for " a good way to tell which task was being worked on when process. crashed" or "I am not sure how exactly to change the Worker.py code which we did not touch "since ever" w/o too much risk", then sorry i am not sure how to do it without giving feedback that will be rejected as "implementation details"

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-22T14:05:26Z)

in other words: it will be a bit of work and require a lot of testing. If we decide to do it, let's open a new issue and discuss details there.

Adding detection of dead workers e.g. in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/40a796ffe3d1c7b1b2cddf6a6e74c3b08e2b5a3a/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L246
by adding an `is_alive` check should be easy and as long as we simply record a message, safe !

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-23T05:01:59Z)

What's about handling the task that causes the child's process to crash?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-23T05:20:45Z)

> One way I can think f now it to change MasterWorker to fork a separate process for each task, up to a maximun number of concurrent ones. Like we do in PublisherMaster. Instead of the current fixed pool of slaves which get work from a shared queue.

I support this idea, also solve https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8350.

We can divide into 2 steps, first is wrap the [work()](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/40a796ffe3d1c7b1b2cddf6a6e74c3b08e2b5a3a/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L99) in `Worker.py` to execute in grandchild process. If this work well, refactor the code at MasterWorker to spawn child each task

One concern is about performance. It will fork grandchild for every task, which costs a lot of CPU overhead.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-05-23T09:16:17Z)

It's also true that TW actions take at least a few seconds, spawning a new process for every task may not be a that much more cpu usage in the grand scheme of things

[1] https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/cbpwWLPIR?orgId=11

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-23T13:44:33Z)

we discussed in the meeting and agreed on Wa's suggestion and can go straight for forking one child to handle each task and take care of timeout at same time. Will open ad-hoc issue

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-23T13:45:56Z)

I am closing this on:
* if HTCondor raises an exception, it is handled properly already
* if HTCondor causes an abort (like in this case) it is the same as "worked died for out of memory or any accident" and we deal with it in new issue
