title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8429: Rucio-ASO should properly handle job/task termination
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8429: Rucio-ASO should properly handle job/task termination

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-23T14:15:16Z
Closed: 2025-05-26T14:18:53Z
Labels: Status: Done, RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8429

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-05-23T14:15:16Z)

properly handle things when
* PostJob fails a job after ASO timeout (7 days currently)
* crab kill command is sent

ASO should cleanup DID's in Rucio and make sure that open blocks are closed so that files properly transferred get published.

After quite some pondering and a little testing, I have settled on the following strategy:

- [x] do not allow anymore resubmission of killed tasks [CMSTalk1](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/coming-changes-to-crab-client/124722/1) [CMSTalk2](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/deprecating-resubmission-of-killed-crab-tasks/124723) #9075
- [x] `crab kill` does a `condor_rm` of all task DAGs, instead of`condor_hold` #9076
- [x] `cache_status.py` detects when DAG's have been killed or otherwise terminated and writes an `overallDagStatus` in `status_cache.json`
- [x] ASO-Rucio reads `status_cache.json` and uses  `overallDagStatus` to decide if to close current dataset
    - [x]  that allows to increase number of files and elapsed time before closing a dataset, to be like Publisher_schedd
- [x] kill, not hold, DAGs when `CRAB_TaskEndTime` is reached #9077
- [x] let PostJob run for as long as needed #9078
- [x] look into a way to defer PostJob for a longer time when waiting on Rucio since days. #9079

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T08:25:22Z)

trikier than I thought.

It is not possible to resubmit jobs once they reached the transfer status, once a file replica is inserted in Rucio a new file with same name can not be added anymore (reminder: Rucio stores permanently the checksum associated to a LFN and our files contain timestamps so checksum is different if same file is created again with same content).

I start to lean to let PJ wait on Rucio until task life time is expired or task is killed.
We can not fail them unless we have a way to prevent a resubmission.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T10:15:57Z)

So let's start with `crab kill`.
**We currently allow tasks to be resubmitted after `crab kill`. But in this case it must be forbidden. We can not risk that a job which had reached the `transferring` status is resubmitted.**

And then about PostJob
**since jobs in transferring can not be resubmitted, do not stop PostJob after 7 days, let it run until Task is terminated/completed, i.e. Rucio eventually succeeds or task is killed or task reaches end of life**

* I need to review what exactly happens when task reaches end of life. Dagman is going to be held[1] but..what does it mean in terms of dag status ? (well, same for kill, that also holds the dag). I see one example of Help dagman which reports FAILED status, but better be sure.
* I have asked HTCondor support https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2025-May/msg00035.shtml

[1]
```console
belforte@vocms0106/~> condor_q 114458146.0

-- Schedd: <email> : <188.184.80.88:4080?... @ 05/13/25 23:19:37
 ID           OWNER            SUBMITTED     RUN_TIME ST PRI SIZE CMD
114458146.0   crabtw          5/13 08:41   0+14:38:30 R  10   0.7 condor_dagman -p 0 -f -l . -Lockfile RunJobs1.su

Total for query: 0 jobs; 0 completed, 0 removed, 0 idle, 0 running, 0 held, 0 suspended
Total for all users: 57740 jobs; 29631 completed, 2343 removed, 19220 idle, 6546 running, 0 held, 0 suspended

belforte@vocms0106/~> condor_q 114458146.0 -l|grep -i period
PeriodicHold = time() > CRAB_TaskEndTime
belforte@vocms0106/~>
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T13:18:35Z)

Best seems to disable resubmission of killed tasks in the REST, modifying
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73a84b54d50a4c1fb11fdcf8212a2503618cb7d3/src/python/CRABInterface/DataWorkflow.py#L285-L286

Which will  make these redundant
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/73a84b54d50a4c1fb11fdcf8212a2503618cb7d3/src/python/CRABInterface/DataWorkflow.py#L296-L298

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T14:26:53Z)

now about killing while ASO-Rucio is running.
DagmanKiller HOLD the DAG and kills all vanilla universe jobs
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanKiller.py#L94-L95

Problem: DAG are also held when they completed with some failed jobs, to allow resubmission. How can ASO tell the
difference ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T17:01:53Z)

hmm... looks like current ASO-Rucio code has no knowledge of DAG status, and will simply wait 6 ours in order to close last block/dataset
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/MonitorLockStatus.py#L188-L204

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-12T17:05:45Z)

that comment is stale, default timeout is 1h
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Main.py#L66
I will send a task with a number of job which is not a multiple of 20 to check.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Main.py#L40

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-13T09:32:09Z)

IIUC the above means that if we kill a task by holding the DAGMAN, i.e. kill running jobs, running postjobs and halt the dagman, ASO-RUcio will wrap up things within 1 hour.
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-interaction.html#suspending-a-running-dag

Should we remove the DAGMAN instead ? If we do not want to allow resubmission, why keep it around in Held status ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-13T15:38:26Z)

thoughts:
* 1h timeout before closing a dataset is too short, just like 20 file per dataset is too little. It will create too many small blocks in DBS
* In view of making the timeout e.g. 4h, we need a way to close thing on ASO-Rucio side when task is killed. Since at that point no more PostJobs will run and no more files will be added to the list of transfers.
* all in all this is what Publsher does now to decide that a task is done and close current block: check if it is KILLED in DB or otherwise fetch status cache from WEBDIR and parse it using same code as in  Client (and new cache_status.py) https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L332
* maybe "as simple as" in `task_proc_wrapper.sh` where we have the following loop, we can have `cache status` report the overall "collapsed DAG status" and pass it to `manage_transfers`
```
    cache_status
    manage_transfers
    sleep 300s
```

I went for adding `overallDagStatus`  key to `task_process/status_cache.json` and reading that file inside ASO-Rucio code

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-13T19:41:06Z)

I have modified `cache_status.py` to add `overallDagStatus` key to the `cache_status.json` file.

Now that can be read amd used to set `shouldClose` in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/MonitorLockStatus.py#L189-L196

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T12:54:24Z)

`crab kill` or `task reached end of life` have same effect: dagbootstrap job is held.
When the job is held, it stops running, so the main dagman exits and in `node_status` we have
```
  Type = "DagStatus";
  DagFiles = {
    "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/4109/0/cluster10224109.proc0.subproc0/RunJobs.dag"
  };
  Timestamp = 1747226438; /* "Wed May 14 14:40:38 2025" */
  DagStatus = 6; /* "STATUS_ERROR (removed)" *
```
and all job nodes have
```
[
  Type = "NodeStatus";
  Node = "Job1";
  NodeStatus = 6; /* "STATUS_ERROR" */
```

so far so good. Now need to check subdags which are instead submitted not by running condor_dagman inside a script, but via `condor_submit_dag` command
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L335

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T13:41:57Z)

the new code (as per last line in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8429#issuecomment-2877010643 ) results in
```
  "overallDagStatus": "FAILED"
```
after a `crab kill` which is fine (again "standard splitting")

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T14:08:47Z)

hmm.. I tried another `condor_hold` of a dagman bootstrap and DagStatus in `node_state` is not `DagStatus = 6; /* "STATUS_ERROR (removed)" *` but `  DagStatus = 3; /* "STATUS_SUBMITTED (held)" */` which `cache_status.py` translates into `RUNNING`, since status 3 is defined as STATUS_SUBMITTED by Dagman. The comment is not propagated in the classAd format when `node_state` is parsed.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T14:15:12Z)

well it looks like the first test was somehow flawed, and the expecte behavior is indeed 'STATUS_SUBMITTED` after the hold.
[This](https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2025-May/msg00038.shtml) from HTCondor Dagman expert:

> Hi Stefano,
>
> Being held is not considered an error for DAGMan. When you run condor_hold on a running DAGMan job, the DagStatus
> attribute in the node status file should actually be 3 (submitted) with an inline comment saying "STATUS_SUBMITTED
> (held)". That being said when writing the node status file, DAGMan checks to see if the DAG is finished executing. This
 > would take precedence over the hold and set the status to done or error.
>
> -Cole Bollig

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T14:35:56Z)

we already have code which checks the dagman jobs so can detect the HOLD status
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c64dc53f28f56a1022121b3680a757daf88f40ad/scripts/task_process/task_proc_wrapper.sh#L91-L92

I'd need a way to catch this info inside `status_cache`.

OTOH `crab klll` will `condor_rm` all jobs so all actice dag nodes should fail and dag end in `FAILED`. But I am not sure in case there are unsubmitted nodes.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T14:39:50Z)

OTOH... does it really matter if when task reaches end of life we simply wait "timeout" hours from last successful postjob before closing last dataset ?

Better stay focused on crab kill.

Given that we deprecate resubmit after kill.. why holding the dagmans vs. simply doing a condor_rm ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-14T15:10:48Z)

hm... after checking https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/JobCleanup.py , we need to make sure that dagman bootstrap jobs stay in the queue so that we can eventually cleanup SPOOL_DIR and WEB_DIR

anyhow JobCleanup.py above looks at all jobs in Scheduler universe and checks only that dag is not running and time since submission, so will clean up removed DAG's as well.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-15T12:26:37Z)

so we **may** use `condor_rm` on dagman's as well when `crab kill` is issued.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-16T10:07:55Z)

I am reluctant to add calls to condor_q inside `cache_status.py`, since that script is only parsing files so far, it has the virtue of being independent from schedd being temporarily busy (condo_q failes at times when duty cycle is high).

I have considered changing the frequency of calling `perform_condorq` in `task_proc_wrapper.sh` from 24h to to something shorter, but passing information from there to `cache_status.py` looks ugly.

And by the way I do not see the point of calling `perform_condorq` every 24h in the script while checking its output every 5min in `exit_now`. But as usual, let's try not to change what works w/o a good reason.

So, putting all together, I am pretty much inclined to `condor_rm`  dagman jobs at  `crab kill` time.
That will put DAG in FAILED status and kill all jobs in each DAG.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-16T12:38:44Z)

I am left with
* PostJob should not wait only 7 days, but until task expires, this means keep going until DAGMAN stops running them. Would be good to have some way to delay re-running from 30 min to hours as time goes.
* Currently DAGMANs are put in Hold when task expires (`PeriodicHold = time() > CRAB_TaskEndTime`) shall I remove them instead ? that's the case for vanilla universe jobs. Maybe kill dagman a few hours later, give condor time to run PostJobs ? Does it matter for removed jobs ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-16T13:17:53Z)

PostJob takes less than a second to run when checking for output and finding that it has to wait [1]. Is really worth to worry about doing it too often? All in all PJ queries Transfersdb every 15 min, and otherwise reuses cached file on disk,  things happen pretty quickly then, most of the time likely goes in starting Python ! So changes to PJ code to e.g. exit immediatey to wait longer may not really help.

We currently allow 10 concurrent PostJobs, 10/sec means 18k in each 30min, so we can check status of a full 10k-job task even if Rucio is fully stuck. And otherwise PostJobs will be automatically delayed. Yet this may go on for weeks.

As long as we do not have tens of tasks in that situation, we should be OK. Main danger is that some largish T2 goes down making Rucio halt transfers there for a while.

All in all I am leaning toward "let it happen and see how it goes". If we run into problems, deal with them when they happen.

The best alternative I can imagine is to add a quick exit  in  `dag_bootstrap.sh` as a way to increase delays between PJ running. The available info there are what's in the arguments
`dag_bootstrap.sh POSTJOB $JOBID $RETURN $RETRY $MAX_RETRIES <task_name> <CRAB_ID> <tmp_LFN>  <final_LFN> ...`
see [DagmanMacros](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-introduction.html#special-script-argument-macros) for the `$*` variables
Unfortunately no quick way to tell how long ago $JOBID was submitted or completed !

Yet, if disaster strikes, we can easily add a random "exit now with code 4" in dag_bootstrap.sh and delay PJ execution.

Or maybe... do it anyhow based on timestamp in task name ?

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8442: Publisher stop.sh fails if the Publisher process stops for longer than the next cycle
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8442: Publisher stop.sh fails if the Publisher process stops for longer than the next cycle

State: closed
Opened: 2024-05-29T09:27:24Z
Closed: 2024-10-31T16:21:52Z
Labels: OPERATION, PyPI, Publisher
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8442

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-05-29T09:27:24Z)

The stop.sh script (or manage.sh stop in new PyPI image) will wait forever if it run after exceed "Next cycle" time and no Publisher process is running.

The script parse timestamp from last log line from `logs/log.txt`:
```
2024-05-29 11:13:12,912:INFO:PublisherMaster,296:Next cycle will start at 11:39:01
```
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97bf5913bd1900c229d87ab77c803e39a15743e1/src/script/Deployment/Publisher/stop.sh#L19-L23

The `delta` is gradually decreasing while the time (epoch) is increasing. No process is running mean no one will update the log line and script will stuck forever.

Workaround is exec to the container and kill `/bin/bash ./stop.sh` to allow Deploy_TW to continue.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-29T09:28:47Z)

Simply check Publisher process if it is still running before checking with time, maybe resolve the issue.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-29T12:42:08Z)

that's surely good ! But maybe we can also introduce a timeout. Originally the idea was that at time a single Publisher iteration could take hours and we did not want to have a timeout + hard kill. Publisher was not designed with the idea of being stateless and idempotent, and I opted for "safety". But we were only using stop as issued by operator. As we try to have something automatic, and  have enough experience, we can probably try a timeout at 2h.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-13T11:06:17Z)

After https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8561, it rarely happens on prod/preprod but happens quite a lot on test env and is super annoying.

My new idea is we do flock using `getLock()` like PostJob.py
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ce559a11ef02c447f909ee166b7d48f218eb021d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L426-L428
Wrap over
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ce559a11ef02c447f909ee166b7d48f218eb021d/src/python/Publisher/Main.py#L69
On the process controller script, just check if flock file exist.

Is this too over-engineering @belforte ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-13T19:31:22Z)

#856 does not exist. Which issue did you want to point to ?
Maybe we can simply use file to record the PID of the running Publisher, like it happens for the REST ?
IIUC the problem is that we end up  waiting forever while there is nothing running.

PostJob has locks to prevent multiple PJs running at same time from trying to update same file a at same time. But here we should not need such locks.

Or maybe I am confused :-), as usual.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-15T11:05:46Z)

modify isPublisherBusy to do a "ps" ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-17T18:07:59Z)

Ok, I remember why I need `getLock()`.
Parsing `logs.txt` to find the time to execute next round is unreliable. But I forgot which case that make `stop.sh` stall.

But...The real problem is that `stop.sh` stall forever in CI.
When it happens, it feels like "everything is fine" because you did not get a fail message within 15mins, but actually the Publisher deployment has been in progress for hours.

The real(?) solution would be to set a timeout, as you said in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8442#issuecomment-2137321230 .
2 hr is too much, 5 mins should be enough for every env.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-17T20:00:30Z)

but stlll.. wouldn't your original idea https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8442#issuecomment-2136962442 be enough ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-17T20:07:43Z)

if you mean to kill Publsher 5min after "next iteration will start at ..." time, I am kind of lost.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-17T20:43:10Z)

> but stlll.. wouldn't your original idea https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8442#issuecomment-2136962442 be enough ?

Yes, and it already implemented in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8562 .
But....there is a case when publisher process is running (publishing/sleeping/whatever) but stop.sh never manage to terminate it and stuck forever. Sorry, I am not sure "how" until I see it again.

> if you mean to kill Publsher 5min after "next iteration will start at ..." time, I am kind of lost.

No. Change stop.sh from "waiting forever" to "exit with error if waiting longer than 5mins".
Then, CI will shout an error, which means manual intervention is required. Not just keep silencing...

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-18T00:18:23Z)

:astonished:
**wow** odd things are going on. Yup let's try to catch em, or at least live with them

We should fix either the logs or the grok pattern

2024-05-30 14:10:51,016:INFO:PublisherMaster,531:Taskname 240530_110157:agungord_crab_CMSDAS_Data_analysis_test0 is OK. Published 22 in 1 blocks.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8456: tasks with numCores>1 stays idle when using submit Object
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8456: tasks with numCores>1 stays idle when using submit Object

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-02T14:44:47Z
Closed: 2024-06-03T21:31:05Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done, Area: HTCondor, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8456

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-02T14:44:47Z)

with reference to #8336

tasks submitted with e.g.
```
config.JobType.numCores = 8
```
stay idle in the scheduler universe and fail to bootstrap.

The problem is that using the old way, the `Requirements` for the dag_bootstrap job, i.e. the one submitted by the TW, is
```
Requirements = true || false && TARGET.OPSYS == "LINUX" && TARGET.ARCH == "X86_64" && TARGET.HasFileTransfer && TARGET.Disk >= RequestDisk && TARGET.Memory >= RequestMemory && TARGET.Cpus >= RequestCpus
```
note that TW only specifies the `true || false` and the rest is added automatically by  [HTCondor](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html)
When the above expression is evaluated all the conditions added by HTC are ANDed with `false` to become irrelevant, and the result is simply `true`, which I guess explains this line which I always found very mysterious:
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/856d1efed8cba1f6c65d9b263ab8ffc20db9cd4d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L482

When using a submit Object, instead of passing the classAds to `schedd.submit` (which is deprecated now), the final `Requirements` add is instead
```
Requirements = (true || false) && (TARGET.Arch == "X86_64") && (TARGET.OpSys == "LINUX") && (TARGET.Disk >= RequestDisk) && (TARGET.Memory >= RequestMemory) && (TARGET.Cpus >= RequestCpus)
```
this time HTCondor added parenthesis, which makes sense and is consistent with the [documentation](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html)

But this time the requirements added by HTC "matter" and although I could not find what is the value for `TARGET.Cpus` (`condor_status -schedd -con 'machine=="vocms0122.cern.ch"' -l|grep -i cpu` returns nothing ), the last member is clearly what prevents the match, since other tasks have the same expression simply w/o the final` && (TARGET.Cpus >= RequestCpus)` and work finely.

Simply removing this line solves the problem
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/856d1efed8cba1f6c65d9b263ab8ffc20db9cd4d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L73

In a way, it is not good to use those classAd to pass requirements for the grid jobs, the correct requirements are already in the `Jobs.submit` file prepared by DagmanCreator.

I presume that one reason to do in this way could have been to make it easier to change those requirements during `crab resubmit` by only sending new ads, w/o  touching the `Job.submit`.

I have not tested if after this change is is stll possible to change numCores in the resubmit, but it is a very bad idea IMHO, we should rather forbid it.

I can't remove other requirements passed as ads here like `RequestMemory` because they are used in PreJob, possibly to make it work with same code for submissions and resubmissions.

In the medium term, we need to rewrite the resubmission anyhow, and will avoid using dagman-job's classAd for this.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T13:58:57Z)

with the fix in https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/commit/c73d3fdb90d75503822b67a6acadf1329f7301a4 tasks get submitted, but the gridjobs have `RequestCpus = 1`
A change in PreJob is needed.
Or a way for scheduler to start those in scheduler universe.
I will do some local tests and write to HTCondor, it may be the least effort path to a short term solution.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T16:30:18Z)

I wrote this to condor support
```

Dear experts,
can you explain why a JDL [1] with three lines in it stays idle forever ?
Universe   = scheduler
requirements = true
RequestCpus = 2

inspecting the job requirements with condor_q -l, I find
Requirements = (true) && (TARGET.Arch == "X86_64") && (TARGET.OpSys == "LINUX") && (TARGET.Disk >= RequestDisk) && (TARGET.Memory >= RequestMemory) && (TARGET.Cpus >= RequestCpus)

The same submission runs withing a few minutes if I put
RequestCpus = 2
and in that case the Requirements expression does not have the final
term  && (TARGET.Cpus >= RequestCpus)

My scheduler is 16-cpu machine, so regardless of whether the
requirement makes sense or not, I'd expect the job to run, no ?

Documentation in https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html says
<quote>
For scheduler and local universe jobs, the requirements expression is evaluated against the Scheduler ClassAd which represents the the condor_schedd daemon running on the access point, rather than a remote machine.
</quote>

But I did find a way to inspect those TARGET.* ads.
condor_status -sched -con 'machine=="vocms059.cern.ch"' -af Cpus Memory ...
simply returns "undefined". Same if I add TARGET.
Just lile "condor_q -af requirements" returns undefined

This is currently breaking CMS CRAB submission when moving to current
schedd.submit(submitObject,...) binding (we can go into details of how
it was working "before" if you care, but it is not relevant, IMHO).
I believe I can find a workaround by changing code in various places,
but if the above could be made to work, it would be the easiest.

Thanks
Stefano

[1] full JDL

Universe   = scheduler
Executable = sleep.sh
Arguments  = 1
Log        = sleep.PC.log
Output     = sleep.out.$(Cluster).$(Process)
Error      = sleep.err.$(Cluster).$(Process)
requirements = true
should_transfer_files = YES
RequestMemory = 2000
RequestCpus = 2
when_to_transfer_output = ON_EXIT
Queue 1

```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T18:43:39Z)

Reply from ToddM is here
https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2024-June/msg00008.shtml

and "solution" is here
https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2024-June/msg00011.shtml

I will test replacing
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7ac2b90193632df3757bcf3bf7750ff27bf736a3/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L481
with
```python
    jobJDL["Requirements"] = "TARGET.Cpus==1"
```

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8460: adapt to FTS Client 3.13

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-03T10:20:26Z

Labels: Type: Bug, Type: Enhancement, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8460

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-03T10:20:26Z)

there is (at least) one non-backward compatible change
```
all our FTS submissions fail with
    job = fts3.new_job(transfers,
TypeError: new_job() got an unexpected keyword argument 'spacetoken'
```
I am communicating with FTS developers about this
<details><summary>mail sent to FTS developers</summary>

</details>

temporary workaround was to  force ([this](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/commit/7028e0593ea2ce42b07f3c555a5ed744ee5a5567) commit and two following ones) older FTS version. See also https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/jobs-stuck-at-transfer/41870/3?u=belforte

Waiting for clarifications from FTS developers before changing our code
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f6c01ebafddb56ea7f15cbcf8f8563baae20114a/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L329-L331

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T16:36:00Z)

here's FTS answer
```
Hello Stefano,

Apologies for creating problems for the CRAB submission system.

From the previous verison to FTS v3.13.0, the "new_job()" and "new_staging_job()" signatures have been changed.
The field "spacetoken" was renamed from "spacetoken" --> "destination_spacetoken".

We checked before releasing with Rucio and DIRAC. I apologies for not checking with CRAB as well.

To move forward:

    I will (probably) tag FTS v3.13.1 which brings back the old "spacetoken" field, but prints a deprecation warning. I assume you aren't the only system impacted.
    Are you reding these deprecation warnings? If we add them to the codebase, will you be able to see and act on them? (I'm afraid these large systems often hide these warnings)
    No matter what, whether in this release or the next big one (FTS v3.14.0), things will get uncomfortable. In FTS v3.14.0 we will add source & destination tokens to the submit functions signatures. If we add the deprecating warning, it is also in FTS v3.14.0 when we will remove the deprecated field
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T18:38:02Z)

and this is the final word
```
en" --> "destination_spacetoken" argument backwards compatible.

All the "fts3.new_job(..)" parameters are optional, with default "None" value. The same applies for the (destination_)spacetoken. So if you don't add "spacetoken" or "destination_spacetoken" when you invoke "fts3.new_job(..)", there is no harm. It's only when you pass "spacetoken" specifically that it breaks in the new version, as seems to be in your case.

In your FTS submission code, I recommend dropping the "source_spacetoken=None" and "spacetoken=None" lines [1] (or replace "spacetoken=None" with "destination_spacetoken=None"). The backwards-compatibility fix will be released, bringing back "spacetoken". If you wait for it, no change will be needed in your code.

However, please prepare for the removal of the "spacetoken" field in FTS v3.14, as well as the addition of source + destination (access) tokens to the "fts3.new_transfer(..)" signature. I will announce those better and ahead of time.
```

new code should work with past and present FTS client. And IIUC also with coming FTS client v3.14

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8463: decouple our qa from epel testing
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8463: decouple our qa from epel testing

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-03T13:42:50Z
Closed: 2024-06-17T08:22:21Z
Labels: OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8463

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-03T13:42:50Z)

by default qa gets rpms from epel-testing, not epel.
This introduces too many unknwon, uncontrolled chances, especially hen for one reason or another we have several machiines in qa. At the very least we need to be aware. Better yet be ready to disable/enable as proper. Here are instructions ([MM](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/it-dep/pl/57tx84o9didm5mxjmo1f8xkt6h)):

![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/b40a9bed-b0ca-4c11-b0c9-0482cb109a34)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T13:45:13Z)

assigning to me to remember to bfing it up for discussion

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-06T13:50:44Z)

we discussed in the meeting today. Pending a final review with @mapellidario the conclusions are:

- stick to epel production for all our VM’s even in qa
- Let other people test epel-testing
- Lock FTS client version anyhow, like we do for HTCondor and when an updated comes upstream, validate it.

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-06-06T14:08:14Z)

uh! this was not easy to catch, good job Stefano (and Wa also?)!
I definitely agree with all your decisions

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2024-06-17T08:22:21Z)

Fixed by disabling epel-testing in `data/hostgroup/vocmsglidein.yaml` See https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/204

Test passed on crab-dev-tw03 See https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/205

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8464: automatic splitting does not work anymore
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8464: automatic splitting does not work anymore

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-03T18:53:52Z
Closed: 2024-06-03T21:34:03Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: In Progress, Area: HTCondor, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8464

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-03T18:53:52Z)

after last changes for modern HTCondor the main dag in automatic splitting writes in
`task_process/RestInfoForFileTransfers.json`

{'host': 'cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch:8443', 'dbInstance': 'preprod', 'proxyfile': '/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5130/0/cluster9615130.proc0.subproc0/e080907cad69528d423bbe562e2f8f9873b2c933'}

i.e. the full path for the proxy file,
this conflicts with code in FTS_Transfers
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7ac2b90193632df3757bcf3bf7750ff27bf736a3/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L75

and the directory path is added twice making FTS calls fail.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-03T19:05:12Z)

The effect of this is that ASO stays in "transferring" forever, which I did not notice initially sine ASO was stuck for everybody due to #8460

testing fix in https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/240603_193544%3Abelforte_crab_20240603_213540

test worked.
Will merge and deploy to preprod for more validation

Dear experts,
sorry to report a new problem when migrating CMS CRAB to submit via
 schedd.submit(submitObject,...)

We add custom classAds to jobs for use in glideinWMS (which still works)
and we also add one which we use later on to use as a constrain
in condor_q, condor_qedit and other commads.

The latter thing fails. I have managed to reproduce to the problem
to a simple test using local submission with python bindings.

Hopefully lines below are self-explaining, if not, ask me.
Note in particular the output of
 condor_q 9620532 -af:h StefanoAd CRAB_TT
And of course the fact that condor_q -con .. does not select any job

Things look as expected if I put same info in a JDL file and do a plain
condor_submit test.jdl and also if I construct the htcondor.submit()
object passing the full jdl to it via ("""jdl lines"""). There are other
oddities,like if in the example below I change 'ROOT' to 'ROT' output
is different and while -con still fails, condor_q -af returns uniformly
"undefined". I can of course change ROOT to a different string in our code, but it would be good to have a rational.

Our "old way" was to use schedd.submit(classAds,...)
and things were OK.

If you prefer to move this to some more interactive channel
(our GH ?) tell me as well.

Thanks a lot
Stefano

here's ToddM explanation/clarification
```

On 04/06/2024 18:36, Todd L Miller via HTCondor-users wrote:
>> jdl['+StefanoAd'] = "TestString"
>> jdl['+CRAB_TT'] = "ROOT"
>
>      Note that this sets the ClassAd expression StefanoAd to the ClassAd
> attribute reference TestString, not the _string_ "TestString",
> which given the name, is probably not what you're expecting.  Likewise,
> CRAB_TT is being set to the attribute reference ROOT, which happens to
> be magical.  I'm not sure why this works in the JDL, but perhaps there's
> more magic in the parser there than I thought.
>
> - ToddM
```

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8480: overflow to T1 broken

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-06T14:05:25Z
Closed: 2024-06-07T10:36:18Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8480

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-06T14:05:25Z)

it is not working since a while
![image](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/1837785/6f0f079e-3c05-4b8c-8314-64e932041d0e)

I think it was broken my me in March when I removed creation of `/etc/condor/config.d/90_jobrouter.config` in puppet https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/commit/2a3422ba2d3b8101414bc9606d67331bce3d4b94

So even if we have `enable_overflow: true` in the `data/fqdns/vocms*.yaml` files, the condor config. variable `JAT_ENABLE_OVERFLOW` is not set and JobAutoTuner log has
```
2024-04-08 13:08:04,345:INFO:JobAutoTuner,261:============  JobAutoTuner-py3 starting ==============
2024-04-08 13:08:04,345:ERROR:JobAutoTuner,70:ERR: Could not find/read the config parameter: JAT_ENABLE_OVERFLOW. Not enabling the service! Additional info: Config key not set in condor.
2024-04-08 13:08:04,345:INFO:JobAutoTuner,272:-------------------- Overflow.py was not enabled  --------------------
```

More changes are needed, because when I set it to True via 99_local_tweaks, log is
```
2024-06-06 15:58:20,328:INFO:JobAutoTuner,264:-------------------- Routes added by Overflow.py  --------------------
2024-06-06 15:58:20,328:INFO:JobAutoTuner,107:=================== An Overflow object instance start! ===================
2024-06-06 15:58:20,897:ERROR:JobAutoTuner,82:ERR: SubScriptAlarm: at: 2024-06-06 15:58:20.897397 / additional info:
Overflow failed with exception: 'ServerTime'
Exception: None
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/crab/JobAutoTuner.py", line 267, in main
    overflow.run()
  File "/data/srv/crab/JobAutoTuner.py", line 256, in run
    self.overflow(jobsInThisSchedd)
  File "/data/srv/crab/JobAutoTuner.py", line 210, in overflow
    if self.needOverflow(jobObj):
  File "/data/srv/crab/JobAutoTuner.py", line 177, in needOverflow
    currIdleTime = jobObject["ServerTime"] - jobObject["QDate"]
KeyError: 'ServerTime'
2024-06-06 15:58:20,905:INFO:JobAutoTuner,273:===================================================================
```
So two action items, and no quick solution:
- [x] find simplest way pass enable_oveflow flag from hiera to JobAutoTuner and implement it
- [x] fix JobAutoTuner.py code  (`ServerTime is supposed to [exist](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html#ServerTime) )

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-06T14:08:17Z)

the problem with ServerTime is very strange, it **is** always defined
```
belforte@vocms0137/crab> condor_q -con 'jobuniverse==5&&jobstatus==1' -af servertime|uniq
1717682834
belforte@vocms0137/crab>
```
seems problem with python bindings. There was a bug in HTC that made it go missing, was fixed in 10.0.2 https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/v10_0/version-history/lts-versions-10-0.html#version-10-0-2

yet...
```
[crabtw@vocms0137 ~]$ python3
Python 3.9.18 (main, Jan 24 2024, 00:00:00)
[GCC 11.4.1 20231218 (Red Hat 11.4.1-3)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import htcondor
>>> htcondor.version()
'$CondorVersion: 10.2.0 2023-01-05 BuildID: 621409 PackageID: 10.2.0-1 $'
>>> constraint="jobuniverse==5"
>>> projection=['ServerTime']
>>> sk=htcondor.Schedd()
>>> rr=sk.query(constraint, projection)
>>> rr[0]
[  ]
>>>
```
while from my account, where I have more recent bindings in my local
```
belforte@vocms0137/~> python3
Python 3.9.18 (main, Jan 24 2024, 00:00:00)
[GCC 11.4.1 20231218 (Red Hat 11.4.1-3)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import htcondor
>>> htcondor.version()
'$CondorVersion: 23.7.2 2024-05-16 BuildID: UW_Python_Wheel_Build $'
>>> constraint="jobuniverse==5"
>>> projection=['ServerTime']
>>> sk=htcondor.Schedd()
>>> rr=sk.query(constraint, projection)
>>> rr[0]
[ ServerTime = 1717687105 ]
>>>
```
looks like 10.2.0 is some separate branch (non LTS) which did not get the fix.

Of course we could use `time.time()` instead, since script runs on same machine as the scheduler, no reason to ask the scheduler what the time is !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8488: cleanup TaskType names
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8488: cleanup TaskType names

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-11T21:03:36Z
Closed: 2024-08-19T16:44:12Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High, Area: Code Cleanup, Area: HTCondor
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8488

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-11T21:03:36Z)

in the context of Modernize HTC calls
see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8337#issuecomment-2161576067

- [x] rename TaskType ad to CRAB_DAGType
- [x] rename ROOT type to MAIN. So that dagman jobs will have CRAB_DagType in ["MAIN",  "PROCESSING", "TAIL"]. "normal" tasks will only have "MAIN". "automatic" will use "MAIN" for running probes, followed by "PROCESSING" and up to 3 "TAIL".
But I am still not happy here. ROOT is more descriptive for a DAG which can be either the full thing standalone or the probe step for automatic splitting. Maybe "BASE" ?
I will start with renaming the classAd, at least it will make it easier later  on to identify where it is used and possibly change the value.

**BEWARE these changes will not be backward compatible ! i.e. `crab kill` and `crab resubmit` will not work on tasks which have TaskType but not CRAB_DAGType.**
 - [x] add a backward-compatibility layer (to be remove after 2 months in production)

Note: ROOT is assigned in initial submission (so it i the same for everybody) in DagamSubmitter. Later on PreDag uses the stage name when it submits the various subdags. Stage name is set in DagmanCreator and used in PreDag and PreJob

List of possible values. Note that CRAB_DAGType is the classAd of a job !! Simply it takes a non trivial value when the job runs in the Scheduler universe to execut a DagMan

|kind of job | universe |CRAB_DAGType | stage name  |
|-|-|-|-|
| main Dagman w/o automatic splitting | scheduler (7) | BASE | conventional |
| main Dagman with automatic splitting | scheduler (7) | BASE  | probe |
| grid job | vanilla (5) | Job | not used |
| task_process | local (12) | undefined | not used |
| processing subDag | scheduler (7) | PROCESSING | processing |
| tail subDag | scheduler (7) |TAIL | tail |

Possible alternative names for ROOT:  MAIN , BASE

TaskType ad is defined in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c826e3856dfb602150c817b4ddf6aa8e8e4ecf2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L529
and
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L104

and in case of automatic splitting in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c826e3856dfb602150c817b4ddf6aa8e8e4ecf2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L338

the `stage` in PreDAG is passed as argument when PreDAG is called during Dag execution:
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c826e3856dfb602150c817b4ddf6aa8e8e4ecf2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L56

and the code which managed the various DAGs creation is the somehow cryptic
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3c826e3856dfb602150c817b4ddf6aa8e8e4ecf2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L998-L1024

TaskType ad is also used in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/scripts/task_process/task_proc_wrapper.sh#L73-L77

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L452

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py#L73

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/RenewRemoteProxies.py#L153

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanKiller.py#L63

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanKiller.py#L75

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8491: Publisher_rucio must check to have all files in a block
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8491: Publisher_rucio must check to have all files in a block

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-12T14:56:44Z
Closed: 2025-06-12T10:36:07Z
Labels: Type: Bug, RUCIO, Priority: TOP, Publisher
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8491

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-12T14:56:44Z)

as described in #8376  the publication flag for individual files is set in PostJob up to 30min after the file replica has been added to the Rucio-dataset/DBS-block by RucioTransfer. So when RucioTransfer adds the last file, declares the block closed and correspondently mark all entries in filetransfersdb, some files in the block may still not have the publish flag set.
If Publisher_Rucio runs "too soon" it will miss some files and since publshed blocks are closed, it will never be able to add them.

Solution is that Publisher checks the block/dataset content in Rucio and waits untill all needed files are ACQUIRED

Subtasks (tested in https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/7641939 )
- [x] make sure that changes for this do not break TaskWorker
- [x] also that configuration is properly constructed inside PreDag to be used when running on scheduler

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-26T09:57:16Z)

I realized that I need the Rucio scope name, in addition to the DBS block name. This is trivial for users, but for groups it would required parsing the LNF, or maybe that's no sufficient. In any case awkward and fragile. I propose to change the `tm_dbs_blockname` column to store the Rucio dataset name `scope:dbs_blockname`. @novicecpp what do you think ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-06-26T10:03:16Z)

Agreed.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-23T17:00:55Z)

While testing, I realized that I had not thoroughly reviewed the use case.
The situation where task is killed is not properly handled in the ASO/Publisher communication

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9094

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-12T10:36:07Z)

the "synchronization with Publisher" is likely solved by #9094

I have found a different problem #9111 which will be addressed separetely

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-06-17T12:27:06Z)

Since we are quickly moving to images build from pypi, abandoning rpms, the docker images that we use for monitoring need to adapt as well.

Effectively, this means that the directories `monit-python` and `monit-taskworker` in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/cicd/build need to go.

I implemented the changes in an upcoming PR.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8509: automatic splitting fails in latest master after #8507

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-18T16:11:23Z
Closed: 2024-06-18T22:00:48Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8509

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-18T16:11:23Z)

this task: https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/240618_133627%3Acmsbot_crab_20240618_153626
PreDag fails to start the processing DAG
https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059/cmsbot/240618_133627:cmsbot_crab_20240618_153626/AutomaticSplitting/DagLog0.txt

relevant error line should be
```
ERROR: unable to read submit append file (subdag.ad)
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-18T16:19:02Z)

this change had gone lost in merging of my modernize_HTC branch to master branch
```diff
@@ -333,7 +333,7 @@ class PreDAG():
         """ Submit a subdag
         """
         subprocess.check_call(['condor_submit_dag', '-DoRecov', '-AutoRescue', '0', '-MaxPre', '20', '-MaxIdle', str(maxidle),
-                               '-MaxPost', str(maxpost), '-insert_sub_file', 'subdag.ad',
+                               '-MaxPost', str(maxpost), '-insert_sub_file', 'subdag.jdl',
                                '-append', '+Environment = strcat(Environment," _CONDOR_DAGMAN_LOG={0}/{1}.dagman.out")'.format(os.getcwd(), subdag),
                                '-append', '+TaskType = "{0}"'.format(stage.upper()), subdag])
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-18T21:18:15Z)

DAG submission is now OK. BUt the correct proxy is not passed to FTS_transfer script. The directory name is  inserted twice !
Things were OK for non-automatic splitting.
I must be missing some other change previously done in my development branch

```
2024-06-18 19:29:02,232: using user's proxy from /data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0//data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/c6ea75e904ebb26531217d954bd562c96db20c11
2024-06-18 19:29:02,232: error during main loop
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 715, in <module>
    algorithm()
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 665, in algorithm
    ftsContext = fts3.Context(FTS_ENDPOINT, proxy, proxy, verify=True)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/context.py", line 182, in __init__
    self._set_x509(ucert, ukey)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/context.py", line 95, in _set_x509
    raise FileNotFoundError(name + " not found!")
FileNotFoundError: Certificate not found!
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-18T21:23:32Z)

indeed
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 task_process]$ cat RestInfoForFileTransfers.json |jq
{
  "host": "cmsweb-test2.cern.ch:8443",
  "dbInstance": "dev",
  "proxyfile": "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/c6ea75e904ebb26531217d954bd562c96db20c11"
}
[crabtw@vocms059 task_process]$
```
But code expect a file name w/o the path
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3f893cf77152dc1bf9ad309bc1cad2411def88e7/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L73-L75

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-18T21:56:44Z)

and here's what I am missing.  I do not understand how is it possible that other tests in #8508 were successful [1]

```diff
LapSB:CRABServer$ git diff modernize_HTC -- src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py
diff --git a/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py
index 5cc59b96..17c235ed 100644
--- a/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py
+++ b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py
@@ -995,7 +995,7 @@ class ASOServerJob():
             #if not os.path.exists('task_process/rest_filetransfers.txt'):
                 restInfo = {'host':self.rest_host,
                             'dbInstance': self.db_instance,
-                            'proxyfile': os.path.basename(self.proxy)}
+                            'proxyfile': self.proxy}
                 with open('task_process/RestInfoForFileTransfers.json', 'w') as fp:
                     json.dump(restInfo, fp)
         else:
@@ -1014,7 +1014,7 @@ class ASOServerJob():
             #if not os.path.exists('task_process/rest_filetransfers.txt'):
                 restInfo = {'host':self.rest_host,
                             'dbInstance': self.db_instance,
-                            'proxyfile': os.path.basename(self.proxy)}
+                            'proxyfile': self.proxy}
                 with open('task_process/RestInfoForFileTransfers.json','w') as fp:
                     json.dump(restInfo, fp)
         return returnMsg
LapSB:CRABServer$
```

[1] I looked at one of those `240618_133632:cmsbot_crab_20240618_153631` and
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$ cat task_process/RestInfoForFileTransfers.json |jq
{
  "host": "cmsweb-test2.cern.ch:8443",
  "dbInstance": "dev",
  "proxyfile": "e080907cad69528d423bbe562e2f8f9873b2c933"
}
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$
```
but PostJob cose was missing the `os.path.basename`. I guess that normal jobs use proxy file name from the env. of `dag_bootstrap.sh`
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$ grep  X509 dag_bootstrap.out
X509_USER_PROXY=e080907cad69528d423bbe562e2f8f9873b2c933
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$
```
while in case of automatic splitting I find
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$ grep  X509 dag_bootstrap.out
X509_USER_PROXY=/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/c6ea75e904ebb26531217d954bd562c96db20c11
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$
```

I **think** that somehow PreDag takes the proxy from the ads of completed probe jobs
```text
finished_jobs/job.0-1.0:x509userproxy = "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6222/0/cluster9636222.proc0.subproc0/c6ea75e904ebb26531217d954bd562c96db20c11"

```
But this is quite intricated. And of course the solution which I already found of removing any possible path in PostJob before writing it out in the file to pass to FTS_Transfer (or Rucio_Transfer) is just fine.

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-06-19T14:55:13Z)

it currently takes O(10) min to build TW container in the pipeline.
I think it is because we still have a list of dependencies from "old rpm times" with all possible things used by all possible WMCore application in  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/requirements.txt
Already https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabserver_pypi/requirements.txt is much more trimmed.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-06-20T08:00:24Z)

Thanks Stefano.
From what I saw in CI machine, most CPU is gone due to I/O wait. Reducing the deps will help cutting time by a lot.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-20T09:02:06Z)

yeah, I had been looking at pipeline log in realtime and noticed that all those pip install were taking a lot.
I built `pypi-test2-reducetwdep` with that and at least TW is built in same time as server. A lot of time goes in conda/gfal as you know. I guess the only way to cut time now is to create a base image with gfal and start from that. Not sure it is worth

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8522: Improve PyPI images building process
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8522: Improve PyPI images building process

State: closed
Opened: 2024-06-20T18:38:01Z
Closed: 2024-09-02T16:23:45Z
Labels: Area: CI/CD, PyPI
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8522

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-06-20T18:38:01Z)

Currently, the `crabtaskworker` image is...too big (3.88 GB uncompressed), mainly because the Dockerfile is not optimized.
Also, newer image could not use the layers from older image even the contents are the same because it get rebuild everytime, make it consume so much space (both dev machine and registry), and time.

We can improve this by
- [x] Improving the Dockerfile
    - This [single line](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f88a9b98f80f9a38e3180ed0a5b2b193a75ee5c0/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L138) cause files duplication in `/data` path.
    - Use [dive](https://github.com/wagoodman/dive) to inspect the layer. It work fine when dump the output to json file.
- [ ] Caching PyPI deps to make pip install layers more idempotent.
- [x] Consider `docker build` instead of `kaniko` to take advantage of image caching and parallelism ([buildx](https://github.com/docker/buildx))
- [x] Split image into multiple image, a.k.a, "base image". We have expert sit in our office (Andrea, CatA Core Software) to consult.
- Else?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-06-20T19:25:53Z)

is this a good topic for the summer student ? Investigate, try, evaluate.... ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-07-09T17:02:52Z)

First, we can improve the size by simply fix [single line]() that cause files duplication.

To confirm, using [dive]() to inspect the image by dump the output to json using this command:
```bash
dive -j crab-taskworker-v3-240618-stable.json registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:v3.240618-stable
```

Here the json output: [crab-taskworker-v3-240618-stable.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16158722/crab-taskworker-v3-240618-stable.json)
(Note that I cannot open dive in interactive mode, it freeze.)

If I interpret output correctly, the `.image.fileReference` field show number of time and the file path that have more than one copy in different layer.

For example from json output:
```json
{
  "image": {
    "sizeBytes": 3880994829,
    "inefficientBytes": 1740276490,
    "efficiencyScore": 0.7727956479413789,
    "fileReference": [
      {
        "count": 2,
        "sizeBytes": 141771252,
        "file": "/data/repos/WMCore/.git/objects/pack/pack-04239b6b0afb94c64c197d9272850b397d18256e.pack"
      },
      {
        "count": 2,
        "sizeBytes": 74617776,
        "file": "/data/miniconda/lib/libopenblasp-r0.3.21.so"
      },
      ....
```

The file `/data/miniconda/lib/libopenblasp-r0.3.21.so` is duplicate, but it may store in different layer.

When I do image flattening (`crane flatten`), the final image is reduce from 3.8GB to 2.98 GB (please ignore the naming here)
```
REPOSITORY                                        TAG                                                                    IMAGE ID       CREATED         SIZE
localhost:44332/test1                             testflatten                                                            9d223d8eba5a   3 hours ago     2.92GB
localhost:44332/test1                             test                                                                   a506bf737f7d   3 hours ago     3.8GB
```

That mean, if we did not make file duplication when build the image, you can reduce final image size up to 900MB.

Now, let take a look at that [single line]() that cause files duplication.
```
RUN chown -R 1000:1000 ${WDIR}
```
This line, We change the owner of all files in `/data/` path, where we install all of necessary script/binary/library for our services.
What docker does is **copy all files in this path** to new layer, then change permission.

Why? (I did not have ref here, but I think this is what happens ) Because of how container image works; each layer is immutable. You need to copy to the new layer in order to modify it.
The 2 major advantages of of immutable layer are integrity and caching. You have hash of each layer and can share togather with other images, save disk/transfer/time.

To fix this, we need to make sure **at the time we create the files inside container, it has a proper permission.** For example

- [line 51](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9728a8552f7e500b9c20445b3773a545246c14ee/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L51), for `COPY` statement, you need to supply [--chown](https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/#copy---chown---chmod) option.
- [line 109-111](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9728a8552f7e500b9c20445b3773a545246c14ee/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L109-L111), `RUN` statement that create the new directoy. You need to do `chown` at the end of statement or switch to `install` command instead.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-02T15:25:47Z)

To summarize the solution for above comment,

Janna removed [the trouble line](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f88a9b98f80f9a38e3180ed0a5b2b193a75ee5c0/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L138) and set proper owner when do `COPY` and `RUN` statement. It quite tedious to fix it all for long Dockerfile files.

But after fix, it surprised me that we actually gain 900MB back!
```
REPOSITORY                                TAG                      IMAGE ID       CREATED       SIZE
registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker   pypi-test12-1724940928   01e0817c31a5   4 days ago    2.97GB
registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker   v3.240809-stable         8332f57c2394   3 weeks ago   3.8GB
```
`v3.240809-stable` is the image version before Janna PR merged.

`dive` still report some files duplication. However, it is a small fraction so no need to bother.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-02T16:13:08Z)

Janna's PR also contains change of image builder from Kaniko to BuildKit, plus the simpler way to caching images across CI build jobs using [external storage backend](https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/) (we use `registry` backend which is already supported by registry.cern.ch). So, Instead of extra maintenance of creating baseimage, we just push all cache to registry. It cost extra space in registry but it reduce building.

I do not have exact data on how much time it reduce from using BuildKit and registry caching, but in gereral:
- The maximum build time now is not more than 5 mins (build everything from scratch)
- Average build time is 2 minutes if you change some files in `src` directory.
- The minimum build time is 1 minute if you just change the process controller scripts.
- The lowest build time I saw is 26 seconds. I am not sure what does it do though.

But the most satisfying thing for me is when you build in CI and try to pull/run on your local machine, sometimes it takes only 5 seconds to complete. It might be because of BuildKit, cache, refactoring the Dockerfile, or all of them.

I love this so much because I only have mobile internet in my apartment and it takes ages to pull image again and again.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-09-02T16:23:45Z)

I think we do not need the "Caching PyPI deps to make pip install layers more idempotent." anymore because caching already work.

There is still some room for improvement to squeeze more building efficiency, which can start from https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/optimize/

But for this issue, this is enough and we (I am pretty sure that not just me) are happy about the result.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-02T17:06:45Z)

VERY HAPPY

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c56db97db0f6ca6e885ff11f95c680201c649971/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/TaskWorker/manage.sh#L43-L50

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c56db97db0f6ca6e885ff11f95c680201c649971/scripts/task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py#L7-L10

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8556: FTS_Transfer does not handle external connection and bookkeeping properly, caused some files to be stale in the state "SUBMITTED"

State: closed
Opened: 2024-07-23T16:43:06Z
Closed: 2024-07-24T14:16:18Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8556

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-07-23T16:43:06Z)

Reported by Oscar in Computing tools: https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/re-stageout-exceptions-from-crab-jobs/44154
Task URL: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/240722_082324%3Aoglez_crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD
`FTS_Transfer.py`'logs: [vocms0194:/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/task_process/transfers/transfer_inject.log](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0194/oglez/240722_082324:oglez_crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD/SPOOL_DIR/task_process/transfers/transfer_inject.log)
Example FileID: `7fbb708684d552f510ba862f5dfb547b25fdc08d214c125bd4041781`, Job ID: `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf`

What happened here was:
1. `check_FTSJob()` finished execute for FTS Job ID `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf`, found `7fbb708684d552f510ba862f5dfb547b25fdc08d214c125bd4041781` was finished.
    `7fbb708684d552f510ba862f5dfb547b25fdc08d214c125bd4041781` were removed from bookkeeping records `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf.json` at [line 276](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L276).
    (log line: 23038-23040)
    ```
    2024-07-22 16:05:26,027: Getting state of job 4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf
    2024-07-22 16:05:26,087: State of job 4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf: ACTIVE
    2024-07-22 16:05:26,234: file XFER OK will remove davs://xrootd.cmsaf.mit.edu:1094/store/temp/user/oglez.c0781276b3d41d890451044b1ce34cb8259a05e4/craboutput/Muon/crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD/240722_082324/0000/log/cmsRun_1.log.tar.gz
    2024-07-22 16:05:26,248: Getting state of job 783f97de-481b-11ef-8fff-fa163e9e00e6
    ```
2. Next FTS Job ID processed normally, until ID `53b71580-4821-11ef-8578-fa163e255442`. Exception was raised at [line 213](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L213), program exited.

    (log line: before 23356)
    ```
    ...
    During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 679, in <module>
        algorithm()
      File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 669, in algorithm
        jobs_ongoing = state_manager(ftsContext, crabserver)
      File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 546, in state_manager
        check_FTSJob(logging, ftsContext, jobid, jobsEnded, jobs_ongoing, done_id, failed_id, failed_reasons)
      File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py", line 174, in check_FTSJob
        file_statuses = fts3.get_job_status(ftsContext, jobid, list_files=True)['files']
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/easy/state.py", line 59, in get_job_status
        return inquirer.get_job_status(job_id, list_files)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/inquirer.py", line 38, in get_job_status
        job_info["dm"] = json.loads(self.context.get("/jobs/%s/dm" % job_id))
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/context.py", line 214, in get
        return self._requester.method(
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/fts3/rest/client/request.py", line 111, in method
        response = requests.request(
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/requests/api.py", line 61, in request
        return session.request(method=method, url=url, **kwargs)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 544, in request
        resp = self.send(prep, **send_kwargs)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 657, in send
        r = adapter.send(request, **kwargs)
      File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/requests/adapters.py", line 516, in send
        raise ConnectionError(e, request=request)
    requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='fts3-cms.cern.ch', port=8446): Max retries exceeded with url: //jobs/53b71580-4821-11ef-8578-fa163e255442/dm (Caused by NewConnectionError('<urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection object at 0x15516a1e5c40>: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 111] Connection refused'))
    2024-07-22 16:05:34,440: transfer_inject.py exiting
    ```
3. FTS\_Transfer.py started new round.
    (log line: 23356)
    ```
    2024-07-22 16:10:36,639: using user's proxy from /data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/7021/0/cluster107037021.proc0.subproc0/0defbdc2956bbbd335400fd42baccb1536baa936
    ```
4. When `check_FTSJob()` execute FTS Job ID `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf` again, it read the `fileIDs` list from json `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf.json`.
    But the `fileIDs` got removed by previous round at point 1. So it simply skipped `7fbb708684d552f510ba862f5dfb547b25fdc08d214c125bd4041781`, only 3 files got added to `done_id['4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf']`.
    (log line: 23680-23684)
    ```
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,541: Getting state of job 4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,610: State of job 4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf: FINISHED
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,725: file XFER OK will remove davs://xrootd.cmsaf.mit.edu:1094/store/temp/user/oglez.c0781276b3d41d890451044b1ce34cb8259a05e4/craboutput/Muon/crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD/240722_082324/0000/outputfile_1.root
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,725: file XFER OK will remove davs://xrootd.cmsaf.mit.edu:1094/store/temp/user/oglez.c0781276b3d41d890451044b1ce34cb8259a05e4/craboutput/Muon/crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD/240722_082324/0000/log/cmsRun_738.log.tar.gz
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,726: file XFER OK will remove davs://xrootd.cmsaf.mit.edu:1094/store/temp/user/oglez.c0781276b3d41d890451044b1ce34cb8259a05e4/craboutput/Muon/crab_og07_22_102320__Muon_Run2022F-22Sep2023-v2_NANOAOD/240722_082324/0000/outputfile_738.root
    2024-07-22 16:11:02,743: Getting state of job d1d81806-4817-11ef-bd53-fa163e4409e3
    ```

5. Then, at the loop [line 593](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L593), those 3 files from point 4 got mark done.
    ```
    (log line: 23958-23959)
    2024-07-22 16:11:16,192: Marking job 3 files done and 0 files failed for job 4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf
    2024-07-22 16:11:16,265: Marked good ['168acb70538eaefb5aba53bf8ba61cb5e89df0c9d380a667f35273cc', '39757f780b4b35dadee5784be561109fbd997c28ff91442904fc0655', '276b440c0ba7b09
    ```

6. Because FTS job status IS "FINISHED" (log line: 23681) so `4442ee32-4824-11ef-9376-fa163eaa97bf` got evicted from FTS IDs ongoing list `fts_jobids.txt` by [line 608](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L608). So, FileID `7fbb708684d552f510ba862f5dfb547b25fdc08d214c125bd4041781` left in stale state `SUBMITTED`, never got processed again.

-----------------

The problems here are 2 things

- We get status of FTS job again at [line 213](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L213) without handling any exception. This cause the error in the first place.
- Then we wrongly handle the bookkeeping of fileIDs, we remove the fileIDs at the stage the fileIDs does not update to FileTransferDB yet.

Quick fix would be reuse `status` at [line 196](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L196) instead.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-07-23T16:43:35Z)

@belforte @mapellidario Could you please verify?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T17:38:29Z)

possibly related to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8323
I need some time to digest this

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T19:33:14Z)

The reason why I left this aside is that I believe that no matter what happens with our handling of FTS, PostJob will give up after 24h, submit a new job, and things will be OK. Of course that requires FTS errors to be rare.
Proper handling of exception is better.

This is hard to make fully robust, since FTS_Transfer is not stateless enough with all those files

I am struggling a bit to understand because you pointed to lines from current master, while log has lines from [v3.240527](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/v3.240527/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T20:06:40Z)

a  bit earlier in the log FTS job `aceb8c56-4828-11ef-99a3-fa163e4409e3` checking also fails, but at line [line 196](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L196), in that case exception is handled and the job is "elegantly" skipped
```
2024-07-22 16:05:33,751: Getting state of job aceb8c56-4828-11ef-99a3-fa163e4409e3
2024-07-22 16:05:33,770: failed to retrieve status for aceb8c56-4828-11ef-99a3-fa163e4409e3
```
The problem with [line 213](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bc76faca7b55d6e351348831517c54501bf26da0/scripts/task_process/FTS_Transfers.py#L213) seems that there is no exception handlling. It **may be** (but I am not sure yet) that if we `return` there similarly to what done at this FTS call few lines above, the FTS_transfer will go on and eventually properly mark in the DB all files which were removed from the `<fts_job_id>.json` files.

We can not reuse the output of L196
```python
status = fts3.get_job_status(ftsContext, jobid, list_files=False)
```
as a substitute for L213
```python
 file_statuses = fts3.get_job_status(ftsContext, jobid, list_files=True)['files']
```
output is different.
maybe we can replace the former with the latter. This was not done in order not to ask to FTS the details of all files in a job while that jobs was simply queued, to avoid overloading the server. Of course... we do not know if the extra load would be too much or not. Maybe it was back then and things improved at FTS side...

Overall what is not good is that we track transfer status in the local `json` files and in the `tranfersdb` table, in difference places of the code separated by a  lot of things which can go wrong. It is "interesting" that the doc lines for `check_FTSJob()` says that file transfer states are updated in Oracle, but they are not !

I think that the update to Oracle was moved out of the loop on FTS jobs in order to use a single POST to crabserver for the list of all files to be udpated in a run of FTS_Transfers, to reduce load on CRABServer.

But I guess we can't rewrite the script to be solid. At least not as long as there's the hope that we can switch to Rucio.

At the moment I favor catching the exception and simply returning from `check_FTSJob`. If something else fails between changing JSON files and writing to Oracle, we will have to rely on eventual PostJob time out and resubmission anyhow. Simply it should be more rare (basically VM reboots).

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-23T20:21:15Z)

OTOH, the reason for all those JSON files seems to be to avoid marking files in Oracle over and over, since an FTS job can contain many files and every time it returns the status of all. But if that's the case, why don't we update the content of that file AFTER a successful POST of the status to CRABServer ?

well.. better is the enemy of good . Let's try to be minimal

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-07-24T09:40:36Z)

Thanks for confirming.

> Overall what is not good is that we track transfer status in the local json files and in the tranfersdb table, in difference places of the code separated by a lot of things which can go wrong.

I think it is OK because it save quite a lot of traffics to rest but you need to be extra careful handle the state there. I am not sure myself if we change to pure REST will make code more clear.

And I agree with you that simply wrap try-exception around L213 should be enough to make it more robust with less code changes.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-24T10:10:42Z)

thanks, I will make a PR

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-07-25T12:39:25Z)

Relate to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8540 but this time is for Publisher.

Some code changes are needed:
- Make the args name consistence for both TW and PB, i.e., replace `--testMode` with `--sequential/pdb/console`.
- Fix import path. For example https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/92b017fa77241833f684bdc1aa9104577540dc65/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L30-L31
    It works because we run PB with command `python3 /path/to/RunPublisher.py`, so basedir of `RunPublisher.py`, `/path/to`, is automatically included in `PYTHONPATH`.
- Also include a simple fix of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8442

In REST, we depend monitoring scripts/binaries from [RPM version of cmsweb image](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/0cb2d75f9b74ff4aea5b80f679c04651aadcf14c/docker/cmsweb/Dockerfile#L72-L81).

This step is lost when migrating to a new PyPI image, [making the monitoring fail](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/ezawwczcojndbgtzsdz1qyan5o).

Note that process fds count is a must for REST service.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8571: introduce a software switch for using HTC bindings v2
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8571: introduce a software switch for using HTC bindings v2

State: closed
Opened: 2024-07-29T16:36:01Z
Closed: 2024-08-09T23:14:12Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High, Area: HTCondor
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8571

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-07-29T16:36:01Z)

- [x] a switch in TaskWorkerConfig.py
- [x] pass this info to Scheduler via a file in the spool directory. Each python script will check that file presence at the beginning before doing `import htcondor` or `import htcondor2 as htcondor`
  * Changed to use an env.variable defined in the submit JDL of the job submitted by DagmanSubmitter

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-07-30T09:30:00Z)

is creating a file in the spool directory the best we can do? do we dislike so much adding an argument in the calls from TW to the schedd?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-30T09:39:58Z)

There no "free arguments". In the call we pass am HTCondor JDL. We could use an env.variable which will be part of the env. where the dag_bootstrap_startup.sh runs. Let's try that

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-30T22:11:38Z)

the pro side of using a file is that it makes it easy to tell if a task is/was using new bindings, but I can still create the file in the dag_bootstrap_startup.sh. An env var  may be more elegant to test in the various python scripts

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-07-31T10:16:47Z)

Well, env variables are printed in the job stdout, it is not that different from checking that a file is in the spool directory

## Comment (belforte, 2024-07-31T10:40:40Z)

matter of taste, you need `sudo crabtw` to read `_condor.stdout` and it is too long for my taste

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-01T18:44:52Z)

https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/allow-v2-bindings-8571 now has a solution for TW
* `config.TaskWorker.useHtcV2 = True` in TaskWorkerConfig.py (if missing, means False)
* managed via Hiera in puppet, can be set in the host.cern.ch.yaml file
* parsed inside `manage.sh` to set an env. variable which is used in TW code to decide whch version to import

@novicecpp @mapellidario feel free to look at [comparison with master](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/compare/master...belforte:CRABServer:allow-v2-bindings-8571?expand=1) and comment

Now I need to pass the env. variable to the dagman startup job in the scheduler and use it in all scripts there.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-01T19:07:52Z)

automatic splitting is failing in an odd way. Let's  use consistently v1 or v2 before worrying more

08/01/24 16:11:23 ERROR: node Job1: job ID in userlog submit event (9693669.0.0) doesn't match ID reported earlier by submit command (9693668.0.0)!  Aborting DAG; set DAGMAN_ABORT_ON_SCARY_SUBMIT to false if you are *sure* this shouldn't cause an abort.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-02T17:51:18Z)

the problem persists when using v2 also in scheduler scripts and comes from DagmanSubmitter, it is due to a chance in HTCondor:   https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8272#issuecomment-2265870173

I will look into a fix. But for the scope of this issue, I think I am OK. Anyhow it is fixed in master branch now !
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8586

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-07T17:01:05Z)

after some trial and error and a discussion among Dario/Stefano/Wa described in #8584 we have settled on the following strategy (a simpler variant of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8571#issuecomment-2263734339 )

 *  config.TaskWorker.useHtcV2 = True in TaskWorkerConfig.py (if missing, means False)
 *  managed via Hiera in puppet, can be set in the host.cern.ch.yaml file
 *  used inside TaskWorkerConfig.py itself to set `$useHtcV2` in the environment, which in turn is used in TW code to decide what to import
 *  pass  `$useHtcV2` env.var. to scripts which run in the scheduler via `environment` directive in jobJDL

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-08T21:34:47Z)

Possibley unrelated to changes here, I have identied problems with PostJob https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8598
1. it does not run again after detecting transfer in progres, so job is stuck in transferring forever
2. it uses the deprecated Transation method which was removed in v2 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8597
```text
Thu, 08 Aug 2024 20:19:19 CEST(+0200):ERROR:PostJob Exception in setting job ClassAd attributes:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/3155/0/cluster9703155.proc0.subproc0/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py", line 2917, in set_state_ClassAds
    with self.schedd.transaction(htcondor.TransactionFlags.NonDurable):
AttributeError: 'Schedd' object has no attribute 'transaction'
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-08T21:35:26Z)

I will simply make sure that things still work for v1 and them we can integrate this to keep debuggin v2

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-08-02T16:30:42Z)

Part of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958 (fifth checkbox)

Why? It take A LOT OF CONCENTRATION to create proper PR (to put correct version name in spec file open PR).

To release new client version, we need to open PR to `cms-sw/cmsdist` default branch.
There are two use cases:
1. update crab-dev to new tag, https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/pull/8856
2. bump crab-prod to  crab-dev tag (and crab-pre to what crab-prod was at same time).  https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/pull/8856

We can leverage GH API to open PR for us, like we do with old Testsuite where we create new issue and post status of testsuite.

Triggering, maybe make it automated for `crab-dev` every time when the new version release, and manually for `crab-prod`.

We need to copy some cmssw people's brilliant ideas how they utilize the gh bot.

State: closed
