Labels: Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8590

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-08-06T18:23:08Z)

When we build from older commits like hot-patch, images like `crabtwfilebeat` also build. However, because we use the static tag (e.g., `crabtwfilebeat:v3.latest`), the hot-patch pipeline will override the latest image on the registry which which has a newer version.

I do not have better idea how to avoid this. Maybe this is just reminder.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-06T20:05:58Z)

I am not sure I understand this. @aspiringmind-code do you ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-06T22:44:31Z)

Do you mean that it just happened something like this ?
-  Let's have tag V1 and deploy it.
-  Then we create V2 and deploy.
-  V2 has a bug, we roll back TW to V1
-  But that dos not change the crabtwfilebeat which stays at V2
    -  operator (Stefano) mistake ?
-  Then you deployed V1.patch and that rolls back crabtwfilebeat to V1

In addition there's the matter of which crabtwfilebeat tag is called `latest` in registry.cern.ch

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-08-07T07:21:25Z)

Yes. I tried to write this last night but I was too tired. Thanks.

Expanding bullet 4 and 5 a bit:
- But that dos not change the crabtwfilebeat which stays at V2
    - Because we use static tag `v3.latest`
    - **Note**: I used `runContainer.sh` script, did not even thing ot crabtwfilebeat ! No matter which tag we use, I left it unchanged
- You create V1.patch which build crabtwfilebeat V1 again and upload it as `v3.latest`.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-07T10:39:35Z)

I think that the disconnect is that when we deploy via pipeline we have a procedure to deploy same tag for each container, but then wanted to roll back only one.
The fact that for `crabtwfilebeat` we always use latest build instead of a named tag, may not be that relevant since it changes rarely. But if could be sorted out as well.
I agree to take this as a reminder only for the time being.
We need more experience with the new system before looking at changing it.

yes! the code in `crabtwfilebeat` should not change much, the most important part is its configuration that comes from puppet. i do not see this as a problem.

instead of forking a CLI command in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3616cf5e4ac018be9445d77a1dca28e190edfa0c/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L335-L339

it is deprecated in HTCondor and in last round of "modernization" I missed a few places
1. in `AdjustSites` it is in a very old and obscure comment: remove. THere is also obsolete code there for the case when "CRABServer REST talks to the schedd", which is not happening anymore. REST does not make any HTC call. Remove that as well
2. in `GenerateMONIT` and `RenewRemoteProxies` we were anyhow using `list(schedd.xquery())` which is exactly what `schedd.query()` does !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8618: getTasks() fails to get tasks if tw_name is not initialised
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8618: getTasks() fails to get tasks if tw_name is not initialised

State: closed
Opened: 2024-08-14T08:08:12Z
Closed: 2024-08-30T12:43:49Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8618

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2024-08-14T08:08:12Z)

[See](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43208f8307874dab3d255415b62aa45c0cd1e32f/src/python/CRABUtils/TaskUtils.py#L10)
The code was initially taken from [here](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/91985873c444711865681a3211f74a72c47730ff/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/TapeRecallManager.py#L190-L207) which works.

Stefano's Diagnosis:
When tw_name column has NULL value, it fails at comparisons with the use of LIKE operator in SQL as the wild character "%".

Fix:
Initialize the tw_name to a default value that is not NULL

References:
[1] https://www.w3schools.com/sql/sql_null_values.asp
[2] https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3924400/like-does-not-accept-null-value
[3] https://stackoverflow.com/a/38765838

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-16T15:31:06Z)

in this case WMCore/Credential/Proxy failes because of a problem with `/tmp/hsperfdata_crab3/760874`
that is a file created by [JavaVM](https://stackoverflow.com/a/2655306)

It is true that `voms-proxi-*` is now a Java application, but one would have thought that it was possible to run two instances at same time. Of course if the file is named after the user `crab3` and the lock owned by the process (the TW slave) there is a chance that different processes try to use it at same time :-(

From [reading around]() it looks like this can only be disabled with a Java option, i.e. inside voms-proxy* commands themselves. I.e, should be reported as a bug to voms-proxy-utils developers.

Maybe... just maybe,the problem is that WMCore/Credential/Proxy.py tries to parse the output of `voms-proxy-info -timeleft` assuming it is a number of seconds. But in this case a warning line is inserted and the is stdout
```
[0.002s,warning,perf,memops] Cannot use file /tmp/hsperfdata_crab3/760874 because it is locked by another process (errno = 11)
447504
```
while the exit code is still 0

The only improvement I can imagine is to add `tail -1` to
```python
timeLeftCmd = 'voms-proxy-info -file ' + proxy + ' -timeleft'
```
in https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/39c50491199ff505886caed4ab1d3661844b2329/src/python/WMCore/Credential/Proxy.py#L731

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-27T13:23:26Z)

another problem [surfaced](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab3-issue-issue-with-crab-task-submission-in-submitfailed-status/46677) lately. I added logging and exception handling and got this in the log which **I annotate** here

2024-08-27 11:50:34,795:INFO:MyProxyLogon:try first to retrieve credential with login name woji_CRAB
2024-08-27 11:50:35,321:ERROR:Proxy:Unable to retrieve delegated proxy using login woji_CRAB for user DN /DC=ch/
DC=cern/OU=Organic Units/OU=Users/CN=woji/CN=871516/CN=Wonjae Ji! Exit code:1 output: **this comes from myproxy-logon**
2024-08-27 11:50:35,732:ERROR:Proxy:Will check proxy lifetime on file /data/certs/creds/ba4cdc8605a942bc85a822a2
0f83b056c9d2ad70 **since no info is passed back by Proxy.py, I need to check the lifetime but the file is not there**
2024-08-27 11:50:36,143:ERROR:Proxy:Retrieved timeLeftLocal is: **i.e. a null string**
2024-08-27 11:50:36,144:ERROR:Proxy:Got exception invalid literal for int() with base 10:   **now I catch this inside Proxy.py instead of raising an unexpected exception which makes MyProxylogon fail**
2024-08-27 11:50:36,145:ERROR:Proxy:Repeat voms-proxy-info with full output  **I added this diagnostics**
2024-08-27 11:50:36,556:ERROR:Proxy:CMD: env -i sh -c 'voms-proxy-info -file /data/certs/creds/ba4cdc8605a942bc8
5a822a20f83b056c9d2ad70 -timeleft '
2024-08-27 11:50:36,556:ERROR:Proxy:RC: 1
2024-08-27 11:50:36,557:ERROR:Proxy:OUT:
2024-08-27 11:50:36,557:ERROR:Proxy:ERR: Proxy not found: /data/certs/creds/ba4cdc8605a942bc85a822a20f83b056c9d2
ad70 (No such file or directory)

2024-08-27 11:50:36,557:ERROR:MyProxyLogon:Could not get a proxy valid for at least 5-days from myproxy.cern.ch for /DC=ch/DC=cern/OU=Organic Units/OU=Users/CN=woji/CN=871516/CN=Wonjae Ji. **and I let it exit with timeleft=0 which causes this**
2024-08-27 11:50:36,558:ERROR:MyProxyLogon:Will try again in verbose mode  ** and it works after that**

**Interpretation**
it seems pretty clear that when we do `voms-proxy-info` on a non-existing file, the error message goes to stderr, and stdout is empty. That's how we can get an empty string in `timeLeftLocal` which of course can't be parsed as an `int`.
But the only way for this to happen, is that `voms-proxy-info` somehow returns with exit code = 0, since in [Proxy.py](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/d618b120c6189cb8d9c89e28f202b440ab6f2bae/src/python/WMCore/Credential/Proxy.py#L722-L750) we have
```python
        timeLeft = 0
        timeLeftCmd = 'voms-proxy-info -file ' + proxy + ' -timeleft | tail -1'
        timeLeftLocal, _, self.retcode = execute_command(self.setEnv(timeLeftCmd), self.logger, self.commandTimeout)
        if self.retcode != 0:
            self.logger.error("Error while checking proxy timeleft for %s" % proxy)
            return timeLeft
        try:
            timeLeft = int(timeLeftLocal.strip())
        except ValueError:
            timeLeft = sum(int(x) * 60 ** i for i, x in enumerate(reversed(timeLeftLocal.strip().split(":"))))
```

With that the TW was reporting `''` as the timeLeftLocal string, and thus raising a silent `ValueError` at `int(timeLeftLocal.strip())` and a fatal one from the `sum(int(x)`

I patched crab-prod-tw01 to use
```python
        self.logger.error("Will check proxy lifetime on file %s", proxy)
        timeLeftCmd = 'voms-proxy-info -file ' + proxy + ' -timeleft | tail -1'
        timeLeftLocal, _, self.retcode = execute_command(self.setEnv(timeLeftCmd), self.logger, self.commandTimeout)

        if self.retcode != 0:
            self.logger.error("Error while checking proxy timeleft for %s" % proxy)
            return timeLeft
        try:
            self.logger.error("Retrieved timeLeftLocal is: %s", timeLeftLocal)
            timeLeft = int(timeLeftLocal.strip())
        except ValueError:
            try:
                timeLeft = sum(int(x) * 60 ** i for i, x in enumerate(reversed(timeLeftLocal.strip().split(":"))))
            except Exception as e:
                self.logger.error("Got exception %s", e)
                self.logger.error("Repeat voms-proxy-info with full output")
                timeLeftCmd = 'voms-proxy-info -file ' + proxy + ' -timeleft '
                out, err, ret = execute_command(self.setEnv(timeLeftCmd), self.logger, self.commandTimeout)
                self.logger.error("CMD: %s", self.setEnv(timeLeftCmd))
                self.logger.error("RC: %s", ret)
```
and problem was solved, with the log above which suggests that `if self.retcode != 0:` was `False` !!!!!!

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8650: Canary deployments - REST, TW, Publisher

State: closed
Opened: 2024-08-26T15:03:29Z
Closed: 2025-02-27T10:41:00Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8650

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-08-26T15:03:29Z)

## introduction

We have always dreamed about processing a small portion of production crab tasks with a new crab version.

We do not have a general solution, each crab system will need to be adapted in a very specific way.

### REST

This requires no change in the code, but requires some experience with k8s deployments. The idea is:

- create a new deployment in `dmwm/CMSKubernetes/helm/crabserver/templates`, call it `crabserver-canary`.
    - change only `metadata.name: crabserver-canary`, do **not** change for example `metadata.labels.app: crabserver` nor `spec.selector.matchLabels.app: crabserver`
- create a new values file `dmwm/CMSKubernetes/helm/crabserver/values-canary.yaml`
- change [deploy.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/helm/crabserver/deploy.sh)  to accept `canary` as an argument, you will need to edit the `cluster_map`.
    - otherwise simply use `helm template crabserver . -f values.yaml -f values-${1}.yaml | kubectl -n crab apply -f -`, but beware to be connected with the proper context (username+cluster)!

### TaskWorker

This requires some change in the code, that have been outlined in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/wiki/TaskWorker-Canary-Deployment

we decided that we run one TW per virtual machine, so that the hostname is enough to identify which TW process/container we are referring to.

### Publisher

This is not defined yet, but we have some ideas. The simplest one is

- run a publisher on every VM where we run TW
- make sure that a single publisher only select jobs that have been submitted by tasks processed by the TW running on the same VM
    - need to add tm_twname to filetransfersdb table or pick it up from task table using a join on taskname. In any case need to change the SQL which picks the files to work on.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8651: schedulers - implement automatic reboot
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8651: schedulers - implement automatic reboot

State: open
Opened: 2024-08-26T15:18:18Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Medium, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8651

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-08-26T15:18:18Z)

## intro

We want to automatically reboot all crab schedulers at least once a year.

## prerequisite

We should figure out how to be nice to HammerCloud on schedd restart if we want to automatically reboot our schedds: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7410

## implementation

We had a brainstorming session in udine and so far the simplest thing that we could think of is

- move the list of enabled schedds that TW should use from gitlab to puppet.
- every schedd in the list should have a new parameter alongside the current "enabled: 0/1", and it should be the desired date of schedd reboot. make sure that there is no overlap in these dates! If you want to be fancy, you could also have a list of dates, in order to accommodate for multiple reboots per year.
- TW reads the configuration and if the "(current time - reboot time) < 1week", then TW should stop using that schedd
- add a daily cronjob to the schedd. if the "(current time - reboot time) < 2d" (using 2 days with a daily cronjob should avoid negative results, maybe they can be a problem in a bash script) then reboot the schedd. the reboot procedure should be
    - hold all the running dagmans, specifying "schedd reboot" as hold reason
    - condor_off
    - reboot
    - (condor_on should be automatic)
    - add a systemctl service unit, systemctl timer, hourly cronjob, whatever system you like, that releases all the hold dagmans that match the "schedd reboot" hold reason

something like this from Eric
```text
The setup should be like this (pseudo-code)

git clone github/belforte/crab (is now called “origin”)
git add remote upstream github/dmwm/crab (is now called upstream)

Then when your repository is out of date with the central:

git checkout master
git fetch upstream            # fetch commits history
git fetch --tags upstream     # also the tags (need two commands)
git merge upstream/master     # merge upstream on your local
git push  origin              # move those changes up
git push --tags origin        # also the tags

To develop something (version 1)

git checkout master # start with latest master
git checkout -b my_feature # checkout and start a new branch
git push --set-upstream origin my_feature # track new branch in your github
# [code]
git commit -m “My feature is awesome”
git push origin # put on your github

Then visit github and make a pull request.

To develop something (version 2)
git checkout master
git checkout -b my_feature
# code
git commit -m “My feature is awesome”
git push origin my_feature  # i.e. use the name of the branch

Then visit github and make a pull request.

You’ll notice in my schemed your changes follow this route:

begin on local branch
pushed to remote branch
pulled/merged onto upstream (DMWM repo) by Marco
only arrive on your local master with the merge of upstream/master
then pushed to your github master
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8667: find a better way to prevent users from recalling PB's
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8667: find a better way to prevent users from recalling PB's

State: open
Opened: 2024-08-28T18:57:31Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8667

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-08-28T18:57:31Z)

current quota check is "lazy" as creation of several rules can sneak in before user account quota is increased in Rucio to where CRAB limit kicks in.
Lately it resulted in one user being able to ask for recall of O(1.2)PB (out of the dreaded 7PB of HeavyIon AOD) before CRAB refused more submissions.

This is all in all rare, so we do not want to add a lot of code, but it was pointed out that it would be nice to have a way to tell the user something like "hey, are you sure you want to do this ?"

There's no clear good idea yet.

Possibilities include
* lowering the current 500PB quota.
* doing something special when HI and AOD appear in the dataset name
* when creating a recall rule, wait until quota has been updated, to limit damage of concurrent creation
* force user to "do something extra" for each large recall (e.g. >100TB or 200TB)
* keep track of recall size in our DB so that it is quick and quota check can be effective
* investigate with Rucio experts if something can be done on that side
* ...

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-08-29T07:53:45Z)

> force user to "do something extra" for each large recall (e.g. >100TB or 200TB)

No, please.

> when creating a recall rule, wait until quota has been updated, to limit damage of concurrent creation

Dumb idea:
- random 0-60 seconds before create quota, create. wait quota to update maximum 2 mins.

Another dumb idea: Do tape recall sequentially.
- Set new stage something like: `TORECALL`
- Recurring action grab `TORECALL` task, then create a recall rule.
- Wait for quota update.
- Then set state to `TAPERECALL`.

as discussed in Udine's workshop we will eliminate this directory and stop pulling the external config from glitlab into CRABServer
- [ ] "compatible versions" --> remove. Since now we control client distribution via CVMFS we do not have to worry about ancient clients laying around anymore

- [ ] delegate-dn --> needs to stay in the server, so that CRABClient can retrieve and create proper credential. So make it part of CRABServer's `config.py` (which should be moved out of secrets) as per #8685  Since this file "never changes" we could even make it part of REST container. And if cluster-dependent minor tweaks will ever be needed, use env.vars. set via [Helm vaues files](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/helm/crabserver)

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-08-30T12:42:04Z)

I would like to commit the new serviceaccount for CI to [CMSKuberentes](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes) but I do not know where to put it. Also, the crab's logstash manifests [is in different place](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/kubernetes/cmsweb/monitoring/crab/logstash.conf).

After discuss with @arooshap, she suggested to put everything together in single helm chart, `helm/crabserver`, and use value flags to render specific resources groups.

We have 3 resource group:

- [crabserver](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/helm/crabserver/templates/deployment.yaml) manifest for crab rest.
- log pipline, which have logstash and crab's filebeat.
- [new CI serviceaccount](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-cicd/gitlab/variables.html#testbed-cluster) that need cluster admin permission.

For example, the `values-testX.yaml` only for render `crabserver`-related manifests:
```
environment: "test"
enabled: true
image:
  tag: "pypi-test12-manual1"
```

To render log pipeline and CI serviceaccount (e.g., `values-admin.yaml`), the value file will look like this:
```
environment: "preprod"
enabled: false
logPipeline:
  enabled: true
ciServiceAccount:
  enabled: true
```

This will be easier for cluster admin to maintain all our services.
And for us, we only need to focus on modifying the `crabserver` resourec group, e.g., adding a new canary deployment.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8689: [CI] Deploy new version on production using gitlab CI

State: open

Labels: Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8689

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-09-04T15:56:26Z)

One of our CI wishlist, second checkbox https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7958

It still use tag-and-push pattern, or trigger through WebUI, which does not have a beautiful interface like Jenkins, but might be more convenient.

The pipeline would have 3 stages: deploy -> runtest -> checktest, to make sure the newly deployed services are running properly.

To deploy on prod, you need 2 variables:
- `DEPLOY_PROD`, value is container tag you want to deploy.
- `DEPLOY_SERVICE`, value is `all` or service name (REST/TaskWorker/Publisher_schedd/Publisher_rucio)

The main blocker (or not?) is to negotiate with Aroosha, to allow us to deploy REST from CI, like we do on testbed, on production backend cluster. I am not sure if she has any security concern about this.

indeed [predag.0.txt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0119/alobanov/240829_122306:alobanov_crab_TTtoLNu2Q/SPOOL_DIR/prejob_logs/predag.0.txt) is full of messages like
Thu, 29 Aug 2024 15:50:55 CEST(+0200):WARNING:LumiBased Skipping runlumi pair (1, 703) as it was already been processed.Will add /store/mc/Run3Summer22MiniAODv4/TTtoLNu2Q_TuneCP5_13p6TeV_powheg-pythia8/MINIAODSIM/130X_mcRun3_2022_realistic_v5-v2/50000/83387792-3d10-4bed-9acc-346be670f881.root to the input files of the job processing the lumi

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-05T10:58:24Z)

hmm.. as I wrote in [cms-talk](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/duplicate-events-in-mini-nano-process/47484/8?u=belforte)

The problem does not seem related to automatic splitting and quite possibly originates from the fact that many (all?) lumis are duplicated in different file of the input dataset [1].
I have not done the test, but suspect that a simple “split by lumi” would have been resulted in similar duplication.

WMCore’s SplittingFactory expects a lumi to be present in one file only and when it detects it in multiple files, it assumes that it was an exceptional situation where it has been split and that those files contains independent sets of events which together make up the full lumi content

I do not fully understand how exactly this may end up with the same input file being list many tens of times to same job (once for every lumi ??). But can’t really try to understand all WMCore internals.

Since this is a SIM dataset, I imgaine that it was simply created in two steps, every time starting lumicout at 1. Run number is always 1 for SIM.

So that the current task may have actually processed only half (?) of the generated sample.

Given my limited understanding, and the fact that setting of lumi numbers in SIM is not a strictly controlled process, I suggest to process SIM in splitByFile mode.

Stefano

So the code to create `InputFiles.tar.gz` was possibly created for `preparelocal`, but eventually

```
transfer_input_files = InputFiles.tar.gz, subdag.jdl
```

The way things work is that DagmanCreator returns https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1255
which gets passed as input to DagmanSubmitter an in there
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L261
followed by https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L399

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L540

that `jobJDL` object is saved in `DAGJob.jdl` file in TW `/data/srv/tmp/_<taskname>` directory
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L543-L544

```text

**site.ad vs. site.ad.json**

manipulation of `site.ad` in AdjustSites,py is unchanged since Brian's commit in 2013.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L481-L487
But I can't find any other place in the code base which references to CRAB_SiteAdUpdate.
Is that code simply "never executed" ?

PreJob uses `site.ad.json` to create site lists `avalaible` (where we can run) and ``datasites` (where data is).
If it does not find it, falls back to `site.ad` to create list of available sites, only, and at first sight it should crash since `datasites` is unconditionally used in following code

There is also this very interesting commit from Brain 10y ago  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/75b85ca950219a823d92121eb231d1d50c2d4a2a which looks like he introduced the JSON, leaving the old code for temporary compatibility (?) and then.. change stuck.

So I am leaning to `site.ad` can be removed.

AFAICT those two files are created by DagmanCreator
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1089-L1090
Yet I can't be sure nor figure out how they are populated from reading the code. Need to run it step-by-step.

`site.ad.json` contains `siteinfo` structure
`site.ad` contains `sitead` strucutre
those structures are initialized to "empty" in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L805-L816
(when DagmanCreator runs in TW, there are no files to read)

so in particular we start with
```python
siteinfo = {'group_sites': {}, 'group_datasites': {}}
```
Then DagmanCreator calls createSubdag() which gets the list of data sites and available sites for each job groups (one job group for each set of locations, IIUC)
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L891
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L896
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L910
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L933
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L943-L944
 and calls  makeDagSpecs() where those are added to `siteinfo` dictionary
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L599-L601
(no comment on the what looks like a horrible dirty trick with L599)

My conclusion from the above is that `site.ad` is old, obsolete, useless and can be simply removed.

State: closed

Labels: Type: Enhancement
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8707

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-09-20T14:48:30Z)

e.g. on REST we have
```console
crab3@crabserver-644cb69d77-n7sqw:/data$ ./manage.py status
crabserver is RUNNING, PID 67
crab3@crabserver-644cb69d77-n7sqw:/data$
```
which by the way is broken, since in that case at least proc 67 is gone and the correct one is 68

but in TW
```console
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ ./manage.py status
Error: Not implemented.
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$
```

We'd like status to not only indicate if process is running, but also whether it run code from the container `/data/srv/current/lib...` or from the local GithHub repository `/data/repos/....`

that can be done with this trick from @novicecpp

```console
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ cat /proc/18/environ |tr '\0' '\n'|grep PYTHONPATH
PYTHONPATH=/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/:
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$
```

`./status.sh` could also print the version number ( tag name)

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8719: change how user "debug" files in `debug_files.tar.gz` are handled
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8719: change how user "debug" files in `debug_files.tar.gz` are handled

State: closed
Opened: 2024-09-26T11:00:06Z
Closed: 2025-03-03T17:15:10Z
Labels: Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8719

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-09-26T11:00:06Z)

currently we put in S3 cache `debug_files.tar.gz` which contains user's config and script exe to help operators debug problems and to create a new task to submit in `crab recovery`

But in order to make those files visible in the UI, we need an URL which points to the text version. We currently do this by placing files in WEB_DIR/debug and fetching via scheduler.

Also for historical reasons the TW sends to the scheduler both the tarball and the explicit files, which is a duplication of content.

Can we do something better, simpler and easier to document and understand ?

Since those files are small, the duplication in sending from TW to scheduler is not a big worry, but confusion and lack of documentation is bad.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-26T11:01:34Z)

move my thoughts here from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8699#issuecomment-2376562701

about `debug` directory in tarball.
the reason to expand `debug_files.tar.gz` in DagmanCreator is to make the files available to the CRABServerUI
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1126
so that in the UI they can be fetched from the scheduler [1]
OTOH this could be done in AdjustSites when WEB_DIR is prepared instead of both copying there  `debug_files.tar.gz` and creating a symlink for `debug/` directory
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L228-L233

And leave for a future optimization to simply put files in S3, like we do for twlog. w/o creating the `debug_files.tar.gz`. That will require changes to `crab recovery` and `crab getsandbox` too, besides of course `task_info.js` where files will be downloaded from S3, not the scheduler.

Having a tar saves on repeated calls to crabserver (to get preapproved url's) and S3 from the client. The idea was that when CRABClient is executed from sites with a large RTT, the fewer http calls, the better.
Maybe do this in the TW ? DagmanCreator could upload the files to S3 instead of adding to `InputFiles.tar.gz`.

Maybe better to settle on the final solution, and do all changes in one go. Avoid putting code there "for a few months" which is hard to remove.

[1]
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/script/task_info.js#L231-L245

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-03T17:10:49Z)

The above has been (silently ?) done already as part of Dagman* and sandbox handling restructuring.
Situation is:

* CRABClient prepares `debug_files.tar.gz` and uploads it to S3
   * https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/bf347bd46487754cc4388af7a8c77a835496df44/src/python/CRABClient/JobType/Analysis.py#L188-L194
* AdjustSites donwloads it from S3 and expands into `WEB_DIR/debug_files`
   *  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5918264f44561765ae22010ed06945c213e5e2b2/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L433

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-03T17:15:10Z)

So all was done, and there is nothing more to do

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8720: remove obsolete `site.ad` file from TW and schedulers
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8720: remove obsolete `site.ad` file from TW and schedulers

State: closed
Opened: 2024-09-26T16:32:11Z
Closed: 2024-09-30T13:02:45Z
Labels: Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8720

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-09-26T16:32:11Z)

since a long time only `site.ad.json` is used ! ref: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8699#issuecomment-2377222298

text pasted here for convenience:
**site.ad vs. site.ad.json**

manipulation of `site.ad` in AdjustSites,py is unchanged since Brian's commit in 2013.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L481-L487
But I can't find any other place in the code base which references to CRAB_SiteAdUpdate.
Is that code simply "never executed" ?

PreJob uses `site.ad.json` to create site lists `avalaible` (where we can run) and ``datasites` (where data is).
If it does not find it, falls back to `site.ad` to create list of available sites, only, and at first sight it should crash since `datasites` is unconditionally used in following code

There is also this very interesting commit from Brain 10y ago  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/75b85ca950219a823d92121eb231d1d50c2d4a2a which looks like he introduced the JSON, leaving the old code for temporary compatibility (?) and then.. change stuck.

So I am leaning to `site.ad` can be removed.

AFAICT those two files are created by DagmanCreator
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1089-L1090
Yet I can't be sure nor figure out how they are populated from reading the code. Need to run it step-by-step.

`site.ad.json` contains `siteinfo` structure
`site.ad` contains `sitead` strucutre
those structures are initialized to "empty" in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L805-L816
(when DagmanCreator runs in TW, there are no files to read)

so in particular we start with
```python
siteinfo = {'group_sites': {}, 'group_datasites': {}}
```
Then DagmanCreator calls createSubdag() which gets the list of data sites and available sites for each job groups (one job group for each set of locations, IIUC)
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L891
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L896
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L910
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L933
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L943-L944
 and calls  makeDagSpecs() where those are added to `siteinfo` dictionary
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L599-L601
(no comment on the what looks like a horrible dirty trick with L599)

My conclusion from the above is that `site.ad` is old, obsolete, useless and can be simply removed.

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-09-27T08:26:28Z)

and while we are at this, do not rely only on `ddm_weight=0` to avoid test RSE's, but explicitely avoid RSE's of type TEST

should modify

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioActions.py#L119

## Comment (amaltaro, 2024-09-27T10:51:09Z)

@belforte in case it makes your life easier, the expression to avoid Test RSEs that we have implemented in WMCore uses `\cms_type=test`, e.g.:
```
"rse_type=TAPE&wmcore_output_tape=True\cms_type=test"
```
HTH.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8727: reorganize scripts directory, simplify creation of TW Tarballs
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8727: reorganize scripts directory, simplify creation of TW Tarballs

State: closed
Opened: 2024-09-30T16:28:45Z
Closed: 2025-08-25T10:26:19Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: High, Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8727

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-09-30T16:28:45Z)

in current [scripts](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/tree/master/scripts) directory we mix files uses for different purposes, which forces us to keep explicit lists of file names in [buildTWTarballs.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/buildTWTarballs.sh)

Instead we can structure `scripts` so that there is a top directory for "things which need to go in the scheduler's SPOOL_DIR" and "things which need to go in the grid job directory"

That will simplify both tarball creations and use and will be safer against adding, renaming files.

See https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8699#issuecomment-2374495276

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-30T16:31:10Z)

I paste here text from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8699#issuecomment-2374495276 for convenience

add two subdirectories in CRABServer/scripts
```text
scripts
├── dagman
│   └── task_process
└── job_wrapper
```
so that in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/buildTWTarballs.sh#L76-L84

we only copy well named directories around, like done now for `task_process`

and also move expanding of job_wrapper tarball
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L49

to the top wrapper script between these lines
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/e8149dda5ff7a4fee80d3b25d5c038ead60c711d/scripts/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L225-L227

## Comment (belforte, 2024-09-30T16:40:12Z)

better do right after #6544 "while memory is fresh" so that I can capture all changes in a documentation #8728

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-05T20:13:00Z)

my branch can submit and run a 1-job task now https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/reorganize-tw-tarballs

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-06T12:32:06Z)

summary of changes:
* TW only creates two tar files: `TaskManagerRun.tar.gz` and `CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz` . They contain "top level scripts" and all python dependencies in `WMCore.zip` and `CRAB3.zip`
* `setup.py` TaskWorker part has been modified not to reference "named files and directories" any more
* `CRAB3.zip` now contains all code in `src/python`
* files created by DagmanCreator and needed on the AP are added to tarballs
* list of input files to transfer in condor_submit is now down to bare minimum (one for AP, two for WN since we add user's sandbox)
* initial script in AP and WN expands tarballs, restoring current situation, so code runs as before
* a couple of files need to be extracted from tarballs in order to be used as command in `condor_submit`: `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh` for the AP is extracted by DagmanCreator, `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh` is extracted by `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh`

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-06T12:39:43Z)

todo:
- [x] test Publisher
   - [x] schedd
   - [x] rucio
 - [ ] test with full tests in CI pipeline

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-06T18:36:11Z)

found an issue: `crab report` tries to download `input_files.tar.gz` and `run_and_lumis.tar.gz` from WEB_DIR, but those are now inside `CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz`
But this should not happen given https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5368

the problem is that `crab report` expects to find those  file at the  top level  in `InputFiles.tar.gz` not inside . But now
```
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$ tar tf InputFiles.tar.gz
CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz
TaskManagerRun.tar.gz
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$
```

Best  approach seems to modify `crab report` to expand those tarballs in the tmp directory where `InputFiles.tar.gz`is downloaded from S3.

Changes to `crab preparelocal` are also likely needed,so will have the usual 3 steps

1. change client to be forward compatible
2. change TaskWorket
3. cleanup client

addressed in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5409 and step 3. will not be needed

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-07T20:50:44Z)

Additionally automatic splitting fails with the following because DagmanCreator needs to update `input_args.json` with the arguments for the new jobs created by PreDAG

```
Wed, 06 Aug 2025 21:36:07 CEST(+0200):DEBUG:DagmanCreator Acquired lock on run and lumi tarball
Wed, 06 Aug 2025 21:36:07 CEST(+0200):DEBUG:DagmanCreator First iteration: creating run and lumi from scratch
Wed, 06 Aug 2025 21:36:07 CEST(+0200):DEBUG:DagmanCreator First iteration: creating inputfiles from scratch
Got a fatal exception: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'input_args.json'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.9/runpy.py", line 197, in _run_module_as_main
    return _run_code(code, main_globals, None,
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.9/runpy.py", line 87, in _run_code
    exec(code, run_globals)
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5791/0/cluster10265791.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/TaskManagerBootstrap.py", line 24, in <module>
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5791/0/cluster10265791.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/TaskManagerBootstrap.py", line 18, in bootstrap
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5791/0/cluster10265791.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py", line 132, in execute
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5791/0/cluster10265791.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py", line 316, in executeInternal
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/5791/0/cluster10265791.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py", line 1102, in createSubdag
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'input_args.json'
[crabtw@vocms059 prejob_logs]$
```

So I have two possibilities:
 1. ship input_args.json to the Job explicitly "at same level as CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz
 2. update it inside the CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz tarball (a bit awkward: untar,, replace, tar again)

I will try 2. first, since is the cleanest

But need to take also of `run_and_lumis.tar.gz ` and `input_files.tar.gz` which both need new info when we create new jobs In this case the error happens in the job wrapper
```

==== Tweak PSet at Mon Aug 11 20:10:35 2025 UTC ====
Failed to get information from tarball run_and_lumis.tar.gz and file job_lumis_1.json. Error : "filename 'job_lumis_1.json' not found"
Failed to get information from tarball input_files.tar.gz and file job_input_file_list_1.txt. Error : "filename 'job_input_file_list_1.txt' not found"
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-13T16:48:31Z)

my [branch](https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/reorganize-tw-tarballs) works (again) for normal tasks after heavy restructuring of DagmanCreator to deal with `run_and_lumis.tar.gz` and `input_files.tar.gz` in PreDag
Time to test again automatic splitting

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-14T10:32:35Z)

almost works. It turns out that when using automatic splitting PostJon needs `runs_and_lumis.tar.gz` to know which lumis were meant to be processed so it can build list of lumis for tail stages.
```text
Thu, 14 Aug 2025 12:18:54 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob ====== Starting saving data for automatic splitting.

  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/3529/0/cluster10273529.proc0.subproc0/CRAB3.zip/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py", line 1872, in saveAutomaticSplittingData
[...]

almost. I had missed these lines in PreDag which only come in to action for tail DAGs
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ac6a37af7fa8fdedfbc9fbf0c1f424133bbc8927/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L365-L372

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-15T20:02:28Z)

looks very promising now, tail jobs created and running

https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250815_160213%3Abelforte_crab_20250815_180209

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-16T13:44:39Z)

all OK

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-16T13:51:36Z)

now.. should I extract `run_and_lumis.tar.gz` from JobWrapper tarball in dagaman_bootstrap_startup ? So that there is no need for changes in PostJob and PreDag ?
And maybe rename `CMSRunaAnalysis.tar.gz` to `JobWrapper.tar.gz` ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-18T14:44:40Z)

expanding tarball in PreDag, which runs 3 times per task at most is OK. But PostJob runs thousands of times, esp. for automatic splitting. I think I better limit tar operations as much as possible. So will extract `run_and_lumis.tar.gz` in `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh`

Ouch. PreDag now adds more lumimask in ` run_and_lumis.tar.gz`, I can't keep using the one created in `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh`, need to keep in SPOOL_DIR the one which was last used in `condor_submit`.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8738: fix Rucio quota checking
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8738: fix Rucio quota checking

State: closed
Opened: 2024-10-11T16:57:34Z
Closed: 2024-10-11T19:02:15Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8738

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-10-11T16:57:34Z)

we have been misled by the (very poor) documentation in https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/client_api/accountclient#get_local_account_usage

after several tests the actual behavior of that API is
 * **it always returns a generator which will span all RSE's where that account has quota**
 * **If you indicate a site, it still returns a generator for all RSE's bt the limit are retrieved only for the indicated site**

See e.g. this python snippet
```text
>>> for q in rucio.get_local_account_usage(account=account, rse='T2_IT_Legnaro'): print(q)
...
{'rse_id': '16eef8c8359d47c985c5cc48dd1a1a56', 'rse': 'T1_DE_KIT_Disk', 'bytes': 755868188, 'files': 1196, 'bytes_limit': 0, 'bytes_remaining': -755868188}

>>>
```

```
rucio list-account-usage crab_test_group
rucio list-account-usage --rse T2_IT_Legnaro crab_test_group
rucio list-account-usage --rse T1_DE_KIT_Disk crab_test_group
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8755: make possible to run validation tests in parallel
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8755: make possible to run validation tests in parallel

State: open
Opened: 2024-10-31T14:43:09Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8755

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-10-31T14:43:09Z)

in the new CI pipeline based on GitLab runner, we have hit the situation where two scripts run at same time creating races in accessing ~/.crab3 cache file.

Should modify test script so that every crab command explicitly uses `-d <directory>` option.
And also point CRAB3_CRAB_CACHE to /dev/null to avoid possible access conflicts, see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5337

- [ ] add a `remakeTask{}` to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/v3.241018/test/testUtils.py  (basically the first lines of current `checkStatus{}` : do a crab remake and returns directory name
- [ ] call it in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/v3.241018/test/makeTests.py so to explicitly pass `-d ...` to each command.
- [ ] remove the now duplicated code from  `checkStatus{}`

That will allow running CCV in parallel with other tests.
CV is not straightforward, since having `-d` option or not should ideally part of the test itself.

It looks to me that ST test is safe on this regard. But should be reviewed.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-13T14:41:42Z)

this may have been solved by now. Should check and if not, make a plan of what to do

A list is accessing an object (0x154e2060ea40) already deleted (list name = TList)

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8774: automatic splitting fails in TW v3.241107
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8774: automatic splitting fails in TW v3.241107

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-07T15:49:45Z
Closed: 2024-11-08T08:22:53Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: In Progress, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8774

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-11-07T15:49:45Z)

```
Problem handling 241107_153134:belforte_crab_20241107_163129 because of 'avgEvtsPerLumi' failure, traceback follows
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py", line 98, in executeAction
    output = work.execute(nextinput, task=self.task, tempDir=self.tempDir)
  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py", line 1216, in execute
    info, params, inputFiles, splitterResult = self.executeInternal(*args, **kw)
  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py", line 1202, in executeInternal
    splittingSummary.addJobs(jobs)
  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Splitter.py", line 165, in addJobs
    avgEventsPerLumi = sum([f['avgEvtsPerLumi'] for f in job['input_files']])/float(len(job['input_files']))
  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Splitter.py", line 165, in <listcomp>
    avgEventsPerLumi = sum([f['avgEvtsPerLumi'] for f in job['input_files']])/float(len(job['input_files']))
KeyError: 'avgEvtsPerLumi'
```

at first sight I moved splittingSummary in DagmanCreator but it does not work for automatic splitting.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97f447747265684589ac1f5be773eed80de02239/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1199-L1204

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T16:26:43Z)

and the problem is from these lines
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97f447747265684589ac1f5be773eed80de02239/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Splitter.py#L163-L168

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T16:35:02Z)

indeed in this case the `<class 'WMCore.DataStructs.File.File'>` object `f` does not have the key 'avgEvtsPerLumi' [1]
Same for the other 4 jobs here (automatic splitting creates the 5 probe jobs in the Splitting action in TW using FileBased splitting [2])

Yet `'avgEvtsPerLumi'` is present also in WMCore/JobSplitting/FileBased.py

[1]
```
(Pdb) jobs[0,'input_files',0].keys()
dict_keys(['lfn', 'size', 'events', 'checksums', 'runs', 'merged', 'last_event', 'first_event', 'locations', 'parents', 'block', 'workflow'])
(Pdb)
```

[2]
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97f447747265684589ac1f5be773eed80de02239/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Splitter.py#L44-L51

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T16:48:27Z)

I am curious if we see same problem in a simple FileBased split.
hmm.. same CI pipeline where automatic splitting failed has this task with used FileSplitting and submitted finely
https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/241107_130406%3Acrabint1_crab_20241107_140406

TW log has no error and `splitter-summary.json` was created w/o problems
```text
crab3@crab-preprod-tw01:/data/srv/tmp/_241107_130406:crabint1_crab_20241107_1404065_e7f1jo$ cat splitting-summary.json
{"algo": "FileBased", "total_jobs": 10, "total_lumis": 0, "total_events": 200100, "max_lumis": 0, "max_events": 24000, "avg_lumis": 0.0, "avg_events": 20010.0, "min_lumis": 0, "min_events": 1800, "total_files": 10, "max_files": 1, "avg_files": 1.0, "min_files": 1}
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T17:09:45Z)

OK. Found.
When using FileBased splitting in the configuration, a different part of splitterSumary code is used
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97f447747265684589ac1f5be773eed80de02239/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Splitter.py#L156-L169

so solution should be simply to add `automatic` to the `if` in line 156

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T17:12:33Z)

that way it submits fine

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-07T17:15:01Z)

all in all this is not surprising, since splittingSummary was previously used only during `submit --dryryun` and CRAB Client says
```console
belforte@lxplus831/TC3> crab submit --dryrun auto.py
Will use CRAB configuration file auto.py
The 'dryrun' option is not compatible with the 'Automatic' splitting mode (default).
```

Simply I thought that maybe splitting-summary could be useful more in general and decided to always create it !

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8779: Include SendVenvFolder test in Client Configuration Validation of gitlab pipeline
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8779: Include SendVenvFolder test in Client Configuration Validation of gitlab pipeline

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-08T13:01:51Z
Closed: 2024-11-12T12:19:38Z
Labels: Status: In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8779

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2024-11-08T13:01:51Z)

Currently, Jenkins runs the SendVenvFolder test in CCV but Gitlab pipeline has it commented out as it throws an error of not finding venv folder.
See [here](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/test/makeTests.py#L272C1-L284C72)
Investigate and add this test as part of the pipeline.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-08T13:22:54Z)

hmm... `venv` folder is created here
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ca67bbf5d6d5f8c2a309d5805813830d48189eb7/test/container/testingScripts/setupCRABClient.sh#L16-L18

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-08T13:34:09Z)

and this test works when executed via Jenkins. DId you try to simply uncomment it ?

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2024-11-08T13:36:58Z)

@belforte  Yes, in the PR I have uncommented, that's why this issue is created as it is being left out of the Cv CCV PR.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-08T13:39:11Z)

I am really curious what happens differently in the pipeline which makes it fail. Feel free to point me at logs.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-08T18:03:38Z)

so the problem is that CRABClient is not setup with that script which I quoted, but by a new one
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/gitlab/setupCRABClient.sh
which is not simply "the old one copied to the new directory" as I thought. But at least lacks the lines which create the `venv` directory.

So fix is easy. But we need to check if there are other differences.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-08T18:09:19Z)

for history: the way to find out was to "notice" the following line in https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/jobs/45743592/raw
```
+ source /home/gitlab-runner/shell/builds/sedxNxqzs/0/crab3/CRABServer/cicd/gitlab/setupCRABClient.sh
```

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2024-11-12T12:19:38Z)

Thanks Stefano for the quick diagnosis! Fixed in the [PR](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8696) Closing this issue.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T12:01:30Z)

after some debugging I believe that in here
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L112-L127
Line 123 is wrong, it should be instead
```
if state == 'failed' and not processFailed:
```
That will make the error in this issue go away. But since things are usually working, there may be something more.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T12:45:29Z)

I believe this problem only happens when all `processing` jobs fail (in our test there is only one such job ! so chances of this increase) and some probe failed.
This lines tell PreDag to use probe jobs for the new splitting estimate since processing jobs failed
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L200-L201
but for reasons obscure to me `processFailed` is set to `False` which makes failed jobs NOT skipped (!!)
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L123-L124
while "normally" the default `processFailed=True` is used
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L174

Surely variable naming is confusing !
Also the fact that the `completedJobs()` method looks for completed jobs in the stage preceding the one indicated as argument
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L117-L118

At this point I have no idea why the `processFailed` argument was introduced. Seems like the original implementor wanted to say:
_"if all jobs in this stage failed, go back to previous stage to generate splitting parameters, but take into account also failed jobs which were skipped before."_

But failed jobs have no throughput report, so can't be used !

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T12:55:41Z)

I made that task DAG complete successfully by [rerunning PreDag manually](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/Crab3OperatorDebugging#To_run_the_preDag_on_the_schedd) after changing
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L201 to
```python
         estimates = set(self.completedJobs(stage='processing', processFailed=True))
```
which basically forces submission of a tail job with same config. as the processing one (OK, since the failure was an accidental 8028).

But I am still worried that making the change in the code for everybody may trigger problems in different situations which I can not imagine/test no.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T12:58:34Z)

Maybe there are situations where processing jobs fail, but still produce a report ? E.g. if they hit the time limit ?
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/scripts/TweakPSet.py#L209-L212

Or will they count as successful ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T13:20:01Z)

that `processFailed` argument was introduced in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/90c08419c59254464a10699415aba61419cb244e

No comments. no issue.

I am still unsure what to do.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T13:55:44Z)

some (but not all) probe jobs failing and all processing jobs failing is all in all a very rare case.
Also fixing this does not help the CI pipeline to complete becasue current code still sees one failed job (the processing one) and keeps trying to resubmit.
Will have to fix the pipeline first to properly deal with automatic splitting: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8794

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-14T16:38:41Z)

I have prepared PR #8795   with that fix. But need to think more about possible side effects

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-15T10:19:21Z)

I am now convinced that the problematic line
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3b2e705c8c5458135c57dfe88d1107aea075c26f/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreDAG.py#L201
is only relevant when all processing jobs fail. And therefore it is correct to change. If the problem never surfaces it must be because all processing jobs failing is very rare and never happened together with some probes also failing.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-19T21:19:30Z)

I tried various simplifications and changes to `()` in an attempt to "fix the requirements", but no matter what I tried, all idle jobs are routed via the same route !

I [wrote](https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2024-November/msg00076.shtml) to HTC support list

```text
Dear experts,

we (CMS-CRAB) have used JobRouter since years to edit queued jobs in CMS global pool to redirect then from busy sites to sites with possibly available slots, something that we call "overflow". Details of why and what happens to those jobs when they run do not matter, simply to introduce the name.

Alas we have been using the deprecated JOB_ROUTER_ENTRIES_CMD macro where custom script of ours was called to create routing on the fly So last month we rewrote our stuff using static routing table in the configuration file reproducing the same desiderata. But once put in production things started to go nuts and we had to disable.

Unfortunately we have no experience with the new configuration, and nobody else in CMS or glideinWms is using it.

We are running $CondorVersion: 23.9.6 2024-08-08 BuildID: 748275 PackageID: 23.9.6-1 GitSHA: dfdd9eaa $
and followed the example in https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/grid-computing/job-router.html defining a list of mutually exclusive routes as in [1]

Let us know if there's any more information which I can send.

Thanks!!!

Stefano

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-20T08:28:51Z)

here's [answer](https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2024-November/msg00077.shtml) from TJ (slightly edited with [tip](https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2024-November/msg00079.shtml))
```text
 In the new syntax the way to set requirements for the route is to use REQUIREMENTS without an = after it.  The same for NAME, and UNIVERSE although NAME will default to the config knob suffix.

Effects that are applied after the route has been matched, most of which can be expressions such as EditJobInPlace are still set using =,   but NAME, UNIVERSE and REQUIREMENTS are transform commands, Requirements = would be treated as a temporary variable and it would not affect the matching of the route to a job.

If you run

    condor_job_router_info you should see that your routes don't have any route REQUIREMENTS, and that the NAME of the route is not what you spacified by Name =, since the default route name is derived from the knob name.

So your routes should be

JOB_ROUTER_ROUTE_T1_DE_KIT @=rtkit
   NAME Overflow:T1_DE_KIT
   REQIREMENTS  (DESIRED_SITES=="T1_DE_KIT")
   EditJobInPlace = True
   SET NEW_SITES "T2_DE_DESY"
   SET HasBeenOverflowRouted True
@rtkit

Sorry about the confusion.   An editing pass to improve the clarity of the manual incorrectly added the =  after REQUIREMENTS in the documentation.
```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-22T10:07:10Z)

So the problem is that we do no clean the environment  before executing e.g. cmsRun
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/99fe41a9b5a2ef0222827c32bff41ec45084a4f7/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L702

The `False` in there was introduced in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/a43a10d461cee1bd58ee36ebadb43b5a7909c5df
which indeed had this in the commets:
```
When we launch cmsRun, we should imitate what WMCore is
doing: do not clean the env, to preserve all the env
variables set for us by the workern node / pilot
and by cmsset_default.sh

Just a (small ?) difference with respect to WMCore:
we do not remove the COMP's python from the pythonpath.
This can be dangerous and should be thoroughly tested.
```

I am trying to remember why we decided not to cleanup PYTHONPATH :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-25T10:32:01Z)

After chat with @mapellidario
* we can not use `cleanEnv=False` because it cleans too much. We need to preserve what site adds via `cmssetup_local.sh` or the pilot does
* we simply need the equivalent of `scram unsetenv` for the COMP python which we setup to run the wrapper
* Since such script does not exits, we will go for the small hack already used in WMCore https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/d3852da7cedd8be489c4d1b980beca7310ce149c/src/python/WMCore/WMSpec/Steps/Executors/CMSSW.py#L267
```python

        envOverride = {}
        # Do not pass WM PYTHONPATH to CMSSW environment
        pythonPath = os.environ.get('PYTHONPATH', '')
        envOverride['PYTHONPATH'] = ""
        # some libraries linked with CMSSW need HOME in the environment
        if 'HOME' not in os.environ:
            envOverride['HOME'] = os.environ.get('PWD', "/")

        os.environ.update(envOverride)
 ```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T16:10:25Z)

fix in https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/commit/20b4abef5c8277931418096702bb12f3a4fd75d5 does not work on CMSSW_9 (and any other oldish CMSSW which relies on its $PYTHONPATH)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T16:40:33Z)

the problem is that CMSSW_9 needs its own PYTHONPATH which is setup e.g. by `cmsenv`.
But the way `scramTool`, i.e. [Scram()](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/d3852da7cedd8be489c4d1b980beca7310ce149c/src/python/WMCore/WMRuntime/Tools/Scram.py#L368-L432) works in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8d59c1bd133a504169ddf8614909de8059e144fe/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L411
is by forking a process and passing to its `stdin` via [procWriter](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/d3852da7cedd8be489c4d1b980beca7310ce149c/src/python/WMCore/WMRuntime/Tools/Scram.py#L379-L384) all env. vars. which make up the CMSSW env before communicating the actual `unset PYTHONPATH; cmsRun` command which `CMSRunAnalysis.py` prepares.

And now I understand why in WMCore they used the apparently convoluted strategy to remove PYTHONPATH from the running process env before calling `scramTool` and add it back afterwards, as indicated above.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8806: add a canary (qa) deployment for TW
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8806: add a canary (qa) deployment for TW

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-21T16:05:22Z
Closed: 2024-12-06T13:52:26Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8806

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-11-21T16:05:22Z)

with ref to #8650

@aspiringmind-code and @belforte had a chat today. Here's notes to guide development:

## Design in words

At very high level we decide which TW is master and which canary and the fraction to be sent. This goes in the conifg. And everything else is “implementation”

Master(primary) TW does scheduling and marks some tasks (up to 2*Nslaves at every poll cycle) with status HOLDING and its TWNAME. We want to change so that X% of those tasks end up with the canary TW name instead.

## Implementation guidelines

### Configuration params:
* I am the master TW (could be the default)
* I am a canary (qa) TW (call it secondary or slave) (default is no)
* If I am master:
   * A param has the name of the canary
   * A param has the fraction to send to the canary

### MasterWorker changes:
* If I am master:
   * _selectWork (move tasks from WAIT to NEW)
   * _lockWork (change to HOLDING and put TWname in DB) changes (1)
   * New step (if we decide to add) (2)
   * _getWork (3) (picks tasks in HOLDING with my TW name in the DB)
   * One of (1) (2) (3) needs to be changed to send X% of tasks to the canary by setting status HOLDING and canary TW name
* If I am Canary:
   * Skip _selectWork and _lockWork. Only do _getWork and following steps

### Extra niceties
* keep track in DB task table if this task was processed  by the primary or the canary TW ? Where does it help ? we already have the TW name
* keep track in DB task table of the version of the TW used to process this task ? still some work.. is it useful ?
* the I-am-master and I-am-slave params are mutually exclusive, can (should?) easily check in TW code, but do we also want something puppet-side to make sure that we do not run two master at same time ? Do we need it ?

Configuration and implementation can be seen [here](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/292) and [here](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8808)

IMHO there should be only one flag: to execute or not a given test, which controls both submission and checking.

It breaks CRABClient for SL7 because `wget` in there does not support the `--method` option
```console
belforte@lxplus940/TC3> cmssw-el7 -- "wget -Sq -O /dev/null --method=HEAD http://a.b.c"
wget: unrecognized option '--method=HEAD'
```
so we need to replace

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7d13f7d51d9bdd5c65dafa6f7a2a9961c86d001e/src/python/ServerUtilities.py#L750-L751

with a call to `curl`

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-25T21:42:29Z)

it took very long to test, but eventually one more change is needed for python2 compatibility.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/362aaee9c7536bace2657d93b53296ad944a2fb6/src/python/ServerUtilities.py#L753-L757

using context manager here results in Exception `AttributeError: '__exit__'`
Need to stick with old-fashioned
```
downloadProcess = subprocess.Popen(...)
```

Something is wrong with our pipleine.

```
Reason is: Impossible to find task 241125_151251:crabint1_crab_transferOutputs in the database.
```
AFAICT the reason is that we had two pipelines running at same time, that one and https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/8586977

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8852: Submission Deferral for HammerCloud does not work anymore
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8852: Submission Deferral for HammerCloud does not work anymore

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-29T18:03:07Z
Closed: 2024-12-02T21:38:39Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8852

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-11-29T18:03:07Z)

as reported by @stlammel [2]

see documentation of the deferral in [1](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/wiki/CRAB-vs-HammerCloud#slow-job-release)

problem is that PreJob [looks](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ddd6ce1ded4d1b49cf92406b39d9a47321bd6776/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreJob.py#L477) for a non-zero value of `CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout` in the dag boostrap [classAds](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ddd6ce1ded4d1b49cf92406b39d9a47321bd6776/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreJob.py#L174).

The way for user to indicate that was implemented ([1]) via adding in crabConfig.
```
config.Debug.extraJDL=['+CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout=Nsec']
```
But `extraJDL` can also contain things which make DAG bootstrap fail , see #8784

So I had to stop passing `extraJDL` ads to the dagman.jdl  and PreJob does not find the ad anymore.

Need a cleaner and explicit way to put `CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout` in `DAGJob.jdl`
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ddd6ce1ded4d1b49cf92406b39d9a47321bd6776/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L459
[...]
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/ddd6ce1ded4d1b49cf92406b39d9a47321bd6776/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L528-L529

The best way would be an additional parameter in crabConfiguration, not an extrajdl classAd.

As a quick patch I can parse extraJdl from `info` in DagmanSubmitter and add `CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout`  if needed :-( Still ugly

[1]
```text
Subject: 	Re: no HammerCloud jobs at Tier-1s
Date: 	Fri, 29 Nov 2024 17:33:53 +0100
From: 	Stephan Lammel <<email>>
To: 	Stefano Belforte <<email>>, Andrea Sciaba <<email>>, Jakrapop Akaranee <<email>>, Malik Shahzad Muzaffar <<email>>
CC: 	Chan-Anun Rungphitakchai <<email>>, cms-service-crab3htcondor (Announcements from IT to CRAB3-HTCondor Project) <<email>>

Many Thanks Stefano!

There is a remaining issue that started Wednesday when first jobs
run again: Jobs seem to be batched together and are not finishing
continuously. If you look at siteStatus, i.e.
https://cmssst.web.cern.ch/siteStatus/summary.html
you see an hour and a half of unknown status/no HC results and
then 30 minutes of ok status/many HC results. (Although Site
Readiness is shown, the pattern comes from HammerCloud. If you
click on a site, for instance
https://cmssst.web.cern.ch/siteStatus/detail.html?site=T1_FR_CCIN2P3
you see it's coming from HammerCloud.)

Was there any change made to the "release a job every 5 minute"
logic that could account for this?
(I can't exclude it's due to scheduling on SI/global pool side but the
"Submit" times on the Grafana dashboard, i.e.

https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=sciaba&var-task=241129_154348:sciaba_crab_HC-211-T1_FR_CCIN2P3-110047-20241129144101&from=1732895028000&to=now

suggests to me it's on CRAB side.)

```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-12-02T09:46:03Z)

`config.Debug.extraJDL` are passed to job anyhow via Job.x.submit files.

`CRAB_NoWNStageout` is used in `cmscp.py` and PostJob. - OK , but ...could it be replaced with `config.General.transferOutputs=False` ?

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-12-06T13:55:16Z)

see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8650

Apparently Wa has done all the work already and we simply need to learn how to activate (in preprod first of course) and then configure one production pod to be canary, decide policy, enable automation... all the things.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-01-27T10:37:54Z)

@novicecpp Hi Wa, We've activated the canary using your new Helm chart template and have learned a lot from it. Since all the the initiatives and work done came from you, Could you kindly do us the honor of closing this issue for us? Thanks!

## Comment (novicecpp, 2025-01-28T16:49:58Z)

Hi Oat,
First of all, thanks for the feedback. I am glad that something I worked on during CRAB operator's years is helpful to the team in the end.
However, I could not take those credit by myself. This task is not possible without comments from @mapellidario, @belforte and some guideline from @arooshap.
And I am not CRAB operator anymore. It should be you who done it to close this issue.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8869: use input_args.json file in CMSRunAnalysis.py via --jobId arg
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8869: use input_args.json file in CMSRunAnalysis.py via --jobId arg

State: closed
Opened: 2025-01-08T11:43:50Z
Closed: 2025-01-20T14:54:56Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8869

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-01-08T11:43:50Z)

Get rid of the awful long arg list in Job.submit (ref. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5288#issuecomment-2577345857)
`
Arguments = "-a $(CRAB_Archive) --sourceURL=$(CRAB_ISB) --jobNumber=$(CRAB_Id) --cmsswVersion=$(CRAB_JobSW) --scramArch=$(CRAB_JobArch) '--inputFile=$(inputFiles)' '--runAndLumis=$(runAndLumiMask)' --lheInputFiles=$(lheInputFiles) --firstEvent=$(firstEvent) --firstLumi=$(firstLumi) --lastEvent=$(lastEvent) --firstRun=$(firstRun) --seeding=$(seeding) --scriptExe=$(scriptExe) --eventsPerLumi=$(eventsPerLumi) --maxRuntime=$(maxRuntime) '--scriptArgs=$(scriptArgs)' -o $(CRAB_AdditionalOutputFiles)"
`
and make it possible to use instead simply `--jobId=$(CRAB_Id)`

Now every task has `input_args.json` in its spool dir, so add it to list of `transfer_input_files` in `Job.submit` and add the new arg to CMSRunAnalysis.py

This will also allow to simplify the `RunJobs.dag` file where all those env.vars. are defined
`
VARS Job1 count="1" runAndLumiMask="job_lumis_1.json" lheInputFiles="False" firstEvent="None" firstLumi="None" lastEvent="None" firstRun="None" maxRuntime="-60" eventsPerLumi="None" seeding="AutomaticSeeding" inputFiles="job_input_file_list_1.txt" scriptExe="None" scriptArgs="[]" +CRAB_localOutputFiles="\"kk.root=kk_1.root\"" +CRAB_DataBlock="\"/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/AODSIM#3517e1b6-76e3-11e7-a0c8-02163e00d7b3\"" +CRAB_Destination="\"davs://eoscms.cern.ch:443/eos/cms/store/user/belforte/GenericTTbar/crab_20241216_165508/241218_101115/0000/log/cmsRun_1.log.tar.gz, davs://eoscms.cern.ch:443/eos/cms/store/user/belforte/GenericTTbar/crab_20241216_165508/241218_101115/0000/kk_1.root\""
`

Since everything is in `input_args.json` !

- [x] start by adding the new `jobId` arg so can test along current code
   - [x] modify CMSRunAnalysis.py and test with preparelocal
   - [x] modify Job.submit in DagmanCreator to transfer input_args.json (circa line 570) and replace args list with --jobId
- [ ] eventually remove old code and possibly rename `--jobId` to `--jobNumber`

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-13T18:08:06Z)

harder than it looked. Can't have a single `input_args.json` since for automatic splitting each subdag will need different one. Can maybe keep adding ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-15T20:47:33Z)

my branch https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/tree/use-jobid-arg-for-CMSRunAnalysis-8869
now has something that I more or less like and works for "traditional" DAGs. Need to worry about automatic splitting subdags. I lean toward making one new input_args_X.json file for each, like done for the RunJobX.dag files
But have to be careful with the "common" Job.submit since subdags may start when the processing dag has not submitted all jobs yet, i.e. not all PreJobs have run and not all Job.N.submit have been created for it (or any other previous subdag).

One possibility is to insert the input_args.json in the PreJob picking the correct json file. But in order to keep CMSRunAnalysis scripts simple and for mind sanity it is better that file in the WN have constant names.

Back to ... add new jobs to same input_args.json as they are created by DagmanCreator

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-01-09T13:02:34Z)

now that we have two TW's (primary and canary) we should avoid that a TW restarts overwrites the TW assignment of QUEUED tasks and any other "interference"

at the moment both primary and canary pick tasks QUEUED by either, set to NEW and then primary handles them again as new with a new decision if to assign to canary or not.

This makes for non-reproducible behavior and makes it difficult to debug.

Once the initial decision on which TW handles a task is taken, it should stay there.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-01-23T14:53:33Z)

I've added the bumping script to ease our routine. Please have a look at the script [here](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8891). #8891
###  How-to-Use
- for bumping to latest version (now=2.3.7.1) > `./scripts/bumpWMCoreVersion.sh`
- for bumping to specific version > `./scripts/bumpWMCoreVersion.sh 2.3.7.6`
_____________________

This script will update tag version in the comment of **_3 requirements.txt_** on both **CRABServer** and **TaskWorker**

1. [cicd/crabserver_pypi/requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabserver_pypi/requirements.txt)

```
-# https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/9c6e83d1d23983c0296eee318c9e6255ff80d01b/requirements.txt
+# https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/2.3.7.1/requirements.txt
```
2. [cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/requirements.txt).
```
-# https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/2.2.4rc6/requirements.txt
+# https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/2.3.7.1/requirements.txt
```
3. [cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/cicd/crabserver_pypi/wmcore_requirements.txt).
```
-https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore 2.3.6rc2
+https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore 2.3.7.1
```

All of the updated version tag in these comments will be retrieve later and WMCore will be either installed via `cicd/crabserver/installWMCore.sh` or `cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile` during CI, docker image building time. As you can see in the following.
``` Dockerfile
RUN wmcore_repo="$(grep -v '^\s*#' wmcore_requirements.txt | cut -d' ' -f1)" \
    && wmcore_version="$(grep -v '^\s*#' wmcore_requirements.txt | cut -d' ' -f2)" \
    && git clone  --depth 1 ${wmcore_repo} -b "${wmcore_version}" /build/WMCore \
    && ( cd /build/WMCore; git status )
```
______________________________
### My Questions:
Should we also include bumping version of *cmsweb* derived image to `cmsweb/cmsweb:20240501-stable` in CRABServer's Dockefile in this procedure as well? Thank you!
``` Dockerfile
FROM registry.cern.ch/cmsweb/cmsweb:20230427-stable AS cmsweb
```

but not sure if this is sufficient to confirm that we are safe to proceed with the bump. please let me know is there any other validation needed.

Beside that, Let me try propose something and learn from your feedbacks.
________________________________
#### Regarding your questions, wishes to reduce our routine workloads.
Weekly/Bi-Weekly/Monthly polling-based Jenkins bot to automatically update dependencies for us.
1. The Jenkins bot polls **WMCore** and **CMSWeb** to check for any changes via github api for their latest stable `tag_name`.
2. Then it creates an `automatic-update-deps-{weekly?}-{year}` branch.
3. It bumps the `tag_name` to the latest stable release.
4. Validation is done by using the git tag to trigger the CI, **build-deploy-test** pipeline.
5. If _testsuite_, _testsuite_CV_, _testsuite_CCV_ and _check_testsuite_ go well:
6. The Jenkins bot commits, pushes, and opens a pull request for us.
7. Finally, Leaving us with one-click of merge PR every Bi-Weekly to decide whether to keep things up-to-date if there exists new releases.

These could also applied to other aspects of `libs`, `deps` versions beyond `WMCore` and `CMSWeb` too.
**3,4,5** utilized our core pipeline, it's already done and well maintained by our CRAB's folks. **1,2,6,7**  could be adopt/extended functionality from our **Jenkins pylint bot**.

**Why don't we use push-based hooks for these events?**
-> From our history we rarely updates these deps version. therefore, periodically might keep things simple, than unpredictable push events.
**Weekly/Bi-Weekly/Monthly?**
-> it depends on how frequently we want to keep up with evolving dependencies, security patches, and vulnerability updates.
