title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8900: crab kill broken in v3.250109
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8900: crab kill broken in v3.250109

State: closed
Opened: 2025-01-29T20:57:41Z
Closed: 2025-01-30T15:55:07Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8900

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-01-29T20:57:41Z)

I only noticed while testing new (extensice) changes to DagmanCreator and DagmanSubmitter that `crab kill` fails. as indicated in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8893#issuecomment-2617090507 (**BUG 5**).

The bug was independent and present already in v3.250109 which we have in preprod since then and luckily did not deploy in production yet.

We need to add `crab kill` to our validation.

The problem is this line2
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5bdfcbfd35295520e171d6d5ca7796bb089b05ce/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanKiller.py#L42-L44

introduced in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/8ed2195d78b2c47daa55f2738bd9d98469f9b8f7 to fix #8874

The problem is that the `task` dictionary at this point in the code is what MasterWorker retrieved via a GET to `workflowdb` REST API in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5bdfcbfd35295520e171d6d5ca7796bb089b05ce/src/python/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py#L430
and that API as per
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5bdfcbfd35295520e171d6d5ca7796bb089b05ce/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTWorkerWorkflow.py#L86-L89
uses the SQL from [Task.GetReadyTasks_sql](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5bdfcbfd35295520e171d6d5ca7796bb089b05ce/src/python/Databases/TaskDB/Oracle/Task/Task.py#L84-L99) which retrieves in the `WHERE`  only a subset of the DB Task table columns. `clusterid` is not one of them !! In spite of what the comment in the API above states. 😠

Of course this must be because initially the `tm_*` columns where "all the information", then developers added more columns and not all SQL's have been changed. I do not know if it is possible to have code which retrieves all colums and properly names them, to avoid the need to list column names in so many places...

Anyhow, I do not feel like changing the REST code now. Will add a call in DagmanKiller to retrieve the full info about the task in order to check `clusterid`

State: closed

*  ref in preprod with v3.250109   https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250131_092508%3Abelforte_crab_20250131_102502 : all OK
* test in test2 with current master https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250131_100639%3Abelforte_crab_20250131_110635

after #8893 all PreJob scripts run at same time at beginning and all jobs are submitted even if `+CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout=60` is correctly propagated to scheduler in Job.submit and DAG file has

```text
SCRIPT DEFER 4 60 PRE  Job1 dag_bootstrap.sh PREJOB $RETRY 1

SCRIPT DEFER 4 1800 PRE  Job30 dag_bootstrap.sh PREJOB $RETRY 30
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T10:48:41Z)

PreJob needs to find `CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout` among the task ads and indeed it is not in _CONDOR_JOB_AD
 file. But it is listed together with all other ads in that file in DagmanSubmitter code
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c90d64829034084e3eafb8b72c9527c9d18e1680/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L60

yet it is not in the DAGJob.jdl logged in the TW temp directory
 ```console
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/tmp/_250131_100639:belforte_crab_20250131_110635rz9qfzbv$ grep CRAB_Job DAGJob.jdl
My.CRAB_JobSW = "CMSSW_13_3_0"
My.CRAB_JobArch = "el8_amd64_gcc12"
My.CRAB_JobCount = 30
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/tmp/_250131_100639:belforte_crab_20250131_110635rz9qfzbv$
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T10:51:09Z)

could this be `+ad` vs. `My.ad` ???

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T11:00:53Z)

using `My.CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout=60` in the crabConfig.py makes it to correctly reach the PreJob
```
[crabtw@vocms059 SPOOL_DIR]$ grep CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout _CONDOR_JOB_AD
CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout = 60
```
But now PreJob fails
```
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/3028/0/cluster10093028.proc0.subproc0/TaskWorker/Actions/PreJob.py", line 470, in needsDefer
    submitTime = int(self.task_ad.get("CRAB_TaskSubmitTime"))
TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a number, not 'NoneType'
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T11:03:11Z)

`CRAB_TaskSubmitTime` is in the `subdag.jdl` and in the `DAGJob.jdl` created in TW, but not in the `_CONDOR_JOB_AD` file.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T11:27:31Z)

the `My.` suffix was lost when preparing DAGJob.jdl.  So these lines
```console
crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/tmp/_250131_105201:belforte_crab_20250131_115157toscgred$ grep CRAB_TaskSubmitTime *jdl
DAGJob.jdl:CRAB_TaskSubmitTime = 1738320746
subdag.jdl:CRAB_TaskSubmitTime = 1738320746
```
define (unusee) variables, not classAds

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-31T11:29:38Z)

bug. `My.` is missing here !
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c90d64829034084e3eafb8b72c9527c9d18e1680/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L415

after that PreJobs run and say things like
```
Fri, 31 Jan 2025 12:35:41 CET(+0100):INFO:PreJob   Defer time of this job (1800 seconds since initial task submission) not elapsed yet, deferring for 1800 seconds
```
but the DEFER is gone from DAG file
```console
[crabtw@vocms059 cluster10093032.proc0.subproc0]$ cat RunJobs.dag|grep PRE|grep -v SKIP|cut -d' ' -f 1-9|head
#SCRIPT PRE FinalCleanup dag_bootstrap.sh FINAL $DAG_STATUS $FAILED_COUNT cmsweb-test2.cern.ch:8443
```

pfff..
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c90d64829034084e3eafb8b72c9527c9d18e1680/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L556
works with `+.CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout` but not with `My.CRAB_JobReleaseTimeout`
I have no idea why they used such a strict check

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-03T13:50:33Z)

must make sure that parameter changing in resubmit (time, memory, sites) works

crab resubmit options (from `crab resubmit --help`)
- [x] --jobid=id
- [x] --sitewhitelist=SITEWHITELIST
- [x] --siteblacklist=SITEBLACKLIST
- [x]   --maxjobruntime=MAXJOBRUNTIME
- [x] --maxmemory=MAXMEMORY
- [x] --numcores=NUMCORES
    - looks like it alwasy failed to me ! DagmanResubmitter sets `CRAB_RequestedCpus`, but the PreJob will use `CRAB_RequestedCores` (which is set in DagmanSubmitter) to configure Job.submit.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8921: remove port 8443 from cmsweb URL's
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #8921: remove port 8443 from cmsweb URL's State: closed Opened: 2025-02-14T15:11:02Z Closed: 2025-05-20T11:08:36Z Labels: Area: Code Cleanup, OPERATION URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8921 ## Opening post (belforte, 2025-02-14T15:11:02Z) Especially in CRABServeer UI, it often makes page download to fail, until one tries again w/o it. Ref also to https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/ym4jn56n6iyqifo9pnx5tism6h This mean some changes to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/html/index.html and/or jquery files used in there ## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-14T15:34:40Z) hmmm... maybe that page is w/o fault. and the 8443 is put in by the RES in building the answer to https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/prod/task?subresource=webdirprx&workflow=.... oh well. It is so difficult for me to tell what the UI is doing, sorry. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-19T13:57:17Z) it is amazingly intricated !! The only solution that comes to mind is to re-work all this webdir vs. webdirproxy thing. Curretly we store in the DB an URL which points to the scheduler's HTTP server, e.g. ```text https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0197/aguven/250306_132816:aguven_crab_20250306_142547 ``` (from `curl "https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/prod/task?subresource=webdirprx&workflow=250306_132816:aguven_crab_20250306_142547"`) which gets transformed in to what this returns `curl "https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/prod/task?subresource=webdir&workflow=250306_132816:aguven_crab_20250306_142547"` via https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTTask.py#L237 and following lines, so the "8443" ultimately comes from https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-shedds-config.json?ref_type=heads while we can start from removing the port # there, getting rid of all this complexity is certainly better ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-05-19T15:08:47Z) Thanks you, for ultimate clues! @belforte You were right, from **getProxiedWebDir** in `src/python/ServerUtilities.py` to **webdirprx** subresource function in `src/python/CRABInterface/RESTTask.py`. they all point to `htcondorSchedds` config in [cmsweb-shedds-config.json](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-shedds-config.json?ref_type=heads), where most of the changes are needed. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/a9c51b514446df1b2138492a29389b32ca3bf274/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTTask.py#L236-L257 ```json { "" : { "proxiedurl": "https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/059", "weightfactor": 0 }, "" : { "proxiedurl": "https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/068", "weightfactor": 1 }, ``` Additionally, the other location i found was hardcoded that i'm not sure whether it's need changed or not is located in `src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py` ```python 509: webDirUrl = f"https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/{schedId}/{username}/{taskName}" 510: stdoutUrl = f"{webDirUrl}/job_out.{jobId}.txt" 511: postJobUrl = f"{webDirUrl}/postjob.{jobId}.txt" ``` Other than that i think the code cleaning/refactoring about webdir vs webdirProxy, could be open as another issue? ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-05-20T08:32:50Z) I've removed 8443 port from [cmsweb-shedds-config.json](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/commit/3dccf287177de3e1886c258dfbda49ef613d1193) and also in [Actions/RetryJob.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9083) that was hardcoded. I will waiting for changes to take effects, new WebDir/JobLog Urls, on production. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-05-20T11:07:26Z) Now, whenever user hover/click on Webdir link. It was properly point to non-8443 url one. as we could try on [test task]( https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250519_123330%3Akphornsi_crab_20250519_143325/dbver/prod). ## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-20T12:52:53Z) the change in RetryJob is actually unrelated since it only affects my own tallying of corrupted files. But it is fine to do w/o the port there as well. Thanks

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8928: add a flag in task Table to indicate that task was UPLOADED to S3
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8928: add a flag in task Table to indicate that task was UPLOADED to S3

State: closed
Opened: 2025-02-17T14:11:13Z
Closed: 2025-05-22T10:49:09Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: High
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8928

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-02-17T14:11:13Z)

for tasks submitted w/o dry run, UPLOADED is a transient status, tasks get there after QUEUED and progress immediately to SUBMITTED and possibly other statuses.
This makes it difficult to tell from Client is task is ready to run `crab preparelocal`  as discussed in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5371#issuecomment-2662962817

Desired behavior could be that when Uploader action is completed a flag is set in the DB and client checks that, keeping UPLOADED status as it was until a few months ago only for tasks "halted" for dry-run submission which wait for a `crab proceed` command in order to progress to SUBMITTED.

Consistently with

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #8935: latest DagmanCreator code only works with HTC v2 API
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8935: latest DagmanCreator code only works with HTC v2 API

State: closed
Opened: 2025-02-18T16:41:16Z
Closed: 2025-02-20T12:05:49Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8935

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-02-18T16:41:16Z)

recent Dagamn* restructuring in https://github.com/belforte/CRABServer/commit/367e5692451b821683af7404cece63eed280d6ce introduced the use of `htcondor.Submit` object  in DagmanCreator .
Code is "HTC v2 only" [*], but we have already set HTC API to v2 in all TaskWorkers.

But for "obscure" reasons the env. var. ` useHtcV2` is not propagated to PreDag when starting the tail subdags, only the processing subdag is OK. So submission of tail dagmans (e.g. in DagLog1.txt is failing with
```
  File "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/6407/0/cluster116926407.proc0.subproc0/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py", line 1158, in createSubdag
    if not 'My.CRAB_FailedNodeLimit' in jobSubmit:
TypeError: argument of type 'Submit' is not iterable
```

since processing DAG submission was OK, it was not easy to notice the problem.

Fixing the env. passing is not useful at this point. I will simply force usage of v2 API
I tested this on a task which had exhibited that failure: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250217_154906%3Acerminar_crab_DoublePhoton_FlatPt-1To100_PU200

and it worked finely.

[*]
Down to technicalities , the semantycs of the HTCondor Submit() object is different in v1 [1] and v2[2].
v2 API is easier to work with and I had ended up in writing code which only works in v2 !

[1]
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 ~]$ python3
Python 3.9.21 (main, Dec  5 2024, 00:00:00)
[GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-2)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import htcondor
>>> htcondor.version()
'$CondorVersion: 24.0.3 2025-01-03 BuildID: 777902 PackageID: 24.0.3-1 GitSHA: ef02b46e $'
>>> js=htcondor.Submit()
>>> js['a']='33'
>>> js
'a = 33\n'
>>> 'a' in js
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
TypeError: argument of type 'Submit' is not iterable
>>>
```

[2]
```text
[crabtw@vocms059 ~]$ python3
Python 3.9.21 (main, Dec  5 2024, 00:00:00)
[GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-2)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import htcondor2
>>> htcondor2.version()
'$CondorVersion: 24.0.3 2025-01-03 BuildID: 777902 PackageID: 24.0.3-1 GitSHA: ef02b46e $'
>>> js=htcondor2.Submit()
>>> js['a']='33'
>>> js
Submit(a = 33
queue
)
>>> 'a' in js
True
>>>
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-18T16:46:14Z)

at this point I will simply enforce usage of Htcondor V2 API everywhere.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-02-27T18:22:58Z)

Done.

I've followed [new registration workflow](https://gitlab.docs.cern.ch/docs/Build%20your%20application/CI-CD/Runners/private-runner-registration/).
to get new Runner authentication tokens for both `crab3` and `crab3-shell`. The new Tokens will have the prefix, `glrt-`.
(P.S. which seems like Wa already updated it once since 2024-04. but i renewed it again anyway.)

I did it by edited `id` and `token` in our currently working gitlab-runner configs and updating it to the corresponding tbag secret keys then manually restarting gitlab runner systemd services for each `crab3`, `crab3-shell` at `crab-ci-runner01` as following.

NOTES: prefix `gitlab-runner-local*` is for shell executor (*crab3-shell*) and prefix `gitlab-runner` is for docker runner (*crab3*)
```
tbag set --hg vocmsglidein/cirunner gitlab-runner-local.config.toml --file config.shell.updated.toml
tbag set --hg vocmsglidein/cirunner gitlab-runner.config.toml --file config.updated.toml
```
```
systemctl restart gitlab-runner-local.service
systemctl restart gitlab-runner.service
```
(P.S. Since, `puppet agent -tv` not triggered systemd restart as i expected, may be because there is no changes in manifests and configs; only tbags)

Now our gitlab pipelines use only new runners. As you can see throughout the jobs in one of my pipeline here: [CI/CD pipelines were using 2 new runners](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/10909499)

Thanks to our comprehensive [CRAB's Folks doc](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-infrastructure/crab-cicd/gitlab/private-runners.html), it's helps me a lot!

@belforte Yes, i also think of elaborate a little bit more about systemd related stuffs, which crucial for managing both daemons (`crab3` and `crab3-shell`) in the same vm but were implicitly mentioned in puppet manifests, and also a little bit details about gitlab-runner config file which hopefully might be helpful for other issue that try to utilize parallelism among runners for validation tests or when we wish for creating a new *crab-ci-runner02,03,04...*

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8953: Adding PsetHash from Edmprovdump fails with CMSSW_15_1

State: closed
Opened: 2025-02-27T14:01:39Z
Closed: 2025-04-14T13:11:26Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8953

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2025-02-27T14:01:39Z)

See [here](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-job-failed-pset-hash-missing-from-edmprovdump/116834)
This [line](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L496) assumes that the hash value will be at the end of the line dumped by edmProvdump. Tests fail therefore. A robust way to get the hash value should be worked out.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T14:10:38Z)

see also discussion in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/47355#discussion_r1973412363

## Comment (makortel, 2025-02-27T14:36:35Z)

I want to have a better and more stable way to communicate what CRAB needs. To me the framework job report XML would sound a good way to convey the necessary information (rather than parsing output of any additional script). Would you agree?

I'd also want to understand better if it is really the PSet hash that is needed here, or e.g. reduced process history ID (which is what the framework internally uses for the segregation of different processing histories).

In particular I'd advise against making any quick patches, because I'll change the `edmProvDump` output (especially this part) more drastically, and then we'd be here again. I'm already restoring the `edmProvDump` output (temporarily) in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/47473 so that we'd have more time to make a proper fix.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T14:51:25Z)

Thanks Matti,

I agree that FJR is preferrable. Even if we may have to do the change in WMCore code https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/WMCore/FwkJobReport/Report.py

As to "what is needed", I'd say that the use case is simple, even if possibly not technically defined: limit the possibilities to users to shoot their own feed and come complaining with use with obscure problems later. That said, we need guidance from FWK Core developers on what to check.

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-02-27T15:07:53Z)

@makortel and @belforte Thank you for your insight. Yes, we'd like to not rely on parsing like this. I'd refrain from doing the regex change as a quick fix. And wait for the final edmProvDump output format to make necessary changes on our end.

## Comment (makortel, 2025-02-27T16:15:02Z)

So if I understood the present situation correctly, CRAB uses the PSet hash as part the dataset name published in DBS as described in https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/Crab3DataHandling#Output_dataset_names_in_DBS, but not for anything else.

I saw references to "PSet hash" in the WMCore repository as well, but it was unclear to me if WMCore uses the PSet hash only to fill the field in DBS or also for something else, and from where WMCore gets the values.

Listing the various options of "IDs"
1. The PSet hash is an ID for the configuration itself (including the process name).
2. The reduced ProcessConfiguration ID adds the major and minor numbers from CMSSW version into the hashing (i.e. cuts the version string to  `CMSSW_15_0`; e.g. `CMSSW_15_0_1` and `CMSSW_15_0_10` are considered the same, and `CMSSW_15_0_1` and `CMSSW_15_1_1` are considered different).
3. The reduced ProcessHistory ID effectively adds the ProcessConfiguration IDs of all the earlier processes in the chain. A single file may contain events with different reduced ProcessHistory IDs (and I think we have seen those).

The CMSSW framework uses the 3) to segregate data. But given that a single file can contain events with different ProcessHistory IDs (e.g. merged MiniAOD files that contain data taken with different HLT configurations), that doesn't seem like a good fit here.

Between 1 and 2 the question is then if CRAB should use the CMSSW major/minor version to segregate datasets.

For complex PSets there is a good chance that some component added a new (tracked) parameter or a value of some existing parameter between CMSSW major or minor versions (e.g. between `CMSSW_14_2` and `CMSSW_15_0`). But for simple PSets the PSet hash alone could have the same value between CMSSW versions, that could then result in a user publishing files produced with two CMSSW versions into the same DBS dataset. But I have no feeling how (im)probable such a case would be.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T16:59:46Z)

Thanks @makortel
I stand corrected. The PSet hash is part of the dictionary needed to publish one block in DBS[1]. CRAB uses the one discussed here. And I do not know if /how that information is used later on.
So WMCore must be filling this field to, or DBS would complain. And I guess @amaltaro or @khurtado are the ones to know where they get it and tell if/how WMCore will be impacted by the change. Maybe this value in DBS is always dummy [2]  ? I can't list it with DAS(goclient) to check what's there.

Do I understand correctly that current edmProdDump prints out ID number `1.` above ?
If yes, I would stay with that and do not take chances with getting more strict. We have no evidence of problems.

OTOH, if you are going to put this in the FJR XML, which is already a very large file, maybe you can write all the three possibility and free yourself :-)

[1]
https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/docs/apis.md
https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/blob/master/dbs/bulkblocks.go

[2]
have we reached the point where current DBS developers are remote enough from original developers that we do not know what the various metadata files mean ?

## Comment (makortel, 2025-02-27T17:14:53Z)

> Do I understand correctly that current edmProdDump prints out ID number `1.` above ?

Correct.

> If yes, I would stay with that and do not take chances with getting more strict. We have no evidence of problems.

Ok.

> OTOH, if you are going to put this in the FJR XML, which is already a very large file, maybe you can write all the three possibility and free yourself :-)

That would indeed a possibility (except maybe for 3, for which there may be multiple values).

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T17:50:55Z)

Indeed it sounds like 3. is only useful for the framework.

One last point. I presume that we will keep using edmProvDump for up to CMSSW_14 (and maybe 15_0 ?) and switch to new way from 15_1 onward, right ?

## Comment (makortel, 2025-02-27T18:46:47Z)

> I presume that we will keep using edmProvDump for up to CMSSW_14 (and maybe 15_0 ?) and switch to new way from 15_1 onward, right ?

You can continue using `edmProvDump` for sure up to CMSSW_14_X_Y. I don't foresee any need to touch `edmProvDump` there. And the new way with FWJR will be part of 15_1_X.

Fate of 15_0_X is a good question. Until this issue I was planning to backport the (present and upcoming) `edmProvDump` changes there (although it's more of it being nice to be able to print the new provenance information we're adding in 15_0_X with a 15_0_X release, than being strictly necessary). I can backport the upcoming change in FWJR to 15_0_X, and I can delay the (possible) backport of `edmProvDump` changes until we have a new version of CRAB in production. But that would mean that CRAB would have to use `edmProvDump` until some X in 15_0_X, and FWJR from X+1 onwards. How feasible would that be?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T22:30:26Z)

> . But that would mean that CRAB would have to use edmProvDump until some X in 15_0_X, and FWJR from X+1 onwards. How feasible would that be?

it still seems a simple `if` to me. No problem. I am sure @aspiringmind-code will have no problem implementing it.
To ease the transition can we put in a small hack to use e.g. edmProvDump from CMSSW_14 in such cases, while a proper change to WMCore and CRAB production releases goes through the pipeline. Will it work on files produced by 15_x ?

So we can decouple our and your timelines.

## Comment (makortel, 2025-02-28T14:33:58Z)

I'd rather not use `edmProvDump` from an earlier release. It might work, but is not guaranteed (in this particular case I'd think it could work, but there are subtleties that I'd prefer not to think about).

One option for a transition would be that CRAB would first try to use the PSet hash from the framework job report, and if it isn't there, then use `edmProvDump`. That an explicit release checks could be avoided, and even backports to earlier CMSSW release cycles would work automatically (as long as the fwjr change is made before or at the same release as the `edmProvDump` change). There would still be some timeline coupling (framework needs to decide the XML schema change, then CRAB can do their change, and only after the deployment of new CRAB can framework deploy more changes to `edmProvDump`). I'd be fine with that though.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-04T16:14:06Z)

Sorry for late reply @makortel
Sure. I am fine with going in the order which you describe
1. define how CRAB will get PSet has from FJR
2. implement this in CRAB+WMCore, with fallback to edmProvDump
3. deploy in production
4. update edmProvDump to new format

@aspiringmind-code @sinonkt I think it is better if you decide who among you is going to do 2. and use the time until 1. is ready to understand where changes will have to be done.

## Comment (makortel, 2025-03-06T22:16:18Z)

We are planning to proceed with the following addition to the FJR XML file (under the `<FrameworkJobReport>` element)
```xml
<Process>
  <Name>PROD1</Name>
  <ReducedConfigurationID>783c5ab60bfe18ac97262801adef9de4</ReducedConfigurationID>
  <ParameterSetID>1f94f8e1ac0ae9d7dade1c99cc5862b3</ParameterSetID>
</Process>
```
The `ParameterSetID` is the element whose content is the "PSet hash". I'm working to open a CMSSW PR soon (I'll let you know here).

> I'm working to open a CMSSW PR soon (I'll let you know here).

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T16:14:25Z)

while you are at this, make sure that code in ServerUtilities which is shared with CRABClient stays compatible with python2.7 and be aware that CRABClient always runs with the python version set by the CMSSW Release specified by the user. Check with Shahzad if there are plans for upgrading python there.

Of course moving code which is not used by Client out of ServerUtilities in some proper (new) file in CRABServer/src/python/CRABUtils can only help, that ServerUtilities file is way too long now.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T17:12:29Z)

Additional complication:
- scripts in the schedulers use code from GH repository but run with /usr/bin/python3
- JobWrapper (CMSRunAnalysis.py, cmscp.py) run with the python3 from /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/COMP which is under WMCore control

So if you can have code which works with both current py3.8 and new py3.13, should be all simple, otherwise a lot of care will be needed and transition will take longer due to the need of multiple backward-compatible steps.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-02-27T17:30:27Z)

On the good side, HTCondor V2 API's should be python-version-independent. Of course to be verified.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-18T15:43:04Z)

Given that
* WMCore and CRAB code are "feature frozen" now
* alma9 will have security fixes (and hence be usable as container base) until [2032](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/)
* python 3.9 is and will always be the python version in Alma9

I believe that we can safely assume that we only need to be compliant with python 3.9 in order to be future-proof.

To keep full compatibility with WMCore, it is good that our code works in 3.12 as well, but we should not use anything which is only available in that.
As far as I know, python3.9 compatible code will also run in py3.12

We can (and likely should) move TW image to use Alma9 container as base, instead of python3.8 Debian one.

Note that in the schedulers (AP's) we already use alma9 and Python 3.9.21

## Comment (nausikt, 2026-01-16T13:31:07Z)

Feeling grateful for [Dario's extra miles made for Tier0 and CRAB](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/issues/12208#issuecomment-2688340975) and your guidelines here which eased the process indeed.

Since, this porting to py3.12 up-to py3.13 compatible code is also more or less coupling with other issues i.e.
1. [moving to latest WMCore 2.4.5 (freeze) version #9150](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9150).
2. ensure that [minor backward refinement for timeless module import syntax #8804](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8804) works on py3.12.
3. [Migrate TW image to Alma9, maintain OS and Python version homogeneity with Schedd (AP's), support Py3.9 → Py3.12 #9252](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9252), as you mentioned aboved.

Therefore, let me break it down into multiple PRs for ease of approval, also split them into two phases as following.
\*\**where all ***Phase 1*** PRs have been ***tested*** as a whole as you can see in* #9251\*\*

## Phase 1
*Ensure *buildable* and runnable on py3.12*, ***regardless** of OS-env*.
- [x] 1. make it compliant with **WMCore 2.4.5**, where *py3.13* support is **guaranteed**.
    PR ***safe*** to merge: #9254 *(was cherry-picked into [3])*
- [x] 2. address CRAB's specific *py3.9* - *py3.12* deprecations and code refinement for better long term support.
    PRs ***safe*** to merge:
            2.1. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9260
            2.2. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9261
            2.3. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9253
           References: [PEP632](https://peps.python.org/pep-0632/), [PEP389](https://peps.python.org/pep-0389/#deprecation-of-optparse)

*N.B. Latest WMCore was 2.4.5.2 (so called [wmfreeze](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1771/repositories/wmagent-base/artifacts-tab)), also wmagent-base image was bumped to Debian Trixie where WM team **treated** Trixie & python 3.12 as default OS & py3 baseline for long term support.*

## Phase 2
*Moving toward **Alma9**: ensure py3.13 availability and future (3.13+) support, revise the GFAL updating method, especially in Alma9 env (where expected to be much easier).*
\*\****Most of the detail will be discussed in separated issue [3]***\*\*
- [x] 3. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9252 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9265
- [x] 4. Once we can lift to py3.13 (better done in **Alma9**), we will address py3.12 -> py3.13 minor shifts.
             > *P.S. Actually, no changes needed. See also [deprecations in py3.13](https://docs.python.org/3.12/deprecations/index.html#pending-removal-in-python-3-13)*
- [x] 5.  revise How can we update gfal and ldap deps in **Alma9** env. (Now, both CRABServer and TaskWorker were refactored [3] lifted to Alma9 with full control, mostly been decoupled from WMCore derived images.)
- [ ] 6. port CRABClient to new py3.13

*P.S. **Alma9** have py3.9 (default) and could naturally provision python up-to py3.12. more details in issue [3]*
*P.S. **Alma9** is where CRAB aims to live for long term, maintaining a homogenous OS-env with Schedd APs* which point to 3.9 as default.

As you can see inside auth-proxy-server daemonset pods, `etc/grid-security/certificates/` was empty led to lot of certs issue.
```
/ # ls /proc/1/root/etc/grid-security/certificates/
/ # ls /proc/1/root/etc/grid-security
certificates
cmsweb-test14-nlkqguzvrfv2-node-0.cern.ch.grid.crt
cmsweb-test14-nlkqguzvrfv2-node-0.cern.ch.grid.key
cmsweb-test14-nlkqguzvrfv2-node-0.cern.ch.grid.pem
hostcert.pem
hostkey.pem
```
P.S. One way to fixed this issue is, For now, we have to manually bumping cern-grid-certificates image by the following patch cmd. (Thanks to CERN IT)
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch ds cern-authz --type='json' -p='[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/image", "value": "registry.cern.ch/kubernetes/cern-grid-certificates:0.6.7"}]'
kubectl rollout restart -n kube-system ds cern-authz
```
[2] When we re-creating the cluster, make sure that all tls-{cert/key}.pem was properly wiped out in all nested directory of services_configs. such that deploy.sh could correctly provisioning/refreshing certs for both APS/XPS.
[3] rollout restart daemonset, help you refreshed newly provisioned key/certs in APS/XPS sometimes.
[4] APS take care of 443, XPS take care of 8443.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-03T09:20:09Z)

thanks @sinonkt . Since deploying cern-authz daemonset and ensuring TLS cert/keys is in CMSWEB responsibility, not CRAB, please make sure that those hints are in some place where CMSWEB people find them !

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #8977: refresh tnsnames.ora regarding CMSR Oracle service intervention

State: closed

Closed: 2025-03-14T14:08:19Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8977

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-03-11T17:17:23Z)

To accomodate, Oracle Intervention.

Right now, *tnsnames.ora* was provisioned from `cmsweb` image as we can see [crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L23-L24](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/f42c47d75ee1a055e99294982477d5f8f8d2ad83/cicd/crabserver_pypi/Dockerfile#L23-L24).

We've to either bumping `cmsweb` image to the latest one, `20250311` (Thanks! Aroosha!) which picking the new *tnsnames.ora* up for us.

OR we could go for separately mounted from k8s configmap by ourself like DBS does.
(which might make things less sensitive to the base image but also introduce more manual operation to keeps things up-to-date)

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-03-12T00:58:09Z)

Since, we still struggling with building new `cmsweb` image therefore we'll go for provisioning `tnsnames.ora` via configmap instead. Here is some deployment result that i've applied & tested in `prod` and `test12`.

*Before*: the `/etc/tnsnames.ora` was provisioned from `cmsweb` image since 27/04/2023.
```
> kubectl exec -it crabserver-845bd5b5bd-4z6zt -n crab -- cat /etc/tnsnames.ora
###
### CERN official tnsnames.ora file
...
##Generation date: Thursday, 27/04/2023 15:18
```

*After*: `tnsnames.ora` was updated by rolling out from new helm chart via `./deploy.sh prod` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/crabserver -n crab` (explicitly rollout needed if we haven't changes image tag or any values related to deployment).
```
> kubectl exec -it crabserver-5f54555666-245bb -n crab -- cat /etc/tnsnames.ora
###
### CERN official tnsnames.ora file
...
##Generation date: Tuesday, 11/03/2025 11:04
```

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-03-12T08:40:49Z)

We've updated to the latest config one `##Generation date: Wednesday, 12/03/2025 06:10` this morning.

N.B. updating could be done atomically with `--dry-run` to generate yaml first then `kubectl apply -f -` (* not sure is it more safe than `delete then create` operation)
N.B. 2 rollout restart are necessary, since patching/swapping configmap alone doesn't refreshed `tnsnames.ora` inside running pod (as i've checking).
```
kubectl create configmap tnsnames-config -n crab --from-file=tnsnames.ora -o yaml --dry-run | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl rollout restart deployment/crabserver -n crab
```

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-03-14T14:08:19Z)

Noted about other solutions:
As Stefano pointed out vocms* might enable yum-cron? (May be not via puppet too) or any rhel package manager features that magically updates `tnsnames.ora` for everyone, specifically updating via `oracle-instantclient-tnsnames.ora` rpm package.

this also aligned with what i've seen in `tzero`'s [t0wmadatasvc](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/t0wmadatasvc) pod that also magically refreshed `tnsnames.ora` via rpm, without neither having to bumping pod to new release tag and rolling out new pod nor mounted new `tnsnames.ora` configmap from host.  (P.S. `tzero` configmap was extremly outdate)

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9012: reduce the update frequency of DAGMAN's node_status file
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9012: reduce the update frequency of DAGMAN's node_status file

State: closed
Opened: 2025-03-20T10:30:54Z
Closed: 2025-05-28T16:08:57Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9012

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-03-20T10:30:54Z)

see discussion in MatterMost with Marco

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c897836-dda7-4640-ac56-3272a20fb7de)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8b665a3-e5cf-42fb-bc0e-479af5df6c5e)

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T10:02:47Z)

[documentation](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-information-files.html) says:
* `quote`

To have DAGMan write the node status file simply use the [NODE_STATUS_FILE](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-reference.html#NODE_STATUS_FILE) commands syntax as follows:

NODE_STATUS_FILE filename [minimumUpdateTime] [ALWAYS-UPDATE]

The status file may be updated once per [DAGMAN_USER_LOG_SCAN_INTERVAL](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/configuration-macros.html#DAGMAN_USER_LOG_SCAN_INTERVAL) in combination with the optional minimumUpdateTime value which defaults to 60 seconds. The status file is also updated a final time when the DAG completes either successfully or not.

Normally the node status file is only updated if the status of some node has changed since the last file update. If provided the optional ALWAYS-UPDATE keyword then DAGMan will always update the status file even if no nodes have changed status.
* `end-quote`

our line is:
`NODE_STATUS_FILE node_state{nodestate} 30 ALWAYS-UPDATE`

I read that for our case as:
  dag status is checked every 30 seconds and a new file written all of the times.
If we simply remove `ALWAYS-UPDATE` it will be:
  dag status is checked every 30 seconds and a new file written if status has changes since last file update

So in addition to removing `ALWAYS-UPDATE` we may want to decrease the update frequency to e.g. a couple minute.
I am wary of making it 5 minutes, since when coupled with the 5 min period of `cache_status.py` it may lead to status information lagging up to almost 10 mins.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9014: TaskWorker stops processing tasks
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9014: TaskWorker stops processing tasks

State: closed
Opened: 2025-03-20T15:41:47Z
Closed: 2025-04-01T13:52:52Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: In Progress, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9014

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-03-20T15:41:47Z)

since switching to [v3.250310](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/releases/tag/v3.250310) we had two incidents, one with canary TW, the other with production TW, where the MasterWorker was reporting 0 free slaves, and hence injecting no new tasks, while the slaves were alive and doing nothing. Indeed periodic actions which are injected independently from the queue status kept going through.

Links to cms-talk

[March 15](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-task-on-status-holding/118483/4)
[March 20](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/tasks-with-status-new-on-command-resubmit-for-a-few-hours/116476/7)

Link to March 20 discussion in MatterMost (with some snapshots from Grafana)
https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/dgc7ntexypb15x4sy511zc1w1c

In both cases problem was solved by TW restart.

From initial look at the code, I believe that something went wrong inside Worker.py.

Action plan:
1. read and understand the code
2. add logging
3. wait for problem to happen again
4. iterate

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-20T16:11:04Z)

**Note**: when production TW was not processing things, canary was not submitting either, why ?
Becase Master could not move any task from NEW to HOLDING and "move to canary" is applied to HOLDING tasks !
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py#L574-L578

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-20T16:22:35Z)

Now. trying to decode what's happened

below there is an example from `proc.c3id_master.pid_18.txt.2025-03-19`

what happens is that this line returns an empty list
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py#L581
because `limit` is 0, from
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py#L561
and
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L310-L318
where ` self.leninqueue` is "hardcoded" to 12
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L200-L202

In other words somehow it must have happened that `self.queuedTasks()` had not been decreased when working on tasks completed.
Note from the log that there is no message after `checking if some has finished`, looks like the multiprocess output queue ia empty
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/70a819bc5215217615ec30aeb43bfcb62af6036f/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L272-L277

IIUC code after that will always log a message `if out is not None`

```text

2025-03-19 23:37:39,608:INFO:MasterWorker:Starting work selection process.
```

It landed on canary, an it got "stuck".
I was hoping for the exception to be in `nohup.out` since i got it on the console anyhow when running with `pdb` [1]. But it got fully swallowed :-(

**Bottom line: this fails**
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7606a362f98751b826841718b726f8be811ce7f1/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L148-L151
**because for DryRun the `outputs` object can not be pickled**

[1]
```text
(Pdb) c

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/multiprocessing/queues.py", line 239, in _feed
    obj = _ForkingPickler.dumps(obj)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/multiprocessing/reduction.py", line 51, in dumps
    cls(buf, protocol).dump(obj)
TypeError: cannot pickle 'htcondor2_impl._handle' object
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T15:04:21Z)

OK. I was seeing the traceback and getting the error in the TW DB becausse the `childWorker` feature uses `multiprocessing` internally, so the exception is being raised before the final message is put in the `results` queue !
And the task is processed "normally", simply with an error. Note that when there is an exception inside the worker (child or not) the `outputs` object is set to contain only the task dictionary
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7606a362f98751b826841718b726f8be811ce7f1/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L122-L123
The problem is when the worker does not raise ! In which case `outputs` is the result of the last action which is a complicated object containing also the input for the next action.
So indeed when not using child worker things are fully silent because there is no try-except around
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7606a362f98751b826841718b726f8be811ce7f1/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L148-L151

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T15:25:39Z)

so the problem was introduced with https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/367e5692451b821683af7404cece63eed280d6ce on Jan 30th
where I set
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7606a362f98751b826841718b726f8be811ce7f1/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1271
and `JobSubmit` is an `htcondor.Submit()` object which can't be picked !

This is not related to changes to Uploader. Simply the type of the output of DagmanCreator changed :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T16:20:01Z)

hmmm.. putting `try...except` around `results.put` does not catch any exception !
Indeed the exception in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9014#issuecomment-2766229808 came from the `self.__get_result()` of the `concurrent.futures` class.

But if there would be an exception in `checkFinished` is should appear in Master log.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T16:34:37Z)

in `checkFinished`
```python
out = self.results.get_nowait()
```
simply returns `queue.Empty`
and indeed while stepping through things I can see that
```text
(Pdb) Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/multiprocessing/queues.py", line 239, in _feed
    obj = _ForkingPickler.dumps(obj)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/multiprocessing/reduction.py", line 51, in dumps
    cls(buf, protocol).dump(obj)
TypeError: cannot pickle 'htcondor2_impl._handle' object
```
is printed to console when the Worker arrives at the end, i.e. at `results.put` time.

I am really annoyed that I can't get to see the error in any other way than with `pdb` !!

Anyhow, let's try to fix.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-31T20:28:09Z)

I have modified the `processWorkerLoop` so that the object put in the shared queue is always the simple
```python
outputs = Result(task=task, result='OK')
```
similarly to what done in case of exceptions, as per https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9014#issuecomment-2766528992

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9031: tasks were submitted even schedulers already saturated.

State: open
Opened: 2025-04-03T13:06:59Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9031

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-04-03T13:06:59Z)

When schedds were saturated, somehow tasks still submitted there thus created number of idle tasks as we can see [here](
https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/CsnjLe6Mk/crab-overview?orgId=11&from=1743588054945&to=1743649757699&viewPanel=115)

ref: https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/tasks-with-submitfailed-or-stuck-after-being-submitted/121750

Stefano:
- even we've functionality of "do not submit if all schedd's are saturated" why it's happened in this case.
- we should have user requests queue in the DB and enforce fair share scheduling.

Example Task that try to submitted to one of saturated schedd.
```
2025-04-02 23:29:01,273:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Try to submit 250402_212720:borzari_crab_sigJecJerNoMet_AMSB_Wino200GeV_ctau1000cm_2022 to [<email>](mailto:<email>) for the 1 time.
2025-04-02 23:29:01,274:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Getting schedd object
2025-04-02 23:29:01,586:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Got schedd object
2025-04-02 23:29:01,586:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Finally submitting to the schedd
2025-04-02 23:29:01,789:DEBUG:DagmanSubmitter:Condor cluster ID returned from submit is: 120772537
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-08T09:52:04Z)

I looked at TW log for the first task indicated in user's report. and that was a RESUBMIT, not a SUBMIT.
We do not limit RESUBMIT even if schedd is saturated. And it bypasses task scheduling.
Difficult/impossible to say if all those tasks in Idle were resubmit or failure to enforce the limit on submit.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-16T12:42:31Z)

Let's assume that it was all RESUBMIT until we can catch a real "mistake" in action and dig into it. We do not have any simple way to stop "RESUBMIT". Maybe we can close new submission before the limit is reached to have some breathing room in the scheduler. Sort of a "watermark" instead of a "limit".
@aspiringmind-code @sinonkt what do you think ? It is easy to do but we have another configuration constant to track, even if we were to hardcode it.

State: closed

Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9034

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-04-07T16:50:31Z)

We recently hit some scale limitation in I/O and memory on schedulers.
A source was in a high rate of job complete/start (or fail/restart !) resulting in a lot of PostJobs running at same time.

Lowering the number of concurrently running PostJobs for a task from 20 to 10 is expected to help by spreading that load over more time, while there should be no significant degradation on "performance". Delay resubmission of failed jobs can only help, and for successful jobs the only effect is a bit of delay in submisson to ASO which anyhow takes O(hours).

While this is controlled also in TaskWorker python configuration, a proper, documented, value in the code will help.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9ac340864c34ce29acc0b732bd1410cd0e6de4ff/scripts/task_process/cache_status.py#L285-L289

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9047

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-04-15T09:58:05Z)

code sort of assumes that there is time to catch all statuses.
But if a job quickly fails twice with message to retry, in the code below the node `status` may fail to be sampled while in STATUS_SUBMITTED in the second attempt, so that `info['State']` will not be changed from `cooloff` when STATUS_POSTRUN is detected.

The point is that while a node is in POSTRUN, i.e. PostJob wating to run, we have no way to know if it is waiting because maxPost in the DAGMAN kicked in, or if it is waiting on the transfer to complete. And the only time we have jobs in cooloff now is when they are back to STATUS_READY or STATUS_PRERUN

Indeed inside STATUS_READY we should check on retry number to tell unsubmitted from cooloff, like done in PRERUN, instead of looking at what the node status was set to in previous iteration of the cache_status.py script (`info['State']) !

Many things can happen between one iteration and the next of the status caching script, it should never rely on previous value, if possible, but only on current information.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9ac340864c34ce29acc0b732bd1410cd0e6de4ff/scripts/task_process/cache_status.py#L275-L294

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-04-23T20:26:38Z)

we get too many of these from TW

(most recent call last):\n  File \"/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Worker.py\", line 108, in processWorkerLoop\n    workOutput = work(resthost, dbInstance, WORKER_CONFIG, task, procnum, inputargs)\n  File \"/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py\", line 174, in handleNewTask\n    rucioClient = getNativeRucioClient(config=config, logger=handler.logger)\n  File \"/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/RucioUtils.py\", line 49, in getNativeRucioClient\n    ret = nativeClient.ping()\n  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/rucio/client/pingclient.py\", line 44, in ping\n    raise exc_cls(exc_msg)\nrucio.common.exception.RucioException: An unknown exception occurred.\nDetails: no error information passed (http status code: 503)\n"]

Maybe it is enough to protect the client intialization ?

The monitoring scripts like recall quota show instead that in a long loop at some point we get
```

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 697, in _update_chunk_length
    self.chunk_left = int(line, 16)
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 16: b''
[....]
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 760, in generate
    for chunk in self.raw.stream(chunk_size, decode_content=True):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 572, in stream
    for line in self.read_chunked(amt, decode_content=decode_content):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 793, in read_chunked
    self._original_response.close()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/contextlib.py", line 131, in __exit__
    self.gen.throw(type, value, traceback)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/urllib3/response.py", line 455, in _error_catcher
    raise ProtocolError("Connection broken: %r" % e, e)
```

which may also be a bug in the client, should handle `b''` like a `None` w/o crashing.

Anyhow... we have this since months now, Should do something.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-28T10:39:47Z)

So the TaskPublisher process for this task was indeed running for those 3 hours, preventing the Publisher from starting another loop and effectively blocking everything.
Publisher cuts blocks at 100 files, so 51 iterations to publish 5100 files are OK.
What is not OK is that it took 2~3 minutes every time.
Sort of "DBS" was overloaded.

While things could be done to make Publisher work in a more continuous way, there is little to gain if we are stuck in writing to DBS.

Was this a special use case ? 5190000 lumis / 5190 files = 1K lumis per file.
Which of course and as usual makes no sense. This [task](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250426_100620%3Achensh_crab_DPStoPsi2SJ_2018_SKIM) was processing a user-generated MC: [/Pythia8_DPStoPsi2SJ_filter3p5/chensh-MC2018_RECO_chensh_v7-a5d501e738bc46974ac8d371aaff19e9/USER](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?view=list&limit=50&instance=prod/phys03&input=/Pythia8_DPStoPsi2SJ_filter3p5/chensh-MC2018_RECO_chensh_v7-a5d501e738bc46974ac8d371aaff19e9/USER) with 1 file per job.

Also all 5190 jobs completing in a short amount of time is very unusual.

Or 5190 jobs all starting in a short time, job duration from `crab status`:   `0:01:03 min, 0:11:22 max, 0:02:54 ave`  :-(

I still have the feeling that even with 1K lumis, one 100-file block should not take 2~3 minutes to publish, but that's a DBS thing.

All considered, I do not see any simple way to resolve this.
This task was totally crazy, the input datsaset has ` Number of events: 4797 Number of files: 9945` , files mostly have 0 or 1 events and yet user ran a SKIM step with 1 file per job as input, no wonder running time is 1min).

I will think if we can put some protection against this.
To be compared with the effort of rewriting the main Publisher loop so that it does not wait for all subprocesses to be completed before checking for new work.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-28T13:34:48Z)

Job completion for that user

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eff52da9-2a51-4845-b7be-a2d2e8bf53a9)
is indeed packed in a short time interval but not extraordinary as rate goes when compared with all users in same interval

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca7d4b6e-f019-4e69-ba77-c536bc41d048)

Comparing with e.g. tasks for user `afelizia` I got convinced that the thing which slows DBS is the old number of lumis evil, with 1K lumis in each input file. I can't find the details of the task which created that dataset with 1K lumis and 1 event per file. I suspect that 1K lumis is some kind of "user default for GEN" and number of events is simply due to heavy filtering.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-28T14:48:03Z)

The original dataset was a GEN from https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250422_150118%3Achensh_crab_DPStoPsi2SJ_2018_GEN
with 10^9 events, 10K jobs, 100K events per job, so given our default of `'tm_events_per_lumi = 100``, indeed 1K lumi per job.
Which gave a dataset with 10K files and 1K lumi per file which was then processed through DIGI, HTL and RECO to obtain the input to this final SKIM.

Clearly 1k lumis per file made no sense here, 1 lumi should be good enough.

I do not remember now why we picked 100 events per lumi as the default, maybe at the time we were seeing 1M event tasks for generation, not 1 billion. I guess that setting as input `lumis_per_files` would be too many code changes ? I'd rather not changes the splitting code based on `events_per_lumi` but we could change the client to set it based on lumis per file with a default of 1.

Most user do not use `events_per_lumi` anyhow.
But I see that some still do, even currently and with more or less sensible values like this task [250428_024650:mmadhu_crab_Pythia3MuMassBBCCTest_cfi_RedecayAprilRoundC1Type9](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250428_024650%3Ammadhu_crab_Pythia3MuMassBBCCTest_cfi_RedecayAprilRoundC1Type9) with `10K jobs, 50M events (so 5K events per job) and 30K events_per_lumi` which eventually lead to 1 lumi per file

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-28T15:35:35Z)

one possibility is to change code in the client so that if user does not specify `events_per_lumi` it gets computed from Njobs and Nevents to be 1 lumi per job.
And give to users with special needs the possibility to indicate a different value of `lumis_per_file` with a BIG warning (maybe implement and do not tell until someone comes up with a use case ? or simply keep in mind but not implement).

I.e. keep current client/server interface based on `events_per_lumi` but stop accepting as input to the client.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-28T22:31:10Z)

I have a tentative implementation of `lumis_per_files` in https://github.com/belforte/CRABClient/tree/add-lumis-per-file which overrides `events_per_lumi`.
Will be very easy to make this default to `1` when `events_per_lumi` is not indicated.
I will try to poll users before implementing.
This should then be moved to a CRABClient issue.

Reworking Publisher is too much effort IMHO. All in all those pathological tasks are bad anyhow, better to prevent them than to accomodate them.
If there are genuine use cases with 1K lumis per file, those should be from real data and not come in 10K jobs each. All in all 1K lumi per file x 10K files is 10M lumis. x 23.3 sec this is 7 years of integrated running time !!

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-04-29T15:32:11Z)

Currently crab status does not show the exit code for failed jobs which will be retried, only when job is terminally failed the exit code is added to the status cache and displayed.

It would be better if CRAB status reports the exit code of the failed job, if we can do w/o confusing users !

Code to change is in here
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1d41fa3554c92583a3ad2c03036e74f9d24f83eb/scripts/task_process/cache_status.py#L226-L230

DAG nodes go in `failed` only when all automatic retries have been exhausted.

Need some way to consistently reproduce so that I can compare `crab status` output "across  changes"

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-29T15:33:17Z)

put high in priority because if I wait I will forget how `cache_status.py` works !!

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-29T19:41:57Z)

at first sight the fix is to change
```python
if 'State' in statedict and statedict['State'] == 'failed' and jobid in data:
```
to
```python
if 'State' in statedict and statedict['State'] in ['cooloff', 'failed'] and jobid in data:
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-29T19:43:50Z)

take this chance to also show that exit status was 0 for jobs in transferring ? which now reports `Unknown`
Or keep it like this to signal that we are waiting for the transfer exit code ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-01T11:00:02Z)

number of retries is wrong in crab status when job finally fails
```text
Extended Job Status Table:

 Job State        Most Recent Site        Runtime   Mem (MB)      CPU %    Retries   Restarts      Waste       Exit Code
   1 failed       T2_CH_CERN              0:04:14         81          0          2          0    0:07:27            8028
```

```text
   1 toRetry      T2_CH_CERN              0:03:15          0          0          2          0    0:02:12         Unknown
```

Of course there's the usual ambiguity whether we count 1 job + N retries or call every iteration a retry.

The 2 comes from `cache_status.py` and is there both in new and old version of the cache file.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-01T17:17:30Z)

hmm... need also to catch when jobs was resubmitted and status is `idle` instead of `cooloff`. What do we want when status is `running` ? "unknwown" or "exit code from last try" ?

maybe change in  crab status output the last column from 'Exit Code' to `Last Exit Code` ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-02T13:00:58Z)

I found that things still work by removing the check on ` staatedict['State'] ` in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1d41fa3554c92583a3ad2c03036e74f9d24f83eb/scripts/task_process/cache_status.py#L227

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-07T19:16:28Z)

There is a bug. See https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5389

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-07T19:52:10Z)

these two codes are not equivalent :-(

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/214d7254-2557-4b2f-9d64-dfd3a69fdeb8)

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9061/files#diff-4cd2ad45dbb4fde4b826893461177ff6ca028a36bdc6127977c76bb0d5acf54eL226-R231

@aspiringmind-code  I have added comments in the code to clarify what the code should do, hopefully clarifying the issue. See the commit above.
I will like advice on how to fix, I find the old format very confusing (I like to blame that for the mistake !)
```
    for jobid, statedict in nodes.items():
        if 'State' in statedict and statedict['State'] == 'failed' and jobid in data:
            # pick error info from last retry (SB: AFAICT only last retry is listed anyhow)
            for key in data[jobid]:
                statedict['Error'] = data[jobid,key]
```
note that I had changed `data` to `fjrReports` in an attempt to clarify.

Let's share the suffering for not having noticed this when looking at the code :-)

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-05-08T15:58:27Z)

How about we use max() to replace the inner loop and keep the outer loop as is?
```
    # Iterate over all jobs in `nodes` that are also present in `fjrReports`.
    for jobid, statedict in nodes.items():
        if jobid in fjrReports:
            # Find the last retry attempt by taking the maximum key (retry number).
            last_retry = max(fjrReports[jobid], key=int)  # Get the latest retry (largest key).
            # Set the error summary from the last retry attempt.
            statedict['Error'] = fjrReports[jobid,last_retry]
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-08T16:05:20Z)

thanks @aspiringmind-code . Let me digest this a a bit. There is already code which makes sure that only last retry is present
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/d0705282d25a832422fa92c6eb513370f5e1dc0b/scripts/task_process/cache_status.py#L455-L462

Maybe the original developer wanted to be double sure

I am not familiar with that `max(.., key=int)` will it cast the retry which now is a string into an int ? Not that >10 retries are possible atm, but... one never knows.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-08T16:15:12Z)

this appears to do, but I find it ugly and not clear
```python
 list(fjrReports[jobid].values())[0]
```

```
>>> jobid='2'
>>> fjrReports
{'2': {'0': [5, 'Error while running CMSSW:\n', {}]}}
>>> error = list(fjrReports[jobid].values())[0]
>>> error
[5, 'Error while running CMSSW:\n', {}]
>>>
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-08T16:22:04Z)

OTOH, there's possibly no alternative to turning the `{'0': [5, 'Error while running CMSSW:\n', {}]}` dictionary into a list, pretty much as the original was doing by iterating over the dictionary content
```python
for retry in fjrReports[jobid]:
    nodes[jobid,'Error'] = fjrReports[jobid,retry]
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-08T16:43:48Z)

after reading https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#max your solution is indeed very elegant. I guess I did not realize that a dictionary is an iterable https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-iterable
🙇

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-05-14T08:27:01Z)

Current code moves tasks from WAITING to NEW in round-robin fashion.

This can be improved:

1. do not move to NEW more tasks then TW can digest (i.e. look at number in NEW)
   * we have seen that when there is a submission burst tasks are moved in NEW very quickly, but once they are in NEW we loose scheduling and things become random (tasks are processed in the order in which they get fetched from DB with a `limit` option in SQL)
 2. get from DB the information  about dag status and number of jobs and reduce the share for users who are already using a lot of resources
   * this may require new API's to fetch data from task table with a "created since" constrain
   * be aware that tasks with failed jobs will appear s completed but can be re-activated by a `crab resubmit`. Can/should we do anything ?

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9074: High number of DNS queries from prod-tw01
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9074: High number of DNS queries from prod-tw01

State: closed
Opened: 2025-05-15T08:03:58Z
Closed: 2025-05-23T12:35:33Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9074

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2025-05-15T08:03:58Z)

We get the following mail from the Spectrum Service occasionally:
```
You are listed as responsible for crab-prod-tw01 (.cern.ch).
Our DNS servers are warning that this host has been sending a VERY HIGH
rate of queries for the last hour (65.71444444444444 requests/sec).

Please, check the cause of this problem and sort it out
since it impacts the central DNS service performance. Please
also consult https://codimd.web.cern.ch/bM1_cKzkTGm0qX-8asLxwQ?view#DNS-Caching (alma9) or
http://service-dns.web.cern.ch/service-dns/faq.asp
for information on setting up dns for high demanding clients (page accessible from CERN network only).

Should this problem continue, we will have to block this system
to avoid performance problems in the central DNS service.

        Thanks in advance,
                                    CERN Network Support

More info: crab-prod-tw01
|                        |               |                  On IP DNS servers | queries/sec during 15 min |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                     --- TOTAL ---  |       65 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                     cmsweb.cern.ch |      65.6 queries/sec     |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                   monit-dc.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                 monit-otlp.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |          caproxylbp-meyrin.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                agileinf-mb.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                     cerndc.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |   cmsgwms-collector-global.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                 cmssst.web.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 |                cmsweb-prod.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
| crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch | 137.138.53.39 | it-puppet-masters-public-b.cern.ch |      0.0 queries/sec      |
-<email>-
<email>
```

It wasn't frequent enough before to call for a deep-dive investigation. See [old issue](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7287) However, since the hypervisor migration on 23 April 2025, it became much too frequent. A [ticket](https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=ticket&table=incident&n=INC4462896) was raised.

The problem and the proposed solution are described below:
crab-prod-tw01.cern.ch, is generating a very high rate of DNS queries (93.2 requests/sec), which is impacting CERN's central DNS service. The issue seems to be linked to how DNS resolution is handled, particularly in the Docker container running on the host.

**Host Configuration:**
The host (/etc/resolv.conf) is configured with a local DNS resolver: 127.0.0.53.
This points to systemd-resolved, which should act as a caching layer to reduce the load on upstream DNS servers.

**Container Configuration:**
Inside the Docker container, the resolv.conf is directly using CERN's DNS servers (137.138.16.5, 137.138.17.5, etc.) instead of 127.0.0.53.
This means systemd-resolved's caching is bypassed entirely, and all DNS queries are sent directly to CERN's DNS servers, resulting in high query rates.

**Docker Networking Mode:**
We are using --net host, which means the container shares the host’s network stack, but it does not automatically use the host's DNS caching (127.0.0.53).
Docker just copies the host's resolv.conf when the container starts.
Since the host's resolv.conf points to 127.0.0.53, Docker replaces it with the actual DNS servers during container startup.

**Missing Tools Inside the Container:**
Basic diagnostic tools like resolvectl and journalctl are not available in the container, which makes it harder to debug DNS resolution from inside.
Most Docker containers don't run systemd by design (they're meant to run a single process).
Use dnsutils for dns resolution instead of systemd resolved
docker logs <container_name> --tail 50 --follow instead of journalctl

**Solutions:**
**Use the Host's Local Resolver (127.0.0.53) Inside the Container:**
Add the following flag when running Docker:
docker run --net host **--dns 127.0.0.53** …
This forces the container to query the host's systemd-resolved instead of CERN's DNS servers directly.
Expose 127.0.0.53 to Docker Containers: Make sure Docker’s --net host mode respects local DNS caching or configure nftable rules

**Monitor DNS Queries:**
Enable debugging on systemd-resolved:
resolvectl log-level DEBUG: Use dnsutils instead
journalctl -f -u systemd-resolved.service: Use docker logs instead
Inside the container, we can also use tcpdump or wireshark to check outgoing DNS queries: tcpdump may have to be installed first…did in TW

**Verify Docker Configuration:**
Ran docker inspect <container-id> and checked the DNS settings.
All DNS options empty/not set
Also, inspected Docker’s global configuration:
cat /etc/docker/daemon.json  This docker folder is empty…has no such file.
Looked for any DNS configurations that might override the host settings.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9079: defer PostJob for a longer time when waiting on Rucio
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9079: defer PostJob for a longer time when waiting on Rucio

State: closed
Opened: 2025-05-16T15:21:39Z
Closed: 2026-04-07T11:01:33Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9079

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-05-16T15:21:39Z)

We may be waiting for Rucio  transfer to many days (failing the PostJob will not help since we can not resubmit jobs which failed in transfer, Rucio will not accept an old LFN with a different checksum).

In this case it is better not to run many PostJobs uselessly every 30min, since we may end up overloading the AccessPoint resources. Better to increase defer time.

The best (only?) way seems to exit immediately from `dag_bootstrap.sh` with exit code 4, i.e. deferral stays at 30min (hardcoded in DAG description file), but PJ duration is minimal and Python is not started, saving a lot on memory.

See
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8429#issuecomment-2886703358

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-16T16:41:33Z)

one idea
* `grep DEFERRING` in PostJob log to find how many times we tried.
   * after 10 times exit immediately with 50% chance and log DEFERRING
   * after 20 times with 10%
   * ...

something like this
| number of DEFERRING | hours since completion | probabiliyt of running PostJob|Hours between PJ runs (average) |
| - | - | - |- |
| 0 | 0 | 1 | 0.5 |
| 8 | 4 | 1/2 | 1 |
|24 |12 | 1/6  |3 |
|48 |24 | 1/12  |6 |
| 96 | 48 | 1/24 | 12 |

which is the simple formula `if Ndefer > 8, prob of runnin PJ is 1/(Ndefer/4)`

I think that the "run or not run" can be done via `/usr/bin/shuf` see [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/a/2556282/13696042)

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-21T15:39:53Z)

PostJob is called by DAGMAN via this POST script macro (broken into multiple lines for readibility)
```
SCRIPT DEFER 4 1800 POST Job1 dag_bootstrap.sh POSTJOB $JOBID $RETURN $RETRY $MAX_RETRIES

/store/temp/user/belforte.4bba3c2d14d54a938291c268ff4eba8b575b197f/GenericTTbar/StefanoTest-240524/250520_093145/0000
/store/user/belforte/GenericTTbar/Stefano-Test-240524/250520_093145/0000
```

as per
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/accd4c8ae43333584366d76cb263155972bfa7f9/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L55

so the arguments for `dag_bootstrap.sh` are:
|`#` |arg| meaning/use
| - |-|-|
1 | stage | (PREJOB/PREDAG/POSTJOB)
2|$JOBID |   the HTCondor job ID [ClusterId.ProcId] of the node job [HTC doc](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-introduction.html#special-script-argument-macros), irrelevant for this
3|$RETURN  | the return value of the HTCondor job [HTC doc](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-introduction.html#special-script-argument-macros), irrelevant for this
4|$RETRY  | the current job retry #, starts at 0 [HTC doc](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-introduction.html#special-script-argument-macros)
5|$MAX_RETRIES | the max number of retries, irrelevant for this
6|TaskName | irrelevant for this
7|crabId | a.k.a. the job number. toghether with $RETRY identifies the postJob log file
8|temp_dir | irrelevant for this
9|out_dir | irrelevant for this
10|log file tarball | irrelevant for this
11|stage | conventional/probe/tail... irrelevant for this
12- |output files | irrelevant for this
