title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9094: Publisher_Rucio disagrees with Rucio on block content
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9094: Publisher_Rucio disagrees with Rucio on block content

State: closed
Opened: 2025-05-23T16:57:58Z
Closed: 2025-06-16T14:52:27Z
Labels: Type: Bug, RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9094

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-05-23T16:57:58Z)

I just hit the opposite problem to #8491

When task is killed, PostJobs do not run anymore, Rucio closed the datasets/blocks with all files transferred at that point, but the publish flag in transersdb will never be updated.

So we end up with more files in Rucio then in filetransfersdb and Publisher waits forever for things to become consistent.

My current thinking is that this is all crazy. Since now Rucio is in full control of the block content, there is no point for the publish flag.

This was sort of due to lazyness. We should have a new API to retrieve files which have `block_complete='OK'` and leave entirely to ASO/Rucio the control, "complementing" https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5175d23489ad7b07e7fd5324e33c2220b6d23fab/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py#L101

Or maybe at the time that ASO/Rucio updates file record in filetransfersdb, also set the publish value.
I.e. change
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5175d23489ad7b07e7fd5324e33c2220b6d23fab/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/MonitorLockStatus.py#L255
and
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5175d23489ad7b07e7fd5324e33c2220b6d23fab/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTFileTransfers.py#L185

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-23T16:58:50Z)

@aspiringmind-code let's talk about this, I need advice before I do such changed

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-26T13:07:24Z)

I am starting to think that when using Rucio there is no need to keep running the PostJob. I believe that it is only needed to resubmit in case of failure. But I still need to be sure of when exactly metadata are uploaded.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-26T13:16:50Z)

PostJob logic is (see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5175d23489ad7b07e7fd5324e33c2220b6d23fab/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2129 and following):
1. call PerformTransfers
2. if it returns 4: defer (returns 4 to Dagman)
3. if it return error or exception (returns 2 (retry me) or 3 (call it failed) to Dagman
4. else (returns 0) upload input and output metadata, publication flag  and exit (return 0 to Dagman)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ef9ae6c-d7ea-4153-ab14-89a321ce6a5a)

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-26T13:23:32Z)

When using Rucio it could upload the metadata submit to ASO and return 0 to Dagman. No matter what happens later, no resubmission is possible.

But we need to modify `cache_status.py` so that it takes into account the transfer status, not only the status from Dagman. Or jobs will be labelled as "completed" even if still in transfer.

Of course we may argue that once things are in Rucio hands, CRAB job is over and indeed jobs is completed successfully.

That will surely save code and effort. Maybe only put this in the documentation ?

We could also change CRAB Client to pick transfer status from Rucio, rather than from HTC AP. So can still offer synoptic view including publication. `crab status` surely has become complicated with time and may use a good cleanup. Possibly at the same time as we remove the code which parses "Dag nodes".

Of keep Rucio handling in `task_process/RUCIO_Transfers.py` and in there write  a JSON summary which `cache_status.py` can parse w/o adding Rucio calls in there.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-26T13:53:24Z)

side note about `publication flag` update in PostJob
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5175d23489ad7b07e7fd5324e33c2220b6d23fab/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2186
as soon as we decide to change PostJob when using Rucio, this could be done by RUCIO_Transfer at the same time it sets  block_complete='OK'. This will also simplify Publisher since it will only retrieve from the DB files in completed blocks.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-28T13:39:12Z)

I need to look at metadata uploading. It would be much simpler if we could avoid "if Rucio" and do all the uploads in any case as soon as job is successful and control handed to ASO.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-03T09:44:54Z)

metadata are inserted in FileMetaData table using LFN as key. Therefore
 * input FMD can be uploaded as soon as job completes OK.
 * output FMD key does not change if jobs is retried, so maybe we can upload that as well.
 * A drawback I see is to upload useless records if the job ultimately fails during ASO.  But we periodically clean up FMD table.
 * **BUT** FMD contains file checksum. If job is retried, checksum changes !  Also outtmplocation will change.
 * current API allows to change outtmplfn and outlfn in the FMD, nut not checksums. But it looks easy to add in DataFileMetadata.py

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-04T13:44:11Z)

I am leaning toward leaving current code unchanged for ASO-FTS and do things differently only for ASO-Rucio where we are sure that there are no resubmissions of successful jobs.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-09T15:08:47Z)

Changing of the publish flag in filetransfersdb has to be done in Rucio, since in the PostJob it depends on ASO to succeed and the `delayed_publicationflag_update` to be turned from False to True. I suspect that that extra logic is an overkill, would only make sense in case of mulitple outputs where only some failed, but if the job is retried, the wrong checksum will be in DBS, Of course chance of this are extremely small, and those checksums are very unlikely to be ever used. Anyhow as usual I am leaving the current part "as is".

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-09T16:05:50Z)

hmm... maybe  I got it wrong, `delayed_publicationflag_update` is set to True during `inject_to_aso()`. Need to test, may I can keep it in PostJob after uploading of output file MD. BTW also uploading of OutputMD only makes sense if publication is not disabled, looks like this was overlooked in PostJob.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-10T09:10:38Z)

The code which I put in does the following:

* only PostJob is changed
* very small changes in any case (better comments and log messages, capturing publish flag updating in a method)
* always upload input metadata before handing control to ASO
* introduce `self.useAsoRucio` and when true upload output metadata and set publish flag to True right after triggering ASO work (in first PJ iteration)
* keep the PJ running also for ASO-Rucio so that job status is reported the same way as it is now.
* no changes to Publisher

I tested in simple tasks. More to come

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-11T13:06:30Z)

The above sort of works.
But when I killed a test task I ended up with a file inserted in a closed Rucio dataset, with an OK lock, but which was not updated in transfersdb, block name and blockStatus=OK are missing, even if publish flag was set to True by PostJob. So Pubisher finds again that number of acquired files does not match what's in Rucio dataset and waits forever.

In a way it looks like a bug in ASO/Rucio. But it is suspicious that it only appeared after I did changes in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9089

Maybe I introduced a situation not foreseen by original developer (Wa) ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-11T14:31:59Z)

notes to myself

`user.belforte:/GenericTTbar/belforte-Stefano-Test-250609-5e829523c2eebdfafa0bc0ee3560a36f_TRANSFER.07e63004/USER`

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-11T15:26:56Z)

I fear that two tasks running at same time got confused and step on each other feet.
Maybe ASO/Rucio adds replicas to Publish container sort of "progressively" while having an open dataset there, instead of "moving closed datasets" ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-11T15:27:54Z)

I will test running a killing a single task to check that things are otherwise OK.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-11T15:47:58Z)

files from different tasks in same Rucio-dataset/DBS-blocks will be very confusing anyhow and may even lead to other problems since those files go in different disk directories. So if problem is confirmed I do not think that changing Publisher is an option

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-12T10:06:47Z)

INdeed, IIUC the ASO/Rucio code, transferred files are added to Publish container "independently of the dataset they are in the transfer container", using code in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/a2e8f430abddc59915bc97bae60a0dd11b5555fa/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/RegisterReplicas.py#L201
which relies on
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/a2e8f430abddc59915bc97bae60a0dd11b5555fa/src/python/ASO/Rucio/Actions/BuildDBSDataset.py#L96
to decide if use a currently open dataset or create a new one, using current status and content in Rucio as bookkeeping.
So once  a task has opened a dataset, another can also use it, until it is time to close.

I am wondering how I did not spot this last year !!

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-12T13:12:00Z)

Never the less, I do not like my solution because for various reasons (including crashes) there can be files with publish flag set to True but without the DBS block name and status=OK in filetransfersdb. They will be acquired but not published by Publisher, so we will "leak" files in Acquired.

Must keep metadata uploading done before transfer is over, but setting of publish flag has to be done inside ASO/Rucio at the same time as setting publication flag.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-12T17:13:50Z)

so above [summary](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9094#issuecomment-2958310206) will be changed to

*   always upload input metadata before handing control to ASO
*   introduce self.useAsoRucio and when true
    * upload output metadata  right after triggering ASO work (in first PJ iteration)
    *  do not and set publish flag to True in PostJob
*   keep the PJ running also for ASO-Rucio so that job status is reported the same way as it is now.
*  in ASO/Rucio/Actions/MonitorLockStatus/updateREESTFileDocsBlockCompletionInfo also set  publish flag to True
*   no changes to Publisher

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-16T12:50:08Z)

the above appears to work now.
The remaining problem is that after a `crab kill`, all jobs in transfer are listed as failed because PostJob did not complete the the "wait for transfer" cycle, but Rucio will still transfer files and ASO-Rucio will close blocks and trigger publishing.
So my test ended up with published files from failed jobs. I am not sure if this is only bad looking or will also give problems for a possible `crab recover`. In my test all jobs were failed, so `crab recover` refused to recover. But realistically that's an extreme case.

I will consolidate work here for the time being.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-18T10:23:54Z)

closing note: in one example I verified that kill + recovery gets the full sample analysed and published. The "problem" is that some jobs are listed as failed in crab status even if everything is fine and output is published.
I have no good idea how to address that.
@dciangot suggestions welcome

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9098: Wrong Dagman status for some tasks

State: closed
Opened: 2025-05-28T16:43:52Z
Closed: 2025-05-30T11:23:23Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: Critical
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9098

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-05-28T16:43:52Z)

following up on user problem report

https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-jobs-stuck-in-toretry-state/125339

I have found that all the 3 tasks indicated suffer of same problem.

At some point all DAG nodes were completed of failed and Dagman exited

But some failed jobs were left in PRERUN status in the `node_status` file, making CRAB report them and ToRetry and preventing resubmission.

Indeed the `node_status` reports a running Dagman with 35 nodes in PRE
```
[crabtw@vocms0121 cluster123521780.proc0.subproc0]$ head -15 node_state
[
  Type = "DagStatus";
  DagFiles = {
    "/data/srv/glidecondor/condor_local/spool/1780/0/cluster123521780.proc0.subproc0/RunJobs.dag"
  };
  Timestamp = 1748301015; /* "Tue May 27 01:10:15 2025" */
  DagStatus = 3; /* "STATUS_SUBMITTED ()" */
  NodesTotal = 2086;
  NodesDone = 2051;
  NodesPre = 35;
  NodesQueued = 0;
  NodesPost = 0;

```
looking at e.g. the metric file, it reports the Dagman as PRERUN (status 2, see  [HTC doc](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-information-files.html#current-node-status-file))
```[crabtw@vocms0121 cluster123521780.proc0.subproc0]$ cat RunJobs.dag.metrics
{

On 29/05/2025 16:28, Cole Bollig wrote:
> Hi Stefano,
>
>     When DAGMan goes to write the final node status on the way out the door, it checks if its state has changed
> before actually writing the node status file. In this case it appears that DAGMan has determined that its state
> had not changed since the prior writing of the DAG node status file.
> If you want to have DAGMan to re-write the node status file at exit regardless of state change,
> you can add the ALWAYS-UPDATE keyword to the declaration in your DAG file.
>
>     Points 2 & 3 are due to the fact that DagStatus means different things in the node status file
> and the metrics file.
>  This discrepancy is something that has sadly existed for a long time,
> and I don't know the best way to address it.
>
>         For the node status file, the DagStatus is equivalent to the value list you
>               provided from our documentation.
>         For the metrics file, the DagStatus is set to the value of the DAGMan jobs ClassAd attribute
 [DAG_Status](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html#DAG_Status).
>
>
> I will update the documentation to better reflect attempting to write the node status file on exit and warn that DagStatus is different between the two files.
>
> Hope this helps,
> Cole Bollig

State: open

Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: Medium

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-06-04T08:21:58Z)

in case there are multiple tasks using same rule for tape recall, current code does not have a way to remove the rule even if they are all killed, since the `handleKill` method in there is a loop on tasks. Even if all tasks are killed, they are processed independently and when checking one there are always other using the rule and rule deletion is skipped.

Rule will eventually be removed 1 month after creation, but in the meanwhile it persists in our dashboard and if partially completed keeps locked data in place affecting quotas.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/760bad67b5fcdef2ce9641399fbe700c6e980ff7/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/TapeRecallManager.py#L68-L87

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-04T08:26:22Z)

In the one case I was looking at, there were two killed tasks and rule was in SUSPENDED status.
Which raises the interesting questions of what to do when TapeRecallManager finds some SUSPENDED rule. Do we report ? Do we delete ? Do we try to fix ?
A way to "try to fix" is to change status from SUSPENDED to STUCK and then boost rule which sets it to REPLICATING so that transfers are attempted again. IIUC Rucio sets rules in SUSPENDED after they have been STUCK (i.e. with some failings) for 15 days and does not try anymore.

a possible way to solve this may be by checking the status of those other tasks

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9111: ASO/Rucio is not safe against multiple simultaneous tasks
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9111: ASO/Rucio is not safe against multiple simultaneous tasks

State: open
Opened: 2025-06-12T10:27:43Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Status: In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9111

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-06-12T10:27:43Z)

Current code assumes that this instance of ASO/Rucio is the only one writing in a given Rucio publish container at any given time, i.e. that it has full control.
But it is possible (as I encountered in #9094 ) that two tasks run with same Pulication tag (i.e. same targed DBS-datsaset/Rucio-Publish-container) in which case we end up with files from different tasks in same DBS-block/Rucio-dataset.

This confuses other code (Publisher e.g.), developers and users since when using ASO/FTS we are consistent with the rule
"multiple tasks can publish in same DBS dataset, each tasks with a separate (set of) block(s)"

Some redesigning and refactoring of ASO/Rucio code is needed, and of its bookkeeping.

Which is also a good time to write down more description of how it works since https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-design/crab-rucio-aso.html#rucio-dataset was not detailed/clear enough to catch this.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9113: Handling Kill in ASO/Rucio
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9113: Handling Kill in ASO/Rucio

State: open
Opened: 2025-06-19T14:33:54Z
Labels: Priority: Medium, Status: On Hold, RUCIO
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9113

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-06-19T14:33:54Z)

In #8429 we addressed
 * it should not break
 * it should leave things in a status where `crab recovery` works

A few questions are still open, which are more soft, and require a decision, before a technical implementation

- do we need to cleanly and thoroughly   separete Killed from Failed (i.e. completed with some failed jobs ?)
- [ ] when a task is killed, all jobs in transfer are marked as failed, even if output can eventually be transferred and even published. Should we find a way to make them appear as `finished` in `crab status` ?
- [ ] should we remove the Rucio rule on the tranfer container when task is killed ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-20T16:44:33Z)

idea from @dciangot : detach the file replicas from the killed jobs from the container(s)
https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/html/client_api/didclient.html#rucio.client.didclient.DIDClient.detach_dids

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-20T16:46:20Z)

or maybe we can find a way to run PJ for so that jobs become successfull/killed/transferring ?
e.g. https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-interaction.html#suspending-a-running-dag

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78ed466a-e3f1-4f53-b35f-36a6f3c7bf0b)

that way jobs killed while running, idle, unsubmitted, will be marked as FAILED but transferring ones will stay transferring, crab status will show exit code 0. And it may not be so bad that they get really transferred and published.

If we want to kill pending transfers as well, we need indeed a non-trivial cleanup in ASO/Rucio.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-20T19:23:11Z)

and here's from Condor experts about how to halt the Dagman
https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2025-June/msg00054.shtml

The problem here is how to signal the Dagman, via  "create a file in the DAG working directory called **<DAG file>.halt**" from the TW. If we hold/release the Dagman is effectively killed and restarted. I do not know what will happen when if it finds the HALT file when starting.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-25T15:21:09Z)

Maybe better to come back to this after we refactor Dagman handling #6270 so that we do much less work in the startup scripts.
All in all nothing is "broken", simply crab status output is not accurate. We can always address that by making `cache_status.py`check Rucio side as well instead of only using condor logs

Looking at Rucio's BaseClient code we will never get the HTTP exception.
```python
[...]
     STATUS_CODES_TO_RETRY = [502, 503, 504]
[...]
   for retry in range(self.AUTH_RETRIES + 1):
            try:
              [...]
                self.logger.debug("HTTP Response: %s %s" % (result.status_code, result.reason))
                if result.status_code in STATUS_CODES_TO_RETRY:
                    self._back_off(retry, 'server returned {}'.format(result.status_code))
                    continue
```
so when it get 502, it backs off (sleep) up to 3 times, and then it just skips forward to code outside that `for` loop.

IIUC, of course.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9129: Dagman Resubmitter uses deprecated resubmit numcores option in checkMemoryWallTime

State: closed
Opened: 2025-07-10T21:15:10Z

Labels: Type: Bug
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9129

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2025-07-10T21:15:10Z)

Problem discovered by pipeline failure.
```
Task name:			250710_124508:crabint1_crab_20250710_144505
Grid scheduler - Task Worker:	<email> - crab-dev-tw03
Status on the CRAB server:	RESUBMITFAILED
Task URL to use for HELP:	https://cmsweb-test12.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/250710_124508%3Acrabint1_crab_20250710_144505
Dashboard monitoring URL:	https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=crabint1&var-task=250710_124508%3Acrabint1_crab_20250710_144505&from=1752147908000&to=now
Warning:			The following sites from the user site whitelist are blacklisted by the CRAB server: ['T2_IT_Rome', 'T2_ES_IFCA', 'T2_IT_Pisa']. Since the CRAB server blacklist has precedence, these sites are not considered in the user whitelist.
Warning:			The following sites appear in both the user site blacklist and whitelist: ['T2_ES_IFCA']. Since the whitelist has precedence, these sites are not considered in the blacklist.
Failure message from server:	Problem handling 250710_124508:crabint1_crab_20250710_144505 because of 'resubmit_numcores' failure, traceback follows
				Traceback (most recent call last):
				  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py", line 96, in executeAction
				    output = work.execute(nextinput, task=self.task, tempDir=self.tempDir)
				  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py", line 123, in execute
				    self.executeInternal(*args, **kwargs)
				  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py", line 60, in executeInternal
				    checkMemoryWalltime(task, 'resubmit', self.logger, self.uploadWarning)
				  File "/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py", line 159, in checkMemoryWalltime
				    ncores = task[cmd+'_numcores']
				KeyError: 'resubmit_numcores'
```

The problem is that DagmanResubmitter relies on checkMemoryWallTime function of DagmanSubmitter script. The resubmitter should not have the resubmit_numcores option as it has been deprecated while submitter must continue to have the option.
See [here](https://github.com/aspiringmind-code/CRABServer/blob/646fbd7bcada83b0624ed05c16055340b4973f1e/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py#L60) and the note in [here](https://github.com/aspiringmind-code/CRABServer/blob/646fbd7bcada83b0624ed05c16055340b4973f1e/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L147C1-L159C35)

@belforte Should I make a copy of the checkMemoryWalltime function in Dagmanresubmitter without the numcores option?

hmm  isn't is enough to replace
```
ncores = task[cmd+'_numcores']
```
with `ncores = task['tm_numcores']` ?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-07-11T09:01:58Z)

In a way it is not-elegant to have this method. Why single out memory and wall time for validation ? But let's not change too much

Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9140

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-08-01T13:08:39Z)

GOAL: Make it possible to use tokens for data read and local stageout, but do not fail if they are not present.

- [x] in e.g. dagman_bootstrap_startup.sh check that `condor_store_cred query-oauth` returns exit code 0 (meaning that `crabtw` has access to a token on that AP)
- [x] if token is OK. Set a flag: `touch TOKEN_OK` or similar
- [x] in PreJob, if `TOKEN_OK` file is present, add to JDL
    ` use_oauth_services = cms_crab`
- [x] in `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh`
     if `/srv/.condor_creds/cms_crab.use` is present, do `export BEARER_TOKEN_FILE=/srv/.condor_creds/cms_crab.use`

This will not tell if it is using token or proxy to read data, the only way would be to `unset X509_USER_PROXY` and check that it still works.
Better to do that in test submissions.

Hallo Stefano,
   you only have a token in the job, not in the schedd. (Only condor/root has access
to the token on the submit node.) So, i think the dagman_bootstrap_startup.sh first
three steps will not apply.
   Where to set BEARER_TOKEN_FILE we should discuss and agree. I am not in favour
of each team doing that on their own (and hardcoding filenames, etc.).
   Thanks,
         cheers,  Stephan

I beg to disagree. The submitter on the AP (`crabtw`) user has access to its token too:

## Comment (stlammel, 2025-08-01T14:22:21Z)

The token on the schedd should be in /var/lib/condor/oauth_credentials which should
NOT be user readable. Where is the token located? and how did you tell httokendecode
where it is?
 - Stephan

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-01T14:27:51Z)

from httokendecode help:
```
If file name not given, follows WLCG Bearer Token Discovery
  which is to first try $BEARER_TOKEN, next $BEARER_TOKEN_FILE,
  and next ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/bt_u`id -u`.
```
so it uses `/tmp/bt_u501` which AFAICT is constantly refreshed
Indeed  `/tmp/bt_u501` is the same file as `/var/lib/condor/oauth_credentials/crabtw/cms_crab.use` (from `diff`)

Ahh, interesting. HTCondor copies it into /tmp. This might just be during the duration
of jobs plus cleanup. We should check with the HTCondor developers if we can rely on
this. I did not recall seeing this in the documentation.

If you want to know if OAuth credentials are available, i would use the
condor_store_cred command with query-oauth. A bit more complex but more
direct/robust.
 - Stephan

The idea is to add the token for a while and see how this goes. If token access is not

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9145: do we need CRABServer/setup.py ?

State: open
Opened: 2025-08-06T13:38:16Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9145

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-08-06T13:38:16Z)

That script is hard to understand for current maintainers, and hence a fragile point.
But.. give that we do not build rpm's any more and have no place to use pip, but can run everything by pointing PYTHONPATH to `CRABSERVER/src/python`  (or a zip file with its content).... why do we keep it around ?

We have only two "builds":
1. CRABServer (REST(
2. TaskWorker

publishers and twmonit run in the TaskWorker container, simply using a different start script.

It seems to me that our setup is only called in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/82a2c5e5bffae25e2c5ce238baba5ee5970de24f/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/buildTWTarballs.sh#L50-L53

But what cops files from the repo clone to `/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/` in the container seems to be Docker
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/82a2c5e5bffae25e2c5ce238baba5ee5970de24f/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L83-L86

Maybe `setup.py` prepares a `CRABServer/build` directory with "the files specified in setup.py" which then Docker copies. But it seems to me that it would be very easy to copy files from the GH clone w/o going through setup.py

I have not looked at CRABServer, but I suspect the only extra thing is the `/data` subdir which needs to contain the stuff for httpd (i.e. the UI).

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-07T12:06:39Z)

As far as i investigated...

[1] `src/python/CRABInterface/RESTWorkerWorkflow.py` it was **Neither** expanded on **REST** here.
```python
143:    result['resubmit_site_whitelist'] = extraargs['site_whitelist'] if 'site_whitelist' in extraargs else None
144:    if result['resubmit_site_whitelist'] is None and 'siteWhiteList' in extraargs: ## For backward compatibility only.

147:    if result['resubmit_site_blacklist'] is None and 'siteBlackList' in extraargs: ## For backward compatibility only.
148:        result['resubmit_site_blacklist'] = extraargs['siteBlackList']
```
[2] Nor on **TaskWorker**`src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py`, when taskparam::`site_whitelist|site_blacklist` there.
```python
src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanResubmitter.py
80:        if ('resubmit_jobids' in task) and task['resubmit_jobids']:
87:                # files are in the directory resubmit_info in the schedd).

95:                            newAdValue = pythonListToClassAdExprTree(task['resubmit_'+taskparam])
97:                            newAdValue = str(task['resubmit_'+taskparam])
```
____
We can **Either**
1. patch on TW at [1] _exapnding on REST. BUT it should be deprecated anyhow.
2. patch on TW at [2] add SiteResolverInfo TaskAction inside `handleResubmit` on TW, BUT we have to be cautious that SiteResolverInfo was not generic enough for DagmanResumitter which not use kwargs[`task`,`tm_site_whitelist`] but instead it use dedicated inkey `['resubmit_site_whitelist']` when come to task_param.
3. patch on TW at [2] try to just expanding sites there w/o resusing SiteResolverInfo, even we introduced some duplicated code here e.g. instantiate CRIC, exapanding...

**PreJob** should be fine when we patched upstream REST [1] or TaskAction [2].

Let me hear your thoughts...

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-07T13:15:47Z)

it looks a problem in list to HTC classAd conversion. Originating from `set` vs. `list` "confusion". We should be more clear and more consistent on what variable is a set and what a list. Or otherwise use an explicit cast all of the times :-(

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-07T13:17:13Z)

> it looks a problem in list to HTC classAd conversion. Originating from `set` vs. `list` "confusion". We should be more clear and more consistent on what variable is a set and what a list. Or otherwise use an explicit cast all of the times :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-07T13:20:56Z)

at same link there's a fixed SiteInfoResolver.  The problem was this line in DagmanResubmitter
```python
if isinstance(task['resubmit_'+taskparam], list)
```
bad things happen when the argument is a `set` :-(

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-07T13:28:17Z)

I see. `set(...)` we need here is just for when we doing set manipulation like intersection checking, e.g. `global_black_list`, check/substract avaibliblesites...acceleratorssite, ...etc.. later.

I will fixed other places where we really need set then.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-07T13:33:05Z)

I think the best way is: whatever variable we have which is called ...list should be a list. We can convert to a set to do the and/or manipulations, but then revert to a list.  We could surely extend `pythonListToClassAdExprTree()` to deal with set as well, but need to change all type checks before the call.

intermixing lists and sets is a bit in line with Python's "duck typing" standard. But that comes at cost of care in implementation, "strong typing" is a bit more annoying, but safer.

In this case we mostly need a clear policy, IMHO.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9149: CRON commands that relies on crabtwmonit, Failed with No such file or directory, mysteriously missing of monit scripts.

State: closed
Opened: 2025-08-12T12:35:00Z
Closed: 2025-08-12T13:19:31Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9149

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-08-12T12:35:00Z)

Thanks @aspiringmind-code  for reporting these regarding deluge of cronjob failed emails.

As i try to bring back container `TaskWorker_monit_*` and investigated it, it seems like the underlying problems lies in most of our monit scripts somehow were *missing* from `/data/srv/monit`. Thus cron can't periodically spin up container and run their usual commands.

We expected monit scripts to be there as we already explicitly copies them from repo to container, as you can see monit Dockerfile [5].
Also `runContainer.sh` might not be the one who mounted volumes and overwrite things, they just try to keep cfg, logs persistent. [6]

[1] ReportRecallQuota
```
export loguuid=$(uuidgen); test -f /home/crab3/runContainer.sh && bash /home/crab3/runContainer.sh -v v3.latest -s TaskWorker_monit_reportrecallquota -u ${loguuid} -c 'python3 /data/srv/monit/ReportRecallQuota.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 ; [ -f /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt ] && cat /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt
```
[2] GenerateMONIT
```
export loguuid=$(uuidgen); test -f /home/crab3/runContainer.sh && bash /home/crab3/runContainer.sh -v v3.latest -s TaskWorker_monit_generatemonit -u $loguuid -c 'python3 /data/srv/monit/GenerateMONIT.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 ; [ -f /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt ] && cat /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt
```
[3] aso_metrics_ora
```
export loguuid=$(uuidgen); test -f /home/crab3/runContainer.sh && bash /home/crab3/runContainer.sh -v v3.latest -s TaskWorker_monit_asometrics -u ${loguuid}  -c 'python3 /data/srv/monit/aso_metrics_ora.py' >/dev/null 2>&1 ; [ -f /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt ] && cat /tmp/monit-${loguuid}.txt
```
Same OUTPUT(s) from all above commands.
```
[FATAL tini (8)] exec python3 failed: No such file or directory
```
_____

[4] Somehow our monit scripts unexpectedly not lying there in `/data/srv/monit`, thus all commands can't be run.
```
[crab3@crab-dev-tw02 TaskWorker_monit_reportrecallquota]$ docker exec -it TaskWorker_monit_reportrecallquota bash
crab3@crab-dev-tw02:/data/srv/monit$ ls
cfg  hostdisk  logs
crab3@crab-dev-tw02:/data/srv/monit$ python
bash: python: command not found
crab3@crab-dev-tw02:/data/srv/monit$ ls -alh
total 4.2M
drwxr-xr-x. 5 root  root   45 Aug 12 11:37 .
drwxr-xr-x. 4 root  root   30 Aug 12 11:37 ..
drwxr-xr-x. 2 crab3 1399    6 Apr 30  2024 cfg
drwxr-xr-x. 4 crab3 1399   29 Apr 30  2024 hostdisk
drwxr-xr-x. 2 crab3 1399 6.5M Aug 12 10:13 logs
crab3@crab-dev-tw02:/data/srv/monit$ python3 /data/srv/monit/ReportRecallQuota.py
```
[5] Our `cicd/monit_pypi/Dockerfile` looks good, it's confusing me more why `/data/srv/monit` was left empty like in [4]
```Dockerfile
ARG BASE_TAG=latest
FROM registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:${BASE_TAG}

RUN pip install --user pandas

RUN mkdir -p /data/srv/monit/
COPY ./src/python/ServerUtilities.py           \
     ./src/python/RESTInteractions.py          \
     ./src/script/Monitor/GenerateMONIT.py     \
     ./scripts/Utils/CheckTapeRecall.py        \
     ./src/script/Monitor/aso_metrics_ora.py   \
     ./src/script/Monitor/ReportRecallQuota.py \
     /data/srv/monit

ENV PYTHONPATH=/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages:${PYTHONPATH:-}

ENV RUCIO_HOME=/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/current/
ENV RUCIO_ACCOUNT="crab_server"
# no need to source a rucio environment from cvmfs. rucio client is already installed
# via pip, do not pollute the python env with things you do not need!
# ENV PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/x86_64/el9/py3/current/lib/python3.9/site-packages/
# ENV PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/x86_64/el8/py3/current/lib/python3.6/site-packages/

ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"]

CMD bash
# CMD python3 /data/srv/monit/GenerateMONIT.py
# CMD python3.8 /data/srv/monit/CheckTapeRecall.py
    # cp -v RecallRules.html /data/eos/RecallRules-docker.html
    ## we decided to send data to opensearch instead of saving it to eos. no need to copy the file.
```

[6] `runContainer.sh` wish to mount volume only specific stateful paths for writing monitoring states e.g. cfg, logs.
So it's likely not the culprit who wiped out copied monit scripts.
```bash
#list of directories that should exist on the host machine before container start
dir=("/data/container/${SERVICE}/cfg" "/data/container/${SERVICE}/logs")

case $SERVICE in
  TaskWorker_monit*)
    DIRECTORY='monit'
    ;;
  TaskWorker*)
    DIRECTORY='TaskManager'
    ;;
  Publisher*)
    DIRECTORY='Publisher'
    dir+=("/data/container/${SERVICE}/PublisherFiles")
    ;;
  *)
    echo "$SERVICE is not a valid service to start. Specify whether you want to start one of the 'Publisher' variants or 'TaskWorker'." && helpFunction
esac

volumeMounts=()
for d in "${dir[@]}"; do
  if [ -e "$d" ]; then
      volumeMounts+=("-v ${d}:/data/srv/${DIRECTORY}/$(basename "${d}")")
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9152: migrate to ArgoCD
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9152: migrate to ArgoCD State: closed Opened: 2025-08-18T15:41:09Z Closed: 2025-09-15T09:14:39Z Labels: Area: zK8s, Area: CI/CD URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9152 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-08-18T15:41:09Z) Ciao @belforte @aspiringmind-code, Guys, please, allow me to kick start ArgoCD migration via this following Draft below. ## Prelude ArgoCD embraces declarative & GitOps principles: a single source of truth about infrastructure stored in Git, human/PR-gated reviews, operational transparency, built-in version control, and make it easier to maintain, roll back and forth, and fully own our deployment operations through commits and PRs—kind of *decommissioning* direct `kubectl` commands. > Think of ArgoCD as a Puppet agent for Kubernetes—similar in how they have their own agent, polling for VM configs from repo but ArgoCD was tailored for K8s. (P.S. And of course! there's subtle differences!) In our case, we already have such a monorepo (dmwm/CMSKubernetes). But since this repo serves multiple teams, we must address some challenges unique to the shared ownership. ### Key Considerations & Challenges 1. **Shared Monorepo trade-offs**: great for common infra, and CMSWeb we **do have** *common ground*, but less ideal when teams need autonomy and frequent iteration. 2. **PR noise** : when to use PR-gated (human-reviewed) vs Bot-commits. > e.g. our CRAB team alone have 3 DevOps pushing test tags twice daily → ~144 PRs/month flooding github `dmwm/CMSKubernetes`, even if auto-merged. ### Proposed Solution **In short [P1]**: 1. **PR-gated:** for **preprod/prod** and the *base* of **dev/test** manifests remain in GitHub `dmwm/CMSKubernetes`. 2. **Bot-commits:** for *Hot* **dev/test** desired state (*patches/overlays*) moves to a kind of minimal sidecar repo. (e.g. possibly name **crab3/crab-iac** in GitLab). > This gives us autonomy for frequent updates. **where** 1.) Still inherits and respects the base from CMSKubernetes. 2.) Transparency preserved—most code still remains in the shared monorepo. We configure ArgoCD pointng to this, our *team-desired-state* repo, where Bot-commits update hot desired state (tags from crab3/CRABServer pipelines). ** P.S. other Possible sidecar repo names: **crab-dev-iac**, **crab-k8s-infra**, **crab-devtest-infra**, ...etc. **Otherwise [P2]**: > *If sticking to mono repo is something we strongly wish to preserve.* We would need to kindly ask CMSKubernetes maintainers to adopt **branch-based dev/test overlays** with **CODEOWNERS**, so our bot-commits could write directly into them. ## To-Do List - [x] Deploy ArgoCD in test14. - [x] Implement `kustomize` + `vendir` in gitlab `crab-iac` (sidecar) repo, re-organize things current overlays github `sinonkt/CMSKubernetes`. > ArgoCD + Helm is an alternative one, we could do extensive comparison later, **BUT** Since, kustomize are quite intuitive (*no* lots of templates, which a bit hard to comprehend, *IMO*) just plains k8s manifest yaml, have base/overlays concepts, patches on overlays fashions that are highly suitable for large multi-IaC projects that share common ground across team, and among each team envs as CMS. Thus why CMSWeb team choose kustomize approach as default. - [x] Enable Bot-commits workflow in *test14*. - [x] Integrate Bot-commits with current GitLab CI/CD (**crab3/CRABServer**). - [x] Generalize overlays for *test2*, *test12*. - [x] Team (Stefano, Vijay, Krittin) start using *test2*, *test12*, *test14*. - [x] Apply *PR-gated* model in **preprod** (development work on fork **sinonkt/CMSKubernetes**). - [ ] Add mandatory pipeline checks before merge (syntax, conformance, smoke tests, policy checks). > In other words, anywhere/time before we merge, we MUST trigger manifests syntax validations & checking, like kube conformity, in prod, we also might/good-to have to verify against share policies and some smoke tests. ** some pipelines have to be done on our side, some should be integrated to CMSKubernetes in general. ** - [ ] Adopt **CODEOWNERS** rules per overlay dir → enforce path-specific ownership. - [x] Team starts living with *preprod* PR-gated, encounter defects → refine -> iterate. - [ ] Simplify CRABServerAuth secrets (consider multi-env consolidation/generalization if possible). > as Stefano mentioned in the meeting last week. - [ ] Integrate ArgoCD Secrets handling (SOPS + GPG plugin first; later explore alternatives). - [ ] Adopt new ArgoCD-based secrets handling in `test2`, `test12`, `test14` and `preprod`. - [ ] Apply all **lessons learned** to `prod` and `canary`, Switching from **[P1]** to **[P2]** could be made here at this stage, we will discuss again later... Edited: Guys, Please, let me know your thoughts and feels free to comments along the way. I thought of making tutorials and walkthrough around these if you guys would like. This issue will be main Source of Truth for migrating ArgoCD. An input interface for gathering feedbacks, converging to our Team need/convention. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-18T15:43:28Z) 2025 Goals in **Q3**, ArgoCD for our K8s applications in #8879 ## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-18T16:06:07Z) I added values for priority/days so that it shows in the [Workplan](https://github.com/orgs/dmwm/projects/14/views/8) Feel free to change them ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-09-02T09:32:09Z) @belforte @aspiringmind-code Hi, Guys, I've found workaround over current layout and its works now. (but during migration we will stick to my [forked repo]([https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/compare/master...sinonkt:CMSKubernetes:migrate-to-argocd) just for now). ## Comment (belforte, 2025-09-04T11:29:45Z) please take the time to start a new "instruction for ArgoCD" section for this in https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-components/crab-rest/deploy.html which will of course evolve ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-09-04T15:27:09Z) > please take the time to start a new "instruction for ArgoCD" section for this in https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-components/crab-rest/deploy.html which will of course evolve Acknowledge Stefano. P.S. for pipeline testing results could be seen here by use cases: [normal](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/12841421) | [stable-releasing](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/12841502) P.S. will proceeding to secret handling and `prod`, also `canary` on `prod` [1] [2] ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-09-09T12:28:51Z) Guys, Due to the latest strong trends shifting towards `Argo+Helm` in upstream/CMSKubernetes, instead of `Kustomize-First` approach back then. IMO, I love this latest CMSWeb vision a lot, in trading Kustomize readability for long-term operability. Now, `platform` things, e.g. cross-cutting, shared components got started to be helmified. Thus, `Helm` will likely be the one who layering env layouts via clean & clear values.yaml diffs act as deltas/patches in `kustomize` land, This also means current kustomize overlays layouts on upstream/CMSKubernetess will considered to be redundant and likely/better been deprecated. title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9161: High number of DNS queries on schedds.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9161: High number of DNS queries on schedds.

State: closed
Opened: 2025-08-26T08:03:17Z
Closed: 2025-08-26T08:24:49Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9161

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-08-26T08:03:17Z)

We got warning emails from CERN Network Support mentioned 2 of our schedds (vocms0119, vocms0120).

After I've consult with Vijay and also Thanks to his hints from the insightful last time incident write-up that happened on prod-tw01. [#9074](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9074)

We've found that on those schedd machines. Even **systemd-resolved** (The main DNS-caching layer component) was `enabled` and `running`. but `NetworkManager` not aware of **systemd-resolved**, and thus generated `/etc/resolv.conf` as following.
[1]
```
[root@vocms0119 ~]# cat /etc/resolv.conf
# Generated by NetworkManager
search cern.ch
nameserver 137.138.16.5
nameserver 137.138.17.5
nameserver 2001:1458:201:1100::5
# NOTE: the libc resolver may not support more than 3 nameservers.
# The nameservers listed below may not be recognized.
nameserver 2001:1458:201:1000::5
```

which actually `resolv.conf` should point  to `127.0.0.53, systemd-resolved` instead (normally via symlink [2]) for using DNS cache.
[2]
```
[root@vocms0119 ~]# cat /etc/resolv.conf
# This is /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf managed by man:systemd-resolved(8).
# Do not edit.
#
# This file might be symlinked as /etc/resolv.conf. If you're looking at
# /etc/resolv.conf and seeing this text, you have followed the symlink.
#
# This is a dynamic resolv.conf file for connecting local clients to the
# internal DNS stub resolver of systemd-resolved. This file lists all
# configured search domains.
#
# Run "resolvectl status" to see details about the uplink DNS servers
# currently in use.
#
# Third party programs should typically not access this file directly, but only
# through the symlink at /etc/resolv.conf. To manage man:resolv.conf(5) in a
# different way, replace this symlink by a static file or a different symlink.
#
# See man:systemd-resolved.service(8) for details about the supported modes of
# operation for /etc/resolv.conf.
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options edns0 trust-ad
search cern.ch
```

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-08-26T08:24:49Z)

Somehow, every schedds was properly point systemd-resolved's `/etc/resolv.conf` and magically looks good now.... [3]
Don't know why within first hour of incident, The `/etc/resolv.conf` was like [1] generated from NetworkManager.

As ChatGPT educated me, it's very likely that NetworkManager momentarily took control probably triggered by e.g. DHCP renew, link flap, VPN up/down, NM restart thus NM rewrote before systemd-resolved reclaimed it.

[3]
```

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9167: remove CRAB Server external_config

State: closed
Opened: 2025-09-02T19:59:30Z
Closed: 2025-12-03T15:48:36Z
Labels: Status: In Progress, Area: Code Cleanup
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9167

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-09-02T19:59:30Z)

CRABServer pulls from gitlab the external config https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config.json

In a way I'd like to fully get rid of this "external config" things and those obscure "modes".

The only customization that we have now via `'mode` is to use a different S3 bucket, and it would be much more clear if we put that in CRABServer's config.py in CMSKubernetes.

Currently we

* disguise the S3 bucket name as an URL
* put in a JSON file which the REST fetches every 30 minutes
* so that the Client can retrieved it at crab submit time and pass it to the REST again via the DB
* so that the REST knows which bucket to use

Sounds pretty damn stupid.

And I fear that if I am not here, it would take you a long time to figure this out.

**Plan**

- [x] change server `config.py` to support new code by adding following two lines:
   * `data.s3_bucket = 'crabcache_dev'` or `crabcache_preprod` or `crabcache_prod` as appropriate for each cluster
   * `data.compatibleClientVersions = ["v3", "development"]`
   - [x] in test and preprod https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/1657
   - [x] in prod
- [x] change REST ( #9180 ) to:
    - [x] pick bucket from config (alredy picks delegate-dn from there), save it in DB and  ignore `cacheurl` HTTP param in RESTUserWorkflow.py so that it does not matter whether client sends it or not.
    - [x] remove `banned-out-destinations` which we never used
    - [x] remove from  TW  as well (unused code anyhow) #9176
    - [x] move `compatible version` to CRABServer/.../config.py
- [x] deploy new REST
   - [x] in preprod (testbed)
   - [x] in prod
- [x] change `config.py` and   [cmsweb-rest-config.json](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config.json) to eliminate now-useles things (see description in #9180)
   - [x] in test
   - [x] in preprod (testbed)
- [x] cleanup   `cmsweb-rest-config.json` by making it the same as `cmsweb-rest-config-test.json`
    - [x] and verify that prod still work !!!
- [x] change `config.py` in production while keeping it pointing to   `cmsweb-rest-config.json`
- [x] change client not to send useless `cacheurl`  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5411 and once in production (in CrabClient in v3.251020 running in prod CVMFS since Oct 30)
   - [x] remove `cacheurl` submit argument for submit from RESTUserWorkflow.py (where it is now optional) - https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9227

- [x] move handling of `"htcondorPool"` and `htcondorScheddsLink` (i.e. list of enabled schedulers) to TW and manage them via puppet #9201
- [x] deploy new TW, then
   - [x] remove them for REST code `"htcondorPool"` and `htcondorScheddsLink`  #9220
   - [x] remove all references to "external config" everywhere

And finally we can:
- [x] get rid of ` @conn_handler()` everywhere in CRABServer repo

Some of those actions can be pursued independently. I will open ad-hoc issues and possibly hand to DevOps

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9184: Publisher should not try to migrate blocks which are already at destination

State: closed
Opened: 2025-09-11T14:01:52Z
Closed: 2025-09-11T14:54:47Z
Labels: Type: Bug
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9184

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-09-11T14:01:52Z)

While debugging obscure [failed migrations in DBS](https://github.com/dmwm/dbs2go/issues/146) I noticed that [TaskPublish/[y](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/Publisher/TaskPublish.py) tries to migrate all parent blocks, even if they are already at destination.

Usually this is "stupid by harmless" since DBS returnas HTTP 400 and points to the migration which originally put the block in phys03, so TaskPublish checks status of that, finds OK., and goes on happily.

In the case of that issue, the original migration was marked as terminlly failed, and things never recover.

Yet is would be lighter on DBS and more elegant that we check which blocks are at destination and only migrate the missing ones.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-09-11T14:10:59Z)

hmm... we already have such code ! Only look for parent blocks for files which are not in PHYS03
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/4090bc52d466408f02a972270987cc3165762e7b/src/python/Publisher/PublisherDbsUtils.py#L129-L136

Is it possible that we have some files which are not in PHYS03, yet the block was (incompletely) migrated ? Current code does not check for this and will insert a new migration request.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-09-11T14:54:47Z)

Indeed that's exactly what happened
```console
belforte@lxplus813/~> dasgoclient --query 'file block=/BToPhi_MPhi-0p7_ctau-10mm_TuneCP5_13p6TeV_pythia8/Run3Summer22DRPremix-124X_mcRun3_2022_realistic_v12-v2/AODSIM#95a97811-3258-44aa-a400-1fd406bf5d7b instance=prod/global'
/store/mc/Run3Summer22DRPremix/BToPhi_MPhi-0p7_ctau-10mm_TuneCP5_13p6TeV_pythia8/AODSIM/124X_mcRun3_2022_realistic_v12-v2/70000/aa1bb70c-6b2e-4202-97b1-c84eb77ebb97.root
belforte@lxplus813/~> dasgoclient --query 'file block=/BToPhi_MPhi-0p7_ctau-10mm_TuneCP5_13p6TeV_pythia8/Run3Summer22DRPremix-124X_mcRun3_2022_realistic_v12-v2/AODSIM#95a97811-3258-44aa-a400-1fd406bf5d7b instance=prod/phys03'
belforte@lxplus813/~>
```

The problem is that inserting a block is expected to be an atomic operation iN DBS. IIUC DBS has no way to add files to an existing block.
So the partially migrated block will fail forever.

There is nothing that I can do from CRAB side.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9188: Shift to ArgoCD + Helm PRs, update crabserver chart, hands pointers.
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9188: Shift to ArgoCD + Helm PRs, update crabserver chart, hands pointers. State: closed Opened: 2025-09-17T17:00:20Z Closed: 2026-06-02T13:36:53Z Labels: Area: zK8s, Area: CI/CD URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9188 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-09-17T17:00:20Z) There's **2 PRs** here for **2 different concerns**, would like you guys @belforte @aspiringmind-code to review. - [x] First PR: [Refactored CRABServer helm chart for Argo CD monorepo-style and CI/CD](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/1661) [1] - [x] Second PR: `Do-not-merge`, example of pointer manifests, [crab-argocd-application-pointers-for-testx-preprod](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/compare/master...nausikt:CMSKubernetes:crab-argocd-application-pointers-for-testx-preprod) [2] ### Concern #1, Update CRABServer Chart 1. Re-organized, clean-up cross-cutting components (e.g. ingress, filebeat, logstash, ... etc) to eliminated risks of conflicts between apps & platform pointers. 2. Better how we handle deltas as `values-`, their corresponding `default values` and also reduced obscured if-else-conditional such that overall our chart are more intuitive, required less devOperators's cognitive load to comprehend in future, and clearer layering / deltas. ** There's too many *never* been used `values` that Wa's kindly try to accommodated devOps, clusterAdmin but with current direction its better been deprecated, keep it tidy, ** debugging things can moved to our own forked, workbench (crab-k8s-overlays). ** cluster-admin, log-pipeline should be deprecated (e.g. better provisioning from centralized to avoids pointers conflicts, from both resources, ownership perspectives) 3. Support directly customize config.py via chart values, such that it easy for us to test configMap while we developing (we can edited `config.py` in `crab-k8s-overlays` repo right away). This PR are quite straightforward and can be safely merged, since it got tested e2e via CI/CD pipeline, everything wired together and work well. ### Concern #2, Hands CRAB specific pointers to CMSWeb ***Rationales:*** We need to pointed to our dedicated hot values repo, `crab-k8s-overlays`. because we don't want our CI/CD, bots, or us to bug/flooding upstream repo with commits/PRs. (Other team like WMCore, pointed to Dario's forked, P&R also have private gitlab repo overall approach almost identical to us for their `unified` and they use mixtures of kustomize + helm, helm chart also lies in their private gitlab repo, neatly done by Hassan Ahmed) ** Our approach will always treat `dmwm/CMSKubernetes` as our **Single source of Truth** for manifest templating via helm chart, where any changes need PRs. Hot values changes will not bugging as PRs/commits at all, and totally be our control in `crab-k8s-overlays`. CMSWeb expert will be requested by us to do at least 2 things. 1. Let `CMSWeb`'s argocd recognize our private gitlab repo, `crab-k8s-overlays` with `GITLAB_PROJECT_ACCESS_TOKEN`, name `cmsweb-argocd-crab-pointers` with `read_repository`, expired on `Sep 17, 2026`. that could retrieved [here](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays/-/settings/access_tokens?page=1) ``` argocd repo add https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays.git \ --username oauth2 \ --password $GITLAB_PROJECT_ACCESS_TOKEN ``` 2. Apply CRAB's [applicationset](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/compare/master...sinonkt:CMSKubernetes:crab-argocd-application-pointers-for-testx-preprod#diff-72f3e49ff5866630e60d3098873191ea1b1d1dbaebcbe90b6f2831fe2f942b9f). such that `testX`, `preprod` start deployed via `https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays.git`, and CI/CD starting working there too. This step easiest to be done via `kubectl` below. ``` kubectl apply -n argocd -f argo/apps/crab/applicationset ``` BUT, some details need to be checked from CMSWEB side like do CMSWEB allowed us to do this on `preprod`? otherwise it should be commented out, also in this manifest have `project-crab` assigned to this manifest, kind of safety lock, pointer isolation that could be modified to fit `CMSWeb` context, practices. ```yaml apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1 kind: ApplicationSet metadata: name: crab-svcs namespace: argocd spec: generators: - list: elements: # ---------- test2 cluster ---------- - { svc: crabserver, env: test, cluster: test2 } # ---------- test12 cluster ---------- - { svc: crabserver, env: test, cluster: test12 } # ---------- test14 cluster ---------- - { svc: crabserver, env: test, cluster: test14 } # ---------- preprod cluster ---------- - { svc: crabserver, env: preprod, cluster: preprod } template: metadata: name: '{{svc}}-{{cluster}}' # e.g., crabserver-test2 labels: team: crab env: '{{env}}' spec: project: project-crab sources: - repoURL: https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays.git targetRevision: master path: vendor/helm/crabserver helm: valueFiles: - values.yaml - values-{{env}}.yaml - $hot/helm/crabserver/values-{{cluster}}.yaml - repoURL: https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays.git targetRevision: master ref: hot destination: name: cmsweb-{{cluster}} namespace: crab syncPolicy: automated: { prune: false, selfHeal: true } syncOptions: [ CreateNamespace=true ] ``` ### Optional stuffs, better not pursuit now [1] apply project, and parents pointer (app-of-apps, pointer-of-pointers) for crab namespace. so it automatically keep tracking of CRAB's `applicationset` above. ** that could be put to upstream repo for more transparency, tracking, version-control, easier to rollbacking/reverting... ``` kubectl apply -n argocd -f argo/projects/project-crab.yaml # <---- resources isolation and safety lock. kubectl apply -n argocd -f argo/apps/ns-crab.yaml # <---- pointer-of-pointers ``` [2] If `CRABServer` helm chart was serving on `helm chart registry` OR CMSWeb Multi-Tenant ArgoCD've been upgraded to `latest` version ArgoCD ApplicationSet Controller. We can define our pointers with more effective `applicationset` schema and thus we no longer have to relied on `vendir` synchronization, this could be discussed in some of our meeting later. but at the moment, just 2 mandatory requested are sufficient. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-27T15:27:18Z) @belforte, let me write final groks details down here. I've tested finalized Grok patterns on `prod` logs [1,2], they work well and will be as following. - [x] we will no longer extract pod_name from log file path for these 2 log types. - [x] preserved future-proof optional ephemeral ports (mostly occurs in dev/test env.) - [x] add ` - Podname=%{DATA:pod_name} Type=%{WORD:log_type}$` for both log types for pod_name availability. - [x] rename attr from `total` -> `proc` to better represent its value. ### Grok #1, main `crabhttpcall` (basic http, metrics) lines. >>
>> CRAB uses PostJobPrio1 and PostJobPrio2. It has been there since ever
>> and I can't say off the top of my head what it does for us and why is there.
>> Which makes me thing that nothing will break if it is taken away.
>> I will did a bit.
>>
>> Stefano
>>
>>
>> On 19/09/2025 12:20, Marco Mascheroni wrote:
>>> Thanks a lot Jamie! Tier0 jobs all belong to the same user and Tier0 has its own accounting group. so I think we have what we need with USE_GLOBAL_JOB_PRIOS=True
>>>
>>> >  CMS uses PostJobPrio1 and PostJobPrio2. I’m unaware of anyone else who uses the Pre or Post attributes. If we wanted to remove the Pre and Post attributes, would it be feasible for CMS to adjust to using just JobPrio?
>>>
>>> I think this is a question for the WMCore team:
>>>
>>> https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/904ab737b46f4f0bbfcf3de48bfa4b21b8c4d612/src/python/WMCore/BossAir/Plugins/SimpleCondorPlugin.py#L650-L651
>>>
>>> Alan, how much is the PostJobPrio used?
>>>
>>> Jamie, can the JobPrio be an expression? Or better, has anybody ever used an expression for the JobPrio?
>>>
>>> From: Jaime Frey [<<email>>](mailto:<email>)
>>> Sent: Thursday, September 18, 2025 17:40
>>> To: Florian Von Cube [<<email>>](mailto:<email>)
>>> Cc: Marco Mascheroni [<<email>>](mailto:<email>); Antonio Linares Sancho [<<email>>](mailto:<email>); Jan Eysermans [<<email>>](mailto:<email>); CMS Submission Infrastructure [<<email>>](mailto:<email>)
>>> Subject: Re: Question about job priority and schedd ordering in HTCondor
>>>
>>> I can fill in some details that the summary linked below leaves out.
>>> First, there are two types of priority. One is user priority, which influences how the pool’s slots are divided between multiple submitters. A smaller numerical value is better. This value is maintained by the negotiator and you can see it with condor_userprio. The other is job priority, which influences which jobs are matched first for a given submitter. A larger numerical value is better. This value is in the job ClassAd in the schedd and the user can set it however they want in the submit file or with condor_prio.
>>>
>>> Second, if you’re using accounting groups with hierarchical group quotas, then submitters in accounting groups are considered first, with the submitters who are furtherest below their quota going first. Within an accounting group and among submitters not in an accounting group, the submitter with the best user priority is considered first by the negotiator.
>>>
>>> When a submitter has jobs on multiple schedds, the negotiator will talk with one schedd at a time in an undefined order. Each schedd will send idle jobs (actually resource requests clumped by autocluster) to the negotiator in job priority order.
>>>
>>> If you set USE_GLOBAL_JOB_PRIOS=True for your negotiator (which the CMS global pool does), that changes how the negotiator talks to the schedds for a given submitter. The negotiator will first talk to the schedd that has the job with the best job priority for that submitter and ask for more jobs to match until another schedd has the job with the best job priority (which hasn’t been considered yet in the current cycle). The negotiator then talks to that schedd. This switching back and forth between multiple schedds adds overhead to the negotiation cycle, so it’s disabled by default.
>>>
>>> And one final note and question about job priority. A job’s job priority is actually 5-value tuple, given by the attributes PreJobPrio1, PreJobPrio2, JobPrio, PostJobPrio1, and PostJobPrio2. The Pre and Post attributes are almost completely undocumented. CMS uses PostJobPrio1 and PostJobPrio2. I’m unaware of anyone else who uses the Pre or Post attributes. If we wanted to remove the Pre and Post attributes, would it be feasible for CMS to adjust to using just JobPrio?
>>>
>>>  - Jaime
>>>
>>> > On Sep 18, 2025, at 5:20 AM, Florian Von Cube [<<email>>](mailto:<email>) wrote:
>>> >
>>> > Hi all, just to add:
>>> >
>>> > I think the description of the negotiation cycle is now found here:
>>> >[ https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/cm-configuration.html*the-negotiation-cycle__;Iw!!Mak6IKo!L7b6XmRPZcQW1gdsNa1vs9xHWXlmnwMxNvqVRaxrbGpUxBYGdnnMQAPWNlVJaivtbMJFWMUXI5HXWLeeEDJgT3XJYgLlLA$](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/cm-configuration.html*the-negotiation-cycle__;Iw!!Mak6IKo!L7b6XmRPZcQW1gdsNa1vs9xHWXlmnwMxNvqVRaxrbGpUxBYGdnnMQAPWNlVJaivtbMJFWMUXI5HXWLeeEDJgT3XJYgLlLA$)
>>> >
>>> > It states “Fetch an idle job from a condor_schedd holding jobs from that submitter.”, but doesn’t specify how exactly the schedd and job is chosen.
>>> >
>>> > Cheers,
>>> >  Florian
>>> >
>>> >> On 18 Sep 2025, at 10:27, Marco Mascheroni [<<email>>](mailto:<email>) wrote:
>>> >>
>>> >> Hi Jamie,
>>> >> There has been some concern about the following sentence in the 23.0 HTCondor manual:
>>> >> “With jobs from a single condor_schedd daemon, jobs are typically returned in job priority order. When more than one condor_schedd daemon is involved, they are contacted in an undefined order. All jobs from a single condor_schedd daemon are considered before moving on to the next.”
>>> >> I didn’t find the same text in the "latest" manual:
>>> >>[ https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/23.0/admin-manual/user-priorities-negotiation.html*negotiation__;Iw!!Mak6IKo!L7b6XmRPZcQW1gdsNa1vs9xHWXlmnwMxNvqVRaxrbGpUxBYGdnnMQAPWNlVJaivtbMJFWMUXI5HXWLeeEDJgT3WVzOvzXQ$](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/23.0/admin-manual/user-priorities-negotiation.html*negotiation__;Iw!!Mak6IKo!L7b6XmRPZcQW1gdsNa1vs9xHWXlmnwMxNvqVRaxrbGpUxBYGdnnMQAPWNlVJaivtbMJFWMUXI5HXWLeeEDJgT3WVzOvzXQ$)
>>> >> Could you clarify whether the concept of priority is "global" in HTCondor? I’m wondering:
>>> >>    • Are slots/claims handed out in priority order across schedds during a negotiation cycle?
>>> >>    • Or does the negotiator loop scheduler by scheduler?
>>> >> My understanding is that only once claims (slots) are handed over to schedulers, priority becomes "local." But since we setCLAIM_WORKLIFE = 1200, that shouldn’t have a big effect.
>>> >> From the logs it seems that (1) is true, but from the documentation it seems (2) is true. Could you clarify?
>>> >> Thanks,
>>> >> Marco
>>> >
>>> >
>>>

>

>> Hi Stefano,
>>
>> What makes you think this is not important?
>>
>> - Running a few jobs from each task as early as possible was seen as a helpful way to alert users early of broken tasks.
>> - Prioritizing job retries over first job tries of other tasks was seen as important for reducing the “tail” of the workload.
>>
>> Certainly these were seen as important at the time.  Are they no longer relevant?
>>
>> Brian

*

On 19/09/2025 17:19, Stefano Belforte wrote:
>
> Yes,
> that's why I think we can do w/o this. Since we never really had it, nor
> desperately need it.
>
> Stefano, with love, of course
>
> On 19/09/2025 17:02, Jaime Frey wrote:
>> A few observations on the “blame target” code:
>>
>> * For jobs with the same set of job priority values, the schedd sorts lower job ids first. This is equivalent to the QDate used for PostJobPrio1.
>>
>> * By using QDate for PostJobPrio1 and crab_retry for PostJobPrio2, retry jobs take priority only over jobs submitted at the exact same time (and with the same JobPrio). The retry jobs will not be prioritized over first-try jobs that were submitted earlier, and the QDate (or the schedd’s sort by job id if you removed PostJobPrio1 and PostJobPrio2) will prioritize the retry jobs over jobs submitted later.
>>
>> * By setting PreJobPrio1 for the first few jobs in a task, those jobs will be ordered before all jobs of any priority (aside from other jobs that also set PreJobPrio1). That’s different from the intention expressed in the comment for the code.
>>
>>  - Jaime

From the [documentation](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTCache.py#L30-L54) the desired URL should have `subresource=retrieve`, not `subresource=download`. Okk since problem are well defined now, i can take care the REST! ## Comment (belforte, 2025-10-07T16:41:45Z) `tm_cache_url` stored in DB's `tasks` table still has `S3` in it ``` tm_cache_url S3/crabcache_dev ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2025-10-07T16:43:08Z) but I fear that with such value this line will go nuts https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/script/task_info.js#L298 ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-07T17:00:40Z) > but I fear that with such value this line will go nuts > > [CRABServer/src/script/task_info.js](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/script/task_info.js#L298) > > Line 298 in [c45cf9b](/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd) > > url=cacheUrl.split("S3")[0] + "crabserver/" + dbVersion + "/cache?subresource=download&objecttype=twlog&taskname="+inputTaskName; Man, could it be because cacheUrl back then looks like these? ``` https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_dev http://s3.cern.ch/crabcache_dev https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod https://cmsweb-auth.cern.ch:8443/crabcache https://cmsweb.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_dev https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod https://cmsweb.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod ``` Such that changes https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py#L533-L534 into something like these should solved the issue? ```python cacheurl = f"{self.restHost}/S3/{self.config.s3_bucket}" ``` P.S. I think we might not need to touch js. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-07T17:31:07Z) > > but I fear that with such value this line will go nuts > > [CRABServer/src/script/task_info.js](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/script/task_info.js#L298) > > Line 298 in [c45cf9b](/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd) > > url=cacheUrl.split("S3")[0] + "crabserver/" + dbVersion + "/cache?subresource=download&objecttype=twlog&taskname="+inputTaskName; > > Man, could it be because cacheUrl back then looks like these? > > ``` > https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_dev > http://s3.cern.ch/crabcache_dev > https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod > https://cmsweb-auth.cern.ch:8443/crabcache > https://cmsweb.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod > https://cmsweb-test2.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_dev > https://cmsweb-testbed.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod > https://cmsweb.cern.ch/S3/crabcache_prod > ``` > > Such that changes > > [CRABServer/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py#L533-L534) > > Lines 533 to 534 in [c45cf9b](/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/c45cf9bd796bde455d6288a88a1c28d5c46f16cd) > > > cacheurl = f"S3/{self.config.s3_bucket}" # record S3 bucket in task table > into something like these should solved the issue? > > cacheurl = f"{self.restHost}/S3/{self.config.s3_bucket}" > P.S. I think we might not need to touch js. Forgive me, removing the baseURL actually was originally your goal. I found that utilize `window.location.origin` this way might solved issue, by letting UI pick up their own baseURL on client side in browser. ```javascript const url = new URL(`/crabserver/${dbVersion}/cache`, window.location.origin); url.search = new URLSearchParams({ subresource: 'download', objecttype: 'twlog', taskname: inputTaskName, }).toString(); console.log(url.toString()); // e.g. https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/v1/cache?subresource=download&objecttype=twlog&taskname=... ``` OR ```javascript url= window.location.origin + "/crabserver/" + dbVersion + "/cache?subresource=download&objecttype=clientlog&taskname="+inputTaskName; ``` ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-07T18:38:16Z) ### In Summary. the extra uri came from when we call ajax with pre-mature url cause by `cacheUrl.split("S3")[0]` was empty string, As a result, our ajax call ended up like. ## Opening post (belforte, 2025-10-09T11:30:09Z)

we have evidence that many user specify the maximul allowed (5GB) even if their jobs only use 1~2 GB or RAM.
Usual problem of "sticking, copied/pasted configuration".

US people pointed out that in there alone this leads to as many idle cores as a a full T2 !!!

We converged on the following approach:
 1) Reduce Max for 1 core from 5 to 3 GB in initial submission
 2) Allow user to ask more (up to 5) in crab resubmit
 3) Possibly, at a later time,  make 2) automatic

No changes for multicore.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9208: High-Mem CRAB Jobs monitoring and dashboard to demystifies the situation.

State: closed
Opened: 2025-10-10T10:30:06Z
Closed: 2026-08-24T15:47:03Z
Labels: Priority: High, Area: MONIT, Area: HTCondor, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9208

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-10-10T10:30:06Z)

Here is what i've digested from experts's discussions.

There are 2 category of questions/purposes for these dashboard and monitoring to addressed.
1. **Reassuring/Confirming** of this widespread phenomenon, make CRAB fact-based transparent in this phenomenon. [1]
2. **Improved/Easing High-Mem job tracing routine monitoring**, for tracking down **abuse** case. [2]

______
### [1] Bird-Eye views for this specific widespread phenomenon.
**Objectives**:
1. make phenomenon transparent.
2. At least, we should been able to confirm the before/after effects of our following actions by ourself,
 1) Reduce Max for 1 core from 5 to 3 GB in initial submission.
 2) Allow user to ask more (up to 5) in crab resubmit.

these dashboards should be able to shown **back then** cores-mem utilization, thus could be use as one of *quick* post-analysis tools, for any enforcements/policies we just introduced or upcomming in the future.

Serving as one-bottomline metrics and dashboards for us (also future operators) as a summary of this whole phenomenon, such that we can just have a glance and can tell whether everything is O.K. or need to dive deeper in [2]
_____
### [2] Easy to trace, `abuse` use-cases
**Objectives**:
1. As name implied.
2. reduce tracing time from abuse-to-user, so operators can warn user.
3. has potential to gathering facts fast for identifying novel `abuse` use-cases.

this collection of dashboard, quite close to what SI have as Marco & Antonio Perez's shown or what Open Search could offers that CRAB already have as you plotted. but we will port it to grafana and emphasized/highlights on
1. mem-per-core utilization of both avg. and max mem usages
2. "ask for more cores for more memory but actually never used" abuse.
3. ambient copy-paste config low-utilization jobs.
_______
TLDR; We will have 1 set of Big-picture dashboards and 1 set of Finer-grained dashboards, both will serve different purposes.

Please, @belforte guides me on how to do these things properly and really addressed the problem we all faced, forgive me for any missing crucial details, please kindly pointed me out.

P.S. Apologize for the delayed. Yesterday, is not going well from my side. 😷

I am not sure that we need to do anything in this area

@aspiringmind-code
That solution does not work, see e.g. https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/jobs/70352581

And by the way none of the ST checks in the pipeline pointed to in the PR #9268 completed successfully.  Seems that task submission failed. We clearly need to revisit the way we declare the pipeline to be OK.

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-10-15T15:32:11Z)

as discussed in today's CRAB [meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1601406/?note=352640) we want to have an "emergency" switch so that we can allow to go over the new 3GB max memory limit for single core jobs in case a user has a need.

Plan is to update TW config locally in TaskWorker so that the new limit is in effect until we restart TW again (puppet will reset to the default).

We do not see the need to have this as a hiera variable in puppet which would allow a persistent change on a per-TW base controlled via a Gitllab commit. But of course that can be done later if such a need arise. Chances are that we never need this !!

Of course could do via editing `/data/srv/current/lib/python/site-packages/ServerUtilities.py` and `start.sh -c`, but using the config. makes it a bit more clear and easy to do better in the future. It becomes like the canary fraction.

P.S. Now, i start to appreciated `kustomize` features even more, that they try to suffixing the configmap name/ and their corresponding deployment mounting config (suffix with content hash), which will automatically triggered rollout restart every time content changed. [1] filebeat.yml config inside mounted in pod, wasn't refreshed for all this time though. ```bash filebeat@filebeat-crab-27jgb:~$ cat /etc/filebeat.yml filebeat.inputs: - type: container paths: - /var/log/pods/crab_crabserver*/crabserver/*.log include_lines: - '\] crabserver-\w+-\w+ \d' tags: - "crabhttpcall" - type: container paths: - /var/log/pods/crab_crabserver*/crabserver/*.log include_lines: - 'MeasureTime:seconds - ' - 'MeasureSize:bytes - ' tags: - "crabrest" output.logstash: hosts: ["logstash:5044"] compression_level: 3 bulk_max_size: 4096 queue.mem: events: 65536 logging.metrics.enabled: false logging.level: infofilebeat@filebeat-crab-27jgb:~$ ``` [2] Logstash start to pick up canary logs from filebeat thus Timber is starting to show canary response status by pod now. Or you can have a look at Grafana [CRAB crabserver timber](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/VML5DJEnk/crab-crabserver-timber?orgId=11&refresh=1m&from=now-12h&to=now&viewPanel=42). ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-27T13:16:32Z) > if this is not straightforward, what about finalizing grok pattern around current setup and complete transition to arguscd. Then come back to the missing pods mistery ? Ack Stefano, will get it done now. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-10-27T13:22:58Z) do I read it correctly that arguscd would have fixed this as well ? ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-27T13:34:22Z) > do I read it correctly that arguscd would have fixed this as well ? In Short: **No**, having to implement a bit. ArgoCD alone, in case of configmap content changed. will **not** automatically trigger rollout restart on relevant deployment/daemonset. We have to implement this features in `Helm` templating [1] ourself, thus deployment or daemonset aware of content changes somehow. OR in case of `Kustomize`'s configMapGenerator, it will take care of suffixing the configmap name as another way to versioning it thus automatically rollout restart for us by default. [1] Exp, trivial implementation on Helm chart. ```yaml spec: template: metadata: annotations: configHash: "{{ .Values.configMap | toYaml | sha256sum }}" ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2025-10-27T13:48:52Z) 😮 do I have to fear that same "config change does not trigger restart" applies to e.g. changes to CRAB's config.py or CRABServerAuth.py ? Sorry for being so confused here, I do not really understand what configmap refers to. Anyhow your [1] looks very good. Thanks !!! ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-27T13:53:35Z) We have to fear man... it does applied to all configmaps in general. but don't worry we will patch this feature covered all configmaps in upstream PR, helm chart update, as well.

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-10-20T14:24:00Z)

DagmanCreator uses LDAP to get content of e-group `highPrioUsers` in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bad7564a9705d2da18d31e21353f6a1482bd417c/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L1190-L1196

In that we allow for a list of high-prio e-groups to be passed in TW config file, but since years we only use
e-group `cms-crab-HighPrioUsers`

Info for that can be pulled from CRIC with an HTTP call https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/group/query/?json
(maybe there's a way to retrieve only that group ?)

ALso, CRIC group can be populated from a list of e-groups, so we do not loose generality by sticking with CRIC group `CMS_CRAB_HighPrioUsers`

That will allow deprecating
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9812df1e758317ea53af08d8e64a5d8cfd787d52/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py#L20

      "cms-crab-HighPrioUsers"
    ],
    "last_modified": "2024-02-02T13:07:45.328702",
    "name": "CMS_CRAB_HighPrioUsers",
    "role": "high-priority-users",
    "tag_name": "crab3",
    "tag_relation": "group",
    "users": []

}belforte@lxplus802/~>
```

Need to call this from python to parse the JSON. [WMCore CRIC](https://github.com/khurtado/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/WMCore/Services/CRIC/CRIC.py) class which we use does not have the group API and IIUC always insert a `&preset=" argument in the URL which the group API does not support.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-28T16:44:04Z)

Now that we have `requests` python package via PIP in our container, a simple implementation would be
```python

url="https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/group/query/?json&name=CMS_CRAB_HighPrioUsers"
cert='/data/certs/robotcert.pem'
key='/data/certs/robotkey.pem'

after which
```

```
