```
>>> urlA="https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/group/query/?json&name=CMS_CRAB3_Admin"
>>> r=requests.get(urlA,cert=(cert,key),verify=False)
/usr/local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py:1043: InsecureRequestWarning: Unverified HTTPS request is being made to host 'cms-cric.cern.ch'. Adding certificate verification is strongly advised. See: https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/1.26.x/advanced-usage.html#ssl-warnings
  warnings.warn(
>>> for u in r.json()['CMS_CRAB3_Admin','users']: print(u['login'])
...
belforte
>>>
```

But I will also explore using `CRABServer/src/pyhton/RESTInteractions.py` in case it offers caching.

oh rats !!!

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/bad7564a9705d2da18d31e21353f6a1482bd417c/src/python/RESTInteractions.py#L158-L159
but while
https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/group/query/?json works,
https://cms-cric.cern.ch/api/accounts/group/query%3Fjson returns `code=404, reason=Not Found`

So it works fine with CRABServer, but can't be used here.
(commenting out that line makes things work, but I am not sure if some CRABServer call would break, maybe it was put there for a reason... the #2557 quoted in the comment does not correspond to anything in this GH repo)

I could look at using full blown WMCore/Service/Service which amounts to a small rewriting of WMCore's CRIC class

Maybe I better stick with the simple `requests` and write a small caching on file myself.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9225: Implement configHash to automatically trigger rollouts of relevant deployments via ArgoCD + Helm
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9225: Implement configHash to automatically trigger rollouts of relevant deployments via ArgoCD + Helm State: closed Opened: 2025-10-27T16:09:28Z Closed: 2025-10-28T15:30:57Z Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Medium, Area: zK8s, Area: CI/CD, Area: zDesired Feature URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9225 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-10-27T16:09:28Z) From time to time, We occasionally end up in a situation where the ConfigMap has already been updated, but the deployment has not been explicitly rolled out yet. P.S. And sometimes its might took so long to realize these, like in my case #9221. P.S. thus, why one of `Kustomize`'s killing feature, is to automatically update/trigger roll out via suffixing the configmap name, as default feature. Since, we go with ArgoCD + Helm, we better make this process automated as well, aware of ConfigMap content changes, via helm templating for each components in our CRABServer helm Chart. P.S. Should we better included this update into Final Helm Chart update PR now? [dmwm/CMSKubernetes#PR1661](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/1661), or later as seperated PR. P.S. Continuation of updated Finalized Groks, https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9188#issuecomment-3451888006 ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-10-28T15:30:57Z) I've implemented https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/pull/1661/commits/ec3d59aebd02deea9acde57f7140ad4cea4b1caf, tested and deployed on `preprod` for `crabserver` and `filebeat`. Now, we have podAnnotations.`configHash` for each corresponding deployment/daemonset, that will be aware of content changes for us. as you can see in the following example [1] This way, new DevOperator just have to change the config content -> ArgoCD + helm will patched configHash -> rollouts restart for us. P.S. k8s is sensitive to any changes inside pod `template` thus this minimal implementations are sufficient for automatic triggering rollouts restart. P.S. IMO, we don't have to overdo by suffixing the configMap name, where hotswap configmap and audit traceability are necessity/concern or have higher priority than simplicity. current implmentation are much clearer to me to see config diffs. ***Other Important Notes***: 1. I'ven't implmented this feature for `Logstash`, `crab-secrets` yet (e.g. CRABServerAuth.py) Since, we're on an on-going process of moving toward ***global*** logstash, So, we have to keep in mind that `logstash` will need manual rolling-out restart for now. 2. In case of crab-secrets, since its `*.sops` not included in upstream helm chart. So, ArgoCD + Helm can't hashing it during rendering time, can't patched configHash for any changes happens in `services_config`. So, another occasion to remind ourself for manually rollout. [1]

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9230: stop using `import htcondor` or `import classad` in "puppet"
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9230: stop using `import htcondor` or `import classad` in "puppet" State: closed Opened: 2025-11-14T19:37:13Z Closed: 2025-11-18T20:11:00Z Labels: Priority: TOP, OPERATION URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9230 ## Opening post (belforte, 2025-11-14T19:37:13Z) From HTC v25. onward only v2 API's are distributed. The only supported way is: ```python import htcondor2 as htcondor import classad2 as classad ``` We have done this already for the code in this repository, but need to change a few files which are installed on AP's via puppet and used in crontabs (some may even be old unused relics...) So to avoid errors like the following one after we migrated vocms056 to HTC 25.0.3 The list of files to change can be obtained e.g. like this ```console LapSB:it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein$ rg "import htcondor" code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb 136:## in every file to decide if to do "import htcondor" or "import htcondor2 as htcondor" code/files/crabschedd/htcondor_ads.py 3:import htcondor code/files/crabschedd/JobCleanup.py 25:import htcondor code/files/crabschedd/check_maxdags.py 4:import htcondor code/files/crabschedd/glexec_errors.py 4:import htcondor code/files/crabschedd/jobhistoryfeeder.py 3:import htcondor LapSB:it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein$ rg "import classad" code/files/crabschedd/JobCleanup.py 26:import classad code/files/crabschedd/jobhistoryfeeder.py 2:import classad LapSB:it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein$ ``` ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:11:00Z) Apologize for missing this issue notification, also extra delay today... Actually, this should be done in few minutes... I've merged into `qa` as you can see [here](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/379), From now on there should be no surge of JobCleanUp failures emails coming to us, Thank you for your patience! ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:11:32Z) Let me know if you need to promote this to `prod` any time. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T20:16:52Z) yes, you should promote to prod, no reason not to. We are using V2 API everywhere ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:18:05Z) Roger that Boss get it done now. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T20:22:18Z) the problem was not the mails, was that the crontabs are not running so we would miss much needed disk cleanup when we move schedulers to HTC 25. If you are not sure why we do things, ask. Sometimes I have bad ideas, I need critical review. And if I am right, still you need to learn how things work and mostly how to take ownership of things, even things which you understand only partially. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:29:06Z) Thanks man for emphasizing, Forgive me for my poor considered responses. So the critical things is disk SPOOL_DIR doesn't get clean-up as usual on every APs cause by centrally promoted HTC to v25 by SI team. and this enforcement fix things back to normal, including no alerts emails. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:33:38Z) So disk rising to more than 80% in some APs, are also part of this clean-up failures + surge of submissions workloads during this and last week, who accelerated the violation? ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T20:35:50Z) It is not SI which forces us to update HTCondor. It is the plain fact that we want to use the currently supported version with the best bug fixes and improvements. Also v25 has needed fixes for WMA so that they can use v2 API as well and it is good to run all schedd's with same version. Disk usage rising above 80% is not due to lack of cleaning, is a worrying thing in itself. We usually live around 60% usage, which is OK. But do not have good handles to keep it under control. ## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T20:37:25Z) Thanks for clarity man. it's transparent now. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T20:39:05Z) I do not know where exactly all that disk usage come from. title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9235: local group not added anymore to My.CMSGroups ?
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9235: local group not added anymore to My.CMSGroups ? State: closed Opened: 2025-11-19T13:14:26Z Closed: 2026-04-30T14:51:49Z Labels: Status: In Progress, Area: Code Cleanup, OPERATION URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9235 ## Opening post (belforte, 2025-11-19T13:14:26Z) There at least one case where the user membership in local groups is not added to `CMSGroups` classAd See https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/issue-with-processing-private-mc-samples-using-crab/138451/4 pasting here most relevant text ```text matching doesnt work because of stringListsIntersect(CMSGroups,“T3_US_FNALLPC”)` The user is among the local users at LPC: [mmascher@vocms0106 ~]$ grep jingyu /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/T3_US_FNALLPC/GlideinConfig/local-users.txt jingyu ``` As @mmascher pointed out, CRAB should be setting the group information here? https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/b84f876e8c0acc51c27318f846a668c25b03e0a2/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L405-L408 ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-19T14:00:13Z) as simple as "/cvmfs" is not mounted inside the container. ``` crab3@crab-prod-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ ls -ld /cvmfs drwxr-xr-x. 2 root root 0 Aug 21 15:43 /cvmfs crab3@crab-prod-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ ls -ld /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/ ls: cannot access '/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/': No such file or directory crab3@crab-prod-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-19T17:03:16Z) It turned out to be the old problem that at times the mount of CVMFS inside the container goes belly up. I fixed it by restarting the container (`docker stop; docker start`) on prod and canary TW. The more drastic procedure described in https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-components/crab-taskworker/how-to.html#cvmfs-failed-to-mount to address the case when CVMFS fails at "VM-level" was not necessary. We can do a few things, not necessarily one excluding the other: 1. find a way to set an alert/alarm so that we do not run long time with this 2. ask CVMFS support if there is more robust solution than fuse mount, like https ? (all in all CMVFS can be cached via squid) 3. bypass CVMFS, clone https://gitlab.cern.ch/SITECONF in the container and do a periodic `git pull` (e.g. when memory cache expires, see code in [CMSGroupMapper.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/0ac5f0097f4d11af2a97caadeb886bf9f6118ec6/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py#L51) 4. do 3. in the VM in /data disk, refresh via crontab and mount the local directory in the container 5. like 4. but instead of clone/fetch, do a straight `cp` from CVMFS 6. like 5. but only propagate changes * ` rsync -av /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF/ /data/container/SITECONF/` * inside the container that is available as `/data/hostdisk/SITECONF/` so we should modify the code https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3f5c584e274884c08139fb5662cb0d5f79e48e95/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py#L65 FYI @aspiringmind-code I defer to you on deciding how to proceed ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-19T17:04:25Z) keeping open until a follow-up strategy is defined and ad-hoc issue(s) opened. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-19T19:50:06Z) @aspiringmind-code about 1. the place where to catch the problem could be https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/0ac5f0097f4d11af2a97caadeb886bf9f6118ec6/src/python/CMSGroupMapper.py#L65-L73 where today `os.path.isdir(base_dir)` was simply returning `False`. No exception raised and no action taken. ## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-20T08:48:07Z) the clear symptom was that `ls` inside the container showed no directory so maybe a simple alert could be crontab in the TW which does something like `docker exec -ti TaskWorker ls /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF` and prints to stdout in case of error, generating a mail to operators e.g. ``` belforte@crab-dev-tw04/~> docker exec -ti TaskWorker ls /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF ls: cannot access '/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF': No such file or directory belforte@crab-dev-tw04/~> ``` even if the first time I executed it returned nothing, the second the error. ## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-20T15:30:59Z) In December @nausikt has added a crontab to alert if SITECONF access is lost inside the container (option 1.) https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/manifests/crabtaskworker/checksiteconf.pp?ref_type=heads we should decide if to stay with that, or to bypass mounting CVMFS mounting inside the container via option 5. ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-13T15:07:26Z) The problem has not occurred again since November, so I am not sure if it is worth pursuing. If we moved cmvfs reading into a local (disk or memory) caching we could simply put an error reporting in there and fall back to stale cache. Current code in `CMSGroupMapper.py` "looks like doing memory caching", but in reality it does not as described in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9270#issuecomment-3834561226 What I would not like to do is to raise a fatal exception inside every `crab submit` given that most submission do not care about having the local group added to the JDL. Maybe we should pursue the creation of a global caching object at TW startup time, pass it to all subprocesses, and in there take care of cache refreshing. We can certainly detect a too much stale cache there, the question is what to do. I would like to e.g. send a mail to operators, but am currently failing to do this inside the container. @aspiringmind-code @nausikt any suggestion ? Or is your preference for forgetting about this. Or maybe log the issue in twlog, catch in in logstash and raise an alert in Grafana ? That'd be sort of the "ideal" patch, but we do not have a well established procedure (i.e. instructions for dummies) so I am a bit scared of getting lost. The alternative is of course to setup crontab in the VM, so we do get mails, and avoid using cvmfs at all inside the container. ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-02-13T15:56:39Z) > The problem has not occurred again since November, so I am not sure if it is worth pursuing. If we moved cmvfs reading into a local (disk or memory) caching we could simply put an error reporting in there and fall back to stale cache. Current code in `CMSGroupMapper.py` "looks like doing memory caching", but in reality it does not as described in [#9270 (comment)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9270#issuecomment-3834561226) > I like the way we reading cvmfs into a local disk first then directly mounted it to the container, its does decoupling us from any unstable mounting issue. (not sure you means we gonna have crontab to periodically moved to local disk twice a day or something?) > > Maybe we should pursue the creation of a global caching object at TW startup time, pass it to all subprocesses, and in there take care of cache refreshing. We can certainly detect a too much stale cache there, the question is what to do. I would like to e.g. send a mail to operators, but am currently failing to do this inside the container. [@aspiringmind-code](https://github.com/aspiringmind-code) [@nausikt](https://github.com/nausikt) any suggestion ? Or is your preference for forgetting about this. > The global caching object is intriguing to me as a generic caching mechanism. Especially if we have many attrs worth caching that also shared across TW actions. But right now i saw just one `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/SITECONF` for CMSGroups resolving. (**CRIC calls seems to already have their own http caching mechanism wrapped.) So IMHO, if we find few more worthy attrs to cache... then i think its worth to let me pursue the ideal solution. *P.S. alternative also fine for me!* ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-13T16:35:20Z) thanks @nausikt . I'll be happy to work on the "extra config caching module" (as often, hardest part is to find a good name). If I only could solve the `mail` problem ! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-13T16:52:05Z) sending mail was solved thanks to [tip](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/7amnio8j9bykmq9pif6mszpmra) from @juanpablosalas and [example](https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.examples.html) in python doc here's the incantation ```text crab3@crab-dev-tw01:/data/srv/TaskManager$ python3 Python 3.8.16 (default, May 23 2023, 14:26:40) [GCC 10.2.1 20210110] on linux Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information. >>> from email.message import EmailMessage >>> msg = EmailMessage() >>> msg['Subject'] = "this is a test" >>> msg['to']="" >>> msg['from']="" >>> msg.set_content("do not reply. Ignore!") >>> print(msg) Subject: this is a test to: from: Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8" Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit MIME-Version: 1.0 do not reply. Ignore! >>> import smtplib >>> s = smtplib.SMTP(host='cernmx.cern.ch', port=25) >>> s.send_message(msg) {} >>> s.quit ``` and this is my Thunderbird window ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-13T17:42:30Z) > (**CRIC calls seems to already have their own http caching mechanism wrapped.) like for CMSGroupMapper.py, this does not work in our case because every TW action is called in its own subprocess, so objects do not persist in memory from one `crab submit` to the next. We need to put them explicitly among the `args` in the child intiialization https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7aca6b02074c205a4d44f68118d14734d8e8a28c/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L105-L106 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7aca6b02074c205a4d44f68118d14734d8e8a28c/src/python/TaskWorker/ChildWorker.py#L50-L51 ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-02-13T18:30:07Z) Stefano please allows me to clarify. IIUC, In case of CRIC calls, since we've derived from WMCore CRIC Service. I think its implicitly been ***file-based caching***. ## on CRAB Side Every calls goes through the derived **_getResult** function as you can see below. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7aca6b02074c205a4d44f68118d14734d8e8a28c/src/python/TaskWorker/WorkerUtilities.py#L16-L18 https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/7aca6b02074c205a4d44f68118d14734d8e8a28c/src/python/TaskWorker/WorkerUtilities.py#L131-L143 ## on WMCore Side Then Implicitly in [WMCore/Services/CRIC/CRIC.py](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/c11eef48bbd189affcd683aaf5a344ae475d17a4/src/python/WMCore/Services/CRIC/CRIC.py#L60-L71) which inherited [WMCore/Services/Service.py](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/master/src/python/WMCore/Services/Service.py) ```python def _getResult(self, uri, callname="", args=None, unflatJson=True): """ Either fetch data from the cache file or query the data-service :param metricNumber: a number corresponding to the SSB metric :return: a dictionary """ cachedApi = "%s.json" % callname apiUrl = '%s?json&preset=%s' % (uri, callname) self['logger'].debug('Fetching data from %s, with args %s', apiUrl, args) # need to make our own encoding, otherwise Requests class screws it up if args: apiUrl = "%s&%s" % (apiUrl, urlencode(args, doseq=True)) data = self.refreshCache(cachedApi, apiUrl) results = data.read() data.close() results = json.loads(results) if unflatJson: results = unflattenJSON(results) return results ``` It does check cache hit/expired, call/read/write cache file behind the scene through **refreshCache** function. as we can see below with default=1hr. ```python def refreshCache(self, cachefile, url='', inputdata=None, openfile=True, encoder=True, decoder=True, verb='GET', contentType=None, incoming_headers=None, binary=False): """ See if the cache has expired. If it has make a new request to the service for the input data. Return the cachefile as an open file object. If cachefile is None returns StringIO. :param cachefile: cache file name :param url: url value :param inputdata: HTTP (JSON) payload string :param openfile: flag to use open file, boolean :param encoder: flag to use encoder, boolean :param decoder: flag to use decode, boolean :param verb: HTTP method, string :param contentType: HTTP content type value, string :param incoming_headers: set of HTTP headers, dict :param binary: use binary mode to decode HTTP data, boolean :return: either file object or StringIO """ inputdata = inputdata or {} incoming_headers = incoming_headers or {} verb = self._verbCheck(verb) cachefile = self.cacheFileName(cachefile, verb, inputdata) if cache_expired(cachefile, self["cacheduration"]): self.getData(cachefile, url, inputdata, incoming_headers, encoder, decoder, verb, contentType, binary=binary) else: self['logger'].debug('Data is from the Service cache') # cachefile may be filename or file object if openfile and not isfile(cachefile): if binary: return open(cachefile, 'rb') return open(cachefile, 'r', encoding='utf-8') else: return cachefile ``` Thus, i believe its likely been cached across TW action's subprocesses. *P.S. I used to test individual TW Action with cache_duration=few seconds, and see how its works back then. its generated an intermediate cache file and been reused well, no http calls were requested.* ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-13T20:39:23Z) 🙇‍♂️ thanks @nausikt I humbly bow. I had written w/o checking. My bad. I apologize for having turned my brain off. Very good to have you here :-) ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-02-14T15:58:09Z) @belforte humbly bow🙇‍♂️ (Thanks) to you! for having me on your board! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-19T16:01:19Z) recap of what we agreed on (somehow each step is predicated on the one before) - [x] introduce a crontab in puppet which `rsync`'s `SITECONF` from `cvmfs` to `/data/container/TaskWorker/groups/SITECONF` (a directory) and get lilst of highpriority users from CRIC into `/data/container/TaskWorker/groups/highPriorityUsers.json` (a file) - [x] in `crabdev` env for developing/finalizing - [x] in `qa` for testing - [x] in `prod` - [x] change code to read from there. Reading from local disk during each submit handling is no problem, no need for memory caching, so we minimize changes. Current master already does not use `config.TaskWorker.highPrioEgroups = ['cms-crab-HighPrioUsers']` in TW config. - [x] code and test #9278 . Merged but not in [v3.260226](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/releases/tag/v3.260226) - [x] create new tag with it - v3.260330 - [x] deploy - in canary since April 7 - in production (v3.260415) since April 15 - [x] remove from puppet ```code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb 161:config.TaskWorker.highPrioEgroups = ['cms-crab-HighPrioUsers']``` - [x] remove from puppet current crontab ` class { 'hg_vocmsglidein::crabtaskworker::checksiteconf': }` - [x] in qa https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/merge_requests/445 - [x] in master - [x] stop mounting of CVMFS inside the container (change runContainer.sh) #9308 @aspiringmind-code @nausikt do you agree with this ? Did I miss something ? ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-02-19T21:07:25Z) I agree. For clarity, about CRIC in 1. you mean we gonna have another cron to periodically fetch `highPrioEgroups ` from CRIC as file? such that its more dynamic an up-to-date than previous method, propagating via puppet through TW config? ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-20T09:43:46Z) I am simply stating the fact that we will never use anything else than current high priority e-group for setting high priority in submissions. It has been like that since years. We never changed what's in `config.TaskWorker.highPrioEgroups = ['cms-crab-HighPrioUsers']` since it was first introduced 🤷 If really needed, it will be simple enough to change the crontab. ## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2026-02-20T10:03:17Z) > [@aspiringmind-code](https://github.com/aspiringmind-code) [@nausikt](https://github.com/nausikt) do you agree with this ? Did I miss something ? Agreed. Sounds good. Thanks! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-22T13:18:54Z) the new way is now implemented in production, all that is left is to cleanup obsolete crontab and remove obsolete mounting in runContainer.sh as per https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9235#issuecomment-3928199878 ## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-30T14:51:49Z) All actions defined in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9235#issuecomment-3928199878 have been completed now. title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9252: Migrate TW image to Alma9, maintain OS and Python version homogeneity with Schedd (AP's), support Py3.9 → Py3.12
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9252: Migrate TW image to Alma9, maintain OS and Python version homogeneity with Schedd (AP's), support Py3.9 → Py3.12

State: closed
Opened: 2025-12-19T11:53:57Z
Closed: 2026-03-03T15:47:50Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Priority: Medium, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9252

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-12-19T11:53:57Z)

As Stefano pointed out in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8956#issuecomment-3197455329,
> Given that
> * WMCore and CRAB code are "feature frozen" now
> * alma9 will have security fixes (and hence be usable as container base) until [2032](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/)
> * python 3.9 is and will always be the python version in Alma9 and Schedulers (AP's) already used them.
>
> move TW image to use Alma9 container as base, instead of python3.8 Debian one
>

Currently, our TW image basically derived from `wmagent-base` which in time of `wmfreeze` has **Debian 13 (Trixie)** underneath as First class base OS-support by WMCore team.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/620a01ce9db324f0815e5661b0b55693fd620bae/cicd/crabtaskworker_pypi/Dockerfile#L38-L40
*\*\*there is no alma9 build support by WMCore team yet in this `wmagent-base` layer, as we can see in [harbor/wmagent-base](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1771/repositories/wmagent-base/artifacts-tab)\*\**
*N.B. Debian Trixie shipped py3.13 as default, on the other hand Alma9, as a rebuild old RHEL, will officially support py3.9 up-to py3.12 in its default package repositories, further py3.13++ having to be installed from source manually. BUT py3.9 is just fine for our context now.*

_____
AFAICS, we have **3** options to adopt Alma9 in TW could be **Either**
- [1] Ask WMCore team for `wmagent-base`:`alma9-py3.9--YYMMDDDD` build.

**OR** try to derive from lower layer image ourself. **i.e.**
- [2] [dmwm-base](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/pypi/dmwm-base) (where `wmagent-base` derived from, See also [wmagent-base/Dockerfile](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2f52b8ef238cdace2555f15ae8ab74da277e56e3/docker/pypi/wmagent-base/Dockerfile#L1-L27))
5 months ago, Alma9 has been support in this layer via [alma9-based Dockerfile](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/tree/master/docker/pypi/dmwm-alma9-base).
we can see that [harbor/dmwm-base](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1771/repositories/dmwm-base/artifacts-tab) have `alma9-py3.12-20250728-stable` and `alma9-py3.9-20250703-stable` available for us.

**So**, if we work on top of this layer we can switch OS and `py3.9` -> `py3.12` (if AP's was promoted to py3.12 later in the future, we can aligned TW again here) fairly easily via just changing the tag, meanwhile we can have some dmwm's conventions + grounded work out of the box.

*Note: Be aware that we still need to install ***oracle client***, set paths, linking libs a little bit ourself , which used to be handled by `wmagent-base`, where oracle client was provided by Valentin's [cmsweb/oracle](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/docker/oracle/Dockerfile)  which been built in debian based env,
So, here i have **no confident** whether can we copying oracle artifacts across OS-env, and things will magically work out here or not.*
- [3] [cmsweb-alma9-base](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/docker/cmsweb-alma9-base) (See also [harbor/cmsweb-alma9-base](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1771/repositories/cmsweb-alma9-base/artifacts-tab), [Dockerfile](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/master/docker/cmsweb-alma9-base)]
where some CMSWEB required certs & packages was addressed. BUT this image have **NO** grounded work from `dmwm` team, so we have to re-established some civilisation ourself from almost scratch.
____

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9257: HTCondor v2, refreshGSIProxy proxy renewal fails in delegation mode.

State: closed

## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-01-14T19:23:43Z)

See also [[HTCondor-users] refreshGSIProxy stopped working](https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2026-January/msg00023.shtml), the original discussion between Stefano and Jaime Frey.

## Summary
The problem is we migrated AP's from 24.7 to 25.0.3, to [fix submission failures happened](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9245) in the old version after a reboot of the AP moved it to use more recent OpenSSL.

However, we didn't tested and unaware of ***renewRemoteProxies*** had been failing [1] for over a month during the Christmas break. (*Luckily, most of our users ran tasks that completed within 7-day proxy validity period.*)

[1] Our ***renewRemoteProxies*** encounters silent failures when call python binding fn, [*refreshGSIProxy*](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/0ac5f0097f4d11af2a97caadeb886bf9f6118ec6/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Recurring/RenewRemoteProxies.py#L136) (which quite buggy [2]), to call the underlying cpp ([_schedd_refresh_gsi_proxy](https://github.com/htcondor/htcondor/blob/main/src/python-bindings/htcondor2/schedd.cpp#L1543-L1582)) to send actual renewal command to Schedd (AP's) in **delegation** (default) mode where unfortunately is likely to have bugs as Jaime mentioned.

[2] [*refreshGSIProxy*](https://github.com/htcondor/htcondor/blob/2aa6c96a42465f469005de64e8dc7e59c765f603/bindings/python/htcondor2/_schedd.py#L914-L926) HTCondor v2 python binding also contain bugs (*e.g. missing of *self* as first positional arg in fn signature, typos proxy should be proc.*) waiting to be resolved by HTCondor Developers.

## Our workaround
*until the upcoming HTCondor 25.x patches are thoroughly tested*

On **TW** (especially in *canary*)
1. We will remain with HTC 24.7 python binding, v1 interface, since it is guaranteed to work with newer HTC 25.X on APs.
2. We steer away from delegation mode by setting `DELEGATE_JOB_GSI_CREDENTIALS=False` in `/etc/condor/condor_config` . This will do a regular file copy of the proxy (encrypted) when sending to the AP, instead of a delegation as Jamie suggested. #9256

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9262: CMSSW_8_0_36 ships with old Git 1.8.3.1 bin and an obsolete ca-bundle, thus break our CI/CD release pipeline.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9262: CMSSW_8_0_36 ships with old Git 1.8.3.1 bin and an obsolete ca-bundle, thus break our CI/CD release pipeline.

State: closed
Opened: 2026-01-19T09:04:28Z
Closed: 2026-01-19T11:25:13Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Area: CI/CD
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9262

## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-01-19T09:04:28Z)

I encountered [error](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/jobs/67867444) [1] in CI/CD release pipeline only with **CMSSW_8_36**

Specifically while the pipeline is doing *git clone CRABClient*, during the submission testsuite stage

Its turn out that `cmsenv` enforce us to use old git by exports two problematic env variables that override the system-wide Git.
```bash
+++ export GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc7_amd64_gcc530/external/git/1.8.3.1-giojec/share/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
+++ export GIT_EXEC_PATH="/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc7_amd64_gcc530/external/git/1.8.3.1-giojec/libexec/git-core";
```

[1] `SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`
```bash
++ git clone [https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient) /home/gitlab-runner/shell/builds/t3\_ZsMk1N/0/crab3/CRABServer/workdir/CMSSW\_8\_0\_36/src/CRABClient -b master
Cloning into '/home/gitlab-runner/shell/builds/t3\_ZsMk1N/0/crab3/CRABServer/workdir/CMSSW\_8\_0\_36/src/CRABClient'...
fatal: unable to access '[https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/)': SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
~/shell/builds/t3\_ZsMk1N/0/crab3/CRABServer
```

## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-19T10:19:24Z)

Hi @smuzaffar it looks like there is an old ca-bundle in older CMSSW releases. I have found same problem with CMSSW_7_6_7 which points to `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/slc7_amd64_gcc493/external/git/1.8.3.1/share/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt`
More older releases may suffer same problem , most likely the root CA used by github.com has expired and was renewed.
Could a general solution be found ?

## Comment (smuzaffar, 2026-01-19T11:00:35Z)

@belforte , yes this is a know issue ( see https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/issues/49762 ). I can deploy the fix i.e. globally unset GIT_SSL_CAINFO for slc6/slc7

## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-19T11:15:13Z)

Thanks @smuzaffar, and sorry for multiple reporting. We are now OK since   Krittin has changed our build script to use system git for git clone. For us it does not matter whether you distribute git or not or whatever solution you pick for the users at large.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9264: improve resubmission policies
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9264: improve resubmission policies State: closed Opened: 2026-01-20T17:05:53Z Closed: 2026-07-03T19:29:12Z Labels: Type: Enhancement, Type: Support URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9264 ## Opening post (belforte, 2026-01-20T17:05:53Z) We have evidence that more jobs will complete successfully if resubmitted more than the current 3 times (1 + 2 retries). As clear in the [dashboard](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/d07e49f1-7779-42ad-a9ff-d54dd4b9b829/crab-usage-spark?orgId=11&from=now-90d&to=now) created by our summer student last summer Shown here for the most common exit codes There is also a very long tail with many jobs succeeding after 20 attempts or more I have excluded exit code 8028 (fail to open after fallback to xrootd) since that is likely dominated by automatic, immediate, user-initiated retries for files missing or corrupted or located at unavailable sites which usually get OK after a few days. Since most user run wrapper scripts around CRAB which aggressively resubmit failed jobs, the number of retries is not that important IMHO. What we lack here is the fraction of the times that jobs are NOT fixed by retry, e.g. 50115 could often be a CMSSW segfault which can very well be persistent. Overall I think we have these main categories: 1. file open error, which requires retry with delay and/or run at different site 2. jobs which hit memory or wall clock limit, which require increasing it (which users usually do in their resubmissions, see below) 3. jobs which fail during ASO, where I believe that we can not improve on current policy, unless we add a 1 day delay on all ASO failures 4. jobs which failed with various possible exit codes, but due to local problems at the WN where we currently do not retry or retry too soon (I have seen cases where CRAB resubmissions are done so quickly that land on same WN due to HTCondor claim lease and of course suffer same problem) 5. there are errors which are almost never fixed (e.g. CMSSW configuration problem 8006) and we should avoid to retry ten times ! In view of increasing the retry count, and somehow having in mind WMA policy of "10 retries" I looked at which exit codes require more than 10 retries before becoming success (linear and log scale). I do not understand the bin at exit code = 0, hopefully picture is still correct. The clear outlier is 8028. Which is "expected" and well understood. I do not know what to exactly make of 50115 which as said above is a times a sort of catch-all, but we can start by simply retrying that 10 times as well, and in case make an ad-hoc study. Finally I looked at how much users use resubmissions and how much they change requirements (time, memory, sites) see [e-log](https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/how-much-are-users-resubmitting/140275?u=belforte) Summarizing the tables in there I conclude that approximately: * 20% of tasks get resubmitted by users * half of those tasks get some change in requirements !! * mostly users change the running time limit, when they ask for more memory, they also ask for more time * I can not say if those changes are done in a "meditated way", or some people have scripts that always ask for more time when they resubmit * only 6% of resubmitted tasks got a change in site black or white list, clearly only done after human decision and possibly suggestion by us All of this is based on data from last 3 months, so picture may not be fully representative, but that's what we have and surely it is "not too wrong" all in all use patterns are quite constant. ## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-20T17:15:26Z) Now that we hopefully understand what's going on, we can try to make a plan for improving things, i.e. move work from users to CRAB. 1. Introduce in automatic resubmission the possibility to: 1. have a delay 2. have an error code dependent number of retries 3. change site(s) 4. change memory or time requirement2. Review the classification of exit codes in [RetryJob](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/master/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py) (rewrite it ?) and define the more flexible policies above for each 3. make all resubmission have a minimum delay (10min ? 30min?) to avoid the "re-run on same broken WN" effect ? ## Comment (belforte, 2026-02-11T09:27:14Z) @aspiringmind-code do I understand it correctly that you volunteered to work on this ? If so, please change assignment. ## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2026-02-11T09:56:12Z) Yes, thanks! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-03T19:29:12Z) closed via #9319

## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-03-26T11:38:49Z)

Today, Rucio was down almost an hour,
all submissions and rucio commands failed as Stefano reported and fixed by Panos.

## Problem:
Our wait-and-retry logic [1] has effectively ignored 503 errors so far,
because *fatal* `RucioExceptions` were all treated the **same**.

## Solution
We should instead give 503 responses extra tolerance in the retry delay.

*P.S. This should put an end to the almost daily flood of 503 emails [2] whenever Rucio is under stress.*
*P.S. This aligned with retryable mechanism on our REST side[3]*

[1] CRAB wait-n-retry wrapper, treat RucioException as fatal that should be raise immediately.

VM Name | Recommended Action | Flavor | Compatible Flavor | Status -- | -- | -- | -- | -- crab-prod-tw02 | RESIZE | r2.2xlarge | m4.2xlarge | Done vocms0144 | RESIZE | r2.2xlarge | m4.2xlarge | Done vocms0195 | RESIZE | r2.2xlarge | m4.2xlarge | Done vocms0197 | RESIZE | r2.2xlarge | m4.2xlarge | Done vocms0199 | RESIZE | r2.2xlarge | m4.2xlarge | Done ***Please be aware that we need to recreate or resize the VMs to m4 flavors. Operations like rebuild or resize to m2 are not sufficient for this campaign.*** ## Deadline - ***July 30th 2026*** ## Instruction we can resize them to a compatible flavor indicated in the table above. Resize implies a **downtime** depending on **the amount of data on the disk** and the load on the infrastructure during the resize. It may last from 15 minutes to 8 hours.

We've been recommended to run the following cmd to discard any unused filesystem blocks, making the resize operation quicker ``` fstrim -va ```

The full detail of RESIZE operation instruction can be seen here: instructions
## Example 1) Verify current flavor, `openstack server show --fit-width vocms0197` > | flavor | disk='160', ephemeral='0', extra_specs.hw_rng:allowed='True', original_name='r2.2xlarge', | > | | ram='60000', swap='0', vcpus='16' 2) Verify available & compatible flavor, `openstack flavor list` > | | r2.2xlarge | 60000 | 160 | 0 | 16 | False | > | | m4.2xlarge | 60000 | 160 | 0 | 16 | False | 3) On Schedd/VM, clean fs up a bit, shutdown HTCondor, shutdown VM. (After drained) *P.S See also [How to shutdown CRAB](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/operations/crab-shutdown.html#crab-shutdown-drain-schedds), https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/6781* 3.1) as Root, keep list of running dags for holding & releasing after intervention. ```bash condor_q -con 'jobuniverse==7&&jobstatus==2' -af clusterid > Running_DAGs.2026.migrated.hypervisor.list ``` 3.2) hold DagMans, then check `condor_q -con 'jobuniverse==7&&jobstatus==2' -af clusterid` (should return nothing) ``` for dag in `cat Running_DAGs.2026.migrated.hypervisor.list`; do condor_qedit $dag HoldKillSig \"SIGKILL\" condor_hold $dag done ``` 3.3) `condor_off`, make sure logs show ``` [root@vocms0197 ~]# tail /var/log/condor/MasterLog 04/09/26 16:25:35 The SCHEDD (pid 2076280) exited with status 0 04/09/26 16:25:35 All daemons are gone ``` 3.4) `fstrim -va` (took almost 10 mins) ``` [root@vocms0197 ~]# fstrim -va /data: 437 GiB (469189685248 bytes) trimmed on /dev/vdc /home/grid: 150.9 GiB (162040864768 bytes) trimmed on /dev/vdb /boot/efi: 536.5 MiB (562528256 bytes) trimmed on /dev/vda15 /: 159.5 GiB (171220905984 bytes) trimmed on /dev/vda1 ``` 3.5) Then, we can safely `shutdown` VM. 4) Resize, `openstack server resize --flavor m4.2xlarge vocms0197` *verify and confirm resizing (if any there's any issue **openstack server resize revert *** ``` openstack server show --fit-width vocms0197 # if details looks good, then confirm openstack server resize confirm vocms0197 ``` 5) starting and verifying machine. ``` openstack server start vocms0197 root@vocms0197> lscpu Architecture: x86_64 CPU op-mode(s): 32-bit, 64-bit Address sizes: 48 bits physical, 57 bits virtual Byte Order: Little Endian CPU(s): 16 ... root@vocms0197> cat /proc/meminfo MemTotal: 59991236 kB ``` 6) `condor_on` and releasing the hold running DagMans. ``` for dag in `cat Running_DAGs.2026.migrated.hypervisor.list`; do condor_qedit $dag HoldKillSig \"SIGKILL\" condor_release $dag done ``` 7) verify `condor_q -con 'jobuniverse==7&&jobstatus==2' -af clusterid `. *the cmd should gave us same number of running dags been released (in my case 17 dags was running before intervention.* 8) Done. ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-09T15:31:59Z) We've migrated `vocms0197` to a new hypervisor with the `m4.2xlarge` flavor. *(same configuration of 16 vCPUs and 60 GB RAM)* `vocms0197` is now back in service, and `vocms0199` is currently being drained. ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-17T15:05:26Z) `vocms0199` is now back in service, and `vocms0195` is currently being drained. ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-29T08:48:32Z) All remaining machines were force-resized by CERN IT during 20–22 April due to urgent disk issues.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9294: allow a site to force its ASO users to use Rucio

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-04-09T15:44:53Z)

The Italian INFN community would like to at least experiment with forcing their local users to use ASO via Rucio, in order to facilitate disk quota management.

As discussed with @dciangot a viable strategy could be:

* introduce a configuration dictionary, maintained via `puppet` similarly to [tw_htcondorSchedds](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/data/hostgroup/vocmsglidein/crabtaskworker.yaml?ref_type=heads#L25)
   * the dictionary will have the format `{site_name: {forceRucio:'yes'|'no', 'ASO_RSE':name}}` allowing for a site to indicate an RSE for ASO different from the site name. While a site not present among the keys means `forceRucio=NO`, having the flag allows us to keep track of which sites we are playing with and easily enable/disable according to the problem of the day
   * the puppet YAML format will be converted into a python dictionary along the lines of https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb?ref_type=heads#L86-90 and added to the TaskWorkerConfig.py file
* The TaskWorker can then take one of two actions:
   a.  silently override the user submitted configuration
   b. raise a submissionRefused exception telling the user to change LFN prefix and possibly StorageSite

@dciangot what is your preference between `a.` and `b.` ? Or is there some other way as well ?
I personally like `b.` more, because it is easier to implement and ensures that users are aware, since they will have to know and worry about Rucio quota, rules management etc.

@nausikt if we decide to implement this, can you help with the puppet side ? I will take care of TaskWorker changes.

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9295: extend Overflow via JobRouting

State: closed
Opened: 2026-04-09T16:23:16Z

Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: In Progress, OPERATION
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9295

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-04-09T16:23:16Z)

we do overflow via HTCondor JobRouter via the file [/etc/condor/config.d/90_jobrouter.config](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/qa/code/files/crabschedd/90_jobrouter.config?ref_type=heads) in our AP's

That currently covers:
 * when input dataset is present ONLY at one European T1, add same country T2's to `DESIRED_SITES

Recently we have found that sometimes user jobs stay queued for a long time due to lack or CPU at T1's in cases like
* dataset has 2 disk replicas, both at T1's
* job list as DESIRED_SITES T1_US_FNAL and T3_US_FNALLPC (a uses case not covered by overflow via frontend group in gWms [1] ). in particular when users are accessing MINIAOD*
   * Note: T3_US_FNALLPC is always added for all datasets at T1_US_FNAL_Disk, as per CRIC list of  [Allowed Sites](https://cms-cric.cern.ch/cms/storageunit/detail/T1_US_FNAL_Disk/)
   * the above combined with [1] means that jobs which target datasets at FNAL are never overflown inside US.

A partial mitigation  should have come from having increased analysis fraction at T1's by 10%.

Following the discusssion with CompOps in [CMSTRANSF-1323](https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSTRANSF-1323) we should extend the overflow routes to cover those as well.

Also consider the use case
* dataset has 2 disk replicas: one at T1, one at T2.
in that case we end up with the T1 replica being unused, so we may consider overflow for those as well.

I do not know it is makes any difference to limit to dataset being MINIADO*, it is very rare that an other dataset is present at 2 sites. But we may not want to bother with NANO* which presently have 5 replicas.

 [1] https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/jtf5ose3xbnw3ybdiaj453by6h

I believe that I have found the solution to this in JobRouter context.
Use EVALSET, not SET !
i.e.

I should not use:
`SET DESIRED_SITES=strcat(DESIRED_SITES,",...")`
which replaces the DESIRED_SITES ad with a recursive expression,

but:
`EVALSET DESIRED_SITES=strcat(DESIRED_SITES,","...")`
which evaluates the RHS to a string using current value of the ad
and then sets the ad to the new string. See [ref](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/grid-computing/job-router.html#routing-mechanism)

You're right, I apologize for the confusion. Let me provide a working solution.

The most reliable way to match exactly N occurrences is to explicitly ensure there are N occurrences AND no more:

## **Working pattern for exactly N occurrences:**

```perl
/^(?:(?!string).)*(?:string(?:(?!string).)*){N-1}string(?:(?!string).)*$/
```

But that's quite complex. Here's a **simpler and more practical approach**:

```perl
/^([^s]|s(?!tring))*string([^s]|s(?!tring))*string([^s]|s(?!tring))*string([^s]|s(?!tring))*$/
```

**However, the cleanest solution for exactly 3 occurrences of "ERROR":**

```perl
/^((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*$/
```

### **Pattern explanation:**
- `((?!ERROR).)*` - Match any character that's NOT the start of "ERROR"
- `ERROR` - Match the literal string
- Repeat this pattern exactly N times
- The negative lookahead `(?!ERROR)` ensures we don't accidentally skip over occurrences

### **HTCondor example for exactly 3 "ERROR" strings:**
```
regexp("^((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*ERROR((?!ERROR).)*$", LogMessage)
```

This should now correctly match only when there are exactly 3 occurrences of "ERROR".
</details>

also pasted below for easy reference.
The amount of concurrent resource (overflow from a specific T1) is set as
 - 2 when one T1 has the data
 - 1 when two T1's have the data, since jobs are more or less half as likely to hit either
That splitting of overflow accounting is of course imperfect, but I do not see a way to do better, consumption has to
be declared when job is submitted, but which resource is used is only known when the job is matched.

We should now set limits in global pool negotiator and then deploy new routes.

```text
# Configuration file for the JobRouter
#

# Specifiy a global Requirements expression that must be true for all newly routed jobs,
# in addition to any Requirements specified within a routing table entry
#
JOB_ROUTER_SOURCE_JOB_CONSTRAINT =           ( \
    (JobUniverse==5) \
 && (jobstatus==1) \
 && (CRAB_UserHN != "sciaba") \
 && (HasBeenOverflowRouted is undefined) \
 && (CMS_ALLOW_OVERFLOW == "True") \
 && (time() - EnteredCurrentStatus > 3600) \
                                             )

# define a pre-route transform that does the transforms all routes should do
# After experimenting we found that EditJobInPlace and UNIVERSE directives
# do not work if places here. They need to be replicated inside each T1-specific route
#
JOB_ROUTER_PRE_ROUTE_TRANSFORM_NAMES = Defaults

JOB_ROUTER_TRANSFORM_Defaults @=jrd
  SET HasBeenOverflowRouted True
  EVALSET LastRouted time()
  EVALSET DESIRED_SITES_Orig = DESIRED_SITES
@jrd

# Static route names for each T1 (since they are exclusive
# order does not matter, use alphabetic here)
#
JOB_ROUTER_ROUTE_NAMES = T1_DE_KIT T1_ES_PIC T1_FR_CCIN2P3 T1_IT_CNAF T1_UK_RAL T1_US_FNAL TWO_T1 T1_T2

Then there is the usual problem with migrations which keep failing when we retry. ## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-22T17:34:48Z) #9300 should be reverted, and running Publishers rolled back to previous image. ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-22T18:09:25Z) Thank you for the on-point root cause analysis scattered across many write-ups, meeting minutes and MMs so far. I learned a lot! 🙇 ## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-22T20:06:22Z) Do not feel bad. There's very very few people in CMS who have years of experience with DBS, DBS Migrations, and CRAB i/f with them :-)

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-04-27T16:47:10Z)

change in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/367e5692451b821683af7404cece63eed280d6ce in Jam 2-25 broke the fix for #8366  which was done in August 2024 :-(

The problem is that I changed classAd name from `CRAB_ReqName` to `CRAB_Reqname` to make it consistent with the many places where it is used in HTC classAd manipulations and avoid confusion, but in the job wrapper we have case sensitive `grep` in the classAd dump file.

So the $FRONTIER_ID is now set to the useless `CRAB-` string, as Frontier support people just found out

```
Subject: 	CRAB's setting of FRONTIER_ID
Date: 	Mon, 27 Apr 2026 10:18:32 -0500
From: 	Dave Dykstra <<email>>
To: 	Stefano Belforte <<email>>
CC: 	Carl Vuosalo <<email>>, Luis Simas <<email>>, Stephan Lammel <<email>>

Hi Stefano,

We're looking at the CMS CERN squid logs to try to understand some periods of unusually high bandwidth usage, and found that CRAB is no longer setting a useful value in $FRONTIER_ID in jobs that access frontier. The value in the log is always just "CRAB-" rather than some identifier that helps us figure out which set of jobs is doing any particular behavior. Do you have any insight into that, and can it be fixed?

Thanks,

Dave
```

All those `grep` should be case-insensitive, following the HTCondor feature that all classAd comparisons are case-insensitive.

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-05-08T16:46:32Z)

runContainer.sh mounts `PublisherFiles` in the container
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97c04445b571e98ed92e572559db1be2693a750e/src/script/Container/runContainer.sh#L52-L54
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97c04445b571e98ed92e572559db1be2693a750e/src/script/Container/runContainer.sh#L61-L63
so that is available inside the container as `/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles/`
but the code uses a local directory instead

```console
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$ grep taskFiles current/PublisherConfig.py
config.General.taskFilesDir = '/data/srv/Publisher_files/'
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$
```

leaving the directory from host VM "idle"
```console
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$ ls -ld /data/hostdisk/Publisher/PublisherFiles/
drwxr-xr-x. 3 crab3 1399 4096 Dec 30  2021 /data/hostdisk/Publisher/PublisherFiles/
[crab3@crab-prod-tw01 Publisher]$
```

while this is certainly not fatal, it means
* temporary files in `config.General.taskFilesDir` are only cleaned when container restarts so we may risk running out of space in the local container file system
* list of blacklisted tasks in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/97c04445b571e98ed92e572559db1be2693a750e/src/python/Publisher/PublisherMaster.py#L65 is lost every time we restart the container

Simplest solution seems to me to change the PublisherConfig.py erb template in puppet leaving everything else the same.

- [x] change locally in my dev and test
- [x] change in qa
- [x] test in preprod
- [x] check if changes are needed to Publisher utils script
- [x] change in master and deploy to prod
- [x] change documentation as needed
- [x] ensure that old files are cleaned: done in  [cleanTW](https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/files/crabtaskworker/cleanTW.sh?ref_type=heads) crontab

## Comment (belforte, 2026-05-11T20:53:55Z)

All done, but can move `qa` to `master` in puppet because it brings new JobRouter with it.
One possibility is to roll back JObRouter change from `qa` leaving it in `dev` only. Put back AP's in `prod` and change "by hand" vocms0198 and vocms0106, changes to JR will be lost if condor is restarted, but it is unlikely to happen. What do you think @nausikt ?

## Comment (belforte, 2026-05-12T15:22:24Z)

Lacking guidance from my devOps, I went for cherrypicking the change from qa into master. This may require a bit of work next time we merge qa into master, let's hope we do it sooner rather than later.
I then ran puppet agent on cran-prod-tw01, copied files from old to new place and restarted Publisher_schedd container. Everything is fine. Now all json work file, failed blocks dump and blacklist are persistent.

## Comment (vkuznet, 2026-06-20T18:15:38Z)

@stefano, when you asking to gzip do you meant to use it for passed payload or for returning results? That said, here is correct way to ask curl to provide gzip encoded output from DBS API:
```
scurl -v --compressed -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" --data '{"dataset": "/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/AODSIM", "validFileOnly": 0, "detail": false}'   "https://cmsweb-prod.cern.ch:8443/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader/fileArray"
```
You need to provide `--compressed` option which will instruct server to put its output in gzip encoding and curl will decompress it. To verify that you can see its verbose output:
```

```
Pay attention to `accept-encoding` and to `content-encoding` printouts. Therefore for your python client you'll need to provide `Accept-encoding: gzip` and once you receive the gzipped payload you need to decompress it properly.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-21T15:55:31Z)

thanks @vkuznet , by "using `gzip` I mean to instantiate WMCore DBSReader object via
 `self.dbs = DBSReader(dbsurl, useGzip=True)`
which results in WMCore calling up DBSClient as
 ` DbsApi(url=url, useGzip=True)`
I have followed this in the python code and ends in using for communication with DBS this object
```
{'url': 'https://cmsweb-prod.cern.ch:8443/dbs/prod/global/DBSReader', 'proxy': None, 'key': None, 'cert': None, 'userAgent': '', 'accept': 'application/json', 'aggregate': True, 'debug': True, 'http_response': <RestClient.RequestHandling.HTTPResponse.HTTPResponse object at 0x7fbcc7902730>, 'gzip': True, 'rest_api': <RestClient.RestApi.RestApi object at 0x7fbcc796bfa0>}
```
So I am trying to reproduce that with `curl` to give you an example which does not depend on python DBSClient.

Since `self.gzip` is `True` and this is a POST, the data for the post is gzipped in memory and adds `'Content-Encoding':'gzip'` to the Headers  as per
https://github.com/dmwm/DBSClient/blob/1e6acbd55c55497cf747a2a0cf4539936138a04a/src/python/dbs/apis/dbsClient.py#L466-L470
Final call is made with :
` headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Accept': 'application/json', 'UserID': '<email>', 'User-Agent': 'DBSClient/Unknown/', 'Content-Encoding': 'gzip'}`

I do not see a way to separate gzip usage for data in the POST ad returned value.
I use the same  ` DbsApi(url=url, useGzip=True)` when creating the API used to POST new blocks and it works fine.

It seems to me that `fileArray` and `insertBulkBlock` are doing some different handling/validation of data, maybe because `insertBulkBlock` does not return any data. I.e. `gzip` only works when talking to DBSWriter, not Reader.

Looking in DBSClient I see that the lines I point to above are the only place where `self.gzip` is used and that the `decompress()` methos is never called, which makes me suspect that the DBSClient is not capable to accept gzipped data ! When doing a GET

Now, you will surely say that DBSClient in python should not be used and I should change code to fork plain `curl` or use `Requests` etc. etc., but I was simply looking or a small improvement on current situation when CRAB pulls lists of files and lumis for job splitting, sort of a low-hanging-fruit. Major changes in CRAB code are out of scope. I can surely leave things as they are. Changes to DBSClient are surely not in my scope !

FWIW I have tried to add `'Accept-Encoding': 'gzip'` to he headers inside DBS call to server and this time HTTP  returns code 500  with
`UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x8b in position 1: invalid start byte`

That was only curiosity/education, I surely do not want to have my own version of dmwm/DBSClient and dmwm/PycurlClient.

I do not see a way to make progress. And if you agree, I will close this here.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-05-20T08:44:34Z)

Hi @oljemark
everything in current CRABServer/test/python is actually unused. It is was an "exercise" in using pytest and unittest packages to add unit tests to CRAB code which alas never converged to full program of covering the whole tool. Given the manpower situation, that effort was abandoned when the guy who kickstarted it left.
Consensus was that it is too much work to retrofit all code that we have, given that changes are now rare.

I can certainly agree that this is not  professionally maintained and documented package, but since it is now clear that it will not outlive me, we can hopefully keep it sort of frozen for then next few years.

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-06-28T11:15:09Z)

See https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5427

More in general, apparently when  input file validation fails PJ creates a dummy name unique for all jobs. This makes no sense and must be avoided.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T15:24:42Z)

relevant lines
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/b5ea08b82ec0e58ed656a5650673ef2ef951251e/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2427-L2430

as  Kiril pointed out, at the very least the LFN should be unique (i.e. have job # in the suffix) so that counting is correct.
Same two lines above in case there is no input file.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-29T06:21:57Z)

I am not sure what to do in case of no input file in the FJR. How can we count read files and events in this case ?

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-29T09:04:30Z)

looking in code history, the use of DummyLFN in case an input LFN is missing in the FJR was introduced with https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5171
So it was not really thought over in detail. The most likely use case leading to this that I can think of is users running some non-CMSSW script and providing their owm FJR, in which case we can't make any assumption on what's in the FJR,
e.g. it may be used simply to pass an exit code to the job.
If there's no input information in FJR we can not count number of input events anyhow, nor can tell how many files were processed by the job. So I am sticking with a common `DummyLFN`, when users see
```text
  Number of files processed: 1
  Number of events read: 0
```
they will realize that those lines must be ignored. I will look into improving crab client to print `n/a` or similar.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-29T09:16:32Z)

I tested with a config. similar to what  Kiril reported in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5427, i.e. process a list of files with an extra `/` so cmsRun works but input LFN is rejected by Lexicon. 2 jobs, 2 files per job.

With the change in the commit, crab report changes from
```text
Summary from successful jobs (i.e. in status 'finished'):
  Number of files processed: 1
  Number of events read: 39600
  Number of events written in EDM files: 87600
```
to

```text
Summary from successful jobs (i.e. in status 'finished'):
  Number of files processed: 4
  Number of events read: 85200
  Number of events written in EDM files: 85200
```
note how not only the number of files is corrected, but also number of events read/written is consistent (and consistent with what can be derived by looking at FJR's)

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-07-13T15:06:19Z)

In the way that we do resubmissions and retries now, it makes no sense to add time spend in previous submissions in order to check for job having exceeded MAX_WALLTIME.
In particular we want to automatically increase walltime request in subsequent resubmissions.

This part must be reviewed
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/872622c977148a667e0cba9295f9d5951773e20b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L375-L390

- [x] remove `integrated_job_time`
- [x] check whether it is worth to look at `Committed* ad`
- [x] improve logging so that PostJob log shows  actual usage and limit

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-13T15:17:31Z)

current PostJonb log is like this
```
Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:55:04 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob ====== Starting to analyze job exit status.
Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:55:04 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob        -----> RetryJob log start -----
Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:55:04 CEST(+0200):DEBUG:RetryJob Job ads already present. Will not use condor_q, but will load previous jobs ads.
Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:55:04 CEST(+0200):INFO:RetryJob New job_fjr.2180.2.json file content: {"exitMsg": "Not retrying job due to wall clock limit (job automatically killed on the worker node)", "jobExitCode": 50664, "exitCode": 50664}

Wed, 01 Jul 2026 14:55:04 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob The retry handler indicated this was a fatal error.
```

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-13T15:59:31Z)

can compute wall clock time using the ads `JobCurrentStartDate` and `EnteredCurrentStatus` (the latter is the time when job was removed)
**Note:** cannot use `CommittedTime` since when time limit is exceeded, job is evicted, so `CommittedTime` is reset to 0

Here's an example or relevant classAds from a job which hit the time limit from https://cmsweb.cern.ch/scheddmon/0121/nladams/260619_134211:nladams_crab_ScoutingPFRun3F/postjob.2180.2.txt

| Ad | Value | |
| --- | --- | --- |
|                RemoteWallClockTime |   217638.0 | seconds = 3627 min = 60.4 h|
|   LastRemoteWallClockTime    |144053.0 | seconds = 2400.88 min = 40.01 h|
| MaxWallTimeMinsRun  |  2400 | what is used in PeriodicRemove |
|                                LastMatchTime |  1782766448 | |
|       JobCurrentStartDate   |1782766448| |
|      JobCurrentStartExecutingDate | 1782766453| |
|    EnteredCurrentStatus|  1782910501| delta from JobCurrStartDate =  2400.88 min|
|                  CommittedTime   | 0 |
|   NumJobStarts   | 2 |
| NumShadowStarts   | 2 |

**Note:** `RemoteWallCLockTime` includes previous attempts, indeed we not even have 60h pilots !
This means that this line is also wrong https://github.com/dmwm/cms-htcondor-es/blob/5fe8acbeaa03c73a8321a6570423857a870241d0/src/htcondor_es/convert_to_json.py#L698

**Note also** the description of `RemoteWallClockTime` vs. `LastRemoveWallClockTime` in https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html#RemoteWallClockTime and
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html#LastRemoteWallClockTime

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-14T17:18:19Z)

Note that the job in the example above had two starts, the first time ran for about 20h,  then was killed for unknown reasons and restarted by the schedd)  is summed to the second start (which lasted 40h and was ended  by periodic remove).

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-23T14:12:50Z)

The thing is that there is no need for a time check in PostJob ! If job runs too long, PeriodicRemove kills it and we know becasue of the RemoveReason. Period.
 So code can be removed and there's no need to look at `Committed*` ads

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-07-14T15:27:36Z)

Long ago Brian introduced the nice feature that job stdout is returned also when job is e.g. terminated (condor_rm) due to excessice memory or time usage in commit  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/43d18053fbaf05650c3927d23dcf58f804c22b0a

But this does not appear to work anymore.

I broke that when reformatting DagmanCreate to use a jobSubmit object instead of JDL-as-a-string.
 According to current Condor documentation,  the correct attribute in the submission JDL is not `WhenToTransferOutput` but `when_to_transfer_output` see e.g.
https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/man-pages/condor_submit.html
and https://deepwiki.com/search/if-i-specify-whentotransferout_cffdbf73-b080-4906-a55c-ce3061276ace?mode=fast

After submission that resul in that the classAd  `WhenToTransferOutput`  but the way to set it in the JDL is via `when_to_transfer_output`  as it may be implied by [this](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/tutorials/HTCondor-Introduction.html#Schedd) example.  Yet there is no mention of `WhenToTransferOutput` in current job classAd [documentation](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html).
Anyhow I verified that having this in `JobSubmit``
```console
belforte@vocms059/SPOOL_DIR> grep -i when Job.submit
when_to_transfer_output = ON_EXIT_OR_EVICT
```
results in
```console
belforte@vocms059/SPOOL_DIR> condor_q 10568464 -l|grep -i when
WhenToTransferOutput = "ON_EXIT_OR_EVICT"
```

I also notice that when refactoring DagmanCreator for v2 API, I commented out this line
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/872622c977148a667e0cba9295f9d5951773e20b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L437-L438
but it is actually a documented feature https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classad-attributes/job-classad-attributes.html#SpoolOnEvict
and should indeed be `False`  !! Since we do not want to transfer back the sandbox on eviction, we want the job to restart cleanly from scratch.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-15T08:07:11Z)

the simple fix works ! But I notice that when job is killed and partial stdout file ` cmsRun-stdout.log.tmp ` is printed, the final stdout is not "crisply clear".  I think a problem is
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/872622c977148a667e0cba9295f9d5951773e20b/scripts/job_wrapper/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L273-L274
when condor kills the job while user app is running, a signal is sent while line 273 is being executed.
So 276 is not executed and $EXIT_STATUS stays undefined, execution jumps to  `finish{}` function because of
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/872622c977148a667e0cba9295f9d5951773e20b/scripts/job_wrapper/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L76
and the call to `check_application_execution` in there results in these lines in job output
```text
======== Figuring out long exit code of the job for condor_chirp at Wed Jul 15 07:49:05 GMT 2026========
==== Failed to load the long exit code from jobReport.exitCode.txt. Falling back to short exit code ====
======== Short exit code also missing. Settint exit code to 80001 ========
```

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-16T13:41:33Z)

Let's move "improving stdout when killed" to another issue. I am not able to reproduce anymore the "fix".
I.e. job output is not retrieved anymore in spite of `when_to_transfer_output = ON_EXIT_OR_EVICT` in JDL !!

I am puzzled.

I tested again w/o the changes to gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis and it works. So will push that in and create a new issue for a better `trap` handling

# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9348: resubmission delay does not work in new code

State: open

Labels: Type: Enhancement
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9348

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-07-15T20:04:14Z)

refactored Retry/Resubmission code now allows for introducing additional, flexible, delays in the retry policy executed during automatic resubmissions
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1038e05ebaf8cc0ae95906d385899d8344b1d460/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L23-L26
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1038e05ebaf8cc0ae95906d385899d8344b1d460/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreJob.py#L539-L549

but when testing the delay is not applied.

Initial guess is that https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1038e05ebaf8cc0ae95906d385899d8344b1d460/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PreJob.py#L543
points to current retry number while PostJob write the delay policy when processign the previous submission.

But an attempt change to
```python
key = str(crab_retry-1)
```
did not work.

Deeper "digging" is needed.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-15T20:05:07Z)

@aspiringmind-code I will take over as agreed, please write down what you tried and which problems you found.

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2026-07-16T13:42:58Z)

See [task](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=vchakrav&var-task=260715_082255:vchakrav_crab_20260715_102252&from=2026-07-15T07:22:55.000Z&to=now&timezone=utc&var-site=$__all&var-schedd=059&var-cmsUserId=&var-task_str=vchakrav_crab_20260715_102252&var-status=$__all&var-crabid=$__all&var-Filters=&var-rest_host=https:%2F%2Fcmsweb.cern.ch) for example.
The main problem is that the RRN remains the same in the next retry if the delay happens in the last retry (using inkey and str(crab_retry -1) concept). In the given task, RRN=2 for both prejob.1.1.txt and prejob.1.2.txt in which prejob.1.1 TaskManagerBootstrap ended with exit code 4 due to the delay. When prejob.1.2.txt picks it up again, we get `Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:28:49 CEST(+0200):INFO:PreJob RRN for job 1 reused as 2 (interrupted pre-job, not re-incrementing)` and therefore RRN is at 2 in both. We run into prejob.1.3.txt for RRN=3.
Another problem because of this is that the retry in which delay happened (1 in this case) is missing from the all retries [monitoring](https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/goto/dfsacmqss1ybkc?orgId=11)
To summarise, RRN concept needs to be aligned with the delay generated Exit Code 4. RRN originally without delay is reusing the last RRN and not re incrementing it to handle interrupted prejob.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9355: Kill jobs after too many ASO failures
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9355: Kill jobs after too many ASO failures

State: closed
Opened: 2026-07-20T14:37:38Z
Closed: 2026-08-19T15:27:03Z
Labels: Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9355

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-07-20T14:37:38Z)

Implement mechanism to automatically kill a task once a certain number of jobs have failed during ASO (Application Service Operations) failures.

## Objective
Reduce wasted CoreHR spent in jobs that eventually fail due to ASO issues by terminating tasks early when they exceed a failure threshold during ASO operations.

## Implementation Details
- Define a threshold for the number of ASO failures before killing a task in TaskWorkerConfig
- Implement job termination logic when threshold is reached
- Send notification to user with appropriate status message explaining the task termination

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-22T14:32:15Z)

I think best way is to use PostJob exit code 3 to halt the DAG.
- [x] introduce conde in PostJob to do this calling some ad-hoc method where we implement the stop algorithm
- [ ] look to extend this to `condor_rm` running jobs
- [x] handle in PostJob the uploading of Warning Message to task DB
- [x] **investigate what happens with happens to crab resubmit** (first thing to do)

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-27T16:29:58Z)

If we abort the dag via PostJob exiting with code 3, DAG terminates and writes a RescueDag and is ready to be restarted by a `crab resubmit`. As the [doc](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/automated-workflows/dagman-completion.html#stopping-the-dag-on-node-failure) says:
> f the return value for the specified node matches AbortExitValue, the DAG is immediately aborted, meaning that the DAG stops all currently running nodes, cleans up, writes a Rescue DAG, and exits

So I think the best is to also send a kill command to TW. So that task is set in KILLED status and further submissions require a new task.

It should be possible to emulate the client kill command via a POST from PostJob. This will also handle the messaging to the user.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-27T16:37:50Z)

PostJob already has an extensice (and of course a bit cryptic) machinery to collect exit codes in `error_summary.json` and  to count fatally FAILED JOBS IN `task_statistics.FATAL_ERROR` (IIUC). And then abort dag via `PostJob.check_abort_dag()`.

Maybe I can reuse this ?

hmm. I am not even sure that the old `PostJob.check_abort_dag()` works well, it uses files which are not protected against concurrent write.
So I am adding new methods, to keep it clean and safe. Following long tradition of software development practice.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-08T14:16:24Z)

I am introducing 3 new configuration paramenters:
```python
config.TaskWorker.maxFatalAsoNumber             # self explaining
config.TaskWorker.maxFatalAsoRelativeFraction   # fraction of fatal errors in ASO transfers completed so far
config.TaskWorker.maxFatalAsoAbsoluteFraction   # fraction of fatal errors in all jobs in the task
```

The rational is that we want to kill things early, but not to kill a large tasks on a transient.

They will be ANDed. Any can be made irrelevant by setting it to 0 so it is always True.
This should allows to experiment and find best strategy.

## Comment (nausikt, 2026-08-24T12:32:56Z)

After dump a few errors to Claude and some discussions.

Let's briefly classified into 4 mains category.

1. **BadCode** — fails identically on every file, every node, every replica.
The defect is in the release or configuration. Input is irrelevant.
P.S. Can/Should we breakdown BadCode? or no points. IMO, no points leave them alone in 50115.

2. **BadData** — fails on specific events or specific files; other files in the same dataset succeed.
The input is intact but content triggers an unhandled path.

3. **BadFileReplica** (Transient) — fails on one physical copy; the same LFN read from a different site succeeds.
Bytes on disk are wrong. Logical dataset is fine.

4. **FlakySite** (Transient) — fails on one node or during one time window; succeeds elsewhere on the same input.
Nothing wrong with code or data.

## [BadCode/Data, 26.2%, 50AAA, new Permanent]
**262** tasks falls into user code error and were permanent, since they have **NO SUCCEED** after retries.
*Exhaustively retried 3 times.*
```json
{ "succeed_job_after_retry": null, "total_retry_before_succeed": null }
```
**Regexes**: Just capture `segmentation violation` and let this be default route for all user code error
*P.S. Neither we're in business of finding generic error log patterns/regexes nor retry these failure modes anyhow.*

**Actions**:
- Either Introduce new ExitCode (50AAA) OR let them stay with `50115`
- AND *IMHO*, we can let this default route ***Fail Fast*** (**NO Retry**)
*P.S. This way not only we no longer waste resources, but also let users having a faster feedback loop for their code failures.*

## [BadFileReplica/Site-related, at least 56.5%, 50BBB...50XXX, new Transients]
There's **565** tasks that have at least 80% of their job failures came from 50115 and all of 50115 failures eventually succeeded on retry
Thus, we can dive deeper and potentially do log regexes/pattern recognition and classification here.

**Regexes**: **TBD**

**Actions**:
- Introduce new **Recoverable** ExitCode (50BBB...50XXX) give them clear transient definitions.

Hopefully users fixed already bugs which made their code segfault right away. And also there's no big damage in retrying a jobs which used little CPU. But when segfault happen after application has been running for a while, let's report it as such.

labelling the error  as recoverable when it succeeds after 6 retries does not help us to decide how to call it at retry #3, nor to decide a specific action.

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-07-28T17:29:16Z)

currently SPOOL_DIR almost always contains files like
```text
'task_statistics.$$([ifThenElse(GLIDEIN_CMSSite is undefined, "Unknown", GLIDEIN_CMSSite)]).FATAL_ERROR'
'task_statistics.$$([ifThenElse(GLIDEIN_CMSSite is undefined, "Unknown", GLIDEIN_CMSSite)]).RECOVERABLE_ERROR'
```
this is confusing, and annoying since makes `ls` to fall back to one file per line.

This is due to
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/0a4d004e1d6d686e3496b62d62ca96061dd9c2cb/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L662-L663
which try to pick from the `finished_jobs/job.N.R` file a classAd which is defined via an expression.

Simple solution is to use a classAd which has the site name string, like
`
MATCH_GLIDEIN_CMSSite = "T2_CH_CERN"
`

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9374: reduce load on dagman start by lowting MaxPre
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9374: reduce load on dagman start by lowting MaxPre

State: closed
Opened: 2026-08-01T16:36:52Z
Closed: 2026-08-01T16:52:12Z
Labels: Priority: Critical
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9374

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-01T16:36:52Z)

Our schedd's struggle to restart when fully loaded. One contribution is too much memory in python processes.
In particular when schedd restarts all dagman restart at same time, and try to submit. So can have hundreds of PreJob
scripts running at same time.
Currently we allow up to 20 PreJob to run concurrently in each Dagman. But over time we have been added things to
PreJob and they do not really complete very fast.
So as a mitigation we can lower MaxPre from 20 to 10 in

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6e374190d0b47f1a193751bce8876654f834f1f9/scripts/dagman/dag_bootstrap_startup.sh#L282

MaxPost is already 10 and anyhow concurrenty of PostJob could be due to many jobs completing at same time, but it is not immediately affecting schedd restart.
