# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9377: cut job stdout lines length at 1K char (also when job is evicted)

State: closed
Opened: 2026-08-04T17:40:21Z
Closed: 2026-08-11T13:29:31Z
Labels: Status: Done, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9377

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-04T17:40:21Z)

As of https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9349 stdout of evicted jobs is returned again, but its size is not limited strongly enough.
Current code only checks line number and grabs first and last lines
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/cd03a20b880425c44f5140b44be5f10462439367/scripts/job_wrapper/gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh#L193-L204

But we have just encountered a case where the users calls `cmsDriver` in their script, and that prints out in one line the full list of file names in the PREMIX dataset, 500K file names in that case !!!!

So need to do better:
* check file size, not only N lines. 1MByte looks large enough here (after looking at size of job_out*txt one one AP)
   * this avoids that we get killed by a log with <4K lines, but where some are hugely long
* cut each line at 1K characters (for non-evicted jobs `CMSRunAnalysis.py:logCMSSW()` cuts at 3K char. seems too much to me[1])

[1]
the limit at 3K char in `logCMSSW()` has been there since ten years https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/ff9591d3b3fdc11cfb3f432d1b449ab9d9f39189 but there's no record of the rational for that particular value.

So I will cut at 1K character and introduce the 1MB size limit in there as well.

@nausikt @aspiringmind-code any comment, suggestion ? Am I missing some other pitfall ? Or being too much strict w/o reason  ?

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-06T15:54:06Z)

note, how to check file size
**python**
```python
if os.path.getsize(file_path) < 1024 * 1024:
    print("File is smaller than 1 MB")
else:
    print("File is 1 MB or larger")
```
**bash**
```bash
if [ $(stat -c %s "$file") -lt $((1024 * 1024)) ]; then
    echo "File is smaller than 1 MB"
else
    echo "File is 1 MB or larger"
fi
```

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-07T10:09:39Z)

how to limit line length in bash (I am ashamed that myself and Dario did not do this alreaady !!! )
```bash
cat <file> | cut -c 1-1000
head -10 <file> | cut -c 1-1000
tail-10 <file> | cut -c 1-1000
```

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9378: protect PostJob against being run on old job

State: closed
Opened: 2026-08-07T10:29:45Z

Labels: Type: Bug, Type: Enhancement
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9378

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-07T10:29:45Z)

At times Dagman can "loose' the fact that a PostJob process it spawned is completed, and submit the PJ again with same retry number [1]
Currently this make PostJob  to think it is being restart after deferral and plow on, but it fails to update classAd since job left the queue. So it spends O(10) minutes in retrying and eventually crashes w/o any proper logging. This
* slows down Dagman and schedd
* can eat a lot of memory
* creates logs very confusing

[1] here's my analysis of one such event where [postjob.377.4](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/scheddmon/0122/fernance/260806_115656:fernance_crab_GluGluHToDarkShowers-ScenarioA_Par-ctau-0p6-mA-1p67-mpi-5_GENSIM_RAWSIM_HLT2025/postjob.337.4.txt) shows

[... more errors and tracebacks...]
then it looks like process was killed
Thu, 06 Aug 2026 16:21:37 CEST(+0200):INFO:PostJob
======== Starting execution again after deferral

Thu, 06 Aug 2026 16:32:55 CEST(+0200):ERROR:PostJob Failed to set job ClassAd attributes for 5 times, will not retry. Dashboard may report stale job status/exit-code.
Ended TaskManagerBootstrap with code 2
```

I derived the following timelene(s) and observations from `RunJobs.dag.dagman.out` and PostJob logs.
**Note:** every time dagman restarts it replays old events in the log.
"Spurious" lines from that in the log are like
```
08/06/26 16:08:10 Event: ULOG_POST_SCRIPT_TERMINATED for HTCondor Node Job337 (160732540.0.0) {08/06/26 14:16:56} [recovery mode]
```
which indicates that at 16:08 Dagman notices an event happened 2 hours earlier at 16:16. for job 160732540.0
In order to make sense of things one must ignore `ULOG*` lines which end with `[recovery mode]` **and** the lines which immediately follows with same time stamps which AFAIU report details of that old event while alas have a simpler format like the following which do not indicated e.g. to what condor JobId they refer.
```

08/06/26 16:08:10 Node(Job337)::_Status = STATUS_POSTRUN

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9379: Wrong message from TW when site with USER data is blacklisted
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9379: Wrong message from TW when site with USER data is blacklisted

State: open
Opened: 2026-08-07T10:41:26Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9379

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-07T10:41:26Z)

e.g. https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/260806_145805%3Abibehera_crab_NeNe_v0pT_V0_weff_v1_IP10
shows this taskWarningMs

> The CRAB server backend refuses to send jobs to the Grid scheduler. No locations found for dataset /IonPhysics10/bibehera-2pc_NeNe25_V0_v1_IP10-270449d3132be18177651c80f5f48d72/USER. (or at least for what passed the lumi-mask and/or run-range selection). Use `crab checkdataset` command to find block locations and compare with your black/white list Found 5 (out of 5) blocks present only at blacklisted not-whitelisted, and/or non-accelerator sites. Global blacklist contain these T1/T2: ['T2_CN_Beijing', 'T2_PT_NCG_Lisbon', 'T2_US_Nebraska', 'T2_GR_Ioannina', 'T2_RU_IHEP', 'T2_LV_HPCNET', 'T2_AT_Vienna', 'T2_RU_INR', 'T2_CH_CERN_P5', 'T2_PL_Swierk', 'T2_FR_GRIF', 'T2_US_Vanderbilt', 'T2_PK_NCP', 'T2_RU_ITEP', 'T2_CH_CERN_HLT', 'T2_TW_NCHC'] and 41 T3's Full list at https://cmssst.web.cern.ch/cmssst/analysis/usableSites.json

But the real cause is that the input dataset is in Phys03 and [located at T2_US_Vanderbilt](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/das/request?instance=prod/phys03&input=origin_site+dataset%3D%2FIonPhysics0%2Fbibehera-2pc_NeNe25_V0_v1_IP0-270449d3132be18177651c80f5f48d72%2FUSER) which was in downtime when the task was submitted (as shown in the Global blacklist).

The TaskWorker did everything correctly, found location in DBS/Phys03, prepared the jobs, and when submitting compared the deisred sites for each block of jobs (only Vanderbilt here) with the blacklist and refused to submit.

But the message fails to convey this.

Message is OK for datasets in DBS/Global with locations in Rucio. so we need to be careful not to break that part.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9381: Storm of oracle connections problem caused by fds spike on CRABServer
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9381: Storm of oracle connections problem caused by fds spike on CRABServer State: open Opened: 2026-08-10T11:51:37Z URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9381 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-08-10T11:51:37Z) Stefano reported that CRAB REST Server had a small storm of oracle connection problems and we got 5 min of timeout (HTTP 408). [1] Nothing in common among 4 crashed pods they live in difference k8s nodes.[2,3] So it's not about hypervisor degradation issue. Indicate more a generic problem with our heavy query or an abusive submissions. Need to investigate in detail since this start to be recurring and severe enough to cause time out. [1] [2] [3] ``` crabserver-55fd4f78b8-5k5gs 1/1 Running 0 17d 10.100.192.239 cmsweb-k8s-prodsrv-zone-b-m4-2b2nguwnjv4w-node-3 crabserver-55fd4f78b8-cqbns 1/1 Running 0 17d 10.100.186.204 cmsweb-k8s-prodsrv-zone-b-m4-2b2nguwnjv4w-node-0 crabserver-55fd4f78b8-ph69f 1/1 Running 0 17d 10.100.186.195 cmsweb-k8s-prodsrv-zone-b-m4-2b2nguwnjv4w-node-0 crabserver-55fd4f78b8-pxqsp 1/1 Running 0 17d 10.100.82.61 cmsweb-k8s-prodsrv-zone-b-m4-2b2nguwnjv4w-node-1 ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-10T12:20:20Z) Given that we already spent > 1y trying to understand and fix the root cause of those FileDescriptions/DBconnections surges.... I do not think that we have much hopes to find a better solution as long as the current probes restart the pods and revive the service. Nor would it make sense to put a lot of work on this unless problems becomes much more serious. The only thing which comes to mind is to investigate if there's a way for K8s probes to kick-in and restart pods sooner. Current probes only acts when HTTP queries fail, detecting FD ramp may be better.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9384: correct CRAB_JobCount  ad for automatic splitting
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9384: correct CRAB_JobCount  ad for automatic splitting

State: closed
Opened: 2026-08-13T09:26:58Z
Closed: 2026-08-19T14:19:39Z
Labels: Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9384

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-13T09:26:58Z)

every job has a MY.CRAB_JobCount classAd which is meant to report the number of jobs in the task.
But since it is defined in DagmanCreator and passed to AP via the template JobSubmit object,
it represents the number of jobs created by TaskWorker,
so for automatic splitting is stuck to the number of probe jobs (5).
Need to update it for jobs submitted by automatic splitter sub-dags.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1cdeb6c7a7a9817f933cfafc2a018bc7a179c65b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L381

That value is also added to dagman job classAd in DagmanSubmitter via
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1cdeb6c7a7a9817f933cfafc2a018bc7a179c65b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L28
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1cdeb6c7a7a9817f933cfafc2a018bc7a179c65b/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L84

Besides being useful in order to decide whether to kill a job after too many ASO errors ( #9383 ) it will be generally good that each job carries the updated value of  number of jobs in task at the time the job was submitted.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9389: ensure that we can tell analysis from MC in monitoring
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9389: ensure that we can tell analysis from MC in monitoring

State: closed
Opened: 2026-08-19T22:01:10Z
Closed: 2026-08-24T21:45:15Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9389

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-19T22:01:10Z)

we currently rely on "no input dataset" (in details, classAd DESIRED_CMSDataset to be undefined, which is a bit tricky to select in Grafana). But this fails when e.g. users specfifies in the configuration `data.userInputFiles` which is a "data processing workflow" but has no `desired_cmsdataset`

That happens rather frequently now e.g. https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/260815_181226:anstahll_crab_HIPhysicsRawPrime_PHOLEP_HIRun2024_PromptReco_MINIAOD_2026_08_07

In monitoring all of CRAB jobs have `JobType=analysis` and `JobType=Production/Processing` is reserved for WMA. Changing this is likely to break many existing monitoring dashboards and scripts, so it is not an option

some possibilities that come to mind

* clearly set `DESIRED_CMSDataset = "None"` to indicate MC
* set `DESIRED_CMSDataset = "UserFiles"` when  `data.userInputFiles`  is used
* check the CRABClient plugin type `config.JobType.pluginName = 'Analysis'` currently stored in `tm_job_type` and propagate it to OpenSearch "somehow"
* something else or combinations of the above
* adding a new classAd and a new field in OpenSearch
* ....

### Important notes

##### those will require changing the ad parsing in https://github.com/dmwm/cms-htcondor-es/blob/b1c8998e08702ca230831d10cf7910c9dd33cd8d/src/htcondor_es/convert_to_json.py#L764-L769

##### need to worry what happens to aggregated data in the job monitoring dashboard

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T09:44:48Z)

I think that best option is to "extend" `CMS_JobType` which currently is always `Analysis` to be either `Analysis` or `PrivateMC`
That reflects the CRABClient plugin name and is consistent with WMA which uses `CMS_JobTyp` to differentiate Production from Processing.

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9390: add a classAd to flag when IgnoreLocality is used and propagate to MONIT

State: closed

Closed: 2026-08-24T21:45:16Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement, Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9390

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-20T20:04:35Z)

we need to be able to easily see whether given jobs/tasks used IgnoreLocality or not, and to select based on that in OS/Grafana.

Will introduce a new classAd CRAB_IgnoreLocality = True/False to reflect the task table column task['tm_ignore_locality']

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-20T20:05:52Z)

ref https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/wasted-cpu-time-corehours-in-crab/147739/10

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T19:54:09Z)

hmm
`        jobSubmit['My.CRAB_IgnoreLocality'] = classad.quote(task['tm_ignore_locality'])`
leads to
`CRAB_IgnoreLocality = "F"` or ` = "T" `
Which may not be the best for OS

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T20:03:55Z)

should use correct True/False expression for classAds
e.g. we have
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1da960d47eac79e91d3d623945a46b6098186e96/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L346
and
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1da960d47eac79e91d3d623945a46b6098186e96/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L400

`0` and `1` are OK since they will be mapped to `False/True` in the spider's code
https://github.com/dmwm/cms-htcondor-es/blob/b1c8998e08702ca230831d10cf7910c9dd33cd8d/src/htcondor_es/convert_to_json.py#L1380-L1381

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T20:14:15Z)

also `jobSubmit['My.CRAB_IgnoreLocality']=True` or `=False` will do. And is more clear !
The classAd will be "true" or "false" but when extracted in python API it returns "True" or "False" (the python booleans).

```
>>> ad={}
>>> import classad2 as classad
>>> ad=classad.ClassAd()
>>>
>>> ad['test']=True
>>> print(ad)

    [
        test = true
    ]
>>> ad['test']
True
>>>
```

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T21:43:36Z)

But of course I had forgotten that ` jobSubmit['My.CRAB_IgnoreLocality']` is an `htcondor.Submit()` object where values must always be assigned as string !!
So:
```python
jobSubmit['My.CRAB_IgnoreLocality'] = "true" if task['tm_ignore_locality'] == 'T' else "false"
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9398: improve detection of removed (out of bound) jobs in PostJob
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9398: improve detection of removed (out of bound) jobs in PostJob State: closed Opened: 2026-08-24T16:24:11Z Closed: 2026-09-23T13:32:43Z URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9398 ## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-24T16:24:11Z) sometimes jobs are removed by hitting wall or memory limit, bt a FJR is reported to the schedd. This makes PostJob set a confusing exit code = 80001 Should always check job status, and if it was removed, check reason ads and cross check used from ads vs. limits etc. Also introduce new ExitCode for "killed by user", when user issues crab kill, jobs get `RemoveReason = "Python-initiated action (by user crabtw)"` ## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-24T21:35:33Z) It is also likely that PostJob does not get executed after a `crab kill`, so we will have to stick with 80001 from the job wrapper. We can possibly edit this in the spider when pushing to OpenSearch, but it may be confusing to get a value there different form the classAd recorded in condor ! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-15T14:57:09Z) The best and only way is to add a `JobeExitCode` classAd to all jobs before sending `condor_rm`. I will introduce ExitCode 50667 for this. ## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-22T14:24:58Z) Some jobs are condor-rm'ed by Dagman when the DAG itself stops. I have not found any way to flag them They have `RemoveReason` like ``` DAG Removed: User removed scheduler job from queue. (by user crabtw) ``` or ``` DAG Abort: DAG is exiting and writing rescue file. (by user crabtw) ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-23T13:32:43Z) after reviewing the code https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/be37a0af0873e3612a646c22ef0a4a3509bc1fd4/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RetryJob.py#L671-L687 I got convinced that it already will go through CPU and Memory check if FJR is missing Indeed the evidence is that sometimes the classAd update done in the PostJob is not picked up in the monitoring, as I already saw when checking CRAB_TerminationFailure Overall there is a low rate of jobs with an inconsistent set of classAds (e.g. have different `RemoveReason` and `PeriodicRemoveReasons`) which popup when looking in fine details. Here's exit code for all jobs removed due to `RemoveReason"Removed due to wall clock limit` in last 30 days. There is all sort of exit codes (including 0) other than 50664, but those with exit code 80001 are less than 1 in 10^5 In conclusion, we have to live with the current situation.

title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9402: kill early  failing tasks
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer issue #9402: kill early  failing tasks

State: open
Opened: 2026-08-26T15:56:27Z
Labels: Type: Enhancement
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9402

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-08-26T15:56:27Z)

We have situations where some task is misconfigured and all jobs fail. Yet users may not notice/not care and we waste resources.
So as noted (in **bold**) in https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/wasted-cpu-time-corehours-in-crab/147739 we could

* kill task if success rate is e.g. < 80% after 100 jobs. No matter what.

This should be implemented along the lines of what done for excessive ASO failures, with dryRun mode, mail to operators, configurable threshold, and appropriate value for the CRAB_ForcefullyTerminated classAd

## Comment (belforte, 2026-08-26T16:04:00Z)

this is very similar to what current code is already supposed to do
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6c1e83e10af760bc2a62cc7b3c9a56d59fae3246/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L1761-L1764

But
* that has not been used in a very long time and I am not sure it would still wrok
* I never read that code with care and I do not understand it enough to say if it fits the need
* we want to add the kill step (like done for ASO) so that task is nor revived by a "crab resubmit"
* I think that failure/error fraction is a more useful threshold than absolute number of failures

OTOH, if we reuse existing code, so much the better, and otherwise may consider removing it. It was originally meant to give control to the users by specifying the max amount of failures deemed acceptable in a task, but in practice no user ever used the `failureLimit` configuration parameter and we indeed [marked](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile) it as "very dangerous".

## Comment (nausikt, 2026-09-07T12:15:01Z)

For clarity, could it possibly be that

You mean "kill task if **error rate** is e.g. **>** 80% after 100 jobs. No matter what." since this is much safer and well covered wasted tasks use-cases.

P.S. For example, tasks experienced transient issues may have success rate drop below 80% which will eventually completed most of the time.

## Comment (nausikt, 2026-09-07T12:19:12Z)

Or, in other words, should we instead state: "kill task if **success rate** < **20%**"?

## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-07T14:01:04Z)

success rate < 20% (or any other percentage) would kick in at 4 failed, 1 OK in the first five jobs. Too much aggressive IMHO.

There is no good way to deal with transient issues, once task is killed, is killed. The only way is to let enough jobs complete to stay clear of random fluctuations and apply a cut. That's why we need configurable thresholds:
After at least N jobs have completed, kill if at least X have failed (or less than Y succeeded).

## Comment (belforte, 2026-10-14T14:58:07Z)

Given what we have learnt so far, best is to identify tasks where first 20 jobs all fail, send a mail to operator, and investigate.
I suspect that "everything fails" is less frequent than people think.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-10-14T15:09:23Z)

question: do we count jobs including retries, or excluding retries ? is one of the two much easier to implement ?

Abort DAG and kill task ****") killMsg = "Killed by CRAB because output can't be placed at destination site." killMsg += "\nMake sure that your destination site is healthy and" killMsg += "\nthat you have enough free disk space there" killMsg += " before submitting again" self.killThisTask(killMsg) self.logger.info("Tag Jobs as ForcefullyTerminated") self.tagAllJobsInTask(ad='CRAB_ForcefullyTerminated', value='ASO') retmsg += '\ntoo Many Fatal ASO errors. title: dmwm/CRABServer issue #9423: protect against failure to submit task_proc_wrapper
body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9423: protect against failure to submit task_proc_wrapper State: closed Opened: 2026-09-17T17:02:51Z Closed: 2026-09-24T07:14:17Z Labels: Type: Bug, Status: Done URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9423 ## Opening post (belforte, 2026-09-17T17:02:51Z) Investigating ASO failures, I found a task with this with DAGstatus NOT_READY in the UI Then from `crab status` ``` Task name: 260916_101527:nstrautn_crab_Bpark_MiniAOD_DATA_2_2024_runG_PromptReco_SM Grid scheduler - Task Worker: - crab-prod-tw01 Status on the CRAB server: SUBMITTED Task URL to use for HELP: https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/260916_101527%3Anstrautn_crab_Bpark_MiniAOD_DATA_2_2024_runG_PromptReco_SM Dashboard monitoring URL: https://monit-grafana.cern.ch/d/cmsTMDetail/cms-task-monitoring-task-view?orgId=11&var-user=nstrautn&var-task=260916_101527%3Anstrautn_crab_Bpark_MiniAOD_DATA_2_2024_runG_PromptReco_SM&from=1789550127000&to=now Task bootstrapped at 2026-09-16 10:18:24 UTC. 98277 seconds ago Task bootstrapped on schedd more than 1637 minutes ago But no status info is available yet. If this persists report it to ``` Looking in SPOOL_DIR I found that Dagman was happily running, but the `task_process` directory had no logs. Transfer and status_cache scripts had never run. The bootstrap log in `_condor_stderr` reported ``` + chmod +x task_process/task_proc_wrapper.sh + condor_submit task_process/daemon.jdl ERROR: Failed to connect to local queue manager AUTHENTICATE:1006:exceeded 1789553924 deadline during authentication AUTHENTICATE:1004:Failed to authenticate using SCITOKENS ``` So somehow the submission failed dye to some odd error in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/be37a0af0873e3612a646c22ef0a4a3509bc1fd4/scripts/dagman/dag_bootstrap_startup.sh#L258 but `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh` kept going to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/be37a0af0873e3612a646c22ef0a4a3509bc1fd4/scripts/dagman/dag_bootstrap_startup.sh#L282 In a way this was intentional and supposed to be a "feature", since I could "fix" with `sudo su crabtw; condor_submit task_process/daemon.jdl` but in practice jobs have been submitted and executed for > 24h, resulting in ASO timeout in PostJob and total waste of CPU. I.e. we were assuming that the user would notify us of this unusual situation so we would investigate and correct. But it did not happen here, and we do not know how many other times. Options: 1. leave it 2. exit the script, so that dagman does not start. Easy and safe, but starting dagman by hand will be next to impossible, user will have to submit a new task. 3. retry the condor_submit in case it fails 4. send a message to operators in addition 5. investigate if `crab resubmit` could fix, esp. after 2. Which way to go ? ## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-23T16:45:13Z) safest option would be 6. exit the script and somehow mark the task as failed. * but submission of wrapper + dagman start are done in the bash script, while sending a msg to server or changing the status_cache.pkl require python. Introducing a new python script to be called only in this rare case seems too messy to me. Therefore: **Plan:** 1. retry condor_submit after 10 seconds 2. if it still fails, exit w/o starting dagman and let user contact us when they notice so we can say "submit again" ANyhow I have also asked SI to keep FS as first authentication method, which may help avoid timeouts like the one indicated in initial comment: https://gitlab.cern.ch/CMSSI/cmsgwms-htcondor-configurations/-/merge_requests/27 ## Comment (belforte, 2026-09-23T20:07:27Z) When the task wrapper fails to start an attempt to issue `crab resubmit` ends with ``` Error: Status information is unavailable, will not proceed with the resubmission. Try again a few minutes later if the task has just been submitted. ``` So it is pretty clear anyhow. And I see no reason to make this more complicated by trying to change task status in the DB.

Dear CERN Oracle Community,

Please take a moment to  read the following Service Change announcement, oriented towards making Oracle account passwords compliant with the CERN Password Rules.

https://cern.service-now.com/service-portal?id=outage&n=OTG0163272

Important dates to remember :

1-Oct-2026 Password validation campaign starts for PROD and non-PROD databases

11-Jan-2026 Campaign ends for non-PROD databases

5-Apr-2027 Campaign ends for PROD databases

Warning: accounts whose password have not been validated/verified will be locked.

Please take notice of potential impact when the clients use very old Oracle client libraries (older than 12c).

Please contact <email> if you have further questions

Nilo Segura
On behalf of the Oracle Support Team : IT/DA

 cms_analysis_reqmgr_r and cms_analysis_reqmgr_w

reply from Kate is fully reassuring

Kate

Labels: Status: Done
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9426

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-09-23T15:14:13Z)

I have found several removed jobs where classAds in MONIT are not what we expect from PostJob. As e.g. reported in #9398

As a possible way to mitigate we can keep jobs in the queue for some time after PostJob ran to give time to the spider to pick up things. It should pick ads from history in case, but... better to be safe.

`LeaveJonInQueue` is initially set to 30 hours after job termination
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/be37a0af0873e3612a646c22ef0a4a3509bc1fd4/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanCreator.py#L442-L445
which is OK with the 24h ASO timeout, but should be changed when using ASO-Rucio !!

Then  in PostJob
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/be37a0af0873e3612a646c22ef0a4a3509bc1fd4/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/PostJob.py#L2983-L2984

Should change to stay in queue for e.g. 30 more minutes (spider runs every 12 min)

body: # dmwm/CRABServer issue #9438: edmProvDump spits O(1GB) on stdout State: closed Opened: 2026-10-11T16:10:00Z Closed: 2026-10-12T11:04:12Z Labels: Type: Bug, Type: Enhancement, Priority: Critical URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9438 ## Opening post (belforte, 2026-10-11T16:10:00Z) A couple AP WEB_DIRs filled up suddenly and excessively, one reaching 100% Investigation (`du -sm`) showed that the increase was due to two tasks (one per AP) `261009_135121:slehti_crab_TTto2L2Nu_Summer24` and `261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO` where job stdout `job_out.X.Y.txt` was several hundreds of MB, up to almost a GB e.g. ```console [crabtw@vocms0122 261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO]$ ls -lh job_out.184.0.txt -rw-r--r-- 1 crabtw zh 898M Oct 9 23:20 job_out.184.0.txt [crabtw@vocms0122 261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO]$ ``` The problem came from failed attempt to compute PSet hash from user output file, in which case out script adds `edmProvDump` output to log, but somehow here that output was amazingly long... 20M lines !!! Here I captured beginning and end of the output prefixed with line number ``` [crabtw@vocms0122 261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO]$ grep -B2 -A10 -n edmProv job_out.184.0.txt 2748-==== PSet Hash computation STARTING at Fri Oct 9 20:50:52 2026 UTC ==== 2749-==== PSet Hash computation FINISHED at Fri Oct 9 20:51:30 2026 UTC ==== 2750:ERROR: PSet Hash missing from edmProvDump output. Full dump below. 2751----------Processing histories--------- 2752-History: { 2753- SIM [1] 2754- HLT [1] 2755- RECO [1] 2756- PAT [1] 2757- NANO [1] 2758-} 2759-History: { 2760- SIM [1] ``` ``` [crabtw@vocms0122 261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO]$ grep -B10 -A30 -n "Unable" job_out.184.0.txt 20431960- applyAlignment: bool tracked = false 20431961- } 20431962-ESModule: zdcTopologyEP NANO 20431963- parameters: { 20431964- @module_edm_type: string tracked = 'ESProducer' 20431965- @module_label: string tracked = 'zdcTopologyEP' 20431966- @module_type: string tracked = 'ZdcTopologyEP' 20431967- appendToDataLabel: string tracked = '' 20431968- } 20431969- 20431970:WARNING: Unable to parse WMCore's jobReport.json; FJR will not be useful. 20431971- Traceback (most recent call last): 20431972- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 221, in handleException 20431973- report = json.load(fh) 20431974- File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cs9_amd64_gcc11/external/python3/3.9.6-2c93591d796451daeaf67dc8130bfa35/lib/python3.9/json/__init__.py", line 293, in load 20431975- return loads(fp.read(), 20431976- File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cs9_amd64_gcc11/external/python3/3.9.6-2c93591d796451daeaf67dc8130bfa35/lib/python3.9/json/__init__.py", line 346, in loads 20431977- return _default_decoder.decode(s) 20431978- File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cs9_amd64_gcc11/external/python3/3.9.6-2c93591d796451daeaf67dc8130bfa35/lib/python3.9/json/decoder.py", line 337, in decode 20431979- obj, end = self.raw_decode(s, idx=_w(s, 0).end()) 20431980- File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cs9_amd64_gcc11/external/python3/3.9.6-2c93591d796451daeaf67dc8130bfa35/lib/python3.9/json/decoder.py", line 355, in raw_decode 20431981- raise JSONDecodeError("Expecting value", s, err.value) from None 20431982-json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) 20431983- 20431984:ERROR: Exceptional exit at Fri Oct 9 20:51:32 2026 UTC 80453: Unable to compute pset hash for job output. Got exception: 20431985-PSet hash missing from edmProvDump output. 20431986- 20431987-ERROR: Traceback follows: 20431988- Traceback (most recent call last): 20431989- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 505, in AddPsetHashFjr 20431990- raise ValueError("Process element not found under FrameworkJobReport") 20431991-ValueError: Process element not found under FrameworkJobReport 20431992- 20431993-During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: 20431994- 20431995-Traceback (most recent call last): 20431996- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 842, in 20431997- AddPsetHashFjr(report=rep, fjr_filename='FrameworkJobReport.xml') 20431998- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 519, in AddPsetHashFjr 20431999- raise ValueError(f"Error processing XML file: {str(err)}") 20432000-ValueError: Error processing XML file: Process element not found under FrameworkJobReport 20432001- 20432002-During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: 20432003- 20432004-Traceback (most recent call last): 20432005- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 847, in 20432006- AddPsetHashEdmProvDump(report=rep, scramTool=scram) 20432007- File "/srv/CMSRunAnalysis.py", line 479, in AddPsetHashEdmProvDump 20432008- raise Exception("PSet hash missing from edmProvDump output.") 20432009-Exception: PSet hash missing from edmProvDump output. 20432010- 20432011-== Execution site for failed job from site-local-config.xml: T2_CH_CERN 20432012-+ jobrc=69 20432013-+ set +x 20432014-== The job had an exit code of 69 [crabtw@vocms0122 261009_135106:slehti_crab_DYto2Mu_4Jets_M_50_Summer24_LO]$ ``` We clearly need to ensure that this output is "short". I am also amazed that the script could digest it all parse it for the pset hash ! ## Comment (belforte, 2026-10-12T07:36:39Z) one possibility is that failing tasks declared `events.root` as EDM type (via PoolOutputModule in the PSet) while successful jobs did not. The offending jobs were using NANOAODSIM as input and ran instances of `PostProcessor` ```python from PhysicsTools.NanoAODTools.postprocessing.framework.postprocessor import * ``` Here's the task PSET, which likely comes from NanoAODTools ... ```python #this fake PSET is needed for local test and for crab to figure the output filename #you do not need to edit it unless you want to do a local test using a different input file than #the one marked below import FWCore.ParameterSet.Config as cms process = cms.Process('NANO') process.source = cms.Source("PoolSource", fileNames = cms.untracked.vstring(), # lumisToProcess=cms.untracked.VLuminosityBlockRange("254231:1-254231:24") ) process.source.fileNames = [] process.maxEvents = cms.untracked.PSet(input = cms.untracked.int32(-1)) #process.maxEvents = cms.untracked.PSet(input = cms.untracked.int32(10000)) process.output = cms.OutputModule("PoolOutputModule", fileName = cms.untracked.string('events.root') ) process.out = cms.EndPath(process.output) ``` If CRAB had been told that `events.root` was not EDM in the FJR, it would not have tried to compute the PSet hash ! https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2e332185308e37417ed85e4f8e50652c9793cda4/scripts/job_wrapper/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L440-L442 ## Comment (belforte, 2026-10-12T07:38:12Z) should we use this as a last resort protection? ? https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/admin-manual/configuration/schedd.html#MAX_TRANSFER_OUTPUT_MB currently there is no limit ``` -1 # at: # raw: MAX_TRANSFER_OUTPUT_MB = -1 ``` ## Comment (belforte, 2026-10-12T09:38:03Z) I believe that I have found the reason for the problem, and created an Issue in CMSSW GH. But we need to protect CRAB no matter what. So will cut edmProvDump output in any case and add the `MAX_TRANSFER_OUTPUT_MB` to the schedd

## Comment (mapellidario, 2022-03-14T16:51:50Z)

I think this is a consequence of the py3 migration. In py2, `mydict.keys()` returns a list with a static snapshot of the keys of the dictionary. In python3, `mydict.keys()` is a dictionary view, which changes when the dictionary change.

My trivial approach would be to just replicate the py2 behavior in py3 with

```diff
-        blocksWithLocation = locationsMap.keys()
+        blocksWithLocation = list(locationsMap.keys())
[...]
-            secondaryBlocksWithLocation = secondaryLocationsMap.keys()
+            secondaryBlocksWithLocation = list(secondaryLocationsMap.keys())
```

However, if the dictionaries are not huge or and we do not repeat this many times, we can afford to copy them every time, as you did.

## Comment (belforte, 2022-03-14T17:03:02Z)

thanks @mapellidario . That explanation makes everything clear to me finally !
But all in all I would stick here with the dictionary copy, it is more clear.

OTOH... should we worry that there may be more places wherre something like this may have introduced a py2/py3 difference which is not immediately evident ?

## Comment (belforte, 2022-03-14T17:30:36Z)

Dario and myself reviewed all other places where a variable is assigned to `dict.keys()`, `dict.values()` or `dict.items()` and found no other places where the dictionary is modified before that values goes out of scope. So we are safe

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-01-25T12:12:51Z)

Fix https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/5983

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-01-27T13:44:02Z)

Fixes #7509

### status

condor_chirp is broken when running slc6 jobs: still work in progress

### description

I noticed a problem with the python used to retrieve the exit code in #7509 . It's caused by the new jobwrapper, since it does not load into the path any executable called "python", but only `python3`.

I also looked around and fixed all the instances that I could find of ambiguous `python` instead of `python3`.

### future work

We still have many `#!/usr/bin/python` and `#!/usr/bin/env python` that should become `#!/usr/bin/env python3`. I will do it at a later time. They are likely not causing any problem because we are not calling directly the `.py` files, but always using `python3 <myfile>.py`. Still, it's better to be consistent.

Eventually, I needed to have a more in-depth look at how environments
change inside the JobWrapper and I have not answered all the questions I have yet.
I will post this comment anyways not to keep the rest of the team in the dark.

Jobs that require cc7 or el8 work just fine. I may need to give them another look in the next few days, but I do not recall I found anything wrong. Some problems emerge with the new jobwrapper when we run slc6 jobs.

In the next sections, I will compare the two following tasks

- `task1` https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230216_093031%3Admapelli_crab_20230216_103029 . Task requiring slc6, TW that we have in production now with the following debug changes https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/compare/v3.221124...mapellidario:20230215_jobwr_dbg_1
- `task2` https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230216_093555%3Admapelli_crab_20230216_103554 . Task requiring slc6, TW from https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7510 with the same debug changes as above (https://github.com/mapellidario/CRABServer/compare/20230127_jobwr_2...mapellidario:CRABServer:20230215_jobwr_dbg_2)

####  `condor_chirp`. still open question

The condor_chirp command is a bash script [1] that uses a python version found by the gWMS script `gwms-python` [2].

This scripts are shipped to the container by glidein [3]. Nikos showed me an xml config where based
on the singularity container version (let's say rhel6), they decide which version of condor
(9.11 if i remember correctly) to use and which tarball to ship to the container (a condor 8 if I
remember correctly. yes, i know, they dont match, doesnt matter too much apparently).

Currently in production, when we run an slc6 job, `/srv/.gwms.d/bin/gwms-python`
selects python 2.7.13 and everything looks good. [4]

However, when we run an slc6 job with the new jobwrapper, `/srv/.gwms.d/bin/gwms-python`
selects python 2.6.6 and it breaks [5]

I need some more time to understand how `gwms-python` works and make sure that we provide a proper environment when it runs. Maybe I can just throw everything away and let it use the startup environment.

If I understand correctly, we may need to fix the environment for condor_chirp only when we need to use it to compute the exit code [6].

#### task_proc_wrapper. ok

we need to select which python version we should use for populating the `DEST_LFN` variable. The python that we use here is the default schedd one if I understand correctly, so using both py2 and py3 gives the proper result in both [7]

When we use py3 we have the usual TokenManager complaining that it can not find `import jwt`, but it does not seem to affect the outcome.

I would chose to use python3, as we do in this PR.

#### CMSRunAnalysis.sh, "import CMSRunAnalysis; CMSRunAnalysis.logCMSSW()". ok

The python that we use here depends on the COMP environment, so we need to switch to python3, which is what we do in this PR. [8]

---

Addendum, for future me who will wonder how i debugged things:

When we submit an job with a scram arch that requires slc6,
SI spins up an slc6 container where we run all our scripts into.
As stefano mentioned, the container that we run in is
`GWMS_SINGULARITY_IMAGE_HUMAN=/cvmfs/singularity.opensciencegrid.org/cmssw/cms:rhel6`

and can be explored on lxplus with

```
/cvmfs/singularity.opensciencegrid.org/cmssw/cms:rhel6/singularity -- bash
```

I still dont know how to replicate in lxplus what gwms does in the worken nodes, maybe we can just run https://github.com/glideinWMS/glideinwms/blob/master/creation/web_base/glidein_startup.sh, but i am ready to bet that a single script is not enough and that we need to access some tarballs that are on the frontend machine only.

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-02-20T17:36:19Z)

*Tested in `test12`. Will test in preprod again before merge.*

Use environment variable `CRABSERVER_LOGSTDOUT` to switch crablog's handlers, instead of checking `data.loggingFile` from `config.py`:
- `CRABSERVER_LOGSTDOUT=t` will output crablog to stdout.
- else to file using `TimedRotatingFileHandler` (previous behavior).

This will allow us to **deploy only k8s manifest, without changing content of `config.py`** to make log-to-stdout work properly. Make it more easy to operate when you hurry to roll everything back or after you are done rollback and want to deploy it again, without keep forget to apply `config.py`.

Env name and value come from new manifest [crabserver.yaml](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/eca72978f74ea49f020a31eee866bd96f0ba7ef2/kubernetes/cmsweb/services/crabserver.yaml#L65-L66) which also use in the [run.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/eca72978f74ea49f020a31eee866bd96f0ba7ef2/docker/crabserver/run.sh#L73).

Also, put `setFormatter` back to `TimedRotatingFileHandler` that I forget to add it in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7496.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-02-24T10:53:12Z)

> I rather worry about:
>
>     * where exactly do we keep track of all keys which may be in `tm_user_config` ?

As it shown in this PR, [RESTUserWorkflow](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/27fe22629968c70171c1a44976a6538cf702f823/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTUserWorkflow.py#L564) when we receive input from the user and [RESTWorkerWorkflow](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/27fe22629968c70171c1a44976a6538cf702f823/src/python/CRABInterface/RESTWorkerWorkflow.py#L157) when we use it.
You can see that it need to change both files, which I completely forgot to change it, thus this PR.
That why I am not merge it yet because I am not satisfy with current solution, waiting for new ideas/comments.

> general observation: all in all ['tm_user_config'] is "optional things" and it may be good to never take it for granted that all possible prams in there are present before using them in the code. In this way it is different from other tm_* params which comes from DB and thus are always present.

It fine for me if we treat all keys in `user_config` as optional and check if keys exist in TW instead.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-28T21:08:37Z)

thanks for thorough review, I will go through things tomorrow.

At the moment I will address your two questions

> Why secondary dataset is not support?

because it relies on lumi info to know which files from secondary dataset to couple with files in primary dataset for processing and without DBS there is no such info.
AFAIU secondary input in CMSSW works like this:
hey cmsRun, please process this file, one event at a time of course, and for each event look in those other files for the same event, and combine the data in memory so I can process child and parent at same time accessing objects in either.
In there event means the triplet (run/lumi/event).
I am not sure how CMSSW implements it, but I think it reads the list or (run/lumi/event) in all files indicated as secondary, and uses it to pick correct data. So the list of those file can'be "a 500TB, 100K file dataset"

>    I do not understand what you wrote in [RucioDataDiscovery.py#L367-L372](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/98b3af84f8fd3dfdcb64c86de625b9379b8bb893/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/RucioDataDiscovery.py#L367-L372). Could you explain?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-04-02T18:27:57Z)

thanks @novicecpp
good questions, I will address them in line below. If more is needed let's talk on MM or Zoom.
Of course there is not clear documentation in Rucio about those things !

1. Could you give me dataset name you use to test? I have strange feeling about how we decide if block is available on disk in the partial block's era and need to crosscheck.
   * I am afraid that exactly for that reason I do not have such dataset at hand, main problem is that details of what is on disk change. I tested by taking incomplete datasets via `if` in the code. Not ideal, I agree.

2. What is rucio replicas NOT AVAILABLE state mean?
   * if all files which belong to a dataset are AVAILABLE on that RSE, then the dataset replica status is AVAILABLE
      * I could not find a place in Rucio documentation where this is written. Diego told me this. And it matches my experience
   * NOT AVAILABLE can be any of the other possible replica states https://github.com/rucio/rucio/blob/ce39a0bf87105ff50fcc2a9ca5da69d187523f39/lib/rucio/db/sqla/constants.py#L107-L115 .
3. If Rucio reaper delete the files, is replicas still there and change from AVAILABLE state to another OR replicas object get delete from database?
   * We must not confuse file replica and dataset replica. Reaper deletes single files. When a file is deleted the dataset replica still exist on that RSE, but it lacks one file-replica, so it becomes not AVAILABLE. I **think** that it is done [here](https://github.com/rucio/rucio/blob/ce39a0bf87105ff50fcc2a9ca5da69d187523f39/lib/rucio/core/replica.py#L338-L345). If I read the code correctly the when a file replica is deleted, it also gets removed from DB. And again IIUC when a dataset replica has no more files is also removed, but I really do not have guts to fully understand https://github.com/rucio/rucio/blob/master/lib/rucio/core/replica.py and I hope it is not needed

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-04-04T10:40:06Z)

Before submitting a proper review i have a comment.

I know that we can always retrieve the time a task is added to the DB via its taskname (provided that we never change it), but I would prefer to have a column whose sole purpose is to tell me when the user first added the task to the DB. This can be useful for example when aggregating statistics about which dataset is requested when.

Let's say we have a plot "total size of input dataset to crab task vs submission day". If you change the `tm_start_time` after a taperecall, then the contribution of a single task to such plot will move from one day to another. The alternative would be to parse the submission day from the taskname, ugly.

The solution that I would prefer would be to use `tm_start_injection` [1] to compute the classads `CRAB_TaskSubmitTime` and `CRAB_TaskEndTime` .

At the moment, this column in the DB is empty, so some effort may be needed to make sure it is properly passed around the dagmansubmitter functions, but it seems it was designed exactly for this usecase.

# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #7623: jobwrapper - many small improvements

State: closed
Opened: 2023-04-28T17:02:17Z
Closed: 2023-05-16T10:50:51Z
Merged: 2023-05-16T10:50:51Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7623

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-04-28T17:02:17Z)

#### status

tested on test11

- [x] hammercloud https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230428_162937%3Admapelli_crab_jobwr5_20230428_182936
- [x] montecarlo  https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230428_164602%3Admapelli_crab_jobwr5_20230428_184559
- [x] retrieve logs of killed job: https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/230504_191507%3Admapelli_crab_jobwr5_20230504_211505

I propose to merge this PR, create a new tag and continue testing in testbed.

#### details

This PR gathers many small improvements to the jobwrapper.

First of all, I propose change how we manage stdout+stderr of cmsRun / user script. Instead of keeping it in the Popen stdout (which is a pipe [1], and hence in memory), we redirect both stdout and stderr to the file `cmsRun-stdout.log.tmp`. This has two main advantages for CRAB.

- We do not run out of memory if the job processes many events, as it can happen with automatic splitting on nanoaod.
- We can to retrieve the stdout+err from cmsRun if it gets killed by the periodic removal

We decided to buffer the stdout+stderr for up to one line. I am reluctant to buffer more than one line, I worry that it can cause stdout and stderr to go out of order with each other. I do not think it is necessary to turn off buffering.

It is possible that writing often to the local disk can increase I/O and slow down execution. We will keep an eye out for this.

Secondly, I added some auxiliary functions to `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.py` that allow to check the content of the files where we keep information about the cmsRun execution (`cmsRun-stdout.log`, `FrameworkJobReport.xml`, ... ).

Thirdly, I added a trap on sigterm. Combined with the previous two addition, this allows to print the partial cmsRun stdout+stderr in case the job is gracefully killed by condor, for example due to a periodic removal policy. Before this PR, we would have lost stdout+stderr entirely, since at the moment it makes sense to run run `CMSRunAnalysis.py:logCMSSW()` only after the cmsRun execution finishes. We already have a way of intercepting the sigterm from condor [2],  but `CMSRunAnalysis.py:logCMSSW()` requires `cmsRun-stdout.log` to be present on disk (and before this PR we only write such file after the cmsRun completes), so even if condor sends a sigterm to all the child processes and we catch the sigterm in cmsrunanalysis.py, there is no file on disk to dump when the job is killed. This is still untested, as i did not managed yet to have my jobs killed by a periodic removal.

Lastly, I decided to stop using `jobReport.json.$CRAB_Id` for extracting the chirp exit code. I do not want condor_chirp to use python to parse a json. I do not want to rely on `gwms-python` to discover python for me. Moreover, on the remote nodes we do not have `jq` and I did not find a valid alternative to parse a json with pure bash. I'd rather create a new file `jobReport.exitCode.txt` that only contains the exit code, that chirp can read with a simple `cat`.

[1] https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/blob/31d65166dc62c7251edd52890bc4ac2f0b79d7fe/src/python/WMCore/WMRuntime/Tools/Scram.py#L367
[2] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3d7cb32e23e1b3c0da6fd2f93c7f646f093509a5/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L54
[] bash stdout and stderr: https://stackoverflow.com/a/16283739
[] https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/stdbuf-invocation.html

---

Addendum

After reading [a.1], it is clear that dealing with termination signals does only depend on the receiving hand, it also depends on to which process the sigterm is sent to, whether only to the parent process or to the whole parent group.

In our case, we could catch the sigterm in cmsrunanalysis.py [a.2] only if condor sends a sigterm to all the processes in the `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh` group, for example. But this is not the default "send a sigterm" behavior. By default, only the parent process is killed, the child processes are killed independently only afterwards. As Stefano found, the condor docs are pretty vague [a.3].

In this PR, we could avoid writing `cmsRun-stdout.log.tmp` and only write to `cmsRun-stdout.log`, then hope that condor sends a sigterm to all the processes in the parent group id and let logCMSSW() print the cmsRun content.

However, using traps in `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh` feels a bit more robust to changes on how condor kills our processes. I would keep this PR as it is now.

[a.1] https://www.baeldung.com/linux/signal-propagation
[a.2] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3d7cb32e23e1b3c0da6fd2f93c7f646f093509a5/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L54
[a.3] https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/users-manual/priorities-and-preemption.html#details-about-how-htcondor-jobs-vacate-machines

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-05-12T10:04:52Z)

#### conclusion

Thank you Stefano, `print_line` adds a significant overhead. I will remove it

#### experiment

I created a script with only the `print_file` function and executed it on the output of [1]. Then I run the script twice,

- I set `keepAtStart=500`, `keepAtEnd=500`, `maxLineLen=30`, processing a file with 10k lines, 10k characters each line.
- `time print_file test.txt` takes 9s
- I used PS4, suggested at [2]
    ```bash
    set -x
    PS4='+ $(date "+%s.%N ($LINENO) ")'
    time print_file test1.txt
    ```
    in total it takes 12s (this has a 30% overhead, but allows to compute the time taken by each command). It shows that every execution of `read line` takes 7ms, then awk takes 4ms to 5ms.
- accounting for the overhead of PS4, we can estimate that for every line that we want to print `read line` takes 5ms and awk 3ms
- I repeated the experiment with shorter lines. `read line` takes less time, but awk still takes at least 2ms

Without executing `print_line` the script takes 0.4s **in total**.

#### Analysis

- if we do not use `print_line`, we can expect that printing 1000 lines takes about 0.5s (on an ssd) (0.5ms each line)
- if we use `print_line`, every line that we print "costs" at least 2ms (fixed, because of awk) and 1ms for every 1000 characters in the line (because of `read line`).

# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #7649: RUCIO_Transfers.py: Add RegisterReplicas action and separate transfer container from publish container.

State: closed

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-05-30T12:42:30Z)

This PR replaces https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7637, which introduces a major change besides new `RegisterReplicas` action, separating the published and transfer containers.

I use the `outputdataset` field from `transfers.txt` as publish container name. Then, modify `outputdataset` to `/PrimaryDataset/DatasetName_TRANSFER.{MD5OfTaskName[:8]}/USER` and use it as a transfer container name.

For example, given `/GenericTTbar/tseethon-integrationtest-12/USER` a  publish container name, we will get `/GenericTTbar/tseethon-integrationtest-12_TRANSFER.3b1e780f/USER` as a transfer container name.

I also split `RegisterReplicas.register()` into two methods, `addFileToRucio()` to register files to Rucio, and `addReplicasToContainer()` to add newly registered replicas to datasets in the transfer container to let Rucio do transfers. It will be reuse in `MonitorLockStatus` action class later to register transfer completed replicas.

File "/tmp/belforte/WMCore/src/python/WMCore/Services/pycurl_manager.py", line 338, in request
    curl.perform()
pycurl.error: (35, 'Peer does not recognize and trust the CA that issued your certificate.')
```

Current TW container misses `pandas` and a simple `pip install` failed. pff...

[*] in the end it works with my CERN certificate, fails with my INFN/Terena one. The latter works on lxplus, and aslo works with `curl https://cmsweb` from `crab-dev-tw01`.This points to something stale in `/etc/grid-security/certificates` .. oh well. I guess we do not want to solve all world's problems.

Up to you now if you want to setup a crontab with this on crab-...-tw... or rather make it work in the container first.

Grid authentication is always a pain.

problem was https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7681/commits/856ac04009f2f7cc3041774a78b0b3d5b4af5f74
that prepSandbox is needed to place a user script in the current directory, one step above $CMSSW_BASE !

Here's a sketch :
```
/srv                --> cwd. ScriptExe needs to be here
 /srv/CMSSW_13_1_0  --> $CMSSW_BASE: sandbox files picked from "user SCRAM tree" needs to be here
```
FYI @mapellidario

this is consistent with description of `inputFiles` configuration parameter in twiki:
```
The input files will be placed in the working directory where the users' application (e.g. cmsRun) is launched
```

The problem as I understand it now is that in `sandbox.tar.gz` we mix "scram" things and `inputFiles` taken from different places and archive both as "at same level", e.g. this
```
config.JobType.inputFiles = ['kh.tar', 'kh2.tgz', 'kh3.tar.gz']
```
picks files from the directory where `crab submit` is ran (could be anywhere) and in the sandbox we have
```
lib/
lib/slc7_amd64_gcc11/
biglib/
biglib/slc7_amd64_gcc11/
kh.tar
kh2.tgz
kh3.tar.gz
PSet.py
PSet.pkl
PSetDump.py
```
Now some files need to be placed in `/srv` on the WN, some in `/srv/CMSSW_x_y_x`
Current code places expands the sandbox in both places. Ugly, but works.

I do not see a simple way to put each file "only where it is needed" w/o using two tar files. One for `$CMSSW_BASE/...`, one for `/srv`. Maybe those can still be combined in a single sandbox etc. but code changes are needed at least both on client and job wrapper.

A simpler possibility is maybe to modify https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2c31e26c5903fbce0bcbe68f1217ed150ea043bf/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L385 to put needed files in $CMSSW_BASE and do w/o https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2c31e26c5903fbce0bcbe68f1217ed150ea043bf/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L407. But I am not sure if we have a good way of marking which files need to go in $CMSSW_BASE. An explicit list will quickly get obsolete and/or loose client/server syncronization

@mapellidario what do you think ? We need some good idea here !

No wonder that I was always confused as to where the sandbox files go, they go in two places but are only needed in one !
To add to confusion `PSet` is moved from `$CMSSW_BASE` to `/srv` in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/2c31e26c5903fbce0bcbe68f1217ed150ea043bf/scripts/CMSRunAnalysis.py#L414-L415 even if it was there already !

## Comment (mapellidario, 2023-07-26T16:09:35Z)

#### problem

Despite pylint does not find any problem [1], the changes proposed with this PR make appear a bug that was there for a long time. We are using `extConfSchedds` before it is defined [2].

That happens because when we first read the config properly from the web, we remove the `"modes"` key from the dict https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1ebaa01e363c4ed6c0e31564f1590548a7dfb962/src/python/CRABInterface/Utilities.py#L144

Then, the config is no longer available on the web, we use the cached value, the value returned by `retrieveConfig()` is the one of the last time the web was ok and it does not contain the "modes" key, so we skip `if 'modes' in extConfCommon:`, we do not define `extConfSchedds`, but we try to read from it later on.

#### possible solutions

I would either remove

1. https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1ebaa01e363c4ed6c0e31564f1590548a7dfb962/src/python/CRABInterface/Utilities.py#L144

2. or https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/1ebaa01e363c4ed6c0e31564f1590548a7dfb962/src/python/CRABInterface/Utilities.py#L154-L155

I tested 2. and all looks ok, however you may have a better idea of why 1. and 2. are there, so I think it should you the one who decides which solution is the best

---

[1] https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/job/DMWM-CRABServer-PR-pylintpy3/377/artifact/pylintpy3Report.json in this pylint report there is no mention to `extConfSchedds`

Maybe moving L156 to L125 is a better solution ?

I imagined, but i never passed an "accept all" argument to SQL and needed to try it anyways :)

Regarding the solution for the pylint complain.
There is a difference between "static class variables" [a] and "instance variables" [b]. See [1]. Your changes in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/commit/4335bdb74de36c04da0bbf560f2773472db7e296 effectively changed `config`, `restHost` and `dbInstance` from "instance variables" to "static class variables".
Is this a problem? I do not think so. Since TapeRecallManager is likely a singleton (a single instance of the class will ever exist at any time), so it should not make any difference if those variable to be "static class var" or "instance var" . Moreover, your changes are consistent with the other variables (`pollingTime`, `rucioClient`, ...) in TapeRecallManager.py and in TapeRecallStatus.py.

So ok, all good for me

---

[1] https://stackoverflow.com/a/43921843

[a]

```python
class MyClass():
    my_static_class_var = None
```

[b]

```python
class MyClass():
    def __init__():
        self.my_instance_var = None
```

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #7870: Including -stable suffix to crabserver images

State: closed
Opened: 2023-09-12T13:24:26Z
Closed: 2023-09-13T10:30:56Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7870

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-09-12T13:24:26Z)

I got a request from @arooshap to add `-stable` suffix to the crabserver image tag to comply with the new retention policy of cmsweb's space.
(Aroosha, please correct me if I am misunderstanding.) The new retention policy guarantees keeping the latest 3 tags, and older tags **without getting pulled** longer than 30 days will get deleted.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-12T13:28:16Z)

yeah.. it is not clear to me what the point is. If everybody marks their images as `-stable` it would be easier to simply change the policy like e.g. you did for CRAB repository on registry.cern.ch

Also we surely have nothing against deleting images which were not pulled in one month, not even to test them !

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-09-12T13:40:59Z)

> Also we surely have nothing against deleting images which were not pulled in one month, not even to test them !

The case is some legacy software running on a production VM that gets updated once a year.
It also happened to us once early this year, IIRC. Fortunately, we did not need it or rebuild it.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-12T13:46:10Z)

hmmm I must have misunderstood the policy.
I thought: delete after 30 days images which were never pulled, not images which were not pulled in last 30 days !
Indeed we'd like to retain running images as long as we use them.

## Comment (arooshap, 2023-09-12T13:46:36Z)

@novicecpp Thanks for making the changes.

@belforte The reason why we are enforcing this is because we want to ensure that despite the deletion policies, the images that are critical to us, and are deployed in production, remain available. To give you an example, the current image that is deployed in the production cluster for crabserver no longer exists in registry.cern.ch. So, if something happens and the service restarts in the production, it will lead to the `ImagePullBack` error, and thus, compromise the availability of the service.
Secondly, any image that is marked with this particular suffix is immutable because of the immutability rules that we have set up in the registry.

## Comment (arooshap, 2023-09-12T13:48:03Z)

Also please free to participate in the discussion that we are having regarding this issue at https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSKUBERNETES-241.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-12T13:52:38Z)

thanks @arooshap  I second Valentin's comment that screenshots are hard to read and those rules a bit hard to understand anyhow. I also suggest to do like Wa has done, to keep last N tags forever. Having only time-based expiration may not do what we want.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-12T14:26:55Z)

I have added a couple line to the JIRA: https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSKUBERNETES-241?focusedId=4935495&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-4935495

@novicecpp , I suspect that we do not want to tag all builds as `-stable` and have production image replaced via a bunch of test builds. Note that even if we do not use it we e.g. create a new crabserver image everytime we build in order to get a  nee TW or Publisher. Maybe we need a new Jenkins project to declare a tag as stable.
Yeah... a bit too much work for my taste, maybe limp along with a script to be run by hand on lxplus ?

## Comment (arooshap, 2023-09-12T14:50:41Z)

@belforte another option might be to just make sure that whenever you're deploying in production, you also tag it with stable? From our side, we have changed the deploy-srv script to make sure that if you are deploying an image in the production cluster, it has a stable suffix in its name, otherwise, it issues an error.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-12T14:55:52Z)

@arooshap yes, that's same as I was saying, implementation details aside :-)  Sort of wrap deploy-srv with something that marks the image as stable. A script of ours, a script of yours, an option to deploy-srv, an action that we do via Jenkins (we use Jenkins to build images, we can have an option in the build). Of course the flow should be build-test-markAsStable-deployInProd.

## Comment (amaltaro, 2023-09-12T15:10:15Z)

> From our side, we have changed the deploy-srv script to make sure that if you are deploying an image in the production cluster, it has a stable suffix in its name, otherwise, it issues an error.

@arooshap has this been announced anywhere? Since we migrated to CMS Talk, I failed to properly follow things up(!)

> > From our side, we have changed the deploy-srv script to make sure that if you are deploying an image in the production cluster, it has a stable suffix in its name, otherwise, it issues an error.
>
> @arooshap has this been announced anywhere? Since we migrated to CMS Talk, I failed to properly follow things up(!)

@amaltaro Here is the ticket where Valentin requested to do that: https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSKUBERNETES-237. For the services running in the production cluster, including the dmwm namespace, I have already tagged the images with the stable suffix and redeployed them with the stable variant.

Thanks everyone for comments in this PR.

I am closing this PR because we do not want to have every release tag become stable tag.

## Opening post (kpedro88, 2023-09-19T13:09:56Z)

This PR is the CRAB version of https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42798.

It is already unnecessary to use the `-p` or `--parameter-set` flag before specifying the `config.py` file for `cmsRun`, so this PR can be merged immediately with no change in functionality.

After https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 is merged, subsequent CMSSW releases will no longer support the `-p`, `--parameter-set` flags; the `config.py` file will always be provided as a positional argument. (This goes toward better command-line argument support following Python standards.)

Ok, found it.

when calling without passing a username [1], the line

```python
            validate_str('username', param, safe, RX_USERNAME, optional=True)
```

Adds `"username" = None` to the arguments [2], since we specify `optional=True`.

This is why i think we need to add additional checks to make sure that the username is properly set when we actually need it.

[1]

<details>

both

```python
            downloadFromS3(crabserver=self.crabserver,
                        filepath=localSandboxPath,
                        objecttype='sandbox', logger=self.logger,

                        # username=username
                        username=""
                        )
```

and

```python
            downloadFromS3(crabserver=self.crabserver,
                        filepath=localSandboxPath,
                        objecttype='sandbox', logger=self.logger,
                        tarballname=sandboxFilename,
                        # username=username
                        )
```

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/84ea9f28d724b4999fc0d80d18ff4fdcd7336491/src/python/ServerUtilities.py#L761-L762

> does username="" fail even if you specify optional=False

yeah, because as mentioned in the details under [1] in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7892#issuecomment-1735566976 , when we use `username=""` the client does not even set the argument in the request, so the validation with `optional=False` fails.

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-01-26T14:57:19Z)

Related to #6493

### status

Tested, ready to be reviewed

### Description

The purpose of this PR is to run the scripts GenerateMonit, CheckTapeRecall, aso_metrics_ora and ReportRecallQuota inside docker containers.

- GenerateMonit.py runs inside a crabtaskworker container.
- CheckTapeRecall.py, aso_metrics_ora and ReportRecallQuota runs inside a python:3.8

design choices:

- run script inside a docker container. The script runs once per `docker run`
- script output:
    - every script has it's own application log, same as before
    - every script prints to stdout. if the script fails, then the stdout is saved in a file in `/tmp/monit-*.txt`
    - [ ] ? shall we get rid of the application log and send everything to stdout?

next steps

- [x] merge this PR
- [ ] change puppet qa and master so that runcontainer.sh is taken from master branch (not from the branch of this PR)
- [ ] disable scripts on crab-preprod-tw02, enable script on crab-prod-tw02

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-04-18T14:39:12Z)

@novicecpp

> Quick question: could you please remind me why we have 2 containers?

So, `GenerateMONIT.py` script requires `htcondor` to collect information from the schedulers, such as how many jobs are running or idle, how many task_proc, how many dagmans, etc... So I decided to just use the TW container for that script.

Since I did not manage to install numpy on the TW container using the spec files, I decided that the other scripts can be run from a plain usual debian python docker container, where we can install what we want, for example numpy and pandas. I did not try to install and setup `htcondor` on this container. At this point I think we can stay with this for a bit, since when we will have the pypi containers, we can switch to those instead and drop these two containers.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-04-15T11:34:50Z)

Answering your questions:

> what is the purpose of `cicd/buildtools/Dockerfile` ?  I can't find where it is used

It is Dockerfile to build `registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/buildtools`, container we use in this CI (as seen in [line 25](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/.gitlab-ci.yml#L25)).
I will add README.md and short script for building this image.

> with reference to the `build_docker` stage, where is `${CI_PROJECT_DIR}` defined ? And how does the GH code gets there ?

See https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/variables/predefined_variables.html

All details about sync, setup variables, credentials, runner, still not ready yet.
Especially sync, I still have no conclusion about it, either via custom script or webhook magic.
Currently, I push to gitlab directly when I want to run pipeline.

> I know nothing about kaniko, hopefully I can live for a while w/o it

It is tools to build docker container in userspace. I plan to convert to [CERN](https://gitlab.cern.ch/gitlabci-examples/build_docker_image/)'s template later then ask for help from CERN IT.
For now, please consult [upstream docs](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko) directly.

> what does it do the line `  - !reference [.default_rules, rules]` in the `gitlab-ci.yml` ?

https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/jobs/job_control.html#reuse-rules-in-different-jobs

I use it to apply the rules define in [.gitlab-ci.yml#L9-L11](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/acbef6d60cbaf9cccd291d9216576fbae756b15a/.gitlab-ci.yml#L9-L11), i.e., make all jobs run only when tag name is prefix with `pypi-`.

> what is `name: registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/buildtools` ? Something I am not familiar with becasue it is part of the pypi build which I have not digested ?

Image name of docker-runner to run in this job (see also the propose of `cicd/buildtools/Dockerfile` I answered above).
You can choose any image you want for docker-runner, or use default one (setup in runner config) and install/pull/download later.

> IIUC gitlab runner (?) can do ssh into TW VM's as crab3 user. Via its public key. How can this bypass 2FA ? AFAICT we onnly have `cmsbuild` in TW's `.ssh/authorized_keys`

Whitelist the runner host, like we do with Jenkins's hosts, and I use different ssh key to access.

To get a baseline, I timed the use case which gave origin to this https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/crab-task-queued-on-command-submit-for-a-while/39714  i.e.

code is like
```python

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-07T13:36:34Z)

>      IIUC, WMCore Configuration does not have a live configuration update, so updating the puppet will not affect the running process immediately (unless it restarts itself, which is pretty rare).

True.  But Publisher calls executes TaskPublish.py via
`python3 <path>/TaskPublish.py --conf .... --taskname ....`
and it uses ` config.General.taskFilesDir` to know where to pick the JSON input file for every task.

If we move files to a different direcotry `/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles` instead of `/data/srv/Publisher_Files` that and possibly other things will break if the directory content is not ported over.

I think that we should stop the container and start with a modified runContainer which mounts the old directory in the new place or something like that.

I am starting to worry that this is not fully under control yet.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-07T13:37:33Z)

:scream:

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-07T13:55:46Z)

code aside, isn't the true that we simply want to do `mv Publisher_Files Publisher/PublisherFiles` ?
Maybe as simple as
Stop containers, mv  directories in /data/container, run puppet, cross fingers, restart containers ?

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-07T14:05:31Z)

No no.

In the `master` branch,  we do `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/PublisherFiles:/data/srv/Publisher_files` (Reminder, `-v` or "bind mount" format is `-v <host_path>:<container_path>`).
This PR, I do `-v /data/container/Publisher_schedd/PublisherFiles:/data/srv/Publisher/PublisherFiles`.

No need to move data in the host space, only stop the Publisher before applying the Puppet.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-05-07T14:10:14Z)

Beg to disagree.
I think it will be more clear and easier to support if directory structure in the host matches what's used in the container, and have a single mount point for `-v /data/container/Publisher_rucio:/data/srv/Publisher`. Once Publishers are stopped, there's no cost in one `mv`
But of course we can get there in steps :-)

overall I have no problems with this, other than the concern about the transition from old to new configuration.

Ah...I understand you now.
We cannot mount to `/data/srv/Publisher` directly because it contains `manage.sh/start.sh/stop.sh/etc` scripts.
I incline to your idea, but we need to rewire the path inside the container a bit (from `/data/srv/Publisher/logs` to something like `/data/srv/Publisher/hostdisk/logs`.

Let me close this and open another issue/pr for it.

Thanks for comments Stefano, especially on how Publisher work!.

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-05-21T13:32:09Z)

Complete the https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8401

The release pipeline is based on [build-deploy-test](https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/technical/crab-cicd/gitlab/pipelines/build-deploy-test.html) pipeline but has 2 more stages:
- `prepare_release`: changing the version number in source files.
- `tagging_release`: tagging docker images with the release name.

The git tag name must match `v3\.[0-9]{6}.*` regex in order to trigger above jobs.
The final docker image tag, `RELEASE_NAME`, will be `v3.YYMMDD-stable` as we agreed in the issue.

This change also allow to do force release by pushing the git tag name same as above condition (the convention is `v3.YYMMDD__somestring`), provides `RELEASE_NAME=final-tag-name-including-stable` and `SKIP_DEPLOY=t` variable to CI.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-22T11:22:25Z)

This will be long explanation. Please bear with me.

2 things we rely on:
1. We use the pushing tag (`git push <remote> <tag>`) as the way to trigger the pipeline.
2. The release flow will be the same as we do now; go to the release page in GH and create a new release. From there, we use the tools to sync the release tag to Gitlab and trigger Gitlab CI.

(The second mechanism is still not yet finalized, but we can simulate it by simply **pushing** the tag with the same name as the release tag, directly to Gitlab to trigger the pipeline.)

"To trigger the pipeline" in this context means CI selecting the jobs in the `.gitlab-ci.yml` where the `rules` directive of the jobs are satisfied. Then, puts these jobs together and creates a pipeline to run. The rules for `if` directive is test against the CI variables defined each trigger. If the rule does not match, next rule will be evaluate. If no job matches the conditions, no pipeline will be run.

Reading the rule is a bit tricky here because Gitlab offered the yaml tag `!reference` as the way to reference the rule defined in hidden keys.

For example, job `get_env` at [L26-L27](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/068530f45109e7efcd78b1c1eafba3b624c9fe1b/.gitlab-ci.yml#L26-L27) define the rule as:

```yaml
get_env:
  rules:
    - !reference [.default_rules, default]
```

And the key `.default_rules` we define in here is:
```yaml
.default_rules:
  default:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /pypi-.*/
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /v3\.[0-9]{6}.*/
```

Make `get_env` equivalent to:
```yaml
get_env:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /pypi-.*/
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG =~ /v3\.[0-9]{6}.*/
```

This rule means to run this job only when `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` matches the regex `pypi-.*`, OR `v3\.[0-9]{6}.*`.

For `$CI_COMMIT_TAG`, this variable is only available when pushing the tag.

Here is the base "Build-Deploy-Test" pipeline which use the `.default_rules:default`:

![320979971-67321507-67ff-4d62-98a6-0ba484b21d3a](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/96f7500a-7863-4b4e-a841-b19f8e06c768)

Here is the "Release Pipeline" of this PR which some jobs only have `.default_rules:release` rules ([#7420156](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/7420156)):

![Screenshot from 2024-05-22 11-29-00](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/1b474515-f8ec-4712-aed9-d1f0eb945a51)

In some cases, you want to run only some jobs, not all-or-none. One way you can do this is to let users provide some variables and add rules to explicitly not trigger the job. In our case, we want to skip the testing part to release the new image immediately.

For example, `deploy_server` job:

```yaml
deploy_server:
  rules:
    - if: $SKIP_DEPLOY
      when: never
    - !reference [.default_rules, rules]
```

Which mean, if `$SKIP_DEPLOY` is exist, do not run the `deploy_server`. If not, checking next rule.

Here is the pipeline when `$SKIP_DEPLOY` is defined ([#7401218](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/7401218)):

![Screenshot from 2024-05-22 13-24-32](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/0ba0aeb9-12e1-4242-86eb-3d90a5b9c36e)

You can supply any variable to the pipeline each for trigger, by providing the [push option](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/push_options.html#push-options-for-gitlab-cicd) `ci.variables=VARIABLE_NAME=value` when pushing the tag.

The `$RELEASE_NAME` is generated from [parseEnv.sh](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/068530f45109e7efcd78b1c1eafba3b624c9fe1b/cicd/gitlab/parseEnv.sh#L23) in the [get\_env](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/068530f45109e7efcd78b1c1eafba3b624c9fe1b/.gitlab-ci.yml#L25) job which simply appends the `-stage` to `$CI_COMMIT_TAG`, and will be used to re-tag docker image later in the [release\_stable](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/068530f45109e7efcd78b1c1eafba3b624c9fe1b/.gitlab-ci.yml#L216) job. However, to trigger the pipeline from the same commit again, you need the different git tag. Different tag mean different release image tag too. So, `$RELEASE_NAME=tagname` allows you to override the final image tag to whatever you want.

For example, push the tag with name `v3.YYMMDD__manual1`, and push variable `$RELEASE_NAME=v3.YYMMDD-stable` to have final docker image tag `v3.YYMMDD-stable`, and `SKIP_DEPLOY=t` to skip all testing steps.

(The code need some updates to make it more clear, will do it tomorrow).
