## Comment (novicecpp, 2024-05-27T09:19:19Z)

> btw, what's the bad side of forgetting to tag locally before pushing ? is that something that can be (easily) corrected in case ?

Let imagine when you are in hurry and you want to release master immediately.
You go to your local CRABServer directory, current branch is not master because you are testing new multiprocess feature, let call `my-multiprocessor`, then you tag, and you push to gitlab.
The tag you push is actually from latest commit of your branch `my-multiprocessor`, so pipeline build your commit instead of from `master`.

This kind of situation I would like to avoid.

For how we trigger the pipeline to force release, push options is how I "hack" to force pipeline to run. I would like to start from "what should it be" first. But let talk about this in the issue.

# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #8483: Triggering release pipeline via Github Actions

State: closed

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8483

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-06-10T11:52:11Z)

The last part for https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8401. This PR is adding 2 new pipelines:

1. Github Actions: Pipline to trigger another pipeline in [crab3/CRABServer](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/)'s Gitlab-CI.

The pipeline only triggers when push "Publish release" button on [creating a new release's page](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/releases/new).  The job trigger the Gitlab-CI pipeline by running the `curl` command to `https://gitlab.cern.ch/api/v4/projects/<project_id>/trigger/pipeline` endo. The API needs branch/tag to trigger and a token to authenticate. Full API documentation is on <https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/triggers/>.

The token that is used here is "Trigger API token", created on Gitlab's `crab3/CRABServer`, in repository's CI/CD setting.

The only variable we pass through the API is the name of the new tag, the `GITHUB_REF_NAME`.

2. Gitlab-CI: pipeline to pull new tags from GitHub to Gitlab

This pipeline only have single job `sync_release_from_github` doing 2 steps: one is to clone the new tag from `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, and then push it to `crab3/CRABServer`. When it pushed to `crab3/CRABServer`, the [release pipeline](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8421) will be triggered.
The credential that is used to push there is the ssh-key attached to the `crabint1` account, so it will not expire as long as the `crabint1` account is still active. Note that `Developer` access is grant to `crabint1` in order to allow to push.

The interaction diagram between GitHub Action and Gitlab-CI is shown in the following image:

![trigger_from_gh drawio(1)](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/assets/2346664/93524b70-64d0-4c63-a5e4-11271d3752d5)

If we simply want the latest `23.0.X`, we can use `==23.0.*`.

In we instead use ` ~=23.0.12`, it means that we tried and tested 23.0.12, it works, we are satisfied with and please pip do not pick anything previous that, if there is another package that requires htcondor 23.0.5, pip will fail.

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-06-17T12:49:05Z)

Fixes #8504

## status

tested:

- images have been built and tagged in this pipeline [1]
- I run the script on crab-dev-tw02 [2] and data arrived in opensearch [3]

## details

I removed the old docker images, based on pure python and rpm taskworker.

I migrated the same logic to a new docker image inside `monit_pypi` directory.

I added a stage in the pipeline that builds the new monit docker image every time we build taskworker and crabserver images. it takes only 2min, but if this annoys people than we can add some logic to skip this build for most cases.

Every time we build a new monit image, it is tagged with `registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:${IMAGE_TAG}.monit` and pushed.

I added a new tag retention policy in harbor [4] so that we keep the latest 5 images that match `v3.*.monit`.

when the image tag matches `v3.*.*` (or better,, when the pipeline satisfies the rule `.default_rules["release"]`), the new monit image is also tagged with `registry.cern.ch/cmscrab/crabtaskworker:v3.latest.monit` and pushed.

## open questions

I propose to change the crontabs to always use `v3.latest.monit`, so that we can forget about deploying the new docker images for the monitoring scripts, and embrace "continuous delivery" at its fullest :)

If we do not like to do this for production monitoring, I sugggest to at least do it with test monitoring, the one that currently runs in `crab-dev-tw04`. This can be a nice exercise for Vijay.

---

[1]

- https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRABServer/-/pipelines/7583357/builds

[2]

```bash
bash -x runContainer.sh -v v3.latest.monit -s TaskWorker_monit_generatemonit -c "python3 /data/srv/monit/GenerateMONIT.py"
bash -x runContainer.sh -v v3.latest.monit -s TaskWorker_monit_checktaperecall -c "python3 /data/srv/monit/CheckTapeRecall.py"
bash -x runContainer.sh -v v3.latest.monit -s TaskWorker_monit_asometrics -c "python3 /data/srv/monit/aso_metrics_ora.py"
bash -x runContainer.sh -v v3.latest.monit -s TaskWorker_monit_reportrecallquota -c "python3 /data/srv/monit/ReportRecallQuota.py"
```

[3]

https://monit-opensearch.cern.ch/dashboards/goto/8ec71c78057c6ea3150334053ae136ee

Fix https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8428

New `ChildWorker` module to spawn the child process from slave to run [work()](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/40a796ffe3d1c7b1b2cddf6a6e74c3b08e2b5a3a/src/python/TaskWorker/Worker.py#L94-L120) (for example, `handleNewTask` in [Handler.py#L153](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/43a8454abec4059ae5b2804b4efe8e77553d1f38/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py#L153)).

The module can handle timeout (via SIGALARM), coredump, normal error. Then, propagate errors in form of exception back to slave, and to the caller properly.

This mode(?) is behind the feature flags `config.FeatureFlags.childWorker`, can enable it from TW config file.
The TW config will have additional lines:

```python
config.section_("FeatureFlags")
config.FeatureFlags.childWorker = True
config.FeatureFlags.childWorkerTimeout = 3600 # 1 hours
```

the problem is that `HTCondorLocator` is imported in the `TaskWorkerConfig.py`, therefore before the env.var. is set in `Main.py`
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/9be641e6de5358ab5b34a8489ebf5e11150e12d3/src/python/TaskWorker/Main.py#L78-L84
So HTCondorLocator always has v1 bindings, which means that `schedd` object in DagmanSubmitter is a v1 object to which we pass a v2 Submit object causing the failure.

A drastic solution "at the root" would be to remove this form the configuration file, we never use it to pick the function for selecting schedulers anyhow and may very well hardcode the use of `capacityMetricsChoicesHybrid`. See
https://gitlab.cern.ch/ai/it-puppet-hostgroup-vocmsglidein/-/blob/master/code/templates/crabtaskworker/taskworker/TaskWorkerConfig.py.erb#L112
and
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6cacb768c2c2361497841004f14185ce0b4e2fa0/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DagmanSubmitter.py#L242-L246

Another (better) possibility could be to replace in the `TaskWorkerConfig.erb`
```
config.TaskWorker.useHtcV2 = <%= @tw_useHtcV2.to_s %>
```
with
```
import os
os.environ['useHtcV2'] =  "<%= @tw_useHtcV2.to_s %>"
```
and move `import HTCondorLocator` after that.
so that the `TaskWorkerConfig.py` file will look like
```python
import os
os.environ['useHtcV2'] = "True"
import HTCondorLocator
config.TaskWorker.scheddPickerFunction = HTCondorLocator.capacityMetricsChoicesHybrid
```
Also this line needs to be moved down
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/6cacb768c2c2361497841004f14185ce0b4e2fa0/src/python/TaskWorker/Main.py#L10

This surely is less work, and I will give it a try to confirm the bug and the solution. But I fear it will be horribly obscure, even if we plan to remove the v2 vs. v1 sometimes next year and become v2 only getting rid of all these `if`.

I am very tempted to choose the "CLEANUP" way. and get rid of the `config.TaskWorker.scheddPickerFunction`

We are somehow changing the configuration file semantics: from the POV of the TW code, the information will be in the `configuration` object **and** in the environment.  I'd rather have a string in the config than an import and a  pointer to a function. For my taste people tried to be too smart here.

Try to fix https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8436 ~~with over complicate solution.~~

The idea is to use `argparse` to help to parse arguments. Bash is too hard to manage.

Here is how process are called:

ENTRYPOINT (run.sh) -> manage.py (shared in 3 services) -> manage.sh -> [crab-taskworker/crab-publisher/wmc-httpd].

- Ideally, manage.sh should change into python module. But too much work for now.
- pass argument to manage.sh via env vars (we can get rid this line if we change it into python module).
- start.sh/stop.sh/env.sh also shared, just interface to manage.py.

`env.sh` is a bit special. I print (echo) the env vars that would like to use inside `manage.sh` then I wrap it in env.sh with `eval` command. So, to source env vars you can simply run `source ./env.sh`.

## Opening post (jannakam, 2024-08-16T09:54:18Z)

Issue #8522
The following commit includes the following changes:

**.gitlab-ci.yml file:**
- Switched from kaniko to dind (Docker-in-Docker) service. Applied to these jobs: build_rest_image, build-image (formerly build_tw_image), and build_crabtwfilebeat_image.
- Implemented registry caching using the Docker Buildkit tool in jobs build_rest_image and build_image. This uploads an image cache into the registry and pulls from it every time a new image is built, then replaces it with a new cache incase something has changed. Notice this in the use of the same naming of the image 'pypi-$(REST_Instance}-cache' as a parameter for 'cache-to' and 'cache-from' flags, which will pull the current user's test environment from the .env file saved as an artifact in the pipeline.

**Dockerfile:**
- Removed line 143 which was creating a duplicate image
- Added the changing of user ownership manually to the relevant lines of code in the Dockerfile

**Other:**
- Configured a custom runner for compatibility with the dind service. see https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/docker/using_docker_build.html#docker-in-docker-with-tls-enabled-in-the-docker-executor

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2024-08-30T10:10:34Z)

Hello Stefano
Apologies! I wanted to check if this is needed at all.

Rucio should not create transfer requests for expired rules by itself. Have you observed otherwise?
Why do you think this is needed?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-30T10:42:57Z)

It is about races.
We found that expired rules were sticking around for longish time because they had hanging FTS requests stuck in "stage from tape". Since delete has 1h grace period and the daemon which checks for expired rules and the one which submits FTS requests are asynchronous of each other, we are trying to minimize the chance that more FTS transfer requests are issued.

I agree that if we do not do this, eventually it should all clear up by itself. But in a situation like last week, were a user had too many ongoing recalls and we had him kill all tasks, the sooner we remove stuff, the better.

Reference: https://its.cern.ch/jira/browse/CMSDM-198?focusedId=6502570&page=com.atlassian.jira.plugin.system.issuetabpanels:comment-tabpanel#comment-6502570

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2024-08-30T12:46:54Z)

For the ticket you mentioned above, no new requests were being submitted after the rule was marked for deletion.
The issue was that the DB transaction in which a rule is moved from the `rules` table to the `rules_history` table was failing.
But the rule was not being picked up by daemons responsible for initiating transfers.

Now, this 1 hr grace period is what I wanted to check. i.e what purpose was it supposed to serve.
And if new submissions are tried for rules that are to expire in an hour.

In any case, this PR does no harm. So, for me, this is a good thing to do.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-30T13:02:18Z)

>  this 1 hr grace period is what I wanted to check. i.e what purpose was it supposed to serve.

AFAIU it is a protection again operator mistakes, giving people 1h to roll back after a "OOPS I did not want to do that" !

It may still make sense for when users will managed their data via Rucio. For a fully automated DM-WM setup as you are trying to have now, it is likely immaterial.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-08-30T13:03:28Z)

> The issue was that the DB transaction in which a rule is moved from the rules table to the rules_history table was failing.

do you mean that this was unrleated to "pending requests" ?
Well.. I can put the suspend in for "peace of mind", but have to agree that usefulness is doubtful at best !

## Comment (dynamic-entropy, 2024-08-30T20:44:25Z)

> do you mean that this was unrleated to "pending requests" ?

A transfer request status for a rule that has been deleted does not matter.  A rule will not wait for FTS transfers to complete to be cleaned up when expire.

> Well.. I can put the suspend in for "peace of mind", but have to agree that usefulness is doubtful at best !

I agree.

title: dmwm/CRABServer PR #8884: Fix #8809
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #8884: Fix #8809

State: closed
Opened: 2025-01-20T09:49:08Z
Closed: 2025-01-20T11:37:50Z
Merged: 2025-01-20T11:37:50Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8884

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2025-01-20T09:49:08Z)

See https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/8809

- Remove CHECK_TEST_RESULT variable to make it easier to understand and streamlining
- Make the pipeline more robust using rules like skip_check and skip_submit
- Now we only need to set three variables: SUBMIT_STATUS_TRACKING, CLIENT_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATION and CLIENT_VALIDATION_SUITE for both task submission and checking of their respective actions. By default, they are all set to true.
- We additionally have three skip variables SKIP_BUILD, SKIP_DEPLOY and SKIP_SUBMIT which can be used if so desired. By default they are all set to false.

thanks Vijay, yeah.. I have been lazy. Let me add the try...except, thanks for prodding !

## Comment (belforte, 2025-01-30T15:13:29Z)

there is a problem though. HTTP call is already retried up to 20 times with exponential backoff (20*retry# secs) inside the crabserver object
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8599a93ac74bdbabe5c04c90a271f38148b49b14/src/python/TaskWorker/MasterWorker.py#L216-L217
so I would not know what to do after catching an exception other than... "failing" !

And by they way, when crabserver object eventually fails, it raises a generic `Exception`, not an HTTP one.

 If I do nothing here, the DagmanKiller exits on the exception and control is passed to the Handler which  retries any action "no matter what" up to 5 times
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/3db5af84122652734b5cc035ba2f40f1f0e84e04/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/Handler.py#L127 again with increasing delay,

If things still fail... user will have to issue `crab kill` again.

So I think the only "problem" is that the retry policy is not obvious nor written in any prominent place and even I forgot and had to look it up now !!!

Indeed there are places where code still looks for http exception, from old implementation of access to CRAB REST, like
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/8599a93ac74bdbabe5c04c90a271f38148b49b14/scripts/AdjustSites.py#L316-L324
which was coded 10y ago.

So much cleanup .....

Let me know what you think !

## Comment (belforte, 2025-03-12T19:19:35Z)

@aspiringmind-code it appears that nor me nor you noticed that
```python
getattr(aDict, key, None)
```
does not work, always returns `None`. The correct way for a python dictionary is
```python
aDict.get(key)
```
which already returns `None` if the key is missing (not missing key exception). I guess at the time I wrote that I was in python2 world and confused about those thing. Code sort of works the way it is now, but there is no check-pointing, it parses the full log every time. Which may explain why in some limited testing it appeared to be fine. With large tasks the condor log is a very large file O(100MB) and we had been having problems before the check-pointing was introduced.

closing. Work moved to addInfoToTasks-03-25 branch

Very good catch indeed. getattr() works for objects with attributes and not dictionaries key-value pairs.

@aspiringmind-code I suspect that you do not know what this is about, but it may be a way to get to read some HTCondor constrain expressions. I do no think I have syntax errors in there, though. So am rather confident of merging and test in preprod. But as usual in the spirit of "all changes should get a second set of eyes..."

## Comment (belforte, 2025-04-29T14:34:53Z)

thanks @aspiringmind-code

The `=?=` [operator](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classads/classad-mechanism.html#classad-operators) is an extension of `==` to deal with the situation where the classAd may be missing (UNDEFINED). I am not sure it that could happen. Maybe original developers wanted to protect against the presence of jobs non-from-CRAB where our Ad's would be missing. Or maybe someone just got into the habit of adding the `?` to be on the safe side. When I changed the Ad name from `TaskType` to `CRAB_DAGType`  I was afraid of changing.

Usually classAd comparisons are case-insensitive, but same same [link](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classads/classad-mechanism.html#classad-operators) says
```
String comparisons are case insensitive for most operators. The only exceptions are the operators =?= and =!=, which do case sensitive comparisons assuming both sides are strings.
```
which I must confess is new to me. I was believing that all comparisons are case insensitive !

```python
def resolve_available_sites(self, jobgroup, kwargs, global_blacklist, acceleratorsites, ignoreLocality, stage):
    jobs = jobgroup.getJobs()
    jgblocks = set()
    allblocks = set()

    for job in jobs:
        if stage == 'probe':
            random.shuffle(job['input_files'])
        for inputfile in job['input_files']:
            jgblocks.add(inputfile['block'])
            allblocks.add(inputfile['block'])

    self.logger.debug("Blocks: %s", list(jgblocks))

    if not jobs:
        locations = set()
    else:
        locations = set(jobs[0,'input_files',0,'locations'])
    self.logger.debug("Locations: %s", list(locations))

    if not locations and not ignoreLocality:
        return jgblocks, 'no_locations', locations

    if ignoreLocality:
        availablesites = kwargs['task','all_possible_processing_sites']
    else:
        availablesites = locations - global_blacklist

    self.logger.debug("Available sites: %s", list(availablesites))

    if kwargs['task','tm_activity'] in self.config.TaskWorker.ActivitiesToRunEverywhere and kwargs['task','tm_site_whitelist']:
        availablesites = set(kwargs['task','tm_site_whitelist'])

    if not availablesites:
        return jgblocks, 'banned_locations', locations

    if kwargs['task','tm_user_config','requireaccelerator']:
        availablesites &= acceleratorsites
        if availablesites:
            msg = f"Site.requireAccelerator is True. CRAB will restrict sites to run the jobs to {list(availablesites)}."
            self.logger.warning(msg)
            self.uploadWarning(msg, kwargs['task','user_proxy'], kwargs['task','tm_taskname'])
        else:
            return jgblocks, 'banned_locations', locations

    available = set(availablesites)
    siteWhitelist = set(kwargs['task','tm_site_whitelist'])
    siteBlacklist = set(kwargs['task','tm_site_blacklist'])

    if siteWhitelist:
        available &= siteWhitelist
        if not available:
            self._warn_user_skipped_blocks('whitelist', jgblocks, availablesites, kwargs)
            return jgblocks, 'banned_locations', locations

    available -= (siteBlacklist - siteWhitelist)
    if not available:
        self._warn_user_skipped_blocks('blacklist', jgblocks, availablesites, kwargs)
        return jgblocks, 'banned_locations', locations

    return jgblocks, 'ok', locations, availablesites

def _warn_user_skipped_blocks(self, reason, jgblocks, availablesites, kwargs):
    trimmedList = sorted(list(jgblocks))[:3] + ['...']
    if reason == 'whitelist':
        msg = f"{len(jgblocks)} block(s) {trimmedList} present at {list(availablesites)} will be skipped because those sites are not in user white list"
    else:
        msg = f"{len(jgblocks)} block(s) {trimmedList} present at {list(availablesites)} will be skipped because those sites are in user black list"
    self.logger.warning(msg)
    self.uploadWarning(msg, kwargs['task','user_proxy'], kwargs['task','tm_taskname'])
```

Fix #9074
Inside the containers:
DNS was not going through the host’s DNS cache (127.0.0.53 managed by systemd-resolved).
Instead, containers were resolving domains directly via CERN’s upstream DNS servers (137.138.16.5, etc.), bypassing the host's caching and configuration. This behavior was not desired, as it breaks centralized DNS resolution and caching.

By using --dns $HOST_IP Now containers resolve DNS via the host’s DNS stack (e.g., systemd-resolved), achieving DNS caching and consistent config. resolv.conf inside the container matches the host's. DNS queries from inside the container route via the host's resolver (systemd-resolved). No more direct queries from containers to CERN DNS servers.

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-05-27T09:32:03Z)

@belforte This is a work in progress. I'd like your input. Did you envision something like this? Should I change RETRIES and DELAY values? Any other changes? Thanks!

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-27T13:16:30Z)

in this `retry_call` is not specific of Rucio so could go in a more general "utility" file.

As to what I had in mind, I was dreaming of a more transparent implementation.

While this will work, I am not happy with having to change every line where we have a call to Rucio client everywhere in the code base.
Is there some way to make it automatic that the object returned by `getNativeRucioClient()` has retry logic inside it ?

Would decorators help ?

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-05-27T13:22:13Z)

Yes, I agree that using decorators would be better.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-05-27T14:13:16Z)

I believe that we can achieve what I dreamt of by having a new myRucio client which implements all methods which we use from Rucio client and for each wraps a call to Rucio with `retry_call`. But while that's OK for calls to http where we only need to expose put/get/post/delete, Rucio has so many methods that this is certainly crazy.
Maybe there is no way ?

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-06-17T14:16:15Z)

@belforte @sinonkt  In the last commit, I built a proxy class that wraps a real Client and delegates all calls to it, while adding automatic retry for all its methods. To propagate this change, wherever we use `from rucio.client import Client` we can simply shift to `from RucioUtils import Client` I have shown that in a few scripts. There are more places where we will need to change the import statement and will have to make sure different scripts can import from RucioUtils. This is not tested. Do you like this approach? This imo is a concise way to add retries and bring uniformity around rucio calls.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-17T14:38:03Z)

I love this.
I fear a bit that it is so transparent to be confusing... but maybe I am simply scared of changes. Like all old men :-)

## Comment (belforte, 2025-06-17T14:40:27Z)

I would like to understand how this works, just for may education. Maybe we can go through it in some chat ?

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-06-17T15:02:02Z)

> @belforte @sinonkt In the last commit, I built a proxy class that wraps a real Client and delegates all calls to it, while adding automatic retry for all its methods. To propagate this change, wherever we use `from rucio.client import Client` we can simply shift to `from RucioUtils import Client` I have shown that in a few scripts. There are more places where we will need to change the import statement and will have to make sure different scripts can import from RucioUtils. This is not tested. Do you like this approach? This imo is a concise way to add retries and bring uniformity around rucio calls.

I love this approach— it's much more elegant and will definitely provide a solid foundations for us to addressing further complex features around Rucio.

Something minor to add here which you might already planned out, I would love to see `getNativeRucioClient` to simply return `self._client` and all things regarding client initialization was moved out and done centrally in your proxied class thus we utilized proxied class even more. (At my first glance, It's not obvious to me that should we stick to have singleton of rucio client? or we should allow instantiation of new client instance via `getNativeRucioClient`)

So far, It's Looks like a really good direction to me! Thanks!

## Comment (aspiringmind-code, 2025-06-18T08:41:44Z)

@belforte @sinonkt Thanks for your kind and encouraging remarks. Yes, we can discuss more regarding this over zoom chat.

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-06-16T12:53:51Z)

fix #9094
this PR does:

*   always upload input metadata before handing control to ASO
*   introduce self.useAsoRucio and when true
    * upload output metadata  right after triggering ASO work (in first PJ iteration)
    *  do not and set publish flag to True in PostJob
*   keep the PJ running also for ASO-Rucio so that job status is reported the same way as it is now.
*  in ASO/Rucio/Actions/MonitorLockStatus/updateREESTFileDocsBlockCompletionInfo also set  publish flag to True
*   no changes to Publisher

there are also minor changes for `pylint`

## Comment (belforte, 2025-08-15T16:38:23Z)

there's some "history" here.
We used Debian because we wanted to keep compatibility with WMCore and they decided for Debian because Valentin insisted that the correct way to use python 3.8 was via its upstream image, which is Debian. Starting from python3.8 image sort of keeps thing minimal in size. Valentin feels very strongly about that. Alma9 would be "too much bloated" in his opinion.
Since WMCore started from Debian, they had to use all that `conda` gymnic to import gfal, which Wa copy/pasted into CRAB.
In time we learnt that gfal developers do not support the debian package/conda, but only rpm's for alma9 (so for python 3.9) and moreover they are going to stop development for gfal and there  will never be a release for anything by alma9/python3.9.
Same for Rucio, it may work with newer python, but it is currently built and deployed for alma9 and hence python3.9

Now.. why did WMCore developers picked python 3.12 ? AFAIU, in view of freezing the tool, they wanted to make sure that they did the "last transition to newer python" and went to the current top of line. I would not have done it, personally, but it is not for me to decide.

All that said, Dario already tried to build CRAB on alma9 and it went smoothly. And with some "day after wisdom", looking at what little we gained with debian, if any, I am pretty much in favor of building CRAB on alma9 and be able to use packages from CERN where people use RHEL9.

CRABServer uses cmsweb image as base, which is handy as it comes with oracle, cherrypy, sqlalchemy.... and since the only thing we do is to add some python, we should be able to get along with whatever they do. I think that our code is already compatible at least with python3.9,  and likely py3.12. What we need to adapt is setup.py (which I think Vijay did already) and then replace optparse with argparse (or the other way around, I do not remember now) as per the ad-hoc issue which we have.

Sorry for long writeup. Hope things are a bit more clear now na.  As you can see.. nothing really fundamental, just a bunch of choices among ~equivalent paths where the full implications are not known before the work is done.

P.S. I do not regard [2] above as "simplicistic", I always thought of it as an horrible complication with respect to
`yum install 'gfal2-all python3-gfal2-util`

body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9153: Reorganize tw tarballs

State: closed
Opened: 2025-08-18T16:36:49Z
Closed: 2025-08-25T10:26:18Z
Merged: 2025-08-25T10:26:18Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9153

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-08-18T16:36:49Z)

this PR reorganizes the handling of files used in the AP's (aka schedulers, i.e. the VM's where we run the Dagman's) an in the grid WorkerNodes (aka Job Wrapper).

It needs changes to CRABClient for `crab report` and `crab preparelocal` to work:
- [x] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/pull/5410

After this:
* scripts are not mixed anymore in same directory. New structure is
```text
scripts
├── dagman
│   └── task_process
└── job_wrapper
```
* everything needed "outside TaskWorker" is bundled in two tarballs (I am keeping old names, even if not fully descriptive, am open to changing)
   * `TaskManagerRun.tar.gz`   contains what is needed in the AP
   * `CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz` contains what is needed in the JobWrapper
* they are initially created when we build the TW container (by `buildTWTarballs.sh`) but files are later added by DagmanCreator with information specific to this task like job arguments, runs and lumis, input files etc.
* those are structured so that a simple `tar xf` created the needed directory layout in either place
* those are combined in a single `InputFiles.tar.gz` which is stored in S3 and downloaded by AP's bootstrap script (`dagman_bootstrap_startup.sh`) and CRABClient for `preparelocal`
* all python code which contains the needed dependencies is in two "libraries", taking advantage of the fact that python's `import` can pull code from a zipped file
    * `WMCore.zip` which is used both in AP and JobWrapper
    * `CRAB3.zip` which is only used in the AP
       * note: we use `PYTHONPATH=$pwd:CRAB3.zip:WMCore.zip` so files can be unzipped and accessed/edited for debugging
* `buildTWTarballs.sh` which builds that tarballs only refers to directory names, no individual file is listed there anymore, not in `setup.py`
* some changes were of course needed to main drivers for AP and JobWrapper
   * `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh` , `dag_bootstrap.sh` and `gWMS-CMSRunAnalysis.sh`
* largish changes were needed in `DagmanCreator` since it needs to
   * when running in the TW: add files to the tarballs before submission to the AP
   * also be able to run in the AP during automatic splitting

While doing this I have also cleanup code a bit and added many comments.

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-09-08T14:33:16Z)

Address initial part of the "PLAN" in #9167

This requires  that  CRABServer's `config.py` is modified first by adding
* `data.s3_bucket = 'crabcache_dev'` or `crabcache_preprod` or `crabcache_prod` as appropriate for each cluster
* `data.compatibleClientVersions = ["v3", "development"]`

those changes are compatible with current code and can be done at any time

other simplifications can be done after this is deployed:
* remove from CRABServer `config.py`
   * `data.credpath`, `data.phedexurl`,` data.dbsurl`, `data.defaultBlacklist`, `data.mode`
* remove from [cmsweb-rest-config.json](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config.json)
   * "compatible-versions", "banned-out-destinations", "delegate-dn", all "modes"
      * so that it becomes like  https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config-test.json

A successive last cleanup will eliminate all references to external config and get rid of CRAB3ServerConfig once htcondor configuration is moved to TW

I have verified that the new code works both with  [current]( https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config.json) and [new]( https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/CRAB3ServerConfig/-/blob/master/cmsweb-rest-config-test.json) `cmsweb-rest-config-test.json`

And that it works with both [current](https://github.com/sinonkt/CMSKubernetes/blob/migrate-to-argocd/argocd/apps/crab/crabserver/base/config/config.py) config (with the changes indicated above) and the new, leaner one as in [test2](https://gitlab.cern.ch/crab3/crab-k8s-overlays/-/blob/master/argocd/apps/crab/crabserver/overlays/test2/config/config.py)

More testing e.g. in preprod is of course important.

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-09-24T08:10:13Z)

In response to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5413.

when crab report fails in case of automatic splitting, cause by the missing of user's jobs lumis, input_file in S3.
```bash
File job_lumis_1.json not found in run_and_lumis.tar.gz
File job_input_file_list_1.txt not found in input_files.tar.gz
ERROR: KeyError: '1'
```

Actually *0*, parent dag idx, was properly uploaded to s3 cache during first boostrapping once but it just our parent dag (CRAB matter) reached to s3, Other ***1++*** parent_idx/job_ids were missing. (so called User specific jobs/DAG part).

Release notes

Sourced from python-ldap's releases.

3.4.5

Released 3.4.5 2025-10-10

Security fixes:

  • CVE-2025-61911 (GHSA-r7r6-cc7p-4v5m): Enforce str input in ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars with escape_mode=1; ensure proper escaping. (thanks to lukas-eu)
  • CVE-2025-61912 (GHSA-p34h-wq7j-h5v6): Correct NUL escaping in ldap.dn.escape_dn_chars to \00 per RFC 4514. (thanks to aradona91)

Fixes:

  • ReconnectLDAPObject now properly reconnects on UNAVAILABLE, CONNECT_ERROR and TIMEOUT exceptions (previously only SERVER_DOWN), fixing reconnection issues especially during server restarts
  • Fixed syncrepl.py to use named constants instead of raw decimal values for result types
  • Fixed error handling in SearchNoOpMixIn to prevent a undefined variable error

Tests:

  • Added comprehensive reconnection test cases including concurrent operation handling and server restart scenarios

Doc/

  • Updated installation docs and fixed various documentation typos
  • Added ReadTheDocs configuration file

Infrastructure:

  • Add testing and document support for Python 3.13

Fixes:

  • Reconnect race condition in ReconnectLDAPObject is now fixed
  • Socket ownership is now claimed once we've passed it to libldap
  • LDAP_set_option string formats are now compatible with Python 3.12

Doc/

  • Security Policy was created
  • Broken article links are fixed now
  • Bring Conscious Language improvements

Infrastructure:

## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T09:35:46Z)

note that there are other files in `CMSRunAnalysis.tar.gz` which are modified by PreDag, like `input_args.json`. The actions are safe locally to the AP, since PreDag adds information needed to new jobs in tail subdags before those are submitted, but it is possible for PreDag to run and create subdags before the current stage is completed (e.g. when main processing stage is at 80%). Of course if stage is 80% completed, chances are that all jobs have started already, but we can not guarantee it, and since you are putting your hands in this part now, it is good to do it properly.

Further note: when a job is submitted, it is not "safe" yet. It may stay in the queue for a a while, only when it is matched to an available pilot and starts running on the remove WN, condor will copy the tarball there.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T09:44:33Z)

I've slept on this with ChatGPT as well for ideas coverage, Chat suggested quite elegant pattern that completely kill this kind of races **w/o using lock** that i totally intriguing with. (same pattern that HTCondor used for writing some log in schedds)

Every time we ***write***, create it as `temp`.
```python
tmp_name = 'run_and_lumis.tar.gz.tmp'

with tarfile.open(tmp_name, 'w:gz') as tf:
    tf.add(runAndLumisDir, arcname='')
```
Then do atomic replace later
```
os.replace(tmp_name, 'run_and_lumis.tar.gz')  # atomic on POSIX
```
Such that it safe for ***read*** at any moment, `run_and_lumis.tar.gz` is either the ***old valid*** tar, the ***new valid tar***. May i hear your opinions on this too, please?

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T09:47:49Z)

this way we simplify the code by eliminated **all** **Read Lock**, and worries just about **Write Lock** which have much less potential clash places.

P.S. **Read Lock** may required when that piece of code better wait for **new valid tar**, very sensitive to content inside tar.
P.S. In other words if **new valid tar** doesn't naturally arrived on time, they can live with **old valid tar**, in naturally never clashes manner.
P.S. Suite scenarios where there's very few writers at overlap time window, like in our cases here?

## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T09:59:33Z)

well.. sure. `os.rename` is the same as the good old `mv`, you do not need ChatGPT for this ! Indeed there are many places in the code where we do that (create .tmp, then mv). It should be OK here. At least I can't think right away of a reason to wait before reading.
Instead, where PostJob is using the lock atm, there can be a benefit by avoiding many processes doing same work at ~same time, but doing it in one and sharing updated result.
But we can't ask original developers for their reasons where they did not document in the comments.

## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T10:01:15Z)

I guess it was my bad here, to have suggested a lock instead of a `mv`. I was wary of `mv` across file systems (SPOOL_DIR is on CEPH, tmpdir is on /tmp i.e. local hypervisor disk). But we can copy to SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp and then do an atomic move there. That should be safe

## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T10:08:18Z)

Thinking about it, only mv inside the same  file system can be atomic, i.e. the pointer from file name to disk location is changed in "one go". Across file systems there's no alternative to copying bytes around.
If you ask why I did not create tmpdir in /data, it was to limit I/O since tar operations are I/O intensive and we already struggle with IOops on /data = /vdc = SPOOL_DIR

## Comment (belforte, 2025-11-18T10:11:09Z)

thanks for having pointed out my "overkill".

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T10:11:44Z)

> Thinking about it, only mv inside the same file system can be atomic, i.e. the pointer from file name to disk location is changed in "one go". Across file systems there's no alternative to copying bytes around. If you ask why I did not create tmpdir in /data, it was to limit I/O since tar operations are I/O intensive and we already struggle with IOops on /data = /vdc = SPOOL_DIR

Ahhh, that resonated with me both heterogenous file system, I/O ops, so having lock this way sound more convincing to me.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T10:14:33Z)

if I/O heavy atomic mv happened on TW, IMO is tolerable but otherwise on AP/WN not sound good to me.

recap:
1. create new `tarball` in `/tmp`
2. copy to `SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp`
3. `mv SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp SPOOL_DIR/tarbal`

?? I think `mv` does not shuffle disk bytes around, it is not I/O heavy.

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-11-18T10:22:42Z)

> recap:
>
> 1. create new `tarball` in `/tmp`
> 2. copy to `SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp`
> 3. `mv SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp SPOOL_DIR/tarbal`
>
> what do you think ?

For clarity, May i have your clarifications/confirmation? around where 1,2,3 has happened.
From my understanding.
1. local AP disk, `/tmp`
2. [Non-atomic transferring] from local AP disk -> HTCondor shared/parallel NFS `SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp`
3. [expected Atomic] among shared/parallel NFS `SPOOL_DIR/tarball.tmp SPOOL_DIR/tarbal`

So, so it's something like 2-steps copy with atomic guarantee on destination site?

> if I/O heavy atomic mv happened on TW, IMO is tolerable but otherwise on AP/WN not sound good to me.

Apologize, I means write/add/update tar gz as temp that original developer try to lock.

Yes.

https://www-auth.cs.wisc.edu/lists/htcondor-users/2025-December/msg00037.shtml

"
SubDAGs will inherit the configuration file of the parents (all the way up to the root DAG in the case of a Sub-SubDAG). If the SubDAG specifies its own configuration file then DAGMan will use the SubDAG specific configuration file and completely ignore the inherited parent DAG configuration file.

## Opening post (nausikt, 2025-12-08T16:26:19Z)

Resolve #9241

Put `getRucioUsage`, `getRuleQuota` into Vijay's Client wrapper umbrella this way, will allow us to catch *non-RucioExceptions* that highly coupling with unavailability/unstability of Rucio, Thus utilize the centralized retry/attempt mechanism.

I guessed this patch will make monit_reportrecallquota CRON more robust out of the box. thus mitigate currently flooding emails.

## Notes
- [x] [1] we will give this a try in CRON monitoring first, whether its effective or not.
> i've to merged this PR First then making a release tag for monit to use, and leave CRON like that for a week to see whether it effectively mitigate the problem.
- [ ] [2] Then, adopt in other places that also use `getRucioUsage` like in `DBSDataDiscovery` when checking things before making taperecall request.
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/5e84119c18a939ea13f1afde4abf6dc680e4f28d/src/python/TaskWorker/Actions/DBSDataDiscovery.py#L560-L566
- [x] [3] Deprecate `getRucioUsage`, `getRuleQuota` standalone fns in `RucioUtils`, We fully start using them from Vijay's client wrapper instead.
- [x] [4?] adopt exponential backoffs? would it be helpful in general? we help Rucio by not to stressing them too much, ALSO Overall, tasks can tolerate the instabilities of Rucio longer than 3 x (180 ms | 1 seconds) retry attempts, may be can tolerate up to 20 minutes or half an hr for example.

P.S. Please, let me know your opinions on notes OR feel free to give me green right? on proceeding to [2],[3],[4] in this PR.

IIUC, It's turned out that `_send_request` even trying to ***Categorized*** http response into `ServerConnectionException`, `ConnectionError`, `OSError`, `IOError` as we can see in [[2](https://github.com/rucio/rucio/blob/45b19709d28ecccc39cd0e73e4087a7e79a71c49/lib/rucio/client/baseclient.py#L446-L529)].             exc_cls = headers['ExceptionClass']
```python
        if 'ExceptionMessage' in data:
```


## Comment (belforte, 2026-01-21T22:08:01Z)

Some background:
Kenyi uses dictionaries, even if they are called `ad` to eventually create an htcondor.Submit object. Indeed `'UNDEFINED'` (as a string) is a [special value](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classads/classad-mechanism.html#classad-syntax) for classads. We use classad objects, but they can be defined using dictionary semantics, so we could similarly use `jobSubmit[...]="UNDEFINED"` , i.e. assign to the ad the `"UNDEFINED"` string. But in practice it is the same as not setting any value for this attribute which IMHO is more clear.  Currently we do not set a value (not even UNDEFINED) and it works, this means that all code which deals with this inside Condor and glideInWMS is properly written so not to crash on a missing optional ad, using e.g. the [Ternary operator](https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classads/classad-mechanism.html#classad-operators) and/or explicit testing for the ad being defined.
We could also use the python `None` value:  `jobSubmit[...]=None` or the "expert-smelling" `jobSubmit[...]=classad.Value.Undefined` as per https://htcondor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/apis/python-bindings/api/version2/classad2/classad.html#classad2.ClassAd

That said, whether to use one way or another, is mostly a matter of taste !
But you should have tested the new code also on a configuration that does not specify the new accelerator params !

## Comment (nausikt, 2026-01-27T17:31:03Z)

OK, right now we *no longer* relied on `wmagent-base` and `dmwm-base` layers for both **CRABServer** and **TaskWorker**.
*(both now operating in Alma9 with py3.9)*

And this way we also ***Agnostic*** to the building machine.
\*\**I built it on my laptop, with my lxtunnel down. i guessed CERN oracle repo are mirrored repo? still considered to be public unlike repo for **tnsnames.ora**.*\*\*

And Yes, we still have a *little* problem with *only* *sensitive* artifact left (***tnsnames.ora***) which actually best to be mounted at run-time or building time.

But Valentine's way of abstracting problem for everyone by layering are paid-off here. [cmsweb:cmsweb/Dockerfile](https://github.com/dmwm/CMSKubernetes/blob/2f52b8ef238cdace2555f15ae8ab74da277e56e3/docker/cmsweb/Dockerfile#L11-L170)

So any image that derived from `cmsweb/cmsweb` for just picking some sensitive artifacts (things required gpgkey,authens,internal) will be available here. and if the image (also ours) was forced --no-cache rebuilding it will be refreshed, propagating to downstream images well.

_______
Therefore i highly recommended, keep the following this way, should be least confusing to the new operator.
```Dockerfile
FROM registry.cern.ch/cmsweb/cmsweb:wm-freeze AS cmsweb
COPY --from=cmsweb /etc/tnsnames.ora /etc/tnsnames.ora
```
Another remaining derivation is just *cmsweb* utilities commands for debugging inside the container. that we better keep it that way too.
```Dockerfile
FROM registry.cern.ch/cmsweb/exporters:20250519-stable AS exporters
COPY --from=exporters /data/cmsweb-ping /usr/bin/cmsweb-ping
COPY --from=exporters /data/process_exporter /usr/bin/process_exporter
COPY --from=exporters /data/cpy_exporter /usr/bin/cpy_exporter
COPY --from=exporters /data/process_monitor.sh /usr/bin/process_monitor.sh
```

That's all derivations left, coupling with `cmsweb` base images. Hopefully it allow us to gain full control during freezing time.

# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9276: add exit code dependent retry policy

State: closed
Opened: 2026-02-24T13:35:55Z

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9276

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2026-02-24T13:35:55Z)

Fix #9264

Salient Features of the New ExitCode Dependent Resubmission and Retry Policy:

- Automatic calculation of job id specific `resubmit_counter` based on lastExitCode dependent max_retries and crab_retry
- `retries_consumed_for_ec` resets to 0 when exitCode changes
- We start with 100 retries limit. But it increases with every resubmit. By how much is ExitCode dependent. Most popular case would be the limit becoming 103, 106,... with each resubmit. So effectively the user does not hit an upperbound as long as they wish to resubmit. This preserves current behaviour
- In the case of no parameters specified with resubmission, if exit code suggests that increasing maxmemory or maxjobruntime can help, automatic increase by 30% tried until hitting the upperbounds of 7500 MB and 47 hours respectively
- retry delay of 900 s is added for each recoverable error exit code. This delay can be changed for each exit Code
- If exitcode shows that changing site will help, the site of the last retry run is dropped from the availableSet for the current retry. Note that the site is not blacklisted and will be available for subsequent retries. Also note that this feature happens even in the retries of simple submit (i.e. not only for crab resubmit but also for retries of simple crab submit)
- The source of truth is EXIT_RETRY_POLICY dictionary in RetryJob. It has every recoverable exit code with keys like `type, max_retries, delay, msg, change_site, increase_memory, memory_factor, runtime_factor, increase_runtime and handler`
- effective_max_retries will be exit code dependent calculated by the formula `(base_max + 1)*(resubmit_counter + 1) - 1` where `base_max` is specified in the policy dict. So for an exit code like 8020 every resubmit will give additional 3 retries. For exitcode 8028 every resubmit will give additional 10 retries.
- When effective_max_retries for a recoverable error is reached FatalError is raised. User can do resubmit.
- Only recoverable errors specified in the policy are retried. Fatal errors will pass through the default route and won't be retried.
- ToDos for subsequent improvement:
   Make files inside resubmit_info json instead of txt
   Avoid short and long exit code redundancy in the EXIT_RETRY_POLICY

We are limited by the how many PostJob can run concurrently, due to memory constrain. The preferred implementation would be what is done when waiting for ASO, exit with a proper exit code which tells Dagman to rerun the Post (or Pre ?) step after a delay (example of delay in PreJob is the use of `deferTime` in there).

I think that currently jobs are reported in "toRetry" or "cooloff" (unfortunately there is some  inconsistency) when the DAG node is completed with error but not resubmitted yet. At least that's a status that appears at times, but I have

## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-29T16:23:51Z)

In today's (29/04/2026) meeting we discussed how to count/limit retries and resubmissions.
Here's summary
* we agree that `maxRetry` can not be exit-code dependend. Each job which completes with recoverable error is retried, up to a maximum. A fatal error terminates automatic retries. We start with `maxRetry=10`
* There are 3 things which one may want to count (and keep track of)
   * `retryNumber` like now, the number of times a job is submitted for a given crabId, from to max in DagMan (100 currently). This is needed to uniquely identify the condor job, pre/post-job logs, records in OpenSearch etc. LIke now.
      *  Its Semantics is not changing.
   * `resubmitNumber` the number of times a user has issued a `crab resubmit` for this crabId. Easy to define. Hard to compute and track.
      * Its usefulness is not clear, other than as possibly having a role in computing next counter `retryInThisResubmissionCycleNumber`
   *  `retryInThisResubmissionCycleNumber`, let's shorten to RRN : Retry in (Re)submission Number
      * Semantics: this counter is what must be compared with maxRetry (i.e. 10) to decide if a new automatic retry (i.e. a new condor_submit) should be done or the job set to `failed` due to max reached.
      * It is not immediately obvious how to determine this. We discussed two ways:
         1.  guess the resubmission cycle by using `mod(retryNumber,10)` and set RRN as `retryNumber-resubmitNumber*10` (maybe +1 or -1 ... a detail). Pros: easy and simple . Cons: in case of fatal errors next resubmit may have <10 retries, down to possible just one, such undefined max_retry may be confusing for ops and users.
         2. increment RRN at every job submission, but reset to 0 when `crab resubmit` is processed.  Pros: this is exactly what we want. Cons: more code is needed and it is difficult (impossible) to avoid that a Dagman restart (schedd failure or whatever) looks like a `resubmit`

Of course we need to track (i.e. persist on disk) the counters which we will be using, currently this is being done via DAG retry counter inside dagman log and node_status files, and crabId specific files in `SPOOL_DIR/retry_info/job.<crabId>.txt` . New code in this PR also introduces `resubmit_info/job.<crabId>.txt`. We discussed changing to JSON.  If RRN is not coomputed in PreJob (1. above) it will need to be persisted on disk too.

Stefano (who proposed 2.) has some ideas on its implementation:

**Idea1. not good**: Use classAd `CRAB_ResubmitList` in PreJob.py to know that current crabId is being resubmitted. Along the lines of how it is used in PreJob to set `use_resubmit_info`. It does not work because that classAd "sticks" and the PreJob has no way to know if this is a resubmission or not. Also code will get confused if another resubmit arrives while dagman was still starting, possibly with a different jobId list, so the previous list gets lost before it was fully used. We saw during tests that some jobs could "not be resubmitted".

**Idea2. not clearly wrong**: Leverage `adjustSites.py` inside `dag_bootstrap_startup.sh`. It runs when dagman is not running, so we know that nothing changes in DAG status. Persist RRN in for each Job in some file (one per task will suffice). Increment the jobId value in each PreJob (need a lock due to concurrency, or go for thousand small files again)  and compare with `maxRetry` in PostJob (like now) to decide whether to submit again or not. Inside `adjustSites.py` i.e. at each dagman restart, use classAd `CRAB_ResubmitList` to reset RRN for those jobs.
   * In a way this reproduces current (Brian's) implementation where RRN is the Dagman Retry counter and adjust sites hacks Dagman log and status files to do the resetting. By letting Dag node retry counter run free and moving the RRN counter in our scope, we gain robustness, clarity and flexibility. Hopefully all the places in the code where DAG_RETRY was used have been changed already in this PR.
  * About resubmission vs. dagman restarts, since `CRAB_ResubmitList` sticks, every Dagman restart will look to the code like a new `crab resubmit` with same list of jobs to resubmit as last one. This should have no effect on crabIds which have completed by "now", but for those which were being retried it will reset the RRN counter, basically giving them a higher max_retry. Having more retries is not as bad as having less (does not decrease chances for success!) and, since such unintended dagman restarts are rare, chances for confusions are much fewer. An idea to tell resbumits from restarts, could be to inroduce a `thisIsResumit' classAd to be used as a boolean flag: DagmanResubmitter sets it to True, adjustSites  checks it in order to decide if to reset RRN's, then sets it to False after the reset id done. So in case of a restart, RRN's will not be touched.

## Opening post (belforte, 2026-03-29T15:02:22Z)

Fixes #9213
This collects changes from #9280 and #9284 plus fixes to make it all work consistently.
squashing a long and twisted story into a single commit. It also addresses Vijay's comment on #9280

Here's recap of changes

this brings in extensive changes to test pipeline aimed to
* adapt to changes in CRAB (e.g. new status `Running`)
* ensure that test always and only fail when there's real errors (of course this is an open ended task)
* terse reports, yet allow for ` -o ci.variable="VERBOSE=0|1|2|3"
* always wait for tasks to be completed even if sleep step was not long enough
* readable, synoptic, view of test status printed at the end of each iteration
* add CMSSW_15 to what we test
* always use CMSSW_15 (and python3) to run scripts which do not require `crab submit`
* refactoring of StatusTracking tests for clean log and full error catching
* reduced amount of testing for oldish CMSSW version
   * StatusTracking is only run for CMSSW>=13
   * CCV is not run for CMSSW < 10 (SL7 releases)
* allow to test release pipeline via tags like `pypi-test2-blah=v3.010101`

body: # dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9296: Add awareness of Rucio HTTP exceptions and retry up to 10 times over ~20 minutes State: closed Opened: 2026-04-09T20:56:36Z Closed: 2026-07-22T20:19:51Z Merged: 2026-07-22T20:19:51Z Labels: Type: Bug URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9296 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-04-09T20:56:36Z) Resolve https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9285 I've released this patch to **crab-dev-tw02** via `v3.latest`, `v3-260409-tolerate-rucio-http-exceptions`. See also [latest tag in harbour](https://registry.cern.ch/harbor/projects/1891/repositories/crabtwmonit/artifacts-tab) ## How to test From now on, we should expect *one-sided reporting/emailing* from *only* `crab-prod-tw02` about **503 exceptions.** *P.S. If its works well, we will promote it into prod with proper release tag.* ## Comment (cmsdmwmbot, 2026-04-09T20:59:59Z) Jenkins results: * Python3 Pylint check: succeeded * 10 comments to review * Pycodestyle check: succeeded * 13 comments to review Details at https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/view/All/job/DMWM-CRABServer-PR-test/2782/artifact/artifacts/PullRequestReport.html ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-10T14:35:59Z) Acknowledged @belforte, will revise/add better docs! > E.g it is not clear to me what will happen if we get an http exception other than the ones that you list explicitly. Is that fatal ? Ignored ? Retried using default policy ? Put concretely, RucioException("http status code: 555" or whatever "....") will be treated as **Fatal** (raised right away with no retry), just like other native RucioExceptions. Meanwhile, "http status code: {403|429|500|502|503}" are specifically trapped by predicate in retry loop earlier, not raised until the maximum number of retries is reached. > On the substance, are you sure that all other http exceptions deserve a different treatment ? Do we have any evidence of an http exception which is not worth retrying, given that "remote serve is down or anyhow in total confusion" is a condition where retrying after delay is certainly good ? I mostly follow the standard used on the CRAB REST side. That said, I'm still skeptical on only 403 shouldn't be here *P.S. other make sense to me na. e.g. 429: too many requests, 50X: server faults*, what do you think? https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/blob/216d7f5d698a020104d72b1d354fbcfe906b721e/src/python/RESTInteractions.py#L29-L38 ## Comment (belforte, 2026-04-10T14:58:20Z) RESTInteraction is a bit special because it only talks to our server where our code is in control of what http code is returned, and was also based on experience, in practice we almost never see anything different. Server throttling never really worked (something which Valentin tried to add, but ... somehow he did not really finished and the main problem was DBS which was solved by rewrite in go and separating server for users and prod). So 429 never happens. But we have some http 304 e.g. in current grafana which I have no idea what it is, and http 400 which should not be there, because all queries come from our code and therefore should better be good ones. It is also true that those HTTP codes may come from cmsweb FrontEnd, not necessarily CRAB Server... There would be a lot to investigate there. SImly do not take that code as gold standard ! You have to choose between adding http errors from Rucio "as they pop up", possibly after having investigated and figured out what they are, or be proactive and say "retry them all". The former is more work. The latter may potentially obscure some issue worth reporting... But for CRAB Rest we felt we had a duty to fix our server, so preferred to call it fatal any "unknowns" error. For Rucio... what do we do if we get some odd errors at a low rate ? ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-04-10T15:13:55Z) Thanks for extreme clarity & history!🙇‍♂️ Forgive me, for had switched off my brain, the former investigate & patch "as they pop up", make much more sense to me! Will converge to only 503 for now then🫡 ## Comment (cmsdmwmbot, 2026-04-17T15:45:15Z) Jenkins results: * Python3 Pylint check: succeeded * 10 comments to review * Pycodestyle check: succeeded * 13 comments to review Details at https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/view/All/job/DMWM-CRABServer-PR-test/2798/artifact/artifacts/PullRequestReport.html ## Comment (belforte, 2026-05-11T17:22:13Z) @nausikt forgive may failing memory. title: dmwm/CRABServer PR #9300: Mitigate terminally failed migration baseline by adding jitter delays between our Publisher DBS API calls.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9300: Mitigate terminally failed migration baseline by adding jitter delays between our Publisher DBS API calls.

State: closed
Opened: 2026-04-17T23:45:06Z
Closed: 2026-04-18T08:55:33Z
Merged: 2026-04-18T08:55:33Z
Labels: Type: Bug, Priority: Critical
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9300

## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-04-17T23:45:06Z)

Resolve #9299

## Summary
When processing many tasks with 100-200+ blocks simultaneously, the Publisher fires rapid back-to-back
DBS API calls (submitMigration, statusMigration, listBlocks, insertBulkBlock) with
no delay between requests (Like a mini-While-True loop).

This overwhelms/break the DBS server or cms-auth-proxy or may trigger CERN firewall appliances, causing rate-limiting or intermittent/abrupt connection drops, resulting in empty responses or errors, which make files stuck in the acquire-status checking loop and eventually misclassified as terminal migration failures, leaving them permanently stuck in the Acquire state.

## So this PR will resolved/mitigated the issues by:
Added randomized jitter delays (random.uniform) between DBS API calls in:
- `findParentBlocks` — after each parent file lookup round (0.1-0.3s)
- `migrateByBlockDBS3` — between migration submissions (0.2-0.5s)
- `migrateByBlockDBS3` — between migration status checks (0.2-0.5s)
- `TaskPublish.publishInDBS3` — between block insertions (0.2-0.5s)
- `TaskPublishRucio.publishInDBS3` — between block insertions (0.2-0.5s)

## Why **Jitter** (randomized sleep)?
it is used instead of fixed sleep to prevent multiple concurrent Publisher processes from synchronizing, self-organized criticality of hitting DBS simultaneously with same IP.

## Expectations
- [ ] Publisher logs show expected delays between DBS calls.
- [ ] Terminally failed migration, which not running out of their retry_count=10 yet, can make a progress, completed their migrations, or been able to resubmitted request new migrations.
- [ ] Acquired file backlog should decreases over time, since we have less and less terminally failures.
*(Of course, with some kick, manually resubmit, but may never have to **blacklist** tasks?)*

______
*My suggestion is that we should release this PR ASAP to prevent new submissions from getting stuck and to rescue some migrations that are still recoverable or retryable.*
P.S. we've reached all-time-high O(112k) now.

## Opening post (aspiringmind-code, 2026-06-01T06:56:11Z)

Fix #9318
For larger discussion on how we reached here, see #9264 and (few last comments in) #9276

---

## Design Write-Up: CRABServer Resubmission Policy Refactor

---

This PR introduces three interlocking concepts:

1. **RRN (Resubmission Retry Number)** : a new, independent, per-job counter that counts genuine job execution attempts across all resubmission epochs.
2. **EXIT_RETRY_POLICY** : a declarative dictionary in `RetryJob.py` that maps exit codes to retry actions (delay, memory boost, runtime boost, site change).
3. **`resubmit_record.json` and epoch tracking** : a mechanism to allow user-triggered resubmissions to reset RRN counters for targeted jobs, enabling a clean slate while preserving history. Note that epoch is a counter, not time.

---

### The Three Counters: `dag_retry`, `crab_retry`, and `rrn`

Understanding the difference between these is essential.

| Counter | Owned By | What It Counts | Resets? | Stored In |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dag_retry` (`$RETRY`) | DAGMan | DAGMan node submission attempts (pre+job+post cycle) within current DAG run | **Never** | DAGMan internal state |
| `crab_retry` | CRAB PostJob | Number of times PostJob has completed (job ran + postjob ran) | **Never** | `retry_info/job.<id>.txt` |
| `rrn` | CRAB PreJob/AdjustSites | True number of execution attempts (auto + user-triggered) | Only on user resubmit | `rrn_info/job.<id>.txt` |

`crab_retry` is used as a key/index into `resubmit_info/job.<id>.txt` to store per-attempt parameters (memory, runtime, site lists, exit code info). It is strictly increasing and never resets, it serves as a stable record key.

`rrn` is used exclusively to answer: "Has this job been tried enough times overall?" It resets to 0 when the user explicitly resubmits, giving the job a fresh budget of `CRAB_NumAutomJobRetries` (now **10**, up from 2) attempts. PreJob stamps `CRAB_RRN` into the job's classAd so PostJob can read it without touching the filesystem.

`dag_retry` still controls the DAGMan machinery, but PostJob no longer uses it as the gate for "too many retries" , it uses `rrn` instead.

---

### The Lifecycle of a Single Job Attempt

**Step 1 — PreJob runs:**
- Calls `get_rrn()`: reads `rrn_info/job.<id>.txt`, increments the `rrn` field, writes it back (atomic rename, file-locked).
- Stamps `My.CRAB_RRN = <rrn>` into the job submit classAd.
- Reads `resubmit_info/job.<id>.txt` at key `crab_retry - 1` (the previous attempt's data).
  - If `increase_memory` is set, multiplies current memory by `memory_factor` (capped at 7500 MB).
  - If `increase_runtime` is set, multiplies current walltime by `runtime_factor` (capped at 47 h).
- Reads `change_site` from the previous attempt. If set, and there is more than one available site, removes the previous failing site from the candidate set.
- Checks `retry_delay_until` from `resubmit_info` for the current `dag_retry` key. If now < that timestamp, returns True from `needsDefer()` and the job is deferred (held and re-released after the delay).
- Writes the chosen parameters into `resubmit_info/job.<id>.txt` at key `str(crab_retry)`.

**Step 2 — Job runs on the worker node.**

**Step 3 — RetryJob runs (if the job finished with non-zero exit code):**
- Calls `apply_retry_policy(exitCode)`.
- Looks up `exitCode` in `EXIT_RETRY_POLICY`. Falls back to `"default"` (neutral, no adjustments) if not found.
- Calls `store_retry_actions(policy, exitCode)`: writes into `resubmit_info/job.<id>.txt` at key `str(crab_retry)`:
  - `retry_delay_until = time.time() + policy["delay"]` (typically 900 s)
  - `increase_memory`, `increase_runtime`, `change_site` booleans and their factors
  - `site` = the site where this attempt ran (so PreJob can discard it next time if needed)
  - `exitCode`
- If the policy type is `"recoverable"`, dispatches to a handler (if registered), then raises `RecoverableError`.
- If the policy type is `"neutral"`, returns without raising, falls through to the existing `FatalError` raise at the bottom of `check_exit_code`.

**Step 4 — PostJob runs:**
- Calls `get_rrn()`: reads `CRAB_RRN` from the job classAd (stamped by PreJob). Falls back to `rrn_info/job.<id>.txt` if classAd unavailable (e.g., PreJob itself crashed before the job ran).
- Calls `get_max_retry()`: reads `CRAB_NumAutomJobRetries` from the task classAd (default 10).
- If `retryjob_retval == RECOVERABLE_ERROR`: checks `rrn >= max_retry`. If yes → fatal. Otherwise → recoverable (DAGMan will retry).

---

### The EXIT_RETRY_POLICY Dictionary

The old `RetryJob.py` had a linear `if/elif` chain. The new code replaces it with a data-driven dictionary:

```python
EXIT_RETRY_POLICY = {
    1:     {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "...bootstrap failure..."},
    50115: {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..no FJR..", "increase_memory": True, "memory_factor": 1.3},
    195:   {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..no FJR..", "increase_memory": True, "memory_factor": 1.3},
    60403: {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..stageout timeout..", "increase_runtime": True, "runtime_factor": 1.3},
    243:   {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..stageout timeout..", "increase_runtime": True, "runtime_factor": 1.3},
    8020:  {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..FileOpenError..", "change_site": True, "handler": "handle_file_open_or_root_error"},
    8021:  {"type": "recoverable", "delay": 900, "msg": "..FileReadError..", "change_site": True, "handler": "handle_file_open_or_root_error"},
    ...
    "default": {"type": "neutral", "delay": 900, "msg": "..."}
}
```

Key additions:
- `increase_memory` / `memory_factor`: triggers a 1.3× memory increase on the *next* attempt.
- `increase_runtime` / `runtime_factor`: triggers a 1.3× walltime increase on the *next* attempt.
- `change_site`: triggers removal of the failing site from the candidate set on the *next* attempt.
- `handler`: name of a method on `RetryJob` to call before raising `RecoverableError` (for exit-code-specific logic like checking corrupted files or CVMFS issues).
- `"neutral"` type: the exit code is not recognized as explicitly recoverable; falls through to the existing fatal-error path rather than either retrying blindly or failing definitively.

The three handler methods (`handle_file_open_or_root_error`, `handle_sigabrt`, `handle_cvmfs_or_cms_exception`) contain the same logic as the old inline `if` blocks, they are just extracted into named methods and dispatched via the policy table.

---

### User-Triggered Resubmission and RRN Reset

When a user calls `crab resubmit`, `DagmanResubmitter.py` runs. The new code adds:

```python
newEpoch = currentEpoch + 1
resubmitRecord = json.dumps({
    'epoch': newEpoch,
    'job_ids': task['resubmit_jobids']
})
schedd.edit(rootConst, "CRAB_ResubmitEpoch", str(newEpoch))
schedd.edit(rootConst, "CRAB_ResubmitRecord", classad.quote(resubmitRecord))
```

Both `epoch` and `job_ids` are written atomically as a single JSON classAd value (`CRAB_ResubmitRecord`). This prevents AdjustSites from ever seeing a mismatched (new epoch, old job list) pair.

When DAGMan restarts and `AdjustSites.py` runs:
1. `writeResubmitRecord(ad)` reads `CRAB_ResubmitRecord` from the task classAd and writes it to `rrn_info/resubmit_record.json`. Idempotent: skips if the on-disk epoch already matches.
2. `resetRRN()` reads `rrn_info/resubmit_record.json`. For each targeted job (or all jobs if `job_ids` is null), opens `rrn_info/job.<id>.txt`, checks `last_reset_epoch`. If `last_reset_epoch < current_epoch`, sets `rrn = 0`. If `last_reset_epoch >= current_epoch`, we skip with continue. This idempotency in == means DAGMan can restart AdjustSites multiple times safely. The > case should not happen until things have gone very wrong.

After this reset, when PreJob runs for a resubmitted job, `get_rrn()` finds `rrn = 0` and increments it to 1, effectively giving the job a new budget of `max_retry` attempts.

### `reuse_rrn`: Handling Interrupted PreJob

There is a subtle race condition: PreJob can crash or be killed after incrementing RRN but before the job actually runs. This also happens when a resubmission of a different job id happens while another is running. When DAGMan retries the node, PreJob runs again. At this point:
- `retry_info` shows `pre > post` (PreJob ran more times than PostJob)
- `job_out.<id>.<retry>` does not exist (job never ran)

Originally, this case set `prejob_exit_code = 1` (error) only if a job_out existed, implying the job had run. In the new code an `else` branch is added: when `pre > post` and no `job_out`, it sets `self.reuse_rrn = True`. Then `get_rrn()`, instead of incrementing, just returns the current `rrn` value unchanged. This prevents RRN from being double-incremented for a single logical job attempt where PreJob happened to restart.

---

### Summary of Key Changes

| Aspect | Existing | New |
|---|---|---|
| Retry gate counter | `dag_retry` (DAGMan internal) | `rrn` (CRAB-owned, per job) |
| Default max retries | 2 | 10 |
| Max retries storage | `$MAX_RETRIES` baked into DAG | `CRAB_NumAutomJobRetries` in task classAd |
| Exit-code handling | `if/elif` chain in `RetryJob` | Declarative `EXIT_RETRY_POLICY` dict |
| Memory auto-boost | Not present | 1.3× on exit 50115/195, capped 7500 MB |
| Runtime auto-boost | Not present | 1.3× on exit 60403/243, capped 47 h |
| Site change on failure | Not present | Discard failing site on exit 8020/8021 |
| Retry delay enforcement | Not present | `retry_delay_until` checked in PreJob |
| User resubmit resets budget | `adjustMaxRetries` increased max_retries by 1 + numAutomJobRetries  | Explicitly via RRN reset + epoch mechanism |
| Idempotent resubmit record | N/A | Yes, `last_reset_epoch` per job |
| Interrupted PreJob | Exit code 1 if job_out exists | `reuse_rrn=True` — no double-increment |

We could certainly reduce the rate at which we report this in aso_metrics_ora to e.g. once per hour. But one long query every 5 min is not that troubling. IIUC the only fast way would be to have a separate table with all the DONE records so we just ask for the number of rows. Or we can keep a counter, somehow ? Shall we start with an index ?

Yes, there are several good approaches. Let me walk through them from best to most complex:

1. Filtered Index (Quickest Win)

If you're frequently querying a specific value like 'DONE', a filtered/function-based index can make the COUNT near-instant:

-- Oracle: standard index on the column
CREATE INDEX idx_myvar ON mytable (MyVar);

-- Then your COUNT uses the index instead of scanning the table
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mytable WHERE MyVar = 'DONE';

Oracle can do an index range scan and count index entries without touching the table at all. This alone often reduces query time from minutes to milliseconds.

2. Materialized View (Best Balance)

A materialized view pre-computes the grouped counts and can refresh automatically:

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_myvar_counts
REFRESH FAST ON COMMIT  -- auto-refreshes on every COMMIT
AS
SELECT MyVar, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM mytable
GROUP BY MyVar;

-- Your query then hits the tiny MV instead of millions of rows:
SELECT cnt FROM mv_myvar_counts WHERE MyVar = 'DONE';

Requirements for FAST refresh: you need a materialized view log on the base table:

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG ON mytable
WITH ROWID, SEQUENCE (MyVar)
INCLUDING NEW VALUES;

This is the most Oracle-idiomatic solution and avoids any application-layer changes.

3. Counter Table with Triggers (Your Idea)

Yes, your idea works — and it's a classic pattern. You maintain a summary table and fire a trigger on updates:

-- Summary table
CREATE TABLE myvar_counts (
    myvar_value VARCHAR2(50) PRIMARY KEY,
    cnt         NUMBER DEFAULT 0
);

-- Trigger on the main table
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_myvar_count
AFTER UPDATE OF MyVar ON mytable
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
    -- Decrement old value
    IF :OLD.MyVar IS NOT NULL THEN
        UPDATE myvar_counts SET cnt = cnt - 1
        WHERE myvar_value = :OLD.MyVar;
    END IF;
    -- Increment new value
    IF :NEW.MyVar IS NOT NULL THEN
        UPDATE myvar_counts SET cnt = cnt + 1
        WHERE myvar_value = :NEW.MyVar;
    END IF;
END;

⚠️ Caveats with this approach:

  • Triggers fire row-by-row, so bulk updates are slow (e.g. UPDATE mytable SET MyVar='DONE' WHERE ... affecting 100k rows = 100k trigger fires)
  • Counter table can become a hot block contention point under high concurrency
  • You need INSERT/DELETE triggers too to keep counts accurate

4. Approximate Count (Oracle 12c+)

If you just need a fast estimate, Oracle has:

SELECT APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(MyVar) FROM mytable;
-- or
SELECT MyVar, APPROX_COUNT(*) ... -- via SQL Tuning Advisor hints

Recommendation

Scenario | Best Approach -- | -- Read-heavy, rare writes | Materialized View Just need fast WHERE = 'X' | Index on MyVar (try this first) App controls all writes | Counter table + trigger Estimate is acceptable | APPROX_COUNT

Start with the index — it requires zero application changes and often solves the problem entirely. If you need the full GROUP BY across all values to be fast, add the Materialized View on top.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-07-17T12:55:13Z)

thanks for your attention Frederick, but indeed cleaning up down to this level old code is definitely out of scope.
At least for me, risk of breaking something with a typo hugely wins over the pain of knowing that a list of PEP-8 comments is there. Of course major typos will be detected immediately, but if something slips in a rarely executed part of the code, we do not have a way to catch it until it becomes a problem in operations.

My guideline is to limit fixes to what makes for **bold** lines in pylint report. And indeed for old code which worked for years and I do not fully understand, I prefer to silence pylint unless the fix is trivial.

Forgive me, for all poor reviews yesterday. Claude did point out much clearer than what i embarrassingly did.

it mentioned one limitation of (head window) as counter example case [1], which TBH i do not clearly understand this corner cases yet.

Claude also mentioned that 1000 chars may not hold high signal error mesg, hopefully they're rare cases.

But Yeah your script did bounded the logs at ~4 MB no matter what the payload does. That was the original goal and It works, and we better not imagine/assume anything about user logs.

[1] The giant line lands inside the head window
head bounds by lines, not bytes. If the file has >4000 newlines and one of the first 1000 lines is enormous, head faithfully pumps that entire line into the pipe and cut throws away all but 1000 bytes of it. Same file size, giant line in two different places:

```
A) giant line at line 1     (INSIDE head window)
   file size          : 209,969,045 bytes
   bytes through head|: 209,765,046 bytes   <-- read+piped to keep 1000
   print_file output  :     203,962 bytes
   wall clock         : 0.756 s

B) giant line at line 2000  (OUTSIDE head window)
   file size          : 209,970,935 bytes
   bytes through head|:      49,890 bytes
   print_file output  :     204,901 bytes
   wall clock         : 0.258 s
```

title: dmwm/CRABServer PR #9415: Split fatal Application segfaults out of 50115 as 50117.
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9415: Split fatal Application segfaults out of 50115 as 50117.

State: closed
Opened: 2026-09-09T15:14:45Z
Closed: 2026-09-28T17:02:30Z
Merged: 2026-09-28T17:02:29Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9415

## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-09-09T15:14:45Z)

(partially) resolves #9357

## Background

50115 currently means "cmsRun did not produce a valid job report" and is retried three times with a 1.3× memory bump. A survey of 1000 tasks that hit 50115 between 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-30 shows the code covers two populations:
 | tasks | behaviour
-- | -- | --
never succeeded after retries | 262 (26.2%) | retries are pure waste
≥80% of failures were 50115, all eventually succeeded | 565 (56.5%) | retries work as intended

TWiki JobExitCode also already confirm/admits the ambiguity that 50115 "often means cmsRun segfaulted".

## This PR includes
It resolves the subset we can identify with confidence:

A segmentation violation that happened **after the event loop started** which may due to user code error or misconfigurations.
> These are relabelled as 50117 fail-fast and not retried. Everything else remains the current 50115 behaviour.

Users get a faster feedback loop on their own crashes, and the grid stops running three copies of a job that cannot succeed.

## Twiki JobExitCodes

50115 — cmsRun did not produce a valid job report at runtime (cause undetermined; retried)
**50117 — cmsRun terminated with a segmentation violation after processing began (not retried)**

## Why CPU seconds, not wall clock
*Claude opus raised, well recommended us to use Cpu time*
A job stalled on sick CVMFS or a hung xrootd read accumulates wall time while burning almost no CPU — a wall-clock gate would misclassify exactly the transient population this PR is trying to protect. Since 50115 means there is no FJR, the classad (RemoteUserCpu + RemoteSysCpu) is the only available source.

The **SEGFAULT_CPU_THRESHOLD** should be safe threshold and derived from the **survey data of 262 workflows**

## Things will follow up on another PR

New codes for the 565-task transient population. Their behaviour is already correct; new codes there buy monitoring granularity only, and every published code is a permanent commitment in user-facing docs. Revisit once the log patterns are proven.

title: dmwm/CRABServer PR #9432: Notify the user via CRAB_UserEmail on too many fatal ASO errors
body:
# dmwm/CRABServer pull request #9432: Notify the user via CRAB_UserEmail on too many fatal ASO errors State: closed Opened: 2026-09-26T12:46:33Z Closed: 2026-10-01T16:05:36Z Merged: 2026-10-01T16:05:36Z URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9432 ## Opening post (nausikt, 2026-09-26T12:46:33Z) PR on top of #9431 ## Short Summary This PR refactored the existing ASO logic into proper `handleTooManyFatalAsoErrors` handler fn and added `sendMaxFatalAsoMailToUser` as a separate path from operator mailing, which may be used to provide additional debugging information for prod env in the future. Also added safety locks for UserMail firing. ### Context Since #9383/#9416, PostJob kills a task (or, with `maxFatalAsoDryRun`, pretends to) once fatal stageout errors cross the `maxFatalAsoNumber` / `RelativeFraction` / `AbsoluteFraction` thresholds, and mails the operators about it. That path is running in production and is **not changed here**. This PR adds the end-user half of #9419: the same event is reported to the task owner, addressed to the `CRAB_UserEmail` classAd. ### What changes - **`config.TaskWorker.maxFatalAsoSendUserMail`** (new, default `False`) is a safety lock for the user notification: - `False`: the mail is only written to the PostJob log as `Firing email:
` followed by subject and body. Nothing reaches the Mail Transfer Agent (MTA). - `True`: it is handed to `/usr/bin/mail`, same transport as the operators mail. It can be flipped back at any time should users turn out to be flooded. - **`sendMaxFatalAsoMailToUser(killed)`**: builds a user-worded message (different text when the task was really killed vs. left running in dry run), including the same ASO summary as the operators mail and the `FEEDBACKMAIL` address for help. - **`getUserEmailFromAd()`**: tolerates both - counting ASO `userMailSent` separately from Operator's `mailSent`. Refs #9419 (mail-sending mechanism), builds on #9422 (`CRAB_UserEmail` classAd from CRIC). ## Comment (cmsdmwmbot, 2026-09-26T12:49:23Z) Jenkins results: * Python3 Pylint check: succeeded * Pycodestyle check: succeeded * 290 comments to review Details at https://cmssdt.cern.ch/dmwm-jenkins/view/All/job/DMWM-CRABServer-PR-test/2926/artifact/artifacts/PullRequestReport.html ## Comment (nausikt, 2026-09-26T19:42:16Z) I’ve been trying to trigger the numErrors > 100, maxFatalASORelative: 0.5, and maxFatalASOAbsolute: 0.1 conditions in an E2E test manner submit 1000-jobs task, but still no luck.
